knowledge_statements.title: Augmented Lagrangian Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical multiplier iteration for smooth equality-constrained nonlinear programs, using inexact first-order stationary points of augmented-Lagrangian subproblems and an adaptive penalty parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), and define \(\mathcal L_ho(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}c(x)+ rac{ho}{2}\lVert c(x)Vert^2\). Choose \(x^0\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\lambda^0\in\mathbb R^m\), \(ho_0>0\), \(\eta\in(0,1)\), \(\gamma>1\), nonnegative sequences \((\varepsilon_k)_{k\ge0}\), and stopping tolerances \(	au_c,	au_L\ge0\). For each \(k\ge0\), compute \(x^{k+1}\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(\lVert
abla_x\mathcal L_{ho_k}(x^{k+1},\lambda^k)Vert\le\varepsilon_k\), set \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+ho_k c(x^{k+1})\), and set \(ho_{k+1}=ho_k\) if \(\lVert c(x^{k+1})Vert\le\eta\lVert c(x^k)Vert\), or \(ho_{k+1}=\gammaho_k\) otherwise. If \(\lVert c(x^{k+1})Vert\le	au_c\) and \(\lVert
abla f(x^{k+1})+
abla c(x^{k+1})^{\mathsf T}\lambda^{k+1}Vert\le	au_L\), stop and return \((x^{k+1},\lambda^{k+1})\); otherwise continue.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iteration, compute a point satisfying an inexact first-order stationarity test for the current augmented Lagrangian, update the equality-constraint multiplier using the new residual, retain the penalty when the residual contracts sufficiently, and increase it otherwise. Return the current primal-dual pair if the prescribed feasibility and Lagrangian-stationarity tests hold.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) are continuously differentiable.
At every executed iteration, an \(x^{k+1}\) satisfying the stated inexact stationarity test is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the stopping tests hold at an iteration, the returned pair satisfies the prescribed primal-feasibility and Lagrangian-stationarity tolerances.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Three practical ALM formulations for inequality constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A method-family classification, not a convergence claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \text{Practical ALM treatments of nonlinear inequalities may be organized as }\{\text{bound-constrained},\ \text{linearly constrained},\ \text{unconstrained}\}\text{ formulations}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Practical augmented-Lagrangian procedures for nonlinear inequality constraints fall into three principal formulation families: bound-constrained, linearly constrained, and unconstrained inner formulations.
assumptions_latex: \text{The nonlinear program contains inequality constraints to be handled by an augmented-Lagrangian procedure.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The constraint-handling formulation belongs to the bound-constrained, linearly constrained, or unconstrained family.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local positive definiteness and constraint-gradient independence at augmented-Lagrangian minimizers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The point $x_k$ is the unique local augmented-Lagrangian subproblem solution supplied by the preceding part of the same theorem; the result remains conditional on the assumptions of the referenced preceding theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose the assumptions of the referenced preceding theorem hold at $(x^*,\lambda^*)$, let $\bar\mu$ be chosen as in that theorem, and let $x_k$ be the unique local augmented-Lagrangian subproblem solution furnished by the preceding part. Then there exist $\delta,\epsilon,M>0$ such that, for every $(\lambda^k,\mu_k)$ satisfying $\|\lambda^k-\lambda^*\|\leq\mu_k\delta$ and $\mu_k\geq\bar\mu$,
\[
\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L_A(x_k,\lambda^k;\mu_k)\succ0,
\]
and the family $\{\nabla c_i(x_k):i\in\mathcal E\}$ is linearly independent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the assumptions and penalty threshold of the referenced preceding theorem, the unique nearby augmented-Lagrangian subproblem solution has a positive-definite augmented-Lagrangian Hessian, and the equality-constraint gradients at that point are linearly independent, for every multiplier–penalty pair satisfying the stated scaled-neighborhood and lower-penalty conditions.
assumptions_latex: \text{The assumptions of the referenced preceding theorem hold at }(x^*,\lambda^*).
\bar\mu\text{ is chosen as in the referenced preceding theorem.}
x_k\text{ is the unique local subproblem solution furnished by the preceding part.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local existence, uniqueness, and primal error bound for an augmented-Lagrangian subproblem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is conditional on the assumptions and penalty threshold supplied by the referenced preceding theorem; those assumptions are not restated in the extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose the assumptions of the referenced preceding theorem hold at $(x^*,\lambda^*)$, and let $\bar\mu$ be chosen as in that theorem. Then there exist $\delta,\epsilon,M>0$ such that, for every $(\lambda^k,\mu_k)$ satisfying $\|\lambda^k-\lambda^*\|\leq \mu_k\delta$ and $\mu_k\geq\bar\mu$, the problem
\[
\min_x\ \mathcal L_A(x,\lambda^k;\mu_k)\quad\text{subject to }\|x-x^*\|\leq\epsilon
\]
has a unique solution $x_k$, and
\[
\|x_k-x^*\|\leq M\frac{\|\lambda^k-\lambda^*\|}{\mu_k}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the assumptions and penalty threshold of the referenced preceding theorem, positive constants delta, epsilon, and M exist such that every multiplier–penalty pair sufficiently close in the scaled sense yields a unique augmented-Lagrangian minimizer in the epsilon-neighborhood of the solution. Its distance from the solution is at most M times the multiplier error divided by the penalty parameter.
assumptions_latex: \text{The assumptions of the referenced preceding theorem hold at }(x^*,\lambda^*).
\bar\mu\text{ is chosen as in the referenced preceding theorem.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasibility branching and matrix-free trust-region solution in BCL
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The convergence-preserving freedom in numerical constants is stated only as reported; the extract does not specify the admissible ranges of replacement values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \begin{gathered}\|c(x_k)\|\le\eta_k\Rightarrow \mu_{k+1}=\mu_k,\ \lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k-\mu_kc(x_k)\text{ and the tolerances are tightened},\\ \|c(x_k)\|>\eta_k\Rightarrow \mu_{k+1}>\mu_k,\ \lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k.\\ \min_d\ \frac12d^T\!\left[\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda^k)+\mu_kA_k^TA_k\right]d+\nabla_x\mathcal L_A(x_k,\lambda^k;\mu_k)^Td\\ \text{s.t. }l\le x_k+d\le u,\quad \|d\|_\infty\le\Delta.\end{gathered}
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After an approximate inner solve, acceptable constraint reduction causes the BCL method to keep the penalty fixed, update the multiplier estimate, and tighten tolerances; inadequate reduction causes it to increase the penalty, leave the multipliers unchanged, and focus on feasibility. The particular constants 0.1, 0.9, and 100 are not essential, although the extract does not give admissible replacement ranges. A practical inner solver approximately minimizes a box- and infinity-norm-constrained quadratic model with curvature ∇²L+μAᵀA: projected-gradient search first identifies bound components, and conjugate gradients then optimize over free components. This requires matrix-vector products rather than KKT or Jacobian factorizations. The Lagrangian Hessian may be replaced by BFGS or SR1, and partial separability may be exploited.
assumptions_latex: x_k\text{ is an outer BCL iterate after an approximate solution of the bound-constrained subproblem}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The feasibility test selects either multiplier updating at fixed penalty or penalty growth at fixed multipliers, and the stated two-stage inner method can be implemented without KKT or Jacobian factorizations.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The update is identified only by a referenced formula absent from the extract; the theorem is therefore stated conditionally using that referenced update without reconstructing it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose the assumptions of the referenced preceding theorem hold at $(x^*,\lambda^*)$, and let $\bar\mu$ be chosen as in that theorem. Then there exist $\delta,\epsilon,M>0$ such that, for every $(\lambda^k,\mu_k)$ satisfying $\|\lambda^k-\lambda^*\|\leq\mu_k\delta$ and $\mu_k\geq\bar\mu$, the multiplier $\lambda^{k+1}$ defined by the referenced augmented-Lagrangian update satisfies
\[
\|\lambda^{k+1}-\lambda^*\|\leq M\frac{\|\lambda^k-\lambda^*\|}{\mu_k}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the assumptions and penalty threshold of the referenced preceding theorem, positive constants delta, epsilon, and M exist such that, whenever the current multiplier satisfies the stated scaled-neighborhood condition and the penalty is sufficiently large, the referenced augmented-Lagrangian multiplier update reduces the multiplier error to at most M times the current error divided by the penalty parameter.

directory_assessment.rationale: The listed hierarchy has no precise container for local primal–dual stability and convergence estimates of equality-constrained augmented-Lagrangian iterations. This extraction-grounded structural proposal requires independent review.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records the stated numerical initialization, inexactness and feasibility tests, update branches, and stopping rule; it does not assert convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \begin{gathered}\mu_0=10,\quad \omega_0=\mu_0^{-1},\quad \eta_0=\mu_0^{-0.1}.\\ r_k:=x_k-P_{[l,u]}\!\left(x_k-\nabla_x\mathcal L_A(x_k,\lambda^k;\mu_k)\right),\qquad \|r_k\|\le\omega_k.\\ \|c(x_k)\|\le\eta_k:\ \begin{cases}\text{stop if }\|c(x_k)\|\le\eta_*\text{ and }\|r_k\|\le\omega_*,\\ \lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k-\mu_kc(x_k),\ \mu_{k+1}=\mu_k,\\ \eta_{k+1}=\eta_k/\mu_{k+1}^{0.9},\ \omega_{k+1}=\omega_k/\mu_{k+1};\end{cases}\\ \|c(x_k)\|>\eta_k:\ \begin{cases}\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k,\ \mu_{k+1}=100\mu_k,\\ \eta_{k+1}=\mu_{k+1}^{-0.1},\ \omega_{k+1}=\mu_{k+1}^{-1}.\end{cases}\end{gathered}
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from x₀ and λ⁰, set μ₀=10, ω₀=1/μ₀, and η₀=1/μ₀^0.1. At iteration k, approximately solve the box-constrained augmented-Lagrangian subproblem until its projected-gradient residual is at most ω_k. If constraint violation is at most η_k, stop when it and the projected residual also meet the final tolerances; otherwise update λ by λ^{k+1}=λ^k−μ_kc(x_k), keep μ fixed, and tighten both tolerances. If constraint violation exceeds η_k, keep λ fixed, multiply μ by 100, and reset the tolerances from the new penalty value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The iteration stops only when }\|c(x_k)\|\le\eta_*\text{ and }\|r_k\|\le\omega_*;\text{ otherwise it follows the stated successful- or unsuccessful-feasibility update branch.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence property when penalty-reduction iterations occur infinitely often.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the penalty-reduction step is executed infinitely often and the feasibility tolerances satisfy \[\sum_{l=1}^{k_{i+1}-k_i}\eta_{k_i+l}\leq\kappa_\eta\mu_{k_i+1}^{\alpha_\eta}\quad(i\geq0)\] for some \(\kappa_\eta,\alpha_\eta>0\), then \[\lim_{k\to\infty}\mu_k\|y_k\|=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If significant penalty reductions occur infinitely often and the feasibility tolerances satisfy the stated inter-reduction summability bound, then the product of the penalty parameter and the norm of the multiplier estimate converges to zero.
assumptions_latex: \text{The penalty-reduction step is executed infinitely often}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasibility and Optimality of Augmented-Lagrangian Accumulation Points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The algorithm is run with zero tolerance. Boundedness of the full multiplier sequence is required only for the stronger global-optimality conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume that the feasible region \(X\) is nonempty and Algorithm 10.4.1 is run with \(\epsilon=0\). Every accumulation point \(x^*\) of the generated sequence \(\{x_k\}\) is feasible. If, in addition, \(\{\lambda^{(k)}\}\) is bounded, then \(x^*\) is a solution of the original problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonempty feasible problem and zero stopping tolerance, every accumulation point of the primal sequence is feasible. If the multiplier sequence is bounded, every such accumulation point is a global solution of the original problem.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mixed-Constraint Augmented Lagrangian and Multiplier Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the extract's constraint-sign convention. The stationarity identity requires differentiability and exact stationarity of the unconstrained augmented-Lagrangian subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For equality indices \(i\le m_e\), inequality indices \(i>m_e\), and \(\sigma_i>0\), define
\[
P(x,\lambda,\sigma)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^{m_e}\left[-\lambda_i c_i(x)+\tfrac12\sigma_i c_i(x)^2\right]+
\sum_{i=m_e+1}^{m}\begin{cases}
-\lambda_i c_i(x)+\tfrac12\sigma_i c_i(x)^2,&c_i(x)<\lambda_i/\sigma_i,\\
-\tfrac12\lambda_i^2/\sigma_i,&c_i(x)\ge\lambda_i/\sigma_i.
\end{cases}
\]
If \(x_{k+1}\) solves \(\min_xP(x,\lambda^{(k)},\sigma^{(k)})\), update
\[
\lambda_i^{(k+1)}=\lambda_i^{(k)}-\sigma_i^{(k)}c_i(x_{k+1})\quad(i\le m_e),
\]
\[
\lambda_i^{(k+1)}=\max\{\lambda_i^{(k)}-\sigma_i^{(k)}c_i(x_{k+1}),0\}\quad(i>m_e).
\]
Then
\[
\nabla f(x_{k+1})-\sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_i^{(k+1)}\nabla c_i(x_{k+1})=0.
\]
Consequently, for \(k\ge2\), the extract's stated KKT-error measure equals \(\|c^{(-)}(x_k)\|\). If
\[
|c_i^{(-)}(x_{k+1})|\le\tfrac14|c_i^{(-)}(x_k)|
\]
fails, the basic rule sets \(\sigma_i^{(k+1)}=10\sigma_i^{(k)}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The mixed-constraint augmented Lagrangian combines quadratic equality terms with piecewise quadratic inequality terms. Exact subproblem stationarity, direct equality-multiplier updates, and projected inequality-multiplier updates yield the stated Lagrangian stationarity equation. Under this identity, the extract's residual reduces to constraint violation, and a penalty component is increased when its violation fails to contract sufficiently.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The extract explicitly states the multiplier recurrence and additionally invokes bounds (14.2.16) and (14.2.18).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the conditions of Lemma 14.2.2(iii) hold and, for some \(\kappa_{13},\kappa_{14}>0\), \[\lVert y_{k+1}^E-y_*\rVert\leq\kappa_{13}\lVert x_k-x_*\rVert+\kappa_{14}\omega_k\] for every sufficiently large \(k\in\mathcal K\). Then there exist \(\mu_{\max},\kappa_3,\kappa_4,\kappa_5,\kappa_6>0\) and an integer \(k_0\) such that, if \(\mu_{k_0}\leq\mu_{\max}\), bounds (14.2.16) and (14.2.18) hold and \[\lVert y_{k+1}^E-y_*\rVert\leq\kappa_5\omega_k+\kappa_6\mu_k\lVert y_k-y_*\rVert\] for every \(k\in\mathcal K\) with \(k\geq k_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If multiplier estimates are locally controlled by primal error and inner tolerance, then a sufficiently small penalty parameter yields the referenced local bounds and a recurrence controlling the next multiplier error by the tolerance and the current scaled multiplier error.
assumptions_latex: \(\lVert y_{k+1}^E-y_*\rVert\leq\kappa_{13}\lVert x_k-x_*\rVert+\kappa_{14}\omega_k\) for all sufficiently large \(k\in\mathcal K\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(k\in\mathcal K\), \(k\geq k_0\), bounds (14.2.16), (14.2.18), and \(\lVert y_{k+1}^E-y_*\rVert\leq\kappa_5\omega_k+\kappa_6\mu_k\lVert y_k-y_*\rVert\) hold.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The referenced augmented-Lagrangian subproblem and multiplier formulas are supplied by the immediately preceding extracted item; the primal subproblem is only required to be minimized approximately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose \(x_1\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\lambda^{(1)}\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(\lambda_i^{(1)}\ge0\) for inequality indices \(i\in I\), \(\sigma_i^{(1)}>0\), \(\epsilon\ge0\), and set \(k=1\). Find an approximate minimizer \(x_{k+1}\) of
\[
\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}P(x,\lambda^{(k)},\sigma^{(k)}).
\]
Stop if \(\|c^{(-)}(x_{k+1})\|_\infty\le\epsilon\). Otherwise set
\[
\sigma_i^{(k+1)}=\begin{cases}
\sigma_i^{(k)},&|c_i^{(-)}(x_{k+1})|\le\tfrac14|c_i^{(-)}(x_k)|,\\
\max\{10\sigma_i^{(k)},k^2\},&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\]
and update
\[
\lambda_i^{(k+1)}=\lambda_i^{(k)}-\sigma_i^{(k)}c_i(x_{k+1})\quad(i\le m_e),
\]
\[
\lambda_i^{(k+1)}=\max\{\lambda_i^{(k)}-\sigma_i^{(k)}c_i(x_{k+1}),0\}\quad(i>m_e).
\]
Increment \(k\) and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximately minimize the current augmented Lagrangian and stop when the infinity norm of constraint violation is within tolerance. Retain a penalty component when its violation contracts by a factor of at least four; otherwise replace it by the larger of ten times its current value and the squared iteration index. Then update equality multipliers directly and inequality multipliers by nonnegative projection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|c^{(-)}(x_{k+1})\|_\infty\le\epsilon\ \text{at termination; otherwise the penalty and multiplier sequences are updated by the stated rules.}

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), let \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) denote equality residuals, let \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^r\) denote one-sided inequality residuals written as \(g(x)\leq0\), and let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a simple set that may be retained explicitly.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic models with quadratic augmentation; the definition classifies representations, not algorithms or convergence conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An augmented-Lagrangian representation is a parametrized function \(\mathcal A_\rho(x,y)\) minimized over a declared domain \(x\in X\), obtained by combining \(f\), multiplier pairings, and quadratic or projected-quadratic residual terms. Canonical representation classes are: \[\mathcal A_\rho^{\rm eq}(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^Th(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|h(x)\|^2,\] \[\mathcal A_\rho^{\rm ineq}(x,\mu)=f(x)+\frac1{2\rho}\bigl(\|[\mu+\rho g(x)]_+\|^2-\|\mu\|^2\bigr),\quad \mu\in\mathbb R_+^r,\] and their mixed sum, possibly minimized over \(X\). Equivalent slack representations introduce \(s\geq0\) and augment \(g(x)+s=0\); retained-constraint representations leave bounds or linearized constraints in the subproblem domain. Two representations belong to the same class when elimination of their auxiliary variables gives the same reduced function up to an additive term independent of \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An augmented-Lagrangian representation combines the objective with multiplier terms and quadratic or projected-quadratic measures of constraint residuals. Equality constraints use the ordinary quadratic augmented Lagrangian. One-sided inequalities use the positive-part projected formula. Mixed models add the two contributions. Inequalities may equivalently be represented by nonnegative slacks, while simple bounds or linearized constraints may remain explicit in the subproblem. Representations are equivalent when eliminating auxiliary variables produces the same function of the primal variable up to a constant independent of that variable.
assumptions_latex: Any retained set \(X\) and every auxiliary-variable domain are stated as part of the representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The taxonomy is determined by which constraints are augmented, which are retained explicitly, and whether one-sided feasibility is represented by slacks or by projection onto \(\mathbb R_+^r\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(g(x)\leq0\), minimizing the equality augmented Lagrangian of \(g(x)+s=0\) over \(s\geq0\) yields the projected inequality expression, up to an \(x\)-independent constant.
Changing from \(g(x)\leq0\) to \(c(x)=-g(x)\geq0\) changes the multiplier sign convention but not the represented feasible set.
special_cases_latex: With \(r=0\), the mixed model reduces to equality augmentation.
With \(m=0\), it reduces to projected inequality augmentation.
With \(X=\mathbb R^n\), no constraint is retained explicitly.
immediate_consequences_latex: The same nonlinear program can admit several equivalent augmented representations with different subproblem domains.
Additive terms depending on multipliers and \(\rho\), but not on \(x\), do not change primal subproblem minimizers.
boundary_notes: This taxonomy excludes barrier functions and nonsmooth exact penalties unless they are explicitly combined with an augmented term.
Cone-valued residuals require replacing the componentwise positive part by the appropriate cone projection.

notation.meaning: Componentwise projection of a vector onto the nonnegative orthant.
Constraint set retained in each augmented subproblem.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equality augmented Lagrangian and multiplier update
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The infeasibility comparison is an approximate motivation, not a convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \min_x f(x) subject to c_i(x)=0\ (i\in\mathcal E), define
\[
\mathcal L_A(x,\lambda;\mu)=f(x)-\sum_{i\in\mathcal E}\lambda_i c_i(x)+\frac{\mu}{2}\sum_{i\in\mathcal E}c_i(x)^2,\qquad \mu>0.
\]
If \(x_k\) approximately minimizes \(\mathcal L_A(\cdot,\lambda^k;\mu_k)\), then
\[
0\approx\nabla f(x_k)-\sum_{i\in\mathcal E}[\lambda_i^k-\mu_kc_i(x_k)]\nabla c_i(x_k),
\]
which motivates
\[
\lambda_i^{k+1}=\lambda_i^k-\mu_kc_i(x_k),\qquad i\in\mathcal E.
\]
Heuristically, comparison with the KKT conditions gives \(c_i(x_k)\approx-(\lambda_i^*-\lambda_i^k)/\mu_k\); thus a multiplier estimate close to \(\lambda^*\) can yield infeasibility much smaller than the pure quadratic-penalty scale \(1/\mu_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For equality constraints, the augmented Lagrangian combines the ordinary Lagrangian with a quadratic constraint penalty. Approximate stationarity of its primal subproblem suggests correcting each multiplier by subtracting the penalty parameter times the corresponding constraint residual. The resulting heuristic relation explains why an accurate current multiplier estimate can produce substantially smaller infeasibility than a pure quadratic-penalty subproblem at the same penalty parameter.
assumptions_latex: x_k\text{ is an approximate minimizer of }\mathcal L_A(\cdot,\lambda^k;\mu_k)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equality augmented Lagrangian and stationarity-induced multiplier correction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The residual and multiplier relations are heuristic comparisons with the equality-constrained first-order conditions, not convergence or error-bound theorems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the equality-constrained problem \(\min_x f(x)\) subject to \(c_i(x)=0\) for \(i\in\mathcal E\), define
\[
\mathcal L_A(x,\lambda;\mu)=f(x)-\sum_{i\in\mathcal E}\lambda_i c_i(x)+\frac{\mu}{2}\sum_{i\in\mathcal E}c_i(x)^2,\qquad \mu>0.
\]
If \(x_k\) approximately minimizes \(\mathcal L_A(\cdot,\lambda^k;\mu_k)\), then its approximate stationarity condition is
\[
0\approx \nabla f(x_k)-\sum_{i\in\mathcal E}\bigl(\lambda_i^k-\mu_kc_i(x_k)\bigr)\nabla c_i(x_k).
\]
Comparison with the equality-constrained first-order conditions motivates
\[
\lambda_i^{k+1}=\lambda_i^k-\mu_kc_i(x_k),\qquad i\in\mathcal E.
\]
Heuristically, \(c_i(x_k)\approx-(\lambda_i^*-\lambda_i^k)/\mu_k\); hence, when \(\lambda^k\) is close to \(\lambda^*\), the residual can be smaller than the \(1/\mu_k\) scale arising from the pure quadratic-penalty motivation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The equality augmented Lagrangian combines the ordinary Lagrangian with a quadratic penalty. Approximate stationarity of its primal subproblem identifies the corrected multiplier as the current multiplier minus the penalty parameter times the constraint residual. A heuristic comparison with the constrained first-order conditions explains why an accurate multiplier estimate can reduce infeasibility at a moderate penalty value.
assumptions_latex: \text{The residual relation is obtained by heuristic comparison with first-order conditions at }(x^*,\lambda^*)

children.title: Smooth Nonlinear-Programming Models
children.top_down_role: Classical augmented models for smooth equality, inequality, and mixed systems.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^r\) be continuously differentiable, with the nonlinear program \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\leq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear programming. The projected inequality model is continuously differentiable in the primal variable when the data are continuously differentiable, but generally is not twice differentiable at switching surfaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\rho>0\), \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\mu\in\mathbb R_+^r\), the canonical smooth-NLP augmented model is \[\mathcal L_\rho(x,\lambda,\mu)=f(x)+\lambda^Th(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|h(x)\|^2+\frac1{2\rho}\sum_{j=1}^r\left([\mu_j+\rho g_j(x)]_+^2-\mu_j^2\right).\] An augmented subproblem minimizes \(x\mapsto\mathcal L_\rho(x,\lambda,\mu)\), either over \(\mathbb R^n\) or over a separately declared simple set \(X\). This model combines the ordinary equality augmented Lagrangian with the Powell–Hestenes–Rockafellar reduction for inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The canonical smooth nonlinear-programming model adds the equality multiplier and squared-residual terms to the objective and adds, for every inequality, a projected quadratic term based on the positive part of the shifted multiplier. The primal augmented subproblem minimizes this function over all variables or over a separately retained simple set.
assumptions_latex: \(f,h,g\in C^1\) on an open set containing the subproblem domain.
Equality and inequality constraints use the conventions \(h(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\leq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed function is the mixed smooth-NLP augmented-Lagrangian representation and is \(C^1\) in \(x\) whenever \(f,h,g\) are \(C^1\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The inequality contribution equals \(\mu^Tg^+(x,\mu,\rho)+(\rho/2)\|g^+(x,\mu,\rho)\|^2\), where \(g_j^+=\max\{g_j(x),-\mu_j/\rho\}\).
special_cases_latex: If \(r=0\), this is the classical equality-constrained quadratic augmented Lagrangian.
If \(m=0\), only the projected inequality contribution remains.
immediate_consequences_latex: For an inactive component satisfying \(\mu_j+\rho g_j(x)\leq0\), its contribution is the constant \(-\mu_j^2/(2\rho)\).
For an active component satisfying \(\mu_j+\rho g_j(x)>0\), its contribution is \(\mu_jg_j(x)+(\rho/2)g_j(x)^2\).
boundary_notes: Twice continuous differentiability can fail where \(\mu_j+\rho g_j(x)=0\).
Nonsmooth objectives or cone-valued constraints are outside this slot.

children.title: Equality-Constrained Augmented Lagrangians
children.top_down_role: Quadratically augmented equality models and their scaled variants.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in X} f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\), where \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), and \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional equality constraints with Euclidean quadratic augmentation; no convexity or differentiability is required merely to define the function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every penalty parameter \(\rho>0\) and multiplier \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\), the equality-constrained augmented Lagrangian is the function \(\mathcal L_\rho:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) defined by \[\mathcal L_\rho(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^Th(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|h(x)\|_2^2.\] The associated augmented subproblem at fixed \((\lambda,\rho)\) is \(\min_{x\in X}\mathcal L_\rho(x,[0m\lambda)\). Under the scaled multiplier \(u=\lambda/\rho\), the same function is \[\mathcal L_\rho(x,\rho u)=f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|h(x)+u\|_2^2-rac{\rho}{2}\|u\|_2^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an equality-constrained problem, the quadratic augmented Lagrangian is the objective plus the multiplier pairing with the equality residual and one half of the positive penalty parameter times the squared Euclidean residual norm. Fixing the multiplier and penalty parameter gives a subproblem over the retained set. Dividing the multiplier by the penalty parameter gives the equivalent completed-square scaled form.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), and \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed formula defines the canonical quadratic augmented Lagrangian for \(h(x)=0\), and the scaled and unscaled expressions differ only by the multiplier reparameterization \(u=\lambda/\rho\).
special_cases_latex: For \(\lambda=0\), the function is the quadratic penalty function.
For \(h(x)=Ax-b\), the augmentation is quadratic in the affine residual.
immediate_consequences_latex: At every feasible point, \(\mathcal L_\rho(x,\lambda)=f(x)\).
The constant term in the scaled form does not affect minimization with respect to \(x\).
boundary_notes: The definition alone does not assert existence or uniqueness of a subproblem minimizer.
Sign conventions using \(-\lambda^Th(x)\) are equivalent after replacing \(\lambda\) by \(-\lambda\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict local minimality of the augmented Lagrangian at the exact multiplier
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local equality-constrained result for the classical quadratic augmented Lagrangian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x^*\) be a local solution of
\[
\min_x f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad c_i(x)=0,\ i\in\mathcal E.
\]
Assume LICQ at \(x^*\), so \(\{\nabla c_i(x^*):i\in\mathcal E\}\) is linearly independent, and assume the second-order sufficient conditions hold at \((x^*,\lambda^*)\). Then there exists \(\bar\mu\) such that, for every \(\mu\ge\bar\mu\), \(x^*\) is a strict local minimizer of \(\mathcal L_A(\cdot,\lambda^*;\mu)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a local equality-constrained solution satisfies LICQ and the second-order sufficient conditions for its optimal multiplier, then the solution is a strict local minimizer of the augmented Lagrangian evaluated at that multiplier for every sufficiently large penalty parameter.
assumptions_latex: x^*\text{ is a local solution of }\min f(x)\text{ subject to }c_i(x)=0\ (i\in\mathcal E)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\bar\mu\ \forall\mu\ge\bar\mu:\quad x^*\text{ is a strict local minimizer of }\mathcal L_A(\cdot,\lambda^*;\mu).

children.title: Equality-Metric Scaling Family
children.top_down_role: Metric, scaling, and constraint-weighting variants.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), and let \(W\in\mathbb S_{++}^m\) be a positive-definite metric on the equality-residual space.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional equality augmentation with a fixed symmetric positive-definite residual metric. Iteration-dependent or singular metrics are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\rho>0\), \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(W\in\mathbb S_{++}^m\), the metric-scaled equality augmented Lagrangian is \[\mathcal L_{\rho,W}(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^Th(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}h(x)^TWh(x).\] Equivalently, with \(u=\rho^{-1}W^{-1}\lambda\), \[\mathcal L_{\rho,W}(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|h(x)+u\|_W^2-rac{[0m\rho}{2}\|u\|_W^2,\qquad \|v\|_W^2=v^TWv.\] A diagonal \(W=\operatorname{diag}(w_1,[0m\ldots,w_m)\) assigns the effective penalty \(\rho w_i\) to residual \(h_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A metric-scaled equality augmented Lagrangian replaces the Euclidean squared residual by the squared norm induced by a symmetric positive-definite matrix. Completing the square gives an equivalent scaled-multiplier form. A positive diagonal metric gives separate positive weights to the equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family consists precisely of quadratic equality augmentations whose residual penalty is induced by a positive-definite metric \(W\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(W=R^TR\) with nonsingular \(R\), then the penalty is \((\rho/2)\|Rh(x)\|_2^2\).
The Euclidean model is recovered with \(W=I\).
special_cases_latex: Diagonal \(W\) gives componentwise constraint weighting.
A scalar multiple \(W=\alpha I\) is equivalent to replacing \(\rho\) by \(\alpha\rho\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Positive definiteness makes \(\|\cdot\|_W\) a norm and ensures that the quadratic term vanishes exactly when \(h(x)=0\).
boundary_notes: A positive-semidefinite singular matrix may fail to penalize some equality residuals and is not included.
The inspected sources support scalar Euclidean augmentation but did not supply a precise locator for the full positive-definite metric family.
review_flags: A precise authoritative source for the full matrix-weighted family is required; the supplied sources directly support only scalar Euclidean quadratic augmentation.

children.title: Constraint Scaling Variants
children.top_down_role: Equality-model variants based on rescaled constraints or residual coordinates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact boundary between equivalent residual scaling and loss of equality information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a linear residual transformation \(S:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^p\), \(h(x)=0\) implies \(Sh(x)=0\). The converse holds for every residual vector, and hence scaling preserves every equality feasible set, exactly when \(\ker S=\{0\}\). If \(S\) is not injective, any nonzero \(v\in\ker S\) is invisible to the scaled constraint and to the penalty \(\|Sh\|_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual scaling preserves the represented equality system exactly when it is injective; a noninjective scaling can discard violations in its nullspace.

notation.meaning: Residual directions erased by the scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Injectivity Boundary for Constraint Scaling
Constraint Scaling Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality augmented Lagrangians after invertible linear rescaling of residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) be nonsingular and replace \(h(x)=0\) by the equivalent constraint \(S h(x)=0\). With scaled multiplier \(\mu\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(\rho>0\), the resulting augmented Lagrangian is \[\widehat{\mathcal L}_\rho(x,\mu)=f(x)+\mu^{\mathsf T}S h(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert S h(x)\rVert_2^2.\] In the original residual coordinates this equals \(f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}h(x)+(\rho/2)h(x)^{\mathsf T}S^{\mathsf T}S h(x)\), where \(\lambda=S^{\mathsf T}\mu\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invertible scaling preserves the equality feasible set while transforming multipliers and replacing the Euclidean penalty by the metric induced by the scaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat{\mathcal L}_\rho(x,\mu)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}h(x)+(\rho/2)h(x)^{\mathsf T}S^{\mathsf T}S h(x)\) with \(\lambda=S^{\mathsf T}\mu\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spectral Equivalence of Weighted Equality Penalties
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform comparison between a fixed positive-definite weighted residual norm and the Euclidean residual norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(W=W^{\mathsf T}\succ0\), then for every \(r\in\mathbb R^m\), \[\lambda_{\min}(W)\|r\|_2^2\le r^{\mathsf T}Wr\le\lambda_{\max}(W)\|r\|_2^2.\] Consequently the weighted penalty is coercive in residual space, detects feasibility exactly, and differs from the Euclidean quadratic penalty only by fixed spectral factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed positive-definite residual metric is uniformly equivalent to the Euclidean metric, with constants given by its extreme eigenvalues.

notation.meaning: Extreme eigenvalues of the residual metric.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Equivalence of Weighted Equality Penalties
Weighted Equality Metrics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic equality augmentation using a positive-definite residual metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) be symmetric positive definite. For equality residual \(h(x)\in\mathbb R^m\), multiplier \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\rho>0\), the weighted augmented Lagrangian is \[\mathcal L_{\rho,W}(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}h(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}h(x)^{\mathsf T}W h(x).\] The penalty vanishes exactly when \(h(x)=0\), and its residual-space gradient is \(\rho W h(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted equality model measures the residual in a symmetric positive-definite metric instead of the ordinary Euclidean norm.

children.title: Scaling–Weighting Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Interactions between constraint normalization and weighted penalty geometry.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of the equivalence between invertible square scaling and weighted residual geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every symmetric weight \(W\succeq0\) admits a factorization \(W=S^{\mathsf T}S\), but a square factor \(S\) is nonsingular exactly when \(W\succ0\). Therefore a singular positive-semidefinite weight corresponds only to a noninjective square residual scaling and does not preserve the original equality system in general.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive-semidefinite weights factor as squared scalings, but equivalence with invertible square scaling holds exactly for positive-definite weights; singular weights can erase constraint violations.

notation.meaning: Square factor of the residual weight.

knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Compatibility Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonuniqueness of square scaling factors representing one positive-definite residual metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W\succ0\), and let nonsingular \(S_1,S_2\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) satisfy \(S_1^{\mathsf T}S_1=S_2^{\mathsf T}S_2=W\). Then \(Q=S_2S_1^{-1}\) is orthogonal and \(S_2=QS_1\). Conversely, left multiplication of any factor \(S\) by an orthogonal matrix leaves \(S^{\mathsf T}S\) and the weighted penalty unchanged; the scaled augmented model is unchanged after the corresponding multiplier-coordinate transformation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All nonsingular square factors of the same positive-definite weight differ by an orthogonal change of scaled residual coordinates, which does not change the represented weighted model.

notation.meaning: Orthogonal change of scaled residual coordinates.
Two square factors representing the same residual metric.

knowledge_statements.title: Factor Nonuniqueness and Orthogonal Invariance
Scaling–Weighting Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate compatibility between residual scaling and quadratic weighting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) be nonsingular. Scaling \(h(x)=0\) to \(S h(x)=0\) and applying the Euclidean quadratic penalty produces the original-coordinate weight \(W=S^{\mathsf T}S\). Conversely, every symmetric positive-definite \(W\) admits a nonsingular factor \(S\) satisfying \(W=S^{\mathsf T}S\). Under the multiplier transformation \(\lambda=S^{\mathsf T}\mu\), \[f(x)+\mu^{\mathsf T}S h(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert S h(x)\rVert_2^2=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}h(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}h(x)^{\mathsf T}W h(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invertible residual scaling and positive-definite quadratic weighting describe the same model family when multipliers and metrics are transformed consistently.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projected quadratic augmented Lagrangian for inequalities
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)\) subject to \(g(x)\leq0\), where \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^r\) and \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional componentwise one-sided inequalities with nonnegative multipliers and a common positive quadratic penalty parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\rho>0\) and \(\mu\in\mathbb R_+^r\), the canonical inequality augmented Lagrangian is \[\mathcal L_\rho(x,[0m\mu)=f(x)+\frac1{2\rho}\sum_{j=1}^r\left([\mu_j+\rho g_j(x)]_+^2-[0m\mu_j^2\right).\] Equivalently, defining \(g_j^+(x,[0m\mu_j,[0m\rho)=\max\{g_j(x),-[0m\mu_j/[0m\rho\}\), \[\mathcal L_\rho(x,[0m\mu)=f(x)+\mu^Tg^+(x,[0m\mu,[0m\rho)+\frac{[0m\rho}{2}\|g^+(x,[0m\mu,[0m\rho)\|^2.\] The associated augmented subproblem is \(\min_{x\in X}\mathcal L_\rho(x,[0m\mu)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For inequalities written as nonpositive residuals, the augmented Lagrangian uses nonnegative multipliers and the positive part of each shifted multiplier. It can equivalently be expressed with a shifted, truncated residual. The augmented subproblem minimizes this function over the retained domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed projected-quadratic function is the canonical augmented-Lagrangian representation of componentwise one-sided inequalities.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The positive-part and shifted-residual formulas are identical component by component.
It is obtained by minimizing the equality augmented Lagrangian for \(g(x)+s=0\) over \(s\geq0\).
special_cases_latex: For one scalar constraint, the contribution is \(-\mu^2/(2\rho)\) when \(g(x)\leq-\mu/\rho\), and \(\mu g(x)+(\rho/2)g(x)^2\) otherwise.
immediate_consequences_latex: Inactive inequalities can contribute only an \(x\)-independent constant.
At \(\mu=0\), the augmentation is \((\rho/2)\|[g(x)]_+\|^2\).
boundary_notes: The formula depends on the convention \(g(x)\leq0\); the opposite convention changes signs.
Two-sided and cone inequalities require modified projections or separate representations.

children.title: Powell–Hestenes–Rockafellar Models
children.top_down_role: The canonical inequality augmented-Lagrangian family.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(g=(g_1,[0m\ldots,g_r):\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^r\), with feasible inequalities \(g_j(x)\leq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The canonical component-separable quadratic inequality augmented Lagrangian, using nonnegative multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\rho>0\) and \(\mu\in\mathbb R_+^r\), the Powell–Hestenes–Rockafellar model is \[\mathcal L_\rho^{\rm PHR}(x,[0m\mu)=f(x)+\sum_{j=1}^r\phi_\rho(g_j(x),[0m\mu_j),\] where \[\phi_\rho(t,[0m\sigma)=\frac{[\sigma+[0m\rho t]_+^2-[0m\sigma^2}{2\rho}=\begin{cases}\sigma t+\frac{[0m\rho}{2}t^2,&t\geq-[0m\sigma/[0m\rho,\\-\frac{[0m\sigma^2}{2\rho},&t<-[0m\sigma/[0m\rho.\end{cases}\] Its natural multiplier mapping at a primal point is \(\mu^+=[\mu+[0m\rho g(x)]_+\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Powell–Hestenes–Rockafellar model is the sum of separable projected-quadratic kernels, one for each inequality. Above the switching threshold, a kernel is the ordinary multiplier-plus-quadratic expression; below it, the kernel is constant in the residual. The corresponding multiplier mapping projects the shifted multiplier onto the nonnegative orthant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The piecewise kernel \(\phi_\rho\) and the positive-part formula define the same canonical PHR inequality augmented Lagrangian.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\phi_\rho(t,[0m\sigma)=\sigma\max\{t,-[0m\sigma/[0m\rho\}+(\rho/2)\max\{t,-[0m\sigma/[0m\rho\}^2\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The kernel is continuously differentiable in \(t\), with derivative \([\sigma+[0m\rho t]_+\).
Strictly inactive components below the threshold have zero derivative with respect to their residual.
boundary_notes: The kernel generally is not twice differentiable at \(t=-[0m\sigma/[0m\rho\).
This definition does not prescribe a penalty-update or stopping rule.

knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Inequality Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Powell–Hestenes–Rockafellar representation for constraints in nonpositive form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x)\) subject to \(g(x)\leq0\), with multiplier \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\) and \(\rho>0\), the one-sided Powell–Hestenes–Rockafellar augmented Lagrangian is \[\mathcal L_\rho(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\frac{1}{2\rho}\left(\lVert[\lambda+\rho g(x)]_+\rVert_2^2-\lVert\lambda\rVert_2^2\right).\] Componentwise, the contribution of constraint \(i\) is \(((\max\{0,\lambda_i+\rho g_i(x)\})^2-\lambda_i^2)/(2\rho)\), and the associated projected multiplier is \([\lambda+\rho g(x)]_+\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each unilateral constraint contributes a piecewise quadratic term obtained by projecting its shifted multiplier onto the nonnegative orthant.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\phi_{\rho,\lambda}\in C^1(\mathbb R)\), \(\phi'_{\rho,\lambda}(t)=[\lambda+\rho t]_+\), and \(\phi_{\rho,\lambda}\) is not twice differentiable at \(t=-\lambda/\rho\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Piecewise structure and sharp smoothness boundary of a scalar unilateral PHR term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[\phi_{\rho,\lambda}(t)=\frac{[\lambda+\rho t]_+^2-\lambda^2}{2\rho},\] one has \[\phi_{\rho,\lambda}(t)=\begin{cases}-\lambda^2/(2\rho),&t\leq-\lambda/\rho,\\ \lambda t+(\rho/2)t^2,&t\geq-\lambda/\rho.\end{cases}\] Its derivative is \(\phi'_{\rho,\lambda}(t)=[\lambda+\rho t]_+\). Thus the contribution is continuously differentiable but is not twice differentiable at \(t=-\lambda/\rho\). In particular, \(\phi_{\rho,0}(t)=(\rho/2)[t]_+^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scalar unilateral PHR term has constant and quadratic branches joined with a continuous first derivative, but its second derivative jumps at the projection threshold.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(g_j:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) define the unilateral constraint \(g_j(x)\leq0\), with multiplier \(\mu_j\geq0\) and penalty parameter \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A scalar unilateral constraint and finite sums of such constraints; equality terms may be added independently.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The one-sided augmented contribution for \(g_j(x)\leq0\) is \[p_{\rho,j}(x,[0m\mu_j)=\frac{[\mu_j+[0m\rho g_j(x)]_+^2-[0m\mu_j^2}{2\rho}.\] For \(r\) unilateral constraints, the augmented model is \(f(x)+\sum_{j=1}^r p_{\rho,j}(x,[0m\mu_j)\). The switching surface is \(g_j(x)=-[0m\mu_j/[0m\rho\): on its infeasible or active side the term is \(\mu_jg_j(x)+([0m\rho/2)g_j(x)^2\), while on its strictly inactive side it is the constant \(-[0m\mu_j^2/(2\rho)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-sided inequality contributes a projected quadratic term based on its residual and nonnegative multiplier. The term is an ordinary linear-plus-quadratic penalty when the shifted residual is positive and is constant when the inequality is sufficiently inactive. Multiple unilateral constraints contribute additively.
assumptions_latex: For several constraints, the projection and summation are componentwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The function \(p_{\rho,j}\) is the canonical one-sided quadratic augmented term for the unilateral constraint \(g_j(x)\leq0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Introducing \(s_j^2\geq0\) through \(g_j(x)+s_j^2=0\) and minimizing its equality augmented term over \(s_j\) produces \(p_{\rho,j}\).
special_cases_latex: If \(g_j(x)=a_j^Tx-b_j\), the active branch is a quadratic function of \(x\).
If \(\mu_j=0\), the term is the squared positive-part penalty.
immediate_consequences_latex: The derivative with respect to the scalar residual is \([\mu_j+[0m\rho g_j(x)]_+\).
The natural multiplier projection preserves nonnegativity.
boundary_notes: The definition does not represent a lower-and-upper interval with one multiplier.
The opposite sign convention requires replacing the positive part accordingly.

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Sided Inequality Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interval constraints represented by paired one-sided augmented terms, including components with infinite endpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), and consider \(\ell_i\leq c_i(x)\leq u_i\), where \(-\infty\leq\ell_i<u_i\leq+\infty\). Define \(I_L=\{i:\ell_i> -\infty\}\), \(I_U=\{i:u_i<+\infty\}\), \(g^L_i(x)=\ell_i-c_i(x)\) for \(i\in I_L\), and \(g^U_i(x)=c_i(x)-u_i\) for \(i\in I_U\). For \(\alpha\in\mathbb R_+^{|I_L|}\), \(\beta\in\mathbb R_+^{|I_U|}\), and \(\rho>0\), the two-sided augmented Lagrangian is \[\mathcal L_\rho(x,\alpha,\beta)=f(x)+\frac{\lVert[\alpha+\rho g^L(x)]_+\rVert_2^2-\lVert\alpha\rVert_2^2}{2\rho}+\frac{\lVert[\beta+\rho g^U(x)]_+\rVert_2^2-\lVert\beta\rVert_2^2}{2\rho}.\] Thus each finite lower or upper endpoint contributes its corresponding one-sided projected quadratic term, while an infinite endpoint contributes no term.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An interval constraint is represented by separate projected quadratic terms for its finite lower and upper endpoints; infinite endpoints contribute no term.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal L_\rho\) is the sum of the one-sided models for the finite lower-endpoint residuals \(g^L\) and finite upper-endpoint residuals \(g^U\).

notation.meaning: index sets of finite lower and upper endpoints
lower- and upper-endpoint residual mappings on their respective index sets
multipliers for finite lower and upper endpoints

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Single-multiplier model for a two-sided inequality
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(g_j:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and finite bounds \(\alpha_j<[0m\beta_j\) define \(\alpha_j\leq g_j(x)\leq[0m\beta_j\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interval constraints represented with one signed multiplier per interval rather than two nonnegative multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\rho>0\) and a signed multiplier \(\mu_j\in\mathbb R\), define \(u_j(x,[0m\mu_j,[0m\rho)\) by \[u_j=\begin{cases}g_j(x)-[0m\beta_j,&\mu_j+[0m\rho(g_j(x)-[0m\beta_j)>0,\\g_j(x)-[0m\alpha_j,&\mu_j+[0m\rho(g_j(x)-[0m\alpha_j)<0,\\-[0m\mu_j/[0m\rho,&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}\] The interval augmented kernel is \(p_j(g_j(x),[0m\mu_j,[0m\rho)=\mu_ju_j+([0m\rho/2)u_j^2\), and the model for several intervals is \(f(x)+\sum_jp_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-sided constraint can be augmented with one signed multiplier. The selected residual is the violation of the upper bound, the violation of the lower bound, or the constant scaled multiplier when the shifted point lies in the interval's neutral region. The augmented kernel is the multiplier pairing with this selected residual plus its quadratic penalty.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalence of slack and projected inequality augmentation
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^r\), with \(g(x)\leq0\), and introduce a nonnegative slack \(s\in\mathbb R_+^r\) satisfying \(g(x)+s=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact algebraic equivalence at fixed primal point, multiplier, and positive penalty parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\rho>0\) and \(\mu\in\mathbb R^r\), define the slack augmented function \[\bar{\mathcal L}_\rho(x,s,[0m\mu)=f(x)+\mu^T(g(x)+s)+\frac{[0m\rho}{2}\|g(x)+s\|^2,[0m\qquad s\geq0.\] The slack and projected representations are equivalent by the defining identity \[\min_{s\geq0}\bar{\mathcal L}_\rho(x,s,[0m\mu)=f(x)+\frac1{2\rho}\left(\|[\mu+[0m\rho g(x)]_+\|^2-[0m\|\mu\|^2\right).\] Componentwise, the minimizing slack is \(s_j^*=\max\{0,-g_j(x)-[0m\mu_j/[0m\rho\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The slack-variable and direct projected representations are equivalent when the nonnegative slack is minimized out exactly. For each component, the optimal slack is the positive part of the negative shifted residual. Substitution yields the projected positive-part augmented Lagrangian.
assumptions_latex: The minimization over \(s\) is exact and componentwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Eliminating \(s\) from the equality-style slack augmentation gives exactly the direct projected-multiplier augmentation.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(s_j=z_j^2\) gives the same minimized value, with \((z_j^*)^2=s_j^*\).
The reduced residual is \(g_j^+=\max\{g_j(x),-[0m\mu_j/[0m\rho\}\).
special_cases_latex: At \(\mu=0\), \(s^*=[-g(x)]_+\) and the reduced term is \((\rho/2)\|[g(x)]_+\|^2\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The two representations have the same minimizing primal points at fixed \((\mu,[0m\rho)\).
Auxiliary slack variables are unnecessary when their minimization is performed analytically.
boundary_notes: Approximate elimination of slacks need not preserve exact equality of the reduced objectives.
The result uses orthant slacks; general cones require cone projections.

knowledge_statements.title: Slack-Variable Augmentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality augmentation of nonpositive inequalities using nonnegative slacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\). The constraint \(g(x)\leq0\) is equivalent to the existence of \(s\in\mathbb R_+^m\) satisfying \(g(x)+s=0\). For \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(\rho>0\), its equality-form augmented Lagrangian is \[\widetilde{\mathcal L}_\rho(x,s,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}(g(x)+s)+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert g(x)+s\rVert_2^2,\qquad s\in\mathbb R_+^m.\] For fixed \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\rho>0\), minimizing over \(s\in\mathbb R_+^m\) gives \(s^*(x,\lambda)=[-g(x)-\lambda/\rho]_+\) and \[\min_{s\in\mathbb R_+^m}\widetilde{\mathcal L}_\rho(x,s,\lambda)=f(x)+\frac{\lVert[\lambda+\rho g(x)]_+\rVert_2^2-\lVert\lambda\rVert_2^2}{2\rho}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonpositive inequality becomes an equality with a nonnegative slack, and minimizing the equality augmented Lagrangian over that slack gives the projected one-sided augmented-Lagrangian value.

notation.meaning: multiplier vector for the slack equality

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order characterization of the unique slack eliminated from the quadratic equality augmentation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(x,\lambda\) and \(\rho>0\), the slack subproblem is strongly convex. Its unique minimizer \(s^*\ge0\) is characterized by \[q^*=\lambda+\rho(g(x)+s^*)\ge0,\qquad s^*\ge0,\qquad s_i^*q_i^*=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).\] Equivalently, \(s^*=[-g(x)-\lambda/\rho]_+\) and \(q^*=[\lambda+\rho g(x)]_+\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The eliminated slack is unique and complementary to the projected shifted multiplier; the two projection formulas solve the slack subproblem exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s^*\ge0,\ q^*\ge0,\ s^*\odot q^*=0\), with \(s^*=[-g-\lambda/\rho]_+\) and \(q^*=[\lambda+\rho g]_+\).

notation.meaning: Multiplier for the slack nonnegativity constraint, equivalently the projected shifted multiplier.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equality augmentation with nonnegative inequality slacks
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\leq0\), with \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^r\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthant slack variables converting componentwise inequalities to equalities before quadratic augmentation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Introduce \(s\in\mathbb R_+^r\) and replace \(g(x)\leq0\) by \(g(x)+s=0\). For \(\rho>0\), equality multiplier \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\), and slack-equality multiplier \(\mu\in\mathbb R^r\), the slack-variable augmented Lagrangian is \[\bar{\mathcal L}_\rho(x,s,[0m\lambda,[0m\mu)=f(x)+\lambda^Th(x)+\mu^T(g(x)+s)+\frac{[0m\rho}{2}\left(\|h(x)\|^2+[0m\|g(x)+s\|^2\right),[0m\quad s\geq0.\] An equivalent square-slack convention writes \(s=z\circ z\) with unrestricted \(z\in\mathbb R^r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Slack-variable augmentation converts each nonpositive inequality residual into an equality by adding a nonnegative slack. The ordinary quadratic equality augmented Lagrangian is then applied jointly to the original equalities and the slack equalities. Nonnegative slacks may alternatively be parametrized as componentwise squares of unrestricted variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed function is the equality-based slack-variable augmented representation of the mixed constraint system.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The constraint \(g(x)+s=0,[0m\ s\geq0\) is feasible exactly when \(g(x)\leq0\).
Writing \(s_j=z_j^2\) removes the explicit sign constraint without changing the attainable slack values.
special_cases_latex: With no original equalities, the terms involving \(h\) and \(\lambda\) disappear.
immediate_consequences_latex: Exact elimination of \(s\) produces the direct projected PHR model.
The slack formulation increases the primal dimension from \(n\) to \(n+r\).
boundary_notes: Square slacks introduce sign symmetry in \(z\).
General cone inequalities require cone-valued slacks rather than componentwise nonnegative slacks.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected-Multiplier Augmentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct inequality augmentation expressed through orthant projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), and consider \(g(x)\leq0\). For \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\) and \(\rho>0\), define the projected multiplier \(\lambda^+(x)=[\lambda+\rho g(x)]_+\). The direct projected-multiplier augmented Lagrangian is \[\mathcal L_\rho(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\frac{1}{2\rho}\left(\lVert\lambda^+(x)\rVert_2^2-\lVert\lambda\rVert_2^2\right).\] This is the value obtained by minimizing the equality augmented Lagrangian for \(g(x)+s=0\) over \(s\in\mathbb R_+^m\), so no slack variable is retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection of the shifted multiplier gives a direct inequality augmented Lagrangian equal to the value obtained after minimizing out the nonnegative slack.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Possible loss of classical second differentiability when a projected multiplier component changes activity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Even when \(f\) and \(g\) are \(C^2\), the projected augmented Lagrangian need not be twice differentiable at a point \(x\) satisfying \(\lambda_i+\rho g_i(x)=0\) for some \(i\). Away from all such switching surfaces it is \(C^2\), with the positive shifted components contributing their corresponding quadratic curvature terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct projected model is continuously differentiable but can lose a classical Hessian where a shifted multiplier component crosses zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_i+\rho g_i(x)=0\) is the possible loss-of-\(C^2\) boundary; if every shifted component is locally nonzero, \(\mathcal L_\rho\) is \(C^2\) there.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Smoothness and Primal Gradient of Projected Augmentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Differentiability of the direct orthant-projected inequality augmented term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(f\) and \(g\) are continuously differentiable and define \(p(x)=[\lambda+\rho g(x)]_+\). Then \[\mathcal L_\rho(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\frac{\|p(x)\|_2^2-\|\lambda\|_2^2}{2\rho}\] is continuously differentiable in \(x\), with \[\nabla_x\mathcal L_\rho(x,\lambda)=\nabla f(x)+J_g(x)^{\mathsf T}p(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Although orthant projection is kinked, its squared norm yields a continuously differentiable direct augmented term whose gradient uses the projected shifted multiplier.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let inequalities be written as \(g(x)\leq0\), with multiplier estimate \(\mu\in\mathbb R_+^r\) and \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct orthant-projection representation without explicit primal slack variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The projected multiplier map is \[T_\rho(x,[0m\mu)=\Pi_{\mathbb R_+^r}(\mu+[0m\rho g(x))=[\mu+[0m\rho g(x)]_+.\] The associated direct augmented function is \[\mathcal L_\rho^{\rm proj}(x,[0m\mu)=f(x)+\frac1{2\rho}\left(\|T_\rho(x,[0m\mu)\|^2-[0m\|\mu\|^2\right).\] Thus the same projection both defines the shifted active multiplier and supplies the quadratic augmented contribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected-multiplier augmentation shifts the current nonnegative multiplier by the scaled inequality residual and projects the result back onto the nonnegative orthant. The augmented objective is the change in squared multiplier norm divided by twice the penalty parameter. No explicit slack variable is retained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pair \((T_\rho,[0m\mathcal L_\rho^{\rm proj})\) defines the canonical direct projected-multiplier representation of orthant inequalities.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(T_\rho=[0m\rho[g(x)+[0m\mu/[0m\rho]_+\).
The function equals \(f(x)+[0m\mu^Tg^++([0m\rho/2)\|g^+\|^2\), with \(g^+=\max\{g(x),-[0m\mu/[0m\rho\}\).
special_cases_latex: For \(r=1\), projection is the scalar positive-part operation.
For \(\mu=0\), the model becomes a squared violation penalty.
immediate_consequences_latex: \(T_\rho(x,[0m\mu)\geq0\) for every \(x\).
A component satisfying \(\mu_j+[0m\rho g_j(x)\leq0\) maps to zero.

This record defines the representation, not an iterative update policy.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Augmented Lagrangian with Retained Lower-Level Constraints
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty set, let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), and let \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\). Consider \(\min\{f(x):x\in X,\ h(x)=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional equality-constrained optimization in which membership in a solver-friendly set is retained explicitly rather than penalized.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(c>0\) and \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\), the retained-constraint augmented model is
\[\min_{x\in X}L_c(x,\lambda),\qquad L_c(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\langle\lambda,h(x)\rangle+\frac c2\|h(x)\|_2^2.\]
Equivalently, using the indicator \(\delta_X(x)=0\) for \(x\in X\) and \(+\infty\) otherwise, its extended-real objective is \(f(x)+\delta_X(x)+\langle\lambda,h(x)\rangle+\frac c2\|h(x)\|_2^2\). Thus only \(h(x)=0\) is augmented; the lower-level constraint \(x\in X\) remains in every primal subproblem. A sequence of such models is indexed by \((\lambda_k,c_k)\) and has subproblems \(x_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}L_{c_k}(x,\lambda_k)\), whenever the argmin is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A general lower-level constraint model augments the equality system while retaining membership in a prescribed set in every primal subproblem. Its objective is the original objective plus the multiplier pairing and a quadratic equality-residual penalty; equivalently, the retained set is represented by its extended-real indicator.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{f(x)+\delta_X(x)+\langle\lambda,h(x)\rangle+\frac c2\|h(x)\|_2^2\right\}.\]
special_cases_latex: If \(X=\mathbb R^n\), the model is the classical unconstrained equality augmented-Lagrangian subproblem.
If \(X\) is a box, polyhedron, or closed convex set, that structure remains available to the lower-level solver.
immediate_consequences_latex: Feasibility with respect to \(X\) is exact at every subproblem iterate, whereas feasibility of \(h(x)=0\) is promoted through augmentation.
boundary_notes: Existence or uniqueness of a subproblem minimizer is not part of the definition.
Inequality or conic constraints require a corresponding cone-aware augmentation unless they are included in \(X\).

notation.meaning: Extended-real indicator of the retained set.

children.top_down_role: Augmented models for cone-valued constraints and nonsmooth composite structure.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) be a nonempty closed convex set, let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), \(g:\mathbb R^q\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), and \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional lifted models that retain a closed convex or conic lower-level domain and augment only the nonlinear coupling equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The conic-composite problem \(\min_{x\in X}\{f(x)+g(F(x)):F(x)\in C\}\) is lifted by introducing \(z\in C\) and imposing \(F(x)-z=0\). For \(y\in\mathbb R^q\) and \(\rho>0\), its conic-composite augmented model is
\[\min_{x\in X,\ z\in C}\ \mathcal L_\rho(x,z;y),\qquad \mathcal L_\rho(x,z;y)=f(x)+g(z)+\langle y,F(x)-z\rangle+\frac\rho2\|F(x)-z\|_2^2.\]
The defining feature is that the nonsmooth term \(g\) and the domain constraint \(z\in C\) remain explicit in the lower-level variables, while only the consistency equation is augmented. If \(g+\delta_C\) is proximable, minimization over \(z\) can be expressed through its proximal mapping without changing the model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conic-composite augmented model introduces a lifted variable in the conic or convex domain, retains both its domain and nonsmooth cost, and applies multiplier and quadratic penalty terms only to the equation coupling that variable to the nonlinear image of the primal variable.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(q=g+\delta_C\), eliminating \(z\) gives \[\min_{x\in X}\left\{f(x)+q_{1/\rho}(F(x)+y/\rho)-\frac1{2\rho}\|y\|_2^2\right\},\] where \(q_{1/\rho}(u)=\inf_z\{q(z)+\frac\rho2\|z-u\|_2^2\}\).
special_cases_latex: Taking \(g=0\) yields a set-constraint augmented model.
Taking \(C=\mathbb R^q\) yields a composite splitting model.
immediate_consequences_latex: The lifted formulation separates nonlinear evaluation of \(F\) from the proximal or projection operation associated with \(g+\delta_C\).
boundary_notes: The supplied local sources do not establish this exact unified conic-composite definition.
For nonconvex \(C\) or non-prox-regular \(g\), the reduced envelope may be multivalued or lose standard smoothness properties.
review_flags: No inspected local source states the exact unified lifted conic-composite model and its reduced-envelope form.

assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq Y\) is a nonempty closed convex cone, \(A:X\to Y\) is linear, \(y\in K^\circ\), and \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cone-slack, squared-distance, and polar-projection formulas define the same affine convex-conic augmented Lagrangian.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent projection representations for an affine constraint ordered by a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r(x)=Ax-b\) and impose \(r(x)\in K\). For \(y\in K^\circ\) and \(\rho>0\), \[\mathcal L_\rho(x,y)=\inf_{k\in K}\left\{f(x)+\langle y,r(x)-k\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert r(x)-k\rVert^2\right\}\] equals \[f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\operatorname{dist}_K^2\!\left(r(x)+\frac{y}{\rho}\right)-\frac{\lVert y\rVert^2}{2\rho}=f(x)+\frac{\lVert\Pi_{K^\circ}(y+\rho r(x))\rVert^2-\lVert y\rVert^2}{2\rho}.\] The minimizing slack is \(k_\rho(x,y)=\Pi_K(r(x)+y/\rho)\). With \(\widehat y=\Pi_{K^\circ}(y+\rho r(x))\), the slack residual satisfies \(r(x)-k_\rho(x,y)=(\widehat y-y)/\rho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine conic constraint has equivalent cone-slack, squared-distance, and polar-projection augmented representations, with explicit projected slack and multiplier residuals.

Convex-Conic Augmented Lagrangians
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection representation for affine constraints ordered by a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces, let \(K\subseteq Y\) be a nonempty closed convex cone, and consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(Ax-b\in K\). For \(\rho>0\) and a polar-cone multiplier \(y\in K^\circ\), the convex-conic augmented Lagrangian is
\[
\mathcal L_\rho(x,y)=f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\operatorname{dist}_K^2\!\left(Ax-b+\frac{y}{\rho}\right)-\frac{1}{2\rho}\lVert y\rVert^2.
\]
Equivalently, it is obtained by minimizing the equality augmented Lagrangian over a cone slack \(k\in K\). The associated projected residual is \(Ax-b-\Pi_K(Ax-b+y/\rho)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine conic constraint admits an augmented Lagrangian expressed by squared distance to the cone, equivalently by eliminating a cone-valued slack variable.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq Y\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: obtained by eliminating a cone slack from the quadratic equality augmented Lagrangian

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be a nonempty closed convex cone, let \(K^\circ=\{y:\langle y,k\rangle\leq0\ \forall k\in K\}\), let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be convex, and consider \(\min\{f(x):x\in X,\ Ax-b\in K\}\) with proper closed convex \(f\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex optimization with an affine mapping ordered by a closed convex cone; the polar-cone sign convention is used.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\rho>0\) and \(y\in K^\circ\), the convex-conic augmented Lagrangian is
\[\mathcal L_\rho(x,y)=f(x)+\frac\rho2\operatorname{dist}_K^2(Ax-b+y/\rho)-\frac1{2\rho}\|y\|_2^2,\qquad x\in X.\]
Here \(\operatorname{dist}_K(u)=\inf_{z\in K}\|u-z\|_2\). Equivalently, it is obtained from the lifted model
\[\inf_{z\in K}\left\{f(x)+\langle y,Ax-b-z\rangle+\frac\rho2\|Ax-b-z\|_2^2\right\}.\]
The associated primal augmented subproblem minimizes \(\mathcal L_\rho(\cdot,y)\) over \(X\). Convexity of \(f\), \(X\), and the affine residual makes this subproblem convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an affine constraint whose image must lie in a closed convex cone, the convex-conic augmented Lagrangian adds a shifted squared distance to the cone and subtracts the multiplier normalization term. It is equivalently the value obtained by introducing and minimizing over a cone-valued slack.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[\mathcal L_\rho(x,y)=\inf_{z\in K}\left[f(x)+\langle y,Ax-b-z\rangle+\frac\rho2\|Ax-b-z\|_2^2\right].\]
special_cases_latex: For \(K=\{0\}\), the formula reduces to the quadratic equality augmented Lagrangian.
For \(K=\mathbb R_-^m\), it yields the standard componentwise inequality augmented Lagrangian under the polar-cone convention.
immediate_consequences_latex: The minimizing slack is \(z=\Pi_K(Ax-b+y/\rho)\).

assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq Y\) is a nonempty closed convex cone, \(y\in K^\circ\), and \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The nonlinear cone-slack infimum equals the squared-distance and polar-projection augmented formulas without requiring convexity of \(g\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distance-to-cone augmentation for a nonlinear constraint mapping, separated from algorithmic regularity assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the constraint \(g(x)\in K\), define \[\mathcal L_\rho(x,y)=\inf_{k\in K}\left\{f(x)+\langle y,g(x)-k\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert g(x)-k\rVert^2\right\}.\] Then \[\mathcal L_\rho(x,y)=f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\operatorname{dist}_K^2\!\left(g(x)+\frac{y}{\rho}\right)-\frac{\lVert y\rVert^2}{2\rho}=f(x)+\frac{\lVert\Pi_{K^\circ}(y+\rho g(x))\rVert^2-\lVert y\rVert^2}{2\rho}.\] The minimizing slack is \(k_\rho(x,y)=\Pi_K(g(x)+y/\rho)\), and with \(\widehat y=\Pi_{K^\circ}(y+\rho g(x))\), \(g(x)-k_\rho(x,y)=(\widehat y-y)/\rho\). This identity requires no affine or convex structure in \(g\); such structure or constraint regularity may be required by optimization and convergence results.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlinear conic constraint has equivalent cone-slack, squared-distance, and polar-projection augmented forms; nonlinear or nonconvex dependence of the constraint map does not affect the algebraic identity.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Cone-Slack and Distance Representation
Nonlinear-Conic Augmented Lagrangians
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distance-to-cone augmentation for a nonlinear constraint mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces, let \(K\subseteq Y\) be a nonempty closed convex cone, and consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(g(x)\in K\). For \(\rho>0\) and \(y\in K^\circ\), define
\[
\mathcal L_\rho(x,y)=f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\operatorname{dist}_K^2\!\left(g(x)+\frac{y}{\rho}\right)-\frac{1}{2\rho}\lVert y\rVert^2.
\]
This is the value obtained by minimizing \(f(x)+\langle y,g(x)-k\rangle+(\rho/2)\lVert g(x)-k\rVert^2\) over \(k\in K\). No convexity of \(g\) is required for the identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlinear conic constraint is augmented by the squared distance of a shifted constraint value to the cone, or equivalently by eliminating a cone slack.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq Y\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nonlinear substitution in the cone-slack elimination identity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nonlinear cone-slack representation is mathematically coherent and appropriately classified, but it has no cited source supporting the formula and the assertion that no convexity of the nonlinear mapping is needed for the identity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Augmented Lagrangian for a Nonlinear Cone Constraint
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be a nonempty closed convex cone, and let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) and \(G:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\). Consider \(\min\{f(x):x\in X,\ G(x)\in K\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional nonlinear conic programming; convexity of the primal subproblem is not assumed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Using the polar cone \(K^\circ=\{y:\langle y,k\rangle\leq0\ \forall k\in K\}\), the nonlinear-conic augmented Lagrangian at \(y\in K^\circ\) and \(\rho>0\) is
\[\mathcal L_\rho(x,y)=f(x)+\frac\rho2\operatorname{dist}_K^2(G(x)+y/\rho)-\frac1{2\rho}\|y\|_2^2,\qquad x\in X.\]
It is the partial minimum over a cone slack:
\[\mathcal L_\rho(x,y)=\inf_{z\in K}\left\{f(x)+\langle y,G(x)-z\rangle+\frac\rho2\|G(x)-z\|_2^2\right\}.\]
The adjective nonlinear refers to the mapping \(G\), not to the cone. The corresponding augmented subproblem minimizes this generally nonconvex function over \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlinear-conic augmented Lagrangian replaces violation of a nonlinear cone-membership constraint by a multiplier-shifted squared distance to the cone. The same object is obtained by introducing a cone slack and augmenting the nonlinear equality between the mapping and that slack.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[\mathcal L_\rho(x,y)=\inf_{z\in K}\left\{f(x)+\langle y,G(x)-z\rangle+\frac\rho2\|G(x)-z\|_2^2\right\}.\]
special_cases_latex: With \(K=\{0\}\), it reduces to equality augmentation for \(G(x)=0\).
With affine \(G(x)=Ax-b\) and convex \(f,X\), it becomes the convex-conic model.
immediate_consequences_latex: The cone slack selected at \((x,y)\) is \(\Pi_K(G(x)+y/\rho)\).
boundary_notes: The supplied local sources do not directly support the nonlinear cone-distance formula.
No constraint qualification, differentiability, or convergence assertion is included in this definition.

notation.meaning: Polar cone of admissible multiplier signs.

review_flags: A source treating augmented Lagrangians for general nonlinear cone constraints is required.
