children.title: Composite Augmented Lagrangians
children.top_down_role: Models preserving proximable or nonsmooth composite structure.

assumptions_latex: \(F:X\to Z\) is a given mapping and \(\rho>0\).

notation.meaning: split variable representing the composite argument

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Split-variable augmented representation preserving proximal access to a nonsmooth composite term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_x f(x)+h(F(x))\), introduce \(z\) and the equality \(F(x)-z=0\). The augmented Lagrangian is \[\mathcal L_\rho(x,z,y)=f(x)+h(z)+\langle y,F(x)-z\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert F(x)-z\rVert^2.\] Equivalently, its \(z\)-dependent terms are \(h(z)+(\rho/2)\lVert z-(F(x)+y/\rho)\rVert^2\) up to a constant independent of \(z\). Consequently, \[\arg\min_z\mathcal L_\rho(x,z,y)=\operatorname{prox}_{h/\rho}\!\left(F(x)+\frac{y}{\rho}\right).\] Linearity of \(F\) is not needed for this fixed-\(x\) identity, although it may be required by particular convex algorithms or convergence theorems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Splitting the composite argument yields an equality augmented Lagrangian whose auxiliary-variable minimization is the correctly scaled proximal step for the nonsmooth term.
knowledge_statements.title: Composite Splitting and Proximal Elimination
Composite Augmented Lagrangians
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variable-splitting representation that keeps the nonsmooth term proximable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the composite problem \(\min_{x\in X} f(x)+h(Fx)\), introduce \(z\in Z\) and the equality \(Fx-z=0\). For \(\rho>0\) and \(y\in Z\), define
\[
\mathcal L_\rho(x,z,y)=f(x)+h(z)+\langle y,Fx-z\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert Fx-z\rVert^2.
\]
For fixed \(x\) and \(y\), minimizing over \(z\) gives
\[
z^+=\operatorname{prox}_{h/\rho}\!\left(Fx+\frac{y}{\rho}\right),
\]
so the augmentation couples the variables through a quadratic residual while retaining direct proximal access to \(h\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Splitting the composite argument produces an equality augmented Lagrangian whose auxiliary-variable minimization is exactly a proximal step for the nonsmooth term.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct variable splitting and completion of the quadratic square

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The splitting formulation and proximal minimization identity fit this representation leaf, but no source is cited for the composite augmented-Lagrangian correspondence.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), let \(g:\mathbb R^q\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, and let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional composite optimization preserving the nonsmooth outer function through variable splitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the composite problem \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)+g(F(x))\), introduce \(z\in\mathbb R^q\) and the equality \(F(x)-z=0\). For \(y\in\mathbb R^q\) and \(\rho>0\), the composite augmented Lagrangian is
\[\mathcal L_\rho(x,z;y)=f(x)+g(z)+\langle y,F(x)-z\rangle+\frac\rho2\|F(x)-z\|_2^2.\]
The corresponding augmented model minimizes jointly over \(x\in X\) and \(z\in\operatorname{dom}g\). Eliminating \(z\) produces
\[\widehat{\mathcal L}_\rho(x;y)=f(x)+g_{1/\rho}(F(x)+y/\rho)-\frac1{2\rho}\|y\|_2^2,\]
where \(g_{1/\rho}\) is the Moreau envelope. This representation preserves the proximal structure of \(g\) rather than differentiating or quadratically approximating it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composite augmented Lagrangian splits the argument of the nonsmooth outer function into a new variable and augments the equation linking that variable to the nonlinear inner mapping. Minimizing out the split variable yields a shifted Moreau-envelope representation.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[\inf_z\mathcal L_\rho(x,z;y)=f(x)+g_{1/\rho}(F(x)+y/\rho)-\frac1{2\rho}\|y\|_2^2.\]
special_cases_latex: If \(g=\delta_C\), the model becomes a set-constraint or conic augmented Lagrangian.
If \(F\) is linear and \(f,g\) are convex, the lifted model is jointly convex apart from the multiplier-affine term.
immediate_consequences_latex: Any minimizing split variable satisfies \(z\in\operatorname{prox}_{g/\rho}(F(x)+y/\rho)\).
boundary_notes: The supplied local sources do not contain the precise lifted composite and Moreau-envelope formulation.
Proximal uniqueness is not asserted when \(g\) is nonconvex.

notation.meaning: Moreau envelope of the outer function.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equality Penalty-Kernel Family and Induced Multiplier Model
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min\{f(x):h(x)=0\}\), where \(h=(h_1,\ldots,h_m):\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable, continuously differentiable, strictly convex equality-penalty kernels in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An equality penalty kernel is a function \(\phi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) that is continuously differentiable and strictly convex, satisfies \(\phi(0)=\phi'(0)=0\), and obeys \(\lim_{t\to-\infty}\phi'(t)=-\infty\) and \(\lim_{t\to+\infty}\phi'(t)=+\infty\). For \(c>0\), it induces the augmented Lagrangian
\[L_c^\phi(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\langle\lambda,h(x)\rangle+\frac1c\sum_{i=1}^m\phi(ch_i(x)).\]
The associated first-order multiplier architecture selects \(x_k\) by minimizing \(L_{c_k}^\phi(\cdot,\lambda_k)\) and updates each component by
\[\lambda_{k+1}^i=\lambda_k^i+\phi'(c_kh_i(x_k)),\qquad i=1,\ldots,m.\]
A penalty-kernel family is any specified collection of such kernels, possibly with distinct kernels or positive parameters for different constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A penalty-kernel family consists of differentiable strictly convex scalar kernels normalized at zero and having derivative range equal to the real line. Scaling and summing these kernels over equality residuals defines an augmented Lagrangian and a matching componentwise multiplier update.
special_cases_latex: For \(\phi(t)=t^2/2\), the classical quadratic augmented Lagrangian and update \(\lambda_{k+1}=\lambda_k+c_kh(x_k)\) are recovered.
Admissible nonquadratic examples include \(\phi(t)=|t|^p/p\) for \(p>1\) and \(\phi(t)=\cosh(t)-1\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Kernel choice determines both the residual penalty geometry and the nonlinear multiplier correction.
boundary_notes: This definition covers equality kernels; inequality kernels require multiplier-dependent two-argument functions and sign preservation.

notation.meaning: Augmented Lagrangian induced by the kernel.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convexity and Nullspace Structure of Quadratic Kernels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic residual-space geometry of a symmetric positive-semidefinite quadratic penalty kernel.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\phi_W(r)=\tfrac12 r^{\mathsf T}Wr\) with \(W=W^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\), \(\nabla\phi_W(r)=Wr\), \(\nabla^2\phi_W(r)=W\), and \(\phi_W\) is convex. Moreover, \(\phi_W(r)=0\) exactly when \(r\in\ker W\); hence it vanishes only at \(r=0\), and is strongly convex, exactly when \(W\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-semidefinite quadratic kernel is convex with constant Hessian W. A singular weight leaves its nullspace unpenalized, whereas positive definiteness gives strong convexity and exact detection of zero residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla\phi_W(r)=Wr,\ \nabla^2\phi_W(r)=W,\ \phi_W(r)=0\iff r\in\ker W\), and \(\phi_W\) is strongly convex iff \(W\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Convexity and Nullspace Structure of Quadratic Kernels
Quadratic Penalty Kernels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean and weighted quadratic kernels for equality residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r\in\mathbb R^m\) be a constraint residual. A weighted quadratic penalty kernel is
\[
\phi_W(r)=\frac12\langle r,Wr\rangle,
\]
where \(W\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) is symmetric positive semidefinite; it is positive definite when \(W\succ0\). For an equality-constrained problem with residual \(c(x)\), multiplier \(y\), and penalty scale \(\rho>0\), the corresponding augmented Lagrangian is
\[
\mathcal L_{\rho,W}(x,y)=f(x)+\langle y,c(x)\rangle+\rho\phi_W(c(x)).
\]
The Euclidean kernel is the special case \(W=I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic kernel penalizes a residual by one half of a positive-semidefinite weighted squared norm; the identity weight yields the classical Euclidean augmentation.

children.title: Nonquadratic Penalty Kernels
children.top_down_role: Multiplier methods induced by nonquadratic penalty geometries.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\phi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be an equality penalty kernel and consider \(\min\{f(x):h(x)=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable equality augmentation generated by an admissible kernel that is not the pure quadratic kernel.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A nonquadratic penalty kernel is an admissible equality kernel \(\phi\) satisfying continuous differentiability, strict convexity, \(\phi(0)=\phi'(0)=0\), and \(\phi'(t)\to\pm\infty\) as \(t\to\pm\infty\), but for which \(\phi(t)\not\equiv t^2/2\). It induces
\[L_c^\phi(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\langle\lambda,h(x)\rangle+\frac1c\sum_{i=1}^m\phi(ch_i(x))\]
and the multiplier correction
\[\lambda_{k+1}^i-\lambda_k^i=\phi'(c_kh_i(x_k)).\]
The normalization \(c^{-1}\phi(ct)\) makes the quadratic choice equal to \(ct^2/2\). Nonquadraticity may alter residual growth, smoothness, conditioning, and the scale of multiplier corrections while preserving zero value and zero derivative at a feasible residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonquadratic penalty kernel satisfies the standard convex-kernel conditions but is not identically the half-square. It generates an augmented residual term by scaling the kernel and generates multiplier corrections through the kernel derivative.
special_cases_latex: \(\phi(t)=|t|^p/p\) with \(p>1\) and \(p\neq2\) is nonquadratic.
\(\phi(t)=|t|^p/p+t^2/2\) with \(p>1\), or \(\phi(t)=\cosh(t)-1\), gives another admissible geometry.
immediate_consequences_latex: For \(1<p<2\), the power-plus-quadratic kernel is not twice differentiable at zero; for higher-order growth it may control objectives for which quadratic augmentation is unbounded below.
boundary_notes: Nonquadratic does not by itself imply nonsmoothness, exactness, or superior convergence.
Inequality-oriented exponential kernels use a different multiplier-dependent construction.

children.title: Equality-Oriented Nonquadratic Kernels
children.top_down_role: Nonquadratic kernels specialized to equality systems.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Kernel conditions needed for exact equality-feasibility detection and undistorted multipliers at feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonnegative scalar kernel \(\varphi\), \(\sum_i\varphi(c_i(x))=0\) implies \(c(x)=0\) exactly when \(\varphi^{-1}(0)=\{0\}\). Convexity and \(\varphi(0)=0\) alone do not suffice: a convex kernel with a nontrivial zero interval gives zero penalty at some infeasible residuals. If \(\varphi'(0)\ne0\), then at feasibility the effective multiplier is \(y+\rho\varphi'(0)\mathbf 1\), rather than \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A unique kernel zero is required for equality-feasibility detection, and zero derivative at the origin is required for the effective multiplier to equal the supplied multiplier at feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(\varphi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R_+\) is convex and differentiable at zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\varphi^{-1}(0)=\{0\}\) is the feasibility-detection condition, while \(\varphi'(0)=0\) is the multiplier-normalization condition.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Set and Normalization Boundaries

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Effective Multiplier Induced by an Equality Kernel
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order representation of a differentiable separable equality-kernel augmentation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\mathcal L_{\rho,\varphi}(x,y)=f(x)+\langle y,c(x)\rangle+\rho\sum_{i=1}^m\varphi(c_i(x))\), define \(\widehat y_i=y_i+\rho\varphi'(c_i(x))\). Whenever \(f\), \(c\), and \(\varphi\) are differentiable, \(\nabla_x\mathcal L_{\rho,\varphi}(x,y)=\nabla f(x)+Jc(x)^\top\widehat y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Differentiating a separable equality-kernel augmentation gives ordinary Lagrangian stationarity at a kernel-induced effective multiplier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla_x\mathcal L_{\rho,\varphi}(x,y)=\nabla_x L(x,\widehat y)\), where \(\widehat y=y+\rho\varphi'(c(x))\) componentwise.

notation.meaning: Jacobian of the equality residual map

knowledge_statements.title: Effective Multiplier Induced by an Equality Kernel

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-Order Curvature Decomposition for Equality Kernels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hessian representation of a twice-differentiable separable equality-kernel augmentation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\widehat y_i=y_i+\rho\varphi'(c_i(x))\). If \(f\), \(c\), and \(\varphi\) are twice differentiable, then
\[
\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L_{\rho,\varphi}(x,y)
=\nabla_{xx}^2L(x,\widehat y)
+\rho Jc(x)^\top\operatorname{Diag}(\varphi''(c_i(x)))Jc(x).
\]
If \(\varphi\) is convex, the added Jacobian term is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equality-kernel curvature is ordinary Lagrangian curvature at the effective multiplier plus a weighted positive-semidefinite Jacobian term when the kernel is convex.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and every component of \(c\) are twice differentiable at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Curvature Decomposition for Equality Kernels

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on the ability of a smooth equality kernel to add second-order curvature normal to the equality manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At a feasible point \(x\) with \(c(x)=0\) and a normalized twice-differentiable kernel satisfying \(\varphi'(0)=0\),
\[
\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L_{\rho,\varphi}(x,y)=\nabla_{xx}^2L(x,y)+\rho\varphi''(0)Jc(x)^{\mathsf T}Jc(x).
\]
Consequently, if \(\varphi''(0)=0\), increasing \(\rho\) adds no quadratic normal curvature at feasibility. Strict convexity alone does not prevent this degeneracy; \(\varphi(t)=t^4\) is strictly convex and satisfies \(\varphi''(0)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth strictly convex equality kernel need not add quadratic normal curvature when its second derivative vanishes at zero.
assumptions_latex: \(f\), \(c\), and \(\varphi\) are twice differentiable at the relevant arguments.

notation.meaning: Jacobian of the equality residual map

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Curvature Degeneracy at Feasibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Foundational definition of the equality-oriented nonquadratic kernel family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(c(x)=0\), let \(\varphi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R_+\) be differentiable and nonquadratic, with \(\varphi^{-1}(0)=\{0\}\) and \(\varphi'(0)=0\). The normalized separable equality-kernel augmented Lagrangian is
\[
\mathcal L_{\rho,\varphi}(x,y)=f(x)+\langle y,c(x)\rangle+\rho\sum_{i=1}^m\varphi(c_i(x)),\qquad \rho>0.
\]
Its penalty term vanishes exactly when \(c(x)=0\), and its residual derivative at feasibility equals the supplied multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized equality kernel applies a differentiable nonquadratic scalar penalty with a unique zero and zero derivative at the origin while retaining the ordinary multiplier term.
assumptions_latex: \(\varphi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R_+\) is differentiable and nonquadratic.
knowledge_statements.title: Normalized Separable Equality-Kernel Augmentation
Equality-Oriented Nonquadratic Kernels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable smooth convex kernels applied to equality residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(c:X\to\mathbb R^m\) define the equality system \(c(x)=0\). An equality-oriented nonquadratic kernel is generated by a differentiable, strictly convex function \(\varphi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R_+\) satisfying \(\varphi(0)=\varphi'(0)=0\), with \(\varphi\) not quadratic. Its separable augmented Lagrangian is
\[
\mathcal L_{\rho,\varphi}(x,y)=f(x)+\langle y,c(x)\rangle+\rho\sum_{i=1}^m\varphi(c_i(x)),\qquad \rho>0.
\]
Strict convexity and normalization imply that the penalty term is nonnegative and vanishes exactly when every equality residual is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonquadratic equality kernel adds a normalized strictly convex separable penalty that vanishes exactly at zero residual while retaining the ordinary multiplier term.
assumptions_latex: \(\varphi\) is differentiable, strictly convex, nonquadratic, and finite on \(\mathbb R\).

children.title: Inequality-Oriented Nonquadratic Kernels
children.top_down_role: Nonquadratic kernels specialized to one-sided feasibility.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Differentiability and curvature regimes at activation of a shifted positive-part power kernel.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\psi_q(t)=[t]_+^q/q\) with \(q>1\). Then \(\psi_q\in C^1(\mathbb R)\) and \(\psi_q'(t)=[t]_+^{q-1}\). At \(t=0\), if \(1<q<2\), the positive-side curvature \((q-1)t^{q-2}\) is unbounded; if \(q=2\), the one-sided second derivatives disagree; and if \(q>2\), \(\psi_q\in C^2(\mathbb R)\) with \(\psi_q''(0)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive-part powers are continuously differentiable for every exponent above one, but their curvature is singular below two, discontinuous at two, and continuous only above two.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\psi_q\in C^1(\mathbb R)\) for \(q>1\), while \(\psi_q\in C^2(\mathbb R)\) exactly for \(q>2\).
knowledge_statements.title: Power-Kernel Smoothness Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact condition under which the shifted positive-part power kernel assigns zero induced multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[
\widehat y_i=\rho^{2-q}[y_i+\rho g_i(x)]_+^{q-1},
\qquad q>1,
\]
one has
\[
\widehat y_i=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad y_i+\rho g_i(x)\le0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad g_i(x)\le-\frac{y_i}{\rho}.
\]
Hence sufficiently strict satisfaction suppresses the constraint's first-order contribution exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-sided power kernel assigns zero induced multiplier exactly when the shifted residual is nonpositive.
knowledge_statements.title: Inactive-Constraint Suppression Test

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic Endpoint Recovers the Projected PHR Term
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact quadratic specialization at the boundary of the shifted positive-part power family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Extending the shifted positive-part power expression to \(q=2\) gives
\[
\frac{[y_i+\rho g_i(x)]_+^2-y_i^2}{2\rho},
\qquad
\widehat y_i=[y_i+\rho g_i(x)]_+.
\]
These are the projected Powell–Hestenes–Rockafellar one-sided quadratic term and multiplier update. Thus \(q=2\) is the quadratic boundary of the power family rather than a nonquadratic member.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At exponent two, the one-sided power expression becomes the standard projected quadratic augmented-Lagrangian term and update.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Endpoint Recovers the Projected PHR Term

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Foundational one-sided nonquadratic power-kernel family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(g_i(x)\le0\), \(y_i\ge0\), \(\rho>0\), and \(q>1\), \(q\ne2\), define
\[
\mathcal L_{\rho,q}(x,y)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\frac{[y_i+\rho g_i(x)]_+^q-y_i^q}{q\rho^{q-1}}.
\]
Its residual derivative is the nonnegative effective multiplier
\[
\widehat y_i=\rho^{2-q}[y_i+\rho g_i(x)]_+^{q-1}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A shifted positive-part power gives a one-sided nonquadratic augmentation whose residual derivative is a nonnegative effective multiplier.
knowledge_statements.title: Shifted Positive-Part Power Augmentation
Inequality-Oriented Nonquadratic Kernels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Power-kernel extension of one-sided shifted-residual augmentation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For inequalities \(g_i(x)\le0\), multipliers \(y_i\ge0\), a scale \(\rho>0\), and an exponent \(q>1\) with \(q\ne2\), define the one-sided nonquadratic augmentation
\[
\mathcal L_{\rho,q}(x,y)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\frac{[y_i+\rho g_i(x)]_+^q-y_i^q}{q\rho^{q-1}}.
\]
Its derivative with respect to the residual \(g_i(x)\) is
\[
\widehat y_i=[y_i+\rho g_i(x)]_+^{q-1}/\rho^{q-2}\ge0,
\]
which supplies a nonnegative updated multiplier and suppresses sufficiently inactive constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A shifted positive-part power produces a nonquadratic one-sided penalty whose residual derivative is a nonnegative multiplier estimate and vanishes for sufficiently inactive constraints.

notation.meaning: Multiplier estimate induced by residual differentiation.

children.title: Exponential Multiplier Kernels
children.top_down_role: Exponentially generated multiplier models used in separable programming.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the exponential multiplicative update when initialized on the boundary of the nonnegative multiplier cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(y_i^+=y_i\exp(\rho g_i(x))\), strict positivity is invariant when \(y_i>0\). If \(y_i=0\), then \(y_i^+=0\) for every finite \(g_i(x)\) and every \(\rho>0\). Thus an initially zero component cannot become positive even when its constraint is violated or has a positive KKT multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strictly positive initialization is essential because zero is an absorbing state of the multiplicative exponential multiplier update.
knowledge_statements.title: Absorbing Zero-Multiplier Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Log-Space Additive Form of the Exponential Update
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent additive representation of the positive multiplicative multiplier update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(y_i>0\) and \(y_i^+=y_i\exp(\rho g_i(x))\), define \(s_i=\log y_i\). Then
\[
s_i^+=s_i+\rho g_i(x),
\qquad
\log\frac{y_i^+}{y_i}=\rho g_i(x).
\]
Thus the exponential multiplier update is an additive residual step in logarithmic multiplier coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The multiplicative exponential update becomes an additive residual update after taking logarithms of the positive multipliers.
knowledge_statements.title: Log-Space Additive Form of the Exponential Update

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-point limitation of multiplicative exponential updates for inactive inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(y_i>0\) and \(y_i^+=y_i\exp(\rho g_i(x))\),
\[
y_i^+=y_i\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad g_i(x)=0.
\]
Therefore a fixed point in the strictly positive multiplier orthant forces every modeled inequality to be active. An inactive KKT component with \(g_i(x)<0\) and zero multiplier can occur only on the boundary \(y_i=0\), or as a limit with \(y_i\downarrow0\); it is not a strictly positive fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strictly positive exponential multiplier is fixed only at zero constraint residual, so inactive KKT components occur only on or toward the multiplier-cone boundary.
knowledge_statements.title: Strictly Positive Fixed-Point Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Foundational exponential kernel and its induced positive multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For inequalities \(g_i(x)\le0\), \(y_i>0\), and \(\rho>0\), define
\[
\mathcal L^{\exp}_\rho(x,y)=f(x)+\frac1\rho\sum_{i=1}^m y_i\bigl(e^{\rho g_i(x)}-1\bigr).
\]
Its residual derivative and induced multiplier update are
\[
\widehat y_i=\frac{\partial\mathcal L^{\exp}_\rho}{\partial g_i}=y_i e^{\rho g_i(x)},
\qquad y_i^+=\widehat y_i>0.
\]
Violation increases the component, strict satisfaction decreases it, and a zero residual leaves it unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exponential kernel produces a positive multiplicative multiplier update whose change is determined by the inequality residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Exponential Augmented-Multiplier Kernel
Exponential Multiplier Kernels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable exponential kernel for one-sided constraints and positive multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For inequalities \(g_i(x)\le0\), positive multipliers \(y_i>0\), and \(\rho>0\), the separable exponential augmented Lagrangian is
\[
\mathcal L_\rho^{\exp}(x,y)=f(x)+\frac1\rho\sum_{i=1}^m y_i\bigl(\exp(\rho g_i(x))-1\bigr).
\]
Differentiation with respect to \(g_i(x)\) gives the induced multiplier
\[
y_i^+=y_i\exp(\rho g_i(x))>0.
\]
Thus the update preserves positivity, increases a multiplier when its constraint is violated, and decreases it when the corresponding inequality is strictly satisfied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exponential kernel yields a multiplicative multiplier update that preserves positivity and raises or lowers each multiplier according to the sign of its constraint residual.

knowledge_statements.title: Representation Transformations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Slack introduction and elimination connecting inequality and equality augmentations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Represent the scalar inequality \(g(x)\le0\) as the equality \(g(x)+s=0\) with \(s\ge0\). For multiplier \(y\ge0\) and \(\rho>0\), eliminating the slack from the quadratic equality augmentation gives
\[
\inf_{s\ge0}\left\{y(g(x)+s)+\frac{\rho}{2}(g(x)+s)^2\right\}
=\frac{[y+\rho g(x)]_+^2-y^2}{2\rho}.
\]
The minimizing slack is \(s^*=[-g(x)-y/\rho]_+\). Componentwise application yields the standard shifted positive-part representation for a vector inequality system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Introducing a nonnegative slack converts an inequality to an equality; minimizing the equality augmentation over that slack yields the shifted positive-part augmented term.

notation.meaning: Slack minimizing the augmented equality expression.

children.title: Model–Representation Correspondences
children.top_down_role: Correspondences between augmented model choices, constraint encodings, and penalty geometries.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polar-Projection Form of the Cone-Distance Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent polar-cone representation of the distance term arising after cone-slack elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every nonempty closed convex cone \(K\subseteq Y\) and \(z\in Y\), Moreau decomposition gives
\[
z=\Pi_Kz+\Pi_{K^\circ}z,\qquad \langle\Pi_Kz,\Pi_{K^\circ}z\rangle=0,
\]
and consequently
\[
\operatorname{dist}_K^2(z)=\|z-\Pi_Kz\|^2=\|\Pi_{K^\circ}z\|^2.
\]
Hence a shifted distance-to-cone augmented term can equivalently be evaluated through projection onto the polar cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The squared distance to a closed convex cone equals the squared norm of the polar-cone projection, giving an equivalent projection representation of cone augmentation.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq Y\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.

notation.meaning: Euclidean projections onto the cone and its polar

knowledge_statements.title: Polar-Projection Form of the Cone-Distance Model

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact elimination of a cone-valued slack for an arbitrary multiplier vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq Y\) be a nonempty closed convex cone. For every \(z,y\in Y\) and \(\rho>0\),
\[
\inf_{k\in K}\left\{\langle y,z-k\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\|z-k\|^2\right\}
=\frac{\rho}{2}\operatorname{dist}_K^2\!\left(z+\frac y\rho\right)-\frac{\|y\|^2}{2\rho},
\]
and the unique minimizer is
\[
k^*=\Pi_K\!\left(z+\frac y\rho\right).
\]
No polar- or dual-cone membership assumption on \(y\) is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating a closed-convex-cone slack gives a shifted distance-to-cone term and projection minimizer for every multiplier vector.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq Y\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.title: General Cone-Slack Elimination Identity
Model–Representation Correspondences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correspondence between cone-slack and distance-to-cone augmented models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq Y\) be a nonempty closed convex cone and write the conic constraint \(g(x)\in K\) as \(g(x)-k=0\) with \(k\in K\). For \(y\in K^\circ\) and \(\rho>0\),
\[
\inf_{k\in K}\left\{f(x)+\langle y,g(x)-k\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert g(x)-k\rVert^2\right\}
=f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\operatorname{dist}_K^2\!\left(g(x)+\frac y\rho\right)-\frac{\lVert y\rVert^2}{2\rho}.
\]
The minimizing slack is \(k^*=\Pi_K(g(x)+y/\rho)\), establishing an exact correspondence between the two representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating a cone-valued slack from an equality augmented Lagrangian gives exactly the shifted squared-distance-to-cone representation.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq Y\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(k^*=\Pi_K(g(x)+y/\rho)\), and slack elimination equals the displayed distance-to-cone augmentation.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: completion of the square followed by metric projection onto the cone

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cone-slack and distance-to-cone correspondence is mathematically coherent and correctly classified as a representation, but no inspectable source is supplied for the projection identity.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), and \(L_c(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\langle\lambda,h(x)\rangle+\frac c2\|h(x)\|_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-dimensional equality method of multipliers with a positive, possibly variable penalty sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A method-of-multipliers architecture consists of an initial multiplier \(\lambda_0\in\mathbb R^m\), positive penalties \(c_k>0\), and coupled sequences \((x_k,\lambda_k)\) satisfying, for every \(k\geq0\),
\[x_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}L_{c_k}(x,\lambda_k),\qquad \lambda_{k+1}=\lambda_k+c_kh(x_k).\]
The penalty sequence may be fixed, preselected, or generated during computation. More generally, a retained set \(X\) may replace \(\mathbb R^n\), and approximate minimization may replace the argmin condition when an explicit accuracy rule is supplied. The architecture is distinguished from a pure penalty method by the persistent and updated multiplier state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A method-of-multipliers architecture alternates minimization of the current augmented Lagrangian with a residual-scaled update of the multiplier estimate. Its state comprises the primal point, multiplier, and positive penalty parameter, and the penalty policy may be fixed or variable.
equivalent_formulations_latex:
Since \(
abla_xL_{c_k}(x,\lambda_k)=
abla f(x)+
abla h(x)(\lambda_k+c_kh(x))\), the updated multiplier appears in the first-order stationarity equation at an exact differentiable subproblem solution.
special_cases_latex: Constant \(c_k\equiv c\) gives a fixed-penalty architecture.
Setting all multipliers to zero and increasing \(c_k\) instead gives a quadratic penalty method, not the method of multipliers.
immediate_consequences_latex: The primal residual simultaneously measures equality infeasibility and determines the multiplier displacement.
boundary_notes: The definition alone asserts neither existence of global minimizers nor convergence.
Inequality and conic architectures require sign-preserving or projected multiplier updates.

children.title: Classical Equality Method of Multipliers
children.top_down_role: The foundational multiplier architecture for smooth equality systems.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Classical Quadratic Equality Method of Multipliers
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\), with \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical exact Hestenes-Powell equality method using the Euclidean quadratic penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(c>0\), define
\[L_c(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}h(x)+\frac c2\|h(x)\|_2^2.\]
Given \(\lambda_0\in\mathbb R^m\) and positive \(c_k\), the classical equality method of multipliers generates
\[x_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}L_{c_k}(x,\lambda_k),\qquad \lambda_{k+1}=\lambda_k+c_kh(x_k),\qquad k=0,1,\ldots.\]
Thus the same penalty coefficient weights the squared residual in the primal subproblem and scales the residual in the dual update. The method differs from quadratic penalty minimization because \(\lambda_k\) is updated rather than held at zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The classical equality method of multipliers minimizes a quadratic augmented Lagrangian and then adds the penalty-scaled equality residual to the multiplier. The multiplier persists between outer iterations and distinguishes the method from a pure quadratic penalty scheme.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Completing the square gives \[L_c(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\frac c2\|h(x)+\lambda/c\|_2^2-\frac1{2c}\|\lambda\|_2^2.\]
special_cases_latex: For one equality, \(\lambda_{k+1}=\lambda_k+c_kh(x_k)\) is a scalar update.
A retained set \(X\) changes the primal minimization domain but not the equality update.
immediate_consequences_latex: At any feasible primal point, the multiplier update leaves \(\lambda_k\) unchanged.
boundary_notes: Exact global minimization is part of this canonical definition; practical inexact variants require a separate stopping condition.
No inequality multiplier projection is present.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer method-of-multipliers framework with inexact primal solves, nondecreasing penalties, multiplier updates, warm starts, and adjustable inner tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose \(\mu_0>0\), \(\tau_0>0\), a primal starting point \(x_0^s\), and \(\lambda^0\). For \(k=0,1,2,\ldots\): approximately minimize \(\mathcal L_A(\cdot,\lambda^k;\mu_k)\), starting from \(x_k^s\), until
\[
\|\nabla_x\mathcal L_A(x_k,\lambda^k;\mu_k)\|\le\tau_k.
\]
If the convergence test for the equality-constrained problem holds, return \(x_k\). Otherwise set
\[
\lambda_i^{k+1}=\lambda_i^k-\mu_kc_i(x_k)\quad(i\in\mathcal E),
\]
choose \(\mu_{k+1}\ge\mu_k\), set \(x_{k+1}^s=x_k\), choose \(\tau_{k+1}\), and continue.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize a positive penalty, a positive inner tolerance, a primal starting point, and multiplier estimates. At each outer iteration, approximately minimize the augmented Lagrangian until its primal gradient meets the current tolerance. Stop if the original equality-constrained problem passes its convergence test; otherwise update the multipliers from the constraint residuals, choose a nondecreasing penalty, warm-start from the current primal point, and select the next inner tolerance.

children.title: Primal-Multiplier Iteration Coupling
children.top_down_role: The coupled primal-subproblem and multiplier-side organization of the method.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(L_c(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\langle\lambda,h(x)\rangle+\frac c2\|h(x)\|_2^2\), and let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the primal subproblem domain.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact equality method-of-multipliers coupling, viewed as a state transition rather than as two independent sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(c>0\), define the primal solution correspondence
\[P_c(\lambda)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}L_c(x,\lambda)\]
and, for every \(x\in X\), the multiplier transition
\[U_c(\lambda,x)=\lambda+ch(x).\]
The primal-multiplier iteration coupling is the set-valued transition
\[T_c(\lambda)=\{(x,U_c(\lambda,x)):x\in P_c(\lambda)\}.\]
An outer sequence is coupled when, for every \(k\), \((x_k,\lambda_{k+1})\in T_{c_k}(\lambda_k)\). Consequently, the multiplier used to form the current primal objective is \(\lambda_k\), while the same primal point \(x_k\) supplies the residual that defines \(\lambda_{k+1}\). Neither sequence is specified independently of the other.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal-multiplier coupling is the state transition that first selects a minimizer of the augmented Lagrangian formed with the current multiplier and then uses that same primal point's residual to produce the next multiplier.
equivalent_formulations_latex: When the primal minimizer is unique, \(P_c\) is single-valued and the multiplier-only transition is \(\lambda_{k+1}=\lambda_k+ch(P_c(\lambda_k))\).
special_cases_latex: If \(h(x_k)=0\), the transition has \(\lambda_{k+1}=\lambda_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Nonuniqueness of the primal subproblem makes the coupled transition set-valued even though the multiplier formula is single-valued for a selected \(x_k\).
boundary_notes: The definition does not prescribe how a minimizer is selected from a non-singleton correspondence.
Inexact primal solves replace \(P_c\) by an accuracy-dependent correspondence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal phase of the equality method of multipliers with explicitly separated solve conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), form \(L_{\rho_k}(x,y^k)=f(x)+\langle y^k,c(x)\rangle+(\rho_k/2)\lVert c(x)\rVert^2\) and compute \(x^{k+1}\in X\) under one declared convention: exact global minimization, an objective-gap condition \(L_{\rho_k}(x^{k+1},y^k)\le\inf_{x\in X}L_{\rho_k}(x,y^k)+\varepsilon_k\), or the first-order stationarity condition stated separately below. The multiplier phase follows unless the prescribed stopping tests hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Form the current augmented objective and solve it using one explicitly selected exact, value-inexact, or stationarity-inexact convention.
assumptions_latex: The selected solve convention is stated and well-defined.
For the objective-gap convention, the subproblem infimum is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^{k+1}\text{ satisfies the declared primal-subproblem acceptance criterion}.

notation.meaning: objective-gap tolerance when that convention is used

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Augmented-Subproblem Sequence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity-based acceptance criterion distinct from global objective accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex and \(L_{\rho_k}(\cdot,y^k)\) is differentiable, a first-order inexact solve satisfies \[\operatorname{dist}\left(0,\nabla_xL_{\rho_k}(x^{k+1},y^k)+N_X(x^{k+1})\right)\le\varepsilon_k.\] For \(X=\mathbb R^n\), this becomes \(\lVert\nabla_xL_{\rho_k}(x^{k+1},y^k)\rVert\le\varepsilon_k\). Without convexity of the augmented objective, it does not imply a global objective-gap bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normal-cone residual provides a stationary-solve certificate but is not a global-minimization certificate in nonconvex problems.

notation.meaning: normal cone to the retained convex set

Primal Subproblem Sequence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal phase of the classical equality method of multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x^0\in X\), \(y^0\in\mathbb R^m\), positive penalties \(\{\rho_k\}\), and tolerances \(\{\varepsilon_k\}\), the primal phase for minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\) computes, for \(k=0,1,\ldots\), a point \(x^{k+1}\) satisfying
\[
\mathcal L_{\rho_k}(x^{k+1},y^k)\le \inf_{x\in X}\mathcal L_{\rho_k}(x,y^k)+\varepsilon_k,
\]
where \(\mathcal L_\rho(x,y)=f(x)+\langle y,c(x)\rangle+(\rho/2)\lVert c(x)\rVert^2\). It stops when prescribed feasibility and inner-solve criteria hold; otherwise the multiplier phase follows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each outer iteration, approximately minimize the current equality augmented Lagrangian in the primal variable before updating the multiplier.
assumptions_latex: Each augmented subproblem has a finite infimum or an accepted stationary-point convention is specified.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), and let \((\lambda_k,c_k)\in\mathbb R^m\times(0,\infty)\) be outer parameters.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact lower-level problems generated by a quadratic equality augmented-Lagrangian outer iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The primal subproblem sequence is the ordered family
\[\mathcal P_k:\quad \min_{x\in X}\ L_{c_k}(x,\lambda_k)=f(x)+\langle\lambda_k,h(x)\rangle+\frac{c_k}{2}\|h(x)\|_2^2,\qquad k=0,1,\ldots.\]
An exact primal sequence is any selection \(x_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}L_{c_k}(x,\lambda_k)\). The parameters \((\lambda_k,c_k)\) are frozen within \(\mathcal P_k\); only the primal variable is optimized. When \(X=\mathbb R^n\), each member is unconstrained. When \(X\) is retained, every member has the same explicit lower-level feasible set but a changing augmented objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal subproblem sequence is the family of optimization problems obtained by freezing the current multiplier and positive penalty parameter and minimizing the resulting augmented Lagrangian over the retained primal domain.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[x_k\in\arg\min_{x\in X}\left\{f(x)+\frac{c_k}{2}\|h(x)+\lambda_k/c_k\|_2^2\right\},\] since the omitted term \(-\|\lambda_k\|_2^2/(2c_k)\) is constant in \(x\).
special_cases_latex: For fixed \(c_k\equiv c\), only the multiplier-dependent linear term and shift vary across subproblems.
For \(X=\mathbb R^n\), the sequence consists of unconstrained minimizations.
immediate_consequences_latex: The feasibility residual is penalized inside every primal objective without imposing \(h(x)=0\) as a hard lower-level constraint.
boundary_notes: Argmin nonemptiness and uniqueness are not automatic.
An inexact sequence must state a residual, objective-gap, or distance accuracy criterion.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After the primal phase produces \(x^{k+1}\), update \[y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho_kc(x^{k+1}),\qquad \rho_k>0.\] If the prescribed feasibility and stationarity tests fail, use \(y^{k+1}\) in the next primal subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add the penalty-scaled equality residual to the multiplier and pass the result to the next primal phase.

knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity-Transfer Identity
Multiplier Update Sequence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual phase coupled to equality residuals in the method of multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
After obtaining \(x^{k+1}\) from the augmented primal subproblem for \(c(x)=0\), update the equality multiplier by
\[
y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho_k c(x^{k+1}),\qquad k=0,1,\ldots.
\]
The increment is the penalty-scaled primal residual. Equivalently,
\[
y^{k+1}=\nabla_c\!\left(\langle y^k,c\rangle+\frac{\rho_k}{2}\lVert c\rVert^2\right)\bigg|_{c=c(x^{k+1})}.
\]
The sequence stops together with the primal phase when the selected feasibility and stationarity tests are satisfied; otherwise the next primal subproblem uses \(y^{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Update the equality multiplier by adding the current constraint residual scaled by the penalty, then use the result in the next primal subproblem.
assumptions_latex: \(x^{k+1}\) has been produced by the current primal subproblem.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), let \(x_k\) be the kth augmented-subproblem solution, let \(c_k>0\), and choose \(\lambda_0\in\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unprojected equality-multiplier updates for the classical quadratic method of multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The multiplier update sequence is recursively defined by
\[\lambda_{k+1}=\lambda_k+c_kh(x_k),\qquad k=0,1,\ldots.\]
Equivalently, for every \(k\geq1\),
\[\lambda_k=\lambda_0+\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}c_jh(x_j).\]
Each increment \(\lambda_{k+1}-\lambda_k\) is the current equality residual scaled by the same positive coefficient used in the quadratic augmentation of the kth primal subproblem. The update is componentwise \(\lambda_{k+1}^i=\lambda_k^i+c_kh_i(x_k)\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The multiplier sequence starts from a chosen vector and cumulatively adds penalty-scaled equality residuals. The coefficient in each increment is the same coefficient that weights the corresponding primal quadratic penalty.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If the kth primal point is differentiable and stationary, then \(\nabla f(x_k)+\nabla h(x_k)\lambda_{k+1}=0\), because \(\lambda_{k+1}=\lambda_k+c_kh(x_k)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(h(x_k)=0\), then \(\lambda_{k+1}=\lambda_k\).
For constant \(c_k=c\), \(\lambda_k=\lambda_0+c\sum_{j<k}h(x_j)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The sequence records the accumulated signed feasibility error rather than merely its norm.
boundary_notes: This unprojected formula is for equality multipliers; inequality multipliers normally require nonnegativity-preserving updates.
Boundedness or convergence of \((\lambda_k)\) is not included in the definition.

children.top_down_role: Fixed, adaptive, and safeguarded augmentation policies.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Penalty-Management Policy for an Outer Multiplier Iteration
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(c_k>0\) be the augmentation coefficient used in the kth primal subproblem and multiplier update, and let \(s_k\) denote the observable outer state, including residual and stationarity measures.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic penalty control for finite-dimensional augmented-Lagrangian outer iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A penalty-management regime is a rule \(\mathcal C_k\) generating
\[c_{k+1}=\mathcal C_k(c_0,\ldots,c_k;s_0,\ldots,s_k)\in(0,\infty).\]
It is fixed when \(c_k\equiv\bar c\); preselected when the entire positive sequence is specified independently of the observed states; adaptive when \(c_{k+1}\) depends nontrivially on measured progress; and safeguarded when the generated value is modified to satisfy prescribed bounds, such as
\[c_{k+1}\in[c_{\min},c_{\max}],\qquad c_{k+1}/c_k\in[\gamma_{\min},\gamma_{\max}],\]
for positive constants with \(c_{\min}\leq c_{\max}\) and \(0<\gamma_{\min}\leq\gamma_{\max}\). The regime is part of the outer architecture and does not alter the definition of the augmented Lagrangian at a fixed \(c_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A penalty-management regime is the rule that produces the positive augmentation sequence from past parameters and, when adaptive, observed progress. Fixed, preselected, adaptive, and safeguarded regimes differ by whether and how the rule uses state information and protective bounds.
special_cases_latex: \(\mathcal C_k\equiv\bar c\) defines a fixed regime.
\(c_{k+1}=\beta c_k\) for a prescribed \(\beta>1\) defines a geometric preselected regime.
immediate_consequences_latex: Penalty management controls the tradeoff between constraint enforcement and conditioning of the primal subproblems.
boundary_notes: The inspected source explicitly permits preselected or computation-generated penalties but does not formalize every safeguard displayed here.
A penalty policy is not a primal stopping rule or multiplier safeguard.

children.title: Fixed-Penalty Regime
children.top_down_role: Multiplier iterations operating with constant augmentation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constant positive augmentation throughout an equality method-of-multipliers sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A method-of-multipliers sequence is in the fixed-penalty regime if some \(\bar\rho>0\) satisfies \(\rho_k=\bar\rho\) for all \(k\). Its exact form is \[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}L_{\bar\rho}(x,y^k),\qquad y^{k+1}=y^k+\bar\rho c(x^{k+1}).\] An inexact fixed-penalty variant replaces the argmin condition by one explicitly declared value-gap or stationarity tolerance while leaving \(\bar\rho\) unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The augmentation remains one positive constant; exact and inexact variants differ only in the declared primal-solve criterion.
assumptions_latex: Exact iterations require a selected minimizer; inexact iterations require a stated acceptance criterion.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Penalty Method-of-Multipliers Regime
Fixed-Penalty Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constant-augmentation specialization of the equality method of multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A method-of-multipliers sequence is in the fixed-penalty regime when there exists a constant \(\bar\rho>0\) such that \(\rho_k=\bar\rho\) for every outer iteration. The coupled iteration is therefore
\[
x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\left\{f(x)+\langle y^k,c(x)\rangle+\frac{\bar\rho}{2}\lVert c(x)\rVert^2\right\},
\qquad
y^{k+1}=y^k+\bar\rho c(x^{k+1}).
\]
Thus feasibility is pursued through the evolving multiplier while the quadratic augmentation scale remains unchanged; no divergence of the penalty parameter is part of this regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The penalty stays at one positive constant throughout all outer iterations, while primal minimization and residual-based multiplier updates continue.
assumptions_latex: Each displayed primal subproblem admits a selected minimizer.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(L_c(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\langle\lambda,h(x)\rangle+\frac c2\|h(x)\|_2^2\) and choose a constant \(\bar c>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact classical equality method of multipliers with one constant positive augmentation coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A fixed-penalty regime is a method-of-multipliers iteration for which
\[c_k=\bar c\quad\text{for every }k\geq0\]
for one prescribed \(\bar c>0\). Consequently,
\[x_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\left\{f(x)+\langle\lambda_k,h(x)\rangle+\frac{\bar c}{2}\|h(x)\|_2^2\right\},\qquad \lambda_{k+1}=\lambda_k+\bar c\,h(x_k).\]
The term fixed refers only to the augmentation coefficient: the multiplier, primal minimizer, and residual generally vary. Unlike a pure penalty method, the fixed regime can continue to modify constraint enforcement through the changing linear multiplier term even though the quadratic coefficient is constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-penalty regime uses the same positive augmentation coefficient in every primal subproblem and every multiplier correction. Only the coefficient is fixed; the primal and multiplier sequences continue to evolve.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The multiplier sequence satisfies \(\lambda_k=\lambda_0+\bar c\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}h(x_j)\).
special_cases_latex: If an iterate is feasible, the multiplier is unchanged at that step even though \(\bar c\) remains positive.
immediate_consequences_latex: No penalty escalation is triggered by poor feasibility progress.
boundary_notes: Fixed penalty does not mean fixed multiplier.
Whether a particular \(\bar c\) ensures convergence depends on problem and regularity assumptions not included here.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality method of multipliers with an initialized feasibility-progress test and adaptive penalty increases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(x^0\), \(y^0\), \(\rho_0>0\), \(\tau>1\), and \(\eta\in(0,1)\), and set \(r_0=\lVert c(x^0)\rVert\). After approximately solving \(\min_x L_{\rho_k}(x,y^k)\), set \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho_kc(x^{k+1})\), \(r_{k+1}=\lVert c(x^{k+1})\rVert\), and \[\rho_{k+1}=\begin{cases}\rho_k,&r_{k+1}\le\eta r_k,\\ \tau\rho_k,&r_{k+1}>\eta r_k.\end{cases}\] Inner stationarity and outer feasibility are tested separately at their prescribed tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retain the penalty after sufficient feasibility reduction and increase it otherwise, with the initial residual explicitly defined.
assumptions_latex: Each primal subproblem is solved to its stated inner criterion.

Adaptive-Penalty Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained method of multipliers with residual-driven penalty increases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the problem \(\min_{x\in X} f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), choose \(\rho_0>0\), \(\lambda^0\), \(\tau>1\), and \(\eta\in(0,1)\). At iteration \(k\), compute an approximate minimizer \(x^{k+1}\) of \(L_{\rho_k}(x,\lambda^k)=f(x)+(\lambda^k)^\top c(x)+(\rho_k/2)\lVert c(x)\rVert^2\), set \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\rho_k c(x^{k+1})\), and update \[\rho_{k+1}=\begin{cases}\rho_k,&\lVert c(x^{k+1})\rVert\leq\eta\lVert c(x^k)\rVert,\\ \tau\rho_k,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\] Stop when feasibility and a chosen stationarity residual are below their tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize the current augmented Lagrangian, update the multiplier, and increase the penalty only when constraint violation fails to contract sufficiently.
assumptions_latex: \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:X\to\mathbb R^m\) permit the stated subproblem solves.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_k\) is retained after adequate feasibility progress and increased otherwise.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(v_k\geq0\) measure feasibility, let \(r_k\geq0\) measure primal stationarity or subproblem accuracy, and let \(c_k>0\) be the current augmentation coefficient.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic adaptive penalty management driven by computed progress indicators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An adaptive-penalty regime is a positive update rule
\[c_{k+1}=\mathcal C(c_k,v_k,v_{k-1},r_k,r_{k-1})>0\]
that depends nontrivially on observed progress. A canonical feasibility-progress instance fixes \(\tau\in(0,1)\) and \(\gamma>1\) and sets
\[c_{k+1}=\begin{cases}c_k,&v_k\leq\tau v_{k-1},\\ \gamma c_k,&v_k>\tau v_{k-1},\end{cases}\qquad k\geq1,\]
where, for equality constraints, one may take \(v_k=\|h(x_k)\|_2\). A feasibility-and-stationarity variant permits \(c_k\) to remain unchanged only when specified tests involving both \(v_k\) and \(r_k\) pass. Adaptivity means the penalty sequence cannot be determined before the progress data are observed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An adaptive-penalty regime computes the next positive coefficient from current and past feasibility or stationarity indicators. A standard pattern keeps the coefficient when feasibility contracts sufficiently and multiplies it by a factor greater than one otherwise.
special_cases_latex: With \(v_k=\|h(x_k)\|_2\), the rule reacts directly to equality infeasibility.
If every progress test succeeds, the realized regime is fixed after initialization.
immediate_consequences_latex: The generated sequence is positive and nondecreasing for the displayed rule.
Penalty increases occur only on iterations classified as having insufficient feasibility progress.
boundary_notes: The displayed threshold rule is a canonical formalization but is not supported exactly by the inspected local source.
Allowing penalty decreases, noisy tests, or stochastic progress indicators requires a different policy definition.

notation.meaning: Progress threshold and penalty growth factor.

children.title: Safeguarded Penalty Regime
children.top_down_role: Penalty control incorporating bounded changes and protective thresholds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive penalty control with explicit retain and capped-increase branches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(0<\rho_{\min}\le\rho_0\le\rho_{\max}<\infty\), \(\eta\in(0,1)\), \(\delta\ge0\), and \(1<\tau_k\le\tau_{\max}\). With \(r_k=\lVert c(x^k)\rVert\), set \[\rho_{k+1}=\begin{cases}\rho_k,&r_{k+1}\le\eta r_k\ \text{or}\ r_{k+1}\le\delta,\\ \min\{\rho_{\max},\tau_k\rho_k\},&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\] Then \(\rho_k\in[\rho_{\min},\rho_{\max}]\) for all \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retain the penalty after adequate or threshold-level feasibility progress; otherwise increase it by a bounded factor without exceeding the cap.
knowledge_statements.title: Safeguarded Residual-Progress Policy

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure when an upper safeguard prevents reaching the local augmentation threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_x-(a/2)x^2\) subject to \(x=0\), with \(a>0\), the KKT pair is \((0,0)\) and \(L_\rho(x,0)=((\rho-a)/2)x^2\). If \(0<\rho_k\le\rho_{\max}\le a\), then \(x=0\) is never a strict local minimizer of \(L_{\rho_k}(\cdot,0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cap at or below the required curvature threshold can prevent strict augmented minimization permanently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x=0\text{ is not a strict local minimizer of }L_{\rho_k}(\cdot,0)\text{ for any }k.
knowledge_statements.title: Penalty-Cap Curvature Obstruction
Safeguarded Penalty Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive penalty control with bounded growth and protective thresholds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an equality augmented-Lagrangian iteration, fix \(0<\rho_{\min}\leq\rho_{max}<\infty\), \(1<\tau_{max}<\infty\), \(\eta\in(0,1)\), and a feasibility threshold \(\delta>0\). After computing \(x^{k+1}\), define \(r_{k+1}=\lVert c(x^{k+1})\rVert\). If \(r_{k+1}\leq\eta r_k\) or \(r_{k+1}\leq\delta\), retain the penalty; otherwise request an increase. Implement the request by \[\rho_{k+1}=\min\{\rho_{max},\max\{\rho_{min},\tau_k\rho_k\}\},\qquad 1\leq\tau_k\leq\tau_{max}.\] Thus neither a single update nor the full sequence violates the prescribed penalty safeguards.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increase the penalty after inadequate feasibility progress, but cap each increase and keep the parameter within prescribed protective bounds.

children.title: General-Constraint Multiplier Methods
children.top_down_role: Multiplier architectures for inequality and combined constraint systems.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), \(h:X\to\mathbb R^m\), and \(g:X\to\mathbb R^r\). Consider \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\leq0\), with equality multipliers \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\), inequality multipliers \(\mu\in\mathbb R_+^r\), and penalty parameter \(c>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional formulation using the quadratic Powell–Hestenes–Rockafellar one-sided augmentation; the retained set \(X\) is handled explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(g_j^+(x,\mu_j,c):=\max\{g_j(x),-\mu_j/c\}\), define
\[L_c(x,\lambda,\mu)=f(x)+\lambda^\top h(x)+\frac c2\|h(x)\|^2+\sum_{j=1}^r\left(\mu_jg_j^+(x,\mu_j,c)+\frac c2[g_j^+(x,\mu_j,c)]^2\right).\]
Equivalently,
\[L_c=f+\lambda^\top h+\frac c2\|h\|^2+\frac1{2c}\sum_{j=1}^r\left([\max\{0,\mu_j+cg_j(x)\}]^2-\mu_j^2\right).\]
A general-constraint multiplier iteration chooses \(c_k>0\), computes
\[x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}L_{c_k}(x,\lambda_k,\mu_k),\]
and updates
\[\lambda_{k+1}=\lambda_k+c_kh(x_{k+1}),\qquad \mu_{k+1}=[\mu_k+c_kg(x_{k+1})]_+,\]
where projection \([\cdot]_+\) is componentwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A general-constraint multiplier method assigns unrestricted multipliers to equalities and nonnegative multipliers to inequalities, minimizes a one-sided augmented Lagrangian over the explicitly retained set \(X\), and then updates the equality multipliers by the residual \(h(x_{k+1})\) and the inequality multipliers by the projected residual step \([\mu_k+c_kg(x_{k+1})]_+\). The one-sided term penalizes an inequality only according to the shifted positive part \(\max\{0,\mu_j+cg_j(x)\}\).
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty and every displayed subproblem is interpreted only when its minimum is attained.
The sign convention is \(g(x)\leq0\); reversing it requires reversing the multiplier convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1},\mu_{k+1})\) is one step of the general-constraint quadratic augmented-Lagrangian multiplier architecture defined above.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The inequality update is equivalently \(\mu_{k+1,j}=\mu_{k,j}+c_kg_j^+(x_{k+1},\mu_{k,j},c_k)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(r=0\), this is the classical equality method of multipliers.
If \(m=0\), it is a direct one-sided inequality multiplier method.
If \(X=\mathbb R^n\), the primal subproblem is unconstrained.
immediate_consequences_latex: \(\mu_{k+1}\geq0\) whenever \(\mu_k\geq0\).
For an inactive inequality satisfying \(\mu_j+cg_j(x)\leq0\), its one-sided contribution equals \(-\mu_j^2/(2c)\), independent of \(x\) locally while the inequality remains inactive.
boundary_notes: This definition does not assert convergence, global solvability of the subproblems, or a penalty-update rule.
Cone constraints and nonquadratic augmentations require corresponding projections or kernel functions and are outside this slot.

notation.meaning: Componentwise projection of a vector onto the nonnegative orthant.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Powell–Hestenes–Rockafellar treatment of inequalities without slack variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)\) subject to \(g_i(x)\leq0\), initialize \(\lambda^0\in\mathbb R_+^m\) and \(\rho_k>0\). Define \[L_{\rho_k}(x,\lambda^k)=f(x)+\frac{1}{2\rho_k}\sum_{i=1}^m\left(\max\{0,\lambda_i^k+\rho_k g_i(x)\}^2-(\lambda_i^k)^2\right).\] Compute an approximate minimizer \(x^{k+1}\in X\), then set \(\lambda_i^{k+1}=\max\{0,\lambda_i^k+\rho_k g_i(x^{k+1})\}\). Stop when primal feasibility, complementarity, and stationarity residuals meet their tolerances; otherwise retain or adapt \(\rho_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply a one-sided quadratic augmented Lagrangian directly to each inequality and project every multiplier update onto the nonnegative orthant.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_i:X\to\mathbb R\) are defined on the retained set \(X\).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), and \(g=(g_1,\ldots,g_r):X\to\mathbb R^r\). The problem is \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)\) subject to \(g(x)\leq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct finite-dimensional inequality treatment after algebraic elimination of slack variables; no slack variable is retained in the implemented subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(c>0\) and \(\mu\in\mathbb R_+^r\), define
\[L_c^{\mathrm{dir}}(x,\mu):=f(x)+\frac1{2c}\sum_{j=1}^r\left([\max\{0,\mu_j+cg_j(x)\}]^2-\mu_j^2\right).\]
A direct inequality multiplier step is
\[x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}L_{c_k}^{\mathrm{dir}}(x,\mu_k),\qquad
\mu_{k+1,j}=\max\{0,\mu_{k,j}+c_kg_j(x_{k+1})\},\quad j=1,\ldots,r.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A direct inequality multiplier method works only with the original variable \(x\). It minimizes the one-sided augmented model whose \(j\)-th term is the squared positive part of \(\mu_j+cg_j(x)\), normalized by \(2c\), and then projects each multiplier update onto \(\mathbb R_+\). Thus feasible, sufficiently inactive constraints can drop out of the local \(x\)-dependence without introducing explicit slacks.
assumptions_latex: The subproblem minimum over \(X\) exists whenever the step is invoked.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x_{k+1},\mu_{k+1})\) is the direct one-sided multiplier step generated by \(L_{c_k}^{\mathrm{dir}}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(g_j^+=\max\{g_j(x),-\mu_j/c\}\), the \(j\)-th augmented term is \(\mu_jg_j^++\frac c2(g_j^+)^2\).
The update equals \(\mu_{k+1,j}=\mu_{k,j}+c_kg_j^+(x_{k+1},\mu_{k,j},c_k)\).
special_cases_latex: For one constraint, \(r=1\), the construction is the scalar one-sided quadratic augmentation.
immediate_consequences_latex: All multiplier iterates remain nonnegative.

If \(f\) and every \(g_j\) are continuously differentiable, then \(L_c^{\mathrm{dir}}(\cdot,\mu)\) is continuously differentiable, although its Hessian may be discontinuous across \(g_j(x)=-\mu_j/c\).
boundary_notes: The definition is not an interior-point or barrier method.
It does not prescribe exact versus inexact minimization or claim convergence for nonconvex data.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Slack-Based Equality Reformulation and Multiplier Method
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), \(h:X\to\mathbb R^m\), and \(g:X\to\mathbb R^r\). Introduce \(z\in\mathbb R^r\) for the inequalities \(g(x)\leq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth squared-slack reformulation in finite dimensions, followed by the equality-constrained quadratic method of multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The slack equality reformulation is
\[\min_{x\in X,\ z\in\mathbb R^r}f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad h(x)=0,\qquad g_j(x)+z_j^2=0\ (j=1,\ldots,r).\]
For \(c>0\), define
\[\bar L_c(x,z,\lambda,\mu)=f(x)+\lambda^\top h(x)+\frac c2\|h(x)\|^2+
\sum_{j=1}^r\left(\mu_j(g_j(x)+z_j^2)+\frac c2(g_j(x)+z_j^2)^2\right).\]
A slack-based multiplier step minimizes \(\bar L_{c_k}(\cdot,\cdot,\lambda_k,\mu_k)\) over \(X\times\mathbb R^r\), obtaining \((x_{k+1},z_{k+1})\), and sets
\[\lambda_{k+1}=\lambda_k+c_kh(x_{k+1}),\qquad
\mu_{k+1,j}=\mu_{k,j}+c_k(g_j(x_{k+1})+z_{k+1,j}^2).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A slack-based multiplier method replaces every inequality \(g_j(x)\leq0\) by the equality \(g_j(x)+z_j^2=0\). It applies the equality method of multipliers in the expanded variable \((x,z)\), with a multiplier and quadratic penalty for each new equality. Feasibility of the squared-slack equality is equivalent to the original inequality because \(z_j^2\geq0\).
assumptions_latex: The augmented subproblem has a minimizer whenever the step is invoked.
The squared-slack convention is used; an alternative nonnegative slack convention would impose \(s\geq0\) explicitly.
\(c_k>0\), while \(\lambda_k\) and \(\mu_k\) are equality multipliers in the reformulated problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed minimization and residual updates define one slack-based multiplier iteration for the original mixed constraint system.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For fixed \(x\), minimizing over \(z_j\) is equivalent to minimizing over \(u_j=z_j^2\geq0\).
The minimizing squared slack satisfies \(z_j^2=\max\{0,-(\mu_j/c+g_j(x))\}\), yielding the direct one-sided augmented Lagrangian after elimination.
special_cases_latex: With \(h\) absent, only inequality slacks and their multipliers remain.
At a feasible point, an active inequality has \(z_j=0\), whereas an inactive inequality has \(z_j^2=-g_j(x)>0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Eliminating \(z\) from each augmented subproblem produces the direct one-sided formulation.
The expanded equality system represents exactly the feasible \(x\)-set of the original inequalities.
boundary_notes: Squared slacks can create degeneracy at \(z_j=0\); the definition alone does not impose a constraint qualification.
The slack multipliers are unrestricted as equality multipliers during the formal reformulation, although eliminated updates become nonnegative.

notation.meaning: Free squared-slack variable satisfying \(z_j^2=-g_j(x)\) at feasibility.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in X\), \(h(x)=0\), and \(g(x)\le0\), define \[\Phi_{\rho_k}(x;\mu^k,\lambda^k)=f(x)+(\mu^k)^{\mathsf T}h(x)+\frac{\rho_k}{2}\lVert h(x)\rVert^2+\frac{\lVert[\lambda^k+\rho_kg(x)]_+\rVert^2-\lVert\lambda^k\rVert^2}{2\rho_k}.\] Approximately minimize \(\Phi_{\rho_k}\) over \(X\), then set \[\mu^{k+1}=\mu^k+\rho_kh(x^{k+1}),\qquad \lambda^{k+1}=[\lambda^k+\rho_kg(x^{k+1})]_+.\] Apply the declared penalty policy and stop when retained-set feasibility, equality feasibility, inequality feasibility, complementarity, and stationarity tests meet tolerance.

Mixed-Constraint Multiplier Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unified augmented-Lagrangian iteration for equalities, inequalities, and a retained simple set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\leq0\), where projection or constrained minimization over \(X\) is tractable. With \(\mu^k\in\mathbb R^p\), \(\lambda^k\in\mathbb R_+^m\), and \(\rho_k>0\), approximately minimize over \(X\) the sum of \(f(x)+(\mu^k)^\top h(x)+(\rho_k/2)\lVert h(x)\rVert^2\) and \((2\rho_k)^{-1}\sum_i(\max\{0,\lambda_i^k+\rho_k g_i(x)\}^2-(\lambda_i^k)^2)\). Update \(\mu^{k+1}=\mu^k+\rho_k h(x^{k+1})\) and \(\lambda^{k+1}=\max\{0,\lambda^k+\rho_k g(x^{k+1})\}\) componentwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Augment equalities quadratically, treat inequalities one-sidedly, retain simple-set constraints explicitly, and update the two multiplier blocks according to their signs.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is closed and supports the required constrained subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mu^{k+1}\in\mathbb R^p\), \(\lambda^{k+1}\in\mathbb R_+^m\), and every primal iterate remains in \(X\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record correctly targets a mixed equality, inequality, and retained-set architecture, and algorithm is the right content kind. The precise combined augmented model and multiplier updates nevertheless have no cited authoritative locator.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\leq0\), where \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a retained simple set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Architecture coordinating exact treatment of \(X\), quadratic equality augmentation, and direct one-sided inequality augmentation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(c>0\), \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\mu\in\mathbb R_+^r\), define
\[L_c^{\mathrm{mix}}(x,\lambda,\mu)=f(x)+\lambda^\top h(x)+\frac c2\|h(x)\|^2+rac1{2c}\sum_{j=1}^r\left([\max\{0,\mu_j+cg_j(x)\}]^2-\mu_j^2\right).\]
A mixed-constraint multiplier method generates
\[x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}L_{c_k}^{\mathrm{mix}}(x,\lambda_k,\mu_k),\]
\[\lambda_{k+1}=\lambda_k+c_kh(x_{k+1}),\qquad
\mu_{k+1}=[\mu_k+c_kg(x_{k+1})]_+.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The mixed architecture partitions constraints by type. Membership in \(X\) remains an explicit restriction on every primal subproblem; equality residuals enter linearly and quadratically with unrestricted multipliers; inequality residuals enter through shifted positive parts and have projected nonnegative multiplier updates. The three treatments coexist in one subproblem and one coordinated multiplier state.
assumptions_latex: Every displayed primal subproblem is interpreted only when its minimum is attained.
The same penalty parameter is shown for both constraint blocks; block-specific positive penalties are a nearby variant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed subproblem and two block updates define the mixed equality–inequality multiplier architecture with retained set \(X\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The inequality block may be obtained by introducing squared slacks and eliminating them analytically.
The explicit set can be encoded by the indicator \(\delta_X(x)\), replacing \(f\) by \(f+\delta_X\) and minimizing over \(\mathbb R^n\).
special_cases_latex: If \(X=\mathbb R^n\), no simple constraint is retained.
If \(g\) is absent, the equality method of multipliers is recovered.
If \(h\) is absent, the direct inequality method is recovered.
immediate_consequences_latex: Equality and inequality multiplier dimensions remain \(m\) and \(r\), respectively.
The update preserves \(\mu_k\in\mathbb R_+^r\) while imposing no sign restriction on \(\lambda_k\).
boundary_notes: This definition does not cover complementarity constraints, which are not ordinary inequalities.
A convergence statement requires regularity, subproblem-accuracy, and penalty-control hypotheses not included here.

notation.meaning: Extended-real indicator, equal to zero on \(X\) and \(+\infty\) outside it.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(h_1:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_1}\), and \(h_2:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_2}\). Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(h_1(x)=0\) and \(h_2(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained finite-dimensional architecture in which one block is augmented and the other remains explicit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(c>0\) and \(\lambda_1\in\mathbb R^{m_1}\), the partial augmented Lagrangian is
\[L_{1,c}(x,\lambda_1):=f(x)+\lambda_1^\top h_1(x)+\frac c2\|h_1(x)\|^2.\]
A partial-augmentation multiplier step computes
\[x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{h_2(x)=0}L_{1,c_k}(x,\lambda_{1,k})\]
and updates only the augmented block,
\[\lambda_{1,k+1}=\lambda_{1,k}+c_kh_1(x_{k+1}).\]
The block \(h_2(x)=0\) is enforced exactly in every primal subproblem and receives no augmented term or outer multiplier update in this architecture.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partial-augmentation architecture partitions the constraint system into an augmented block \(h_1\) and a retained block \(h_2\). Only \(h_1\) appears in the quadratic augmented Lagrangian and only its multiplier is updated. The retained block remains a hard constraint in each primal minimization.
assumptions_latex: The constrained subproblem over \(\{x:h_2(x)=0\}\) has an accepted local or global solution, according to the chosen regime.
The partition \((h_1,h_2)\) is fixed for the displayed architecture.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pair consisting of the constrained minimization and the update of \(\lambda_1\) defines the partial-augmentation multiplier step.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The retained block may be represented by the indicator \(\delta_{\{h_2=0\}}(x)\) inside the objective.
When \(h_2\) can be locally solved as \(x_2=\phi(x_1)\), the step is the ordinary multiplier method applied to the reduced constraint \(h_1(x_1,\phi(x_1))=0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(m_2=0\), full equality augmentation is recovered.
If \(h_2(x)\) represents simple bounds or another tractable set, the subproblem is a simply constrained augmented-Lagrangian minimization.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every computed primal point satisfies \(h_2(x_{k+1})=0\) exactly under exact subproblem solution.
The outer multiplier state has dimension \(m_1\), not \(m_1+m_2\).
boundary_notes: The definition does not say which partition is computationally preferable.
Approximate enforcement of \(h_2\) would define a different architecture unless its error rule is specified.

notation.meaning: Augmented Lagrangian for the selected block \(h_1\) only.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial Constraint Elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local reduced augmented Lagrangian after eliminating a solvable constraint block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^r\to\mathbb R\), \(h:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^r\to\mathbb R^r\), and \(c:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^r\to\mathbb R^m\). Consider \(\min_{x,y} f(x,y)\) subject to \(h(x,y)=0\) and \(c(x,y)=0\). Suppose there are neighborhoods \(U_x\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(U_y\subseteq\mathbb R^r\) and a single-valued map \(Y:U_x\to U_y\) such that, for every \((x,y)\in U_x\times U_y\), \(h(x,y)=0\) if and only if \(y=Y(x)\). Define \(\bar f(x)=f(x,Y(x))\) and \(\bar c(x)=c(x,Y(x))\). The locally equivalent reduced problem is \(\min_{x\in U_x}\bar f(x)\) subject to \(\bar c(x)=0\), and its augmented Lagrangian is \[\bar L_\rho(x,\lambda)=\bar f(x)+\lambda^\top\bar c(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert\bar c(x)\rVert^2,\qquad \lambda\in\mathbb R^m,\ \rho>0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When one constraint block locally determines the eliminated variables uniquely, substitute that local solution into the objective and remaining constraints, then augment the resulting reduced equality system.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^r\to\mathbb R\), \(h:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^r\to\mathbb R^r\), and \(c:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^r\to\mathbb R^m\) are defined on the stated neighborhoods.
The local solutions of \(h(x,y)=0\) in \(U_x\times U_y\) are exactly the graph \(y=Y(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\mapsto(x,Y(x))\) gives a one-to-one correspondence between the local feasible points of the reduced and original formulations, with \(\bar f(x)=f(x,Y(x))\).

notation.meaning: local neighborhoods for retained and eliminated variables
