knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Partition \(x=(x_1,x_2)\in\mathbb R^{n-m_2}\times\mathbb R^{m_2}\) and consider \(\min f(x_1,x_2)\) subject to \(h_1(x_1,x_2)=0\) and \(h_2(x_1,x_2)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local smooth elimination near a reference feasible point; it is not a global parameterization claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x^*=(x_1^*,x_2^*)\) satisfy \(h_2(x^*)=0\), assume \(h_2\) is continuously differentiable near \(x^*\), and assume \(D_{x_2}h_2(x^*)\) is nonsingular. Partial constraint elimination is the local substitution
\[x_2=\phi(x_1),\qquad h_2(x_1,\phi(x_1))=0,\qquad \phi(x_1^*)=x_2^*,\]
for the locally defined implicit map \(\phi\). The reduced problem is
\[\min_{x_1}\ \tilde f(x_1):=f(x_1,\phi(x_1))
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
\tilde h_1(x_1):=h_1(x_1,\phi(x_1))=0.\]
Its augmented Lagrangian is
\[\tilde L_c(x_1,\lambda_1)=\tilde f(x_1)+\lambda_1^\top\tilde h_1(x_1)+\frac c2\|\tilde h_1(x_1)\|^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial constraint elimination removes the selected block \(h_2=0\) from the explicit optimization model by locally solving it for variables \(x_2\) as a function \(\phi(x_1)\). The objective and remaining constraint block are composed with that parameterization, and augmentation is applied only to the resulting reduced constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(h_2\) is continuously differentiable on a neighborhood where the implicit map is defined.
The reduced formulation is restricted to the corresponding local neighborhoods of \(x_1^*\) and \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The locally feasible manifold \(h_2(x)=0\) is represented by \(x=(x_1,\phi(x_1))\), yielding the reduced augmented model \(\tilde L_c\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Locally, minimizing \(L_{1,c}(x,\lambda_1)\) subject to \(h_2(x)=0\) is equivalent to minimizing \(\tilde L_c(x_1,\lambda_1)\) over the reduced coordinates.
The eliminated multiplier for \(h_2\) need not be part of the outer state because feasibility with respect to \(h_2\) is built into the parameterization.
special_cases_latex: If \(h_2(x_1,x_2)=x_2-\psi(x_1)\), then \(\phi=\psi\) globally wherever the equation is defined.
Linear full-row-rank eliminations reduce to ordinary null-space or substitution methods.
immediate_consequences_latex: The reduced variable dimension is \(n-m_2\).
Every point represented by \((x_1,\phi(x_1))\) satisfies the eliminated constraint exactly.
boundary_notes: Nonsingularity is essential for this coordinate form; rank-deficient constraints require another parameterization.
A local implicit map need not extend globally or cover disconnected feasible components.

notation.meaning: Local implicit solution map for the eliminated variables.
Objective and retained constraints after substitution.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularity and conditioning boundary for partial elimination before augmentation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The implicit reduction based on \(h(x,y)=0\) requires a nonsingular block \(h_y\). If \(h_y\) is singular, a locally single-valued differentiable map \(y=Y(x)\) need not exist. If \(\sigma_{\min}(h_y)\) is small, \[\|Y'(x)\|=\|h_y^{-1}h_x\|\le \|h_y^{-1}\|\,\|h_x\|=\frac{\|h_x\|}{\sigma_{\min}(h_y)},\] so reduced derivatives can be highly sensitive even when elimination remains formally possible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial elimination can fail at a singular dependent-variable Jacobian and becomes sensitive as that block approaches singularity.
assumptions_latex: The displayed sensitivity bound uses an invertible square block \(h_y\) and the Euclidean operator norm.

notation.meaning: smallest singular value of the elimination block

knowledge_statements.title: Singular Elimination Block Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Implicit Derivatives of the Eliminated Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First- and second-order derivative representation after smooth local constraint elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(h(x,Y(x))=0\), \(h\in C^2\), and \(h_y(x,Y(x))\) is nonsingular. Then \(Y\in C^2\) locally and \[Y'(x)=-h_y(x,Y(x))^{-1}h_x(x,Y(x)).\] For any \(C^2\) scalar function \(\phi(x,y)\), its reduction \(\bar\phi(x)=\phi(x,Y(x))\) satisfies \(\nabla\bar\phi(x)=\phi_x(x,Y(x))+Y'(x)^\top\phi_y(x,Y(x))\); analogous chain-rule differentiation gives its reduced Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular dependent-variable Jacobian gives an implicit elimination map whose derivatives generate the reduced objective and constraint derivatives.

notation.meaning: Jacobian with respect to eliminated variables

knowledge_statements.title: Selective Constraint Augmentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Only selected coupling equalities are augmented; tractable local constraints remain explicit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty set whose constraints are enforced directly, let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), and let \(c:X\to\mathbb R^m\) be a selected coupling-constraint map. For \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(\rho>0\), selective augmentation forms \[L_\rho^{\mathrm{sel}}(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^\top c(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert c(x)\rVert^2,\qquad x\in X.\] Thus the constraints defining \(X\) remain explicit in the primal subproblem, whereas the selected equalities \(c(x)=0\) enter through multiplier and quadratic terms. A corresponding multiplier step may choose \(x^+\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}L_\rho^{\mathrm{sel}}(x,\lambda)\) and set \(\lambda^+=\lambda+\rho c(x^+)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keep tractable local constraints explicit and apply multiplier and quadratic augmentation only to the selected coupling equalities.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty and its constraints can be enforced in the primal subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every selected primal point satisfies \(x^+\in X\), while violation of \(c(x^+)=0\) is represented in \(L_\rho^{\mathrm{sel}}\) and the update \(\lambda^+=\lambda+\rho c(x^+)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Selective Augmentation with Retained Local Constraints
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) encode tractable local constraints, and let \(a:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p\) encode coupling constraints. Consider \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)\) subject to \(a(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Only the coupling block is dualized and augmented; the tractable set remains explicit in every primal subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(c>0\) and \(y\in\mathbb R^p\), define the selectively augmented function
\[\mathcal L_c^{\mathrm{sel}}(x,y):=f(x)+y^\top a(x)+\frac c2\|a(x)\|^2,\qquad x\in X.\]
A selective-augmentation multiplier step is
\[x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\mathcal L_{c_k}^{\mathrm{sel}}(x,y_k),
\qquad y_{k+1}=y_k+c_ka(x_{k+1}).\]
Equivalently, for several selected blocks \(a_i(x)=0\) with positive weights \(c_i\), replace the last two terms by \(\sum_i(y_i^\top a_i(x)+\frac{c_i}{2}\|a_i(x)\|^2)\), while all unselected constraints remain in \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selective constraint augmentation designates coupling constraints for multiplier and penalty treatment while preserving easily handled local constraints as the explicit domain \(X\). Selection therefore determines both the augmented terms and the outer multiplier state; unselected constraints are not penalized and must be satisfied by every accepted primal point.
assumptions_latex: The selected coupling constraint uses the equality convention \(a(x)=0\).
The minimum over \(X\) exists whenever a step is declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed minimization over \(X\) and residual update of \(y\) define selective augmentation of \(a(x)=0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(f_X=f+\delta_X\), the method is the ordinary equality multiplier method for \(\min f_X(x)\) subject to \(a(x)=0\).
If the retained constraints admit a parameterization \(x=\phi(z)\), selection can be combined with elimination to augment \(a(\phi(z))=0\).
special_cases_latex: For \(X=\mathbb R^n\), all modeled constraints are augmented.
For \(X=\mathbb R_+^n\), nonnegativity remains exact while the coupling equations are augmented.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every accepted primal iterate lies in \(X\).
The number of maintained multipliers equals the dimension of the selected coupling block.
boundary_notes: Selective augmentation does not imply that the augmented subproblem separates; the quadratic coupling term may destroy separability.
The definition does not select blocks adaptively or specify a convergence-valid switching rule.

children.title: Block-Structured Multiplier Methods
children.top_down_role: Joint multiplier architectures exploiting separable variables or constraint blocks.

assumptions_latex: \(x_j\in X_j\), the objective is \(\sum_{j=1}^q f_j(x_j)\), and the coupling equation is \(\sum_{j=1}^qA_jx_j=b\).
Each block subproblem is solved to its prescribed inner accuracy.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential block minimization of a jointly coupled augmented Lagrangian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\sum_{j=1}^q f_j(x_j)\) subject to \(\sum_{j=1}^qA_jx_j=b\) and \(x_j\in X_j\), define \[L_\rho(x,\lambda)=\sum_{j=1}^qf_j(x_j)+\lambda^\top\left(\sum_{j=1}^qA_jx_j-b\right)+\frac{\rho}{2}\left\|\sum_{j=1}^qA_jx_j-b\right\|^2.\] A block Gauss-Seidel multiplier sweep successively minimizes this function over \(x_j\in X_j\), using \(x_i^{k+1}\) for \(i<j\) and \(x_i^k\) for \(i>j\), and then updates \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\rho_k(\sum_jA_jx_j^{k+1}-b)\). Coupling feasibility and blockwise first-order residuals are the corresponding stopping tests. This definition alone makes no convergence claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sweep sequentially through the primal blocks of the coupled augmented Lagrangian, then update one multiplier from the complete coupling residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Block Gauss-Seidel Multiplier Sweep

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A_i^\top A_j\neq0\text{ for some }i\neq j\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\text{the quadratic augmentation generally couples blocks }i\text{ and }j.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural boundary for independent block minimization of a coupled augmented Lagrangian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(r(x)=\sum_{j=1}^qA_jx_j-b\), \[\frac{\rho}{2}\|r(x)\|^2=\frac{\rho}{2}\sum_j\|A_jx_j\|^2+\rho\sum_{i<j}x_i^\top A_i^\top A_jx_j-\rho b^\top\sum_jA_jx_j+\frac{\rho}{2}\|b\|^2.\] Thus a separable original objective does not generally make the augmented subproblem separable. Vanishing cross terms on the relevant domains is required; \(A_i^\top A_j=0\) for all \(i\neq j\) is sufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The squared joint residual normally introduces cross-block terms, so independently minimizing the blocks is not the same as jointly minimizing the augmented Lagrangian.
knowledge_statements.title: Coupling Penalty Destroys Independent Separability

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous block updates stabilized relative to the preceding joint iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(r(x)=\sum_{j=1}^qA_jx_j-b\), choose self-adjoint \(P_j\succeq0\). A proximal Jacobi sweep computes in parallel
\[
x_j^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_j\in X_j}\left\{f_j(x_j)+\langle\lambda^k,A_jx_j\rangle+\frac{\rho_k}{2}\left\|A_jx_j+\sum_{i\ne j}A_ix_i^k-b\right\|^2+\frac12\|x_j-x_j^k\|_{P_j}^2\right\},
\]
then sets \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\rho_k r(x^{k+1})\). Unlike a Gauss–Seidel sweep, every block subproblem uses only iteration-\(k\) values of the other blocks. This algorithmic definition alone makes no convergence claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Update all primal blocks simultaneously from the same old iterate, optionally using blockwise proximal stabilization, and then update the joint multiplier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_j^{k+1}\) uses \(x_i^k\) for every \(i\ne j\), followed by \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\rho_kr(x^{k+1})\).
knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Jacobi Block-Multiplier Variant

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical convex convergence regime for the exact two-block alternating augmented-Lagrangian architecture.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[
\min_{x\in X,z\in Z} f(x)+g(z)\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax+Bz=b,
\]
where \(f+\delta_X\) and \(g+\delta_Z\) are proper closed convex functions. Suppose the unaugmented Lagrangian has a saddle point and the alternating subproblems attain solutions. For fixed \(\rho>0\), minimize the augmented Lagrangian exactly first in \(x\), then in \(z\), and set \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-b)\). Then \(Ax^k+Bz^k-b\to0\), the objective values converge to the primal optimum, and \(\lambda^k\) converges to a dual solution. Convergence of the individual primal blocks requires additional conditions such as uniqueness or suitable rank and coercivity assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact two-block convex alternating multiplier iterations converge in residual, value, and dual variables when a saddle point exists and the block subproblems are attained; convergence of individual primal blocks needs additional assumptions.
assumptions_latex: \(f+\delta_X\) and \(g+\delta_Z\) are proper, closed, and convex.
The primal-dual problem has a Lagrangian saddle point.
\(\rho>0\) is fixed, both block subproblems attain solutions, and they are solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax^k+Bz^k-b\to0\), \(f(x^k)+g(z^k)\to p^*\), and \(\lambda^k\to\lambda^*\) for some dual solution \(\lambda^*\).

notation.meaning: indicator functions of the explicit block constraint sets

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Block Alternating Multiplier Convergence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual stopping certificate for a separable convex problem with one affine coupling equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F_j=f_j+\delta_{X_j}\), \(r(x)=\sum_{j=1}^qA_jx_j-b\), and
\[
\eta(x,\lambda)=\max\left\{\|r(x)\|,\ \max_j\operatorname{dist}\bigl(0,\partial F_j(x_j)+A_j^{\mathsf T}\lambda\bigr)\right\}.
\]
For proper closed convex \(F_j\), \(\eta(x,\lambda)=0\) exactly when
\[
r(x)=0,\qquad 0\in\partial F_j(x_j)+A_j^{\mathsf T}\lambda\quad(j=1,\ldots,q).
\]
Whenever a saddle point exists, these conditions certify primal and dual optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coupling feasibility together with every block's stationarity residual gives a complete KKT stopping certificate for the convex block problem.
assumptions_latex: Each \(F_j=f_j+\delta_{X_j}\) is proper, closed, and convex.
For the optimality interpretation, the Lagrangian has a saddle point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blockwise primal minimization with a joint multiplier for linear coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\sum_{j=1}^q f_j(x_j)\) subject to \(\sum_{j=1}^q A_jx_j=b\) and \(x_j\in X_j\), define \[L_\rho(x,\lambda)=\sum_{j=1}^q f_j(x_j)+\lambda^\top\left(\sum_{j=1}^qA_jx_j-b\right)+\frac{\rho}{2}\left\lVert\sum_{j=1}^qA_jx_j-b\right\rVert^2.\] Starting from \((x^0,\lambda^0)\), one block-structured method approximately minimizes \(L_{\rho_k}\) successively over each \(x_j\in X_j\), holding the other blocks at their newest available values, and then sets \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\rho_k(\sum_jA_jx_j^{k+1}-b)\). Terminate using coupling-feasibility and block-stationarity residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exploit separable variables by minimizing the augmented Lagrangian blockwise, then update one multiplier vector from the joint coupling residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal steps preserve each \(x_j^{k+1}\in X_j\), and the multiplier update uses the complete coupling residual.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x=(x^1,\ldots,x^B)\), \(x^i\in X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\), and consider \(\min\sum_{i=1}^B f_i(x^i)\) subject to \(\sum_{i=1}^B A_ix^i=b\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex or nonconvex block model at the definitional level; the exact joint augmented subproblem is distinguished from one-sweep multi-block variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(c>0\) and \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\), define
\[\mathcal L_c(x^1,\ldots,x^B,\lambda)=
\sum_{i=1}^B f_i(x^i)+\lambda^\top\left(\sum_{i=1}^B A_ix^i-b\right)
+\frac c2\left\|\sum_{i=1}^B A_ix^i-b\right\|^2.\]
A block-structured multiplier step computes a joint minimizer
\[(x_{k+1}^1,\ldots,x_{k+1}^B)\in
\operatorname*{argmin}_{x^i\in X_i}\mathcal L_{c_k}(x^1,\ldots,x^B,\lambda_k)\]
and updates
\[\lambda_{k+1}=\lambda_k+c_k\left(\sum_{i=1}^B A_ix_{k+1}^i-b\right).\]
The joint minimization may itself be performed by a converged block solver, but the multiplier update occurs only after the prescribed augmented subproblem accuracy is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block-structured multiplier method preserves the Cartesian product domain and additive objective while augmenting a shared coupling residual. The quadratic residual generally couples all blocks even when the unaugmented objective is separable. The canonical method therefore treats the block subproblem jointly, possibly through an inner block-coordinate procedure, before updating the common multiplier.
assumptions_latex: The joint augmented subproblem has an accepted solution.
A single multiplier \(\lambda\) corresponds to the common coupling equation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed joint block minimization and common residual update define the block-structured multiplier method.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Consensus constraints \(x=z^i\) give separate multipliers \(\lambda^i\) and terms \(\frac c2\|x-z^i\|^2\).
The coupling residual can be denoted \(r(x)=\sum_iA_ix^i-b\), giving \(\mathcal L_c=\sum_i f_i+\lambda^\top r+\frac c2\|r\|^2\).
special_cases_latex: For \(B=1\), this is the ordinary linearly equality-constrained augmented-Lagrangian method.
For consensus form, the product-set structure supports cyclic minimization of the inner augmented model.
immediate_consequences_latex: The dual update depends only on the aggregate residual.
Unless cross terms vanish, \(\|\sum_iA_ix^i-b\|^2\) destroys exact primal separability.
boundary_notes: One Gauss–Seidel sweep followed immediately by a multiplier update is a distinct multi-block alternating method and need not inherit the canonical method’s guarantees.
This definition does not assert parallel decomposability.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural boundary for independent block minimization of a coupled augmented Lagrangian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(r(x)=\sum_{j=1}^q A_jx_j-b\), the quadratic augmentation satisfies \[\frac{\rho}{2}\|r(x)\|^2=\frac{\rho}{2}\sum_j\|A_jx_j\|^2+\rho\sum_{i<j}x_i^\top A_i^\top A_jx_j-\rho b^\top\sum_jA_jx_j+\frac{\rho}{2}\|b\|^2.\] Hence the augmented primal objective is block separable only if all cross terms relevant to the variable domains vanish; in particular, \(A_i^\top A_j=0\) for \(i\ne j\) is sufficient. Otherwise independent parallel block minimizations do not minimize the joint augmented Lagrangian.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separable objective does not make the augmented subproblem separable: the squared coupling residual normally introduces cross-block terms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A_i^\top A_j\ne0\text{ for some }i\ne j\ \Longrightarrow\ \text{the quadratic augmentation generally couples blocks }i,j.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unified Primal, Geometric, and Dual Interpretation
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper convex, and consider \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)\) subject to \(Ax=b\). Define \(p(u)=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ Ax-b=u\}\) and \(q(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x)+\lambda^\top(Ax-b)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex linear-equality regime with a closed proper perturbation function and no duality gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(c>0\), the following objects form the augmented-Lagrangian interpretation synthesis:
\[L_c(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^\top(Ax-b)+\frac c2\|Ax-b\|^2,\]
\[\inf_{x\in X}L_c(x,\lambda)=\inf_{u\in\mathbb R^m}\left(p(u)+\lambda^\top u+\frac c2\|u\|^2\right),\]
\[q_c(\lambda)=\max_{y\in\mathbb R^m}\left(q(y)-\frac1{2c}\|y-\lambda\|^2\right).\]
If \(x^+\in\arg\min_{x\in X}L_c(x,\lambda)\), \(u^+=Ax^+-b\), and \(\lambda^+=\lambda+cu^+\), then
\[\lambda^+\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{y}\left(q(y)-\frac1{2c}\|y-\lambda\|^2\right),\qquad
u^+=\nabla q_c(\lambda)=\frac{\lambda^+-\lambda}{c}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The synthesis identifies one multiplier step simultaneously as minimization of an augmented primal objective, minimization of a quadratically tilted perturbation value function, maximization of a quadratically regularized dual function, and an exact proximal step on the concave dual objective. The common linking quantities are the constraint residual \(u^+=Ax^+-b\) and the updated multiplier \(\lambda^+=\lambda+cu^+\).
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is closed and proper and \(p(0)\) is finite.
The augmented primal minimum is attained at \(x^+\).
The convex dual pair uses the stated sign convention for \(q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal augmented minimizer, perturbation minimizer, regularized-dual maximizer, and dual proximal iterate are linked by \(u^+=Ax^+-b\) and \(\lambda^+=\lambda+cu^+\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\lambda^+=\operatorname{prox}_{c(-q)}(\lambda)\), with proximal notation applied to the convex function \(-q\).
\(q_c\) is the concave Moreau envelope of \(q\), and the multiplier step is gradient ascent \(\lambda^+=\lambda+c\nabla q_c(\lambda)\).
special_cases_latex: For \(X=\mathbb R^n\), the primal subproblem is unconstrained.
Linear inequalities can be converted to equalities with nonnegative slacks absorbed into \(X\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The maximizers of \(q_c\) coincide with those of \(q\).
The quadratic augmentation smooths the dual envelope even when \(q\) is nondifferentiable.
boundary_notes: The exact proximal identity stated here is a convex-duality statement; it is not asserted for arbitrary nonconvex programs.
If the primal augmented minimum is not attained, the residual implementation may be unavailable even though the abstract dual proximal point exists.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\), define the perturbation value function \(p(u)=\inf\{f(x):h(x)=u\}\) on its effective domain in \(\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-space interpretation; it may be local near a reference solution or global when the value function is globally defined and attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(c>0\) and \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\), define the augmented value landscape
\[\Phi_{c,\lambda}(u):=p(u)+\lambda^\top u+\frac c2\|u\|^2.\]
The primal interpretation pair is
\[p(u)=\inf_{h(x)=u}f(x),\qquad
\inf_xL_c(x,\lambda)=\inf_u\Phi_{c,\lambda}(u),\]
where \(L_c(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^\top h(x)+\frac c2\|h(x)\|^2\). If \(x_{c,\lambda}\) minimizes \(L_c(\cdot,\lambda)\), then \(u_{c,\lambda}:=h(x_{c,\lambda})\) minimizes \(\Phi_{c,\lambda}\); conversely, a minimizing level \(u_{c,\lambda}\) together with a minimizing \(x\) in the definition of \(p(u_{c,\lambda})\) gives an augmented-Lagrangian minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The pair consists of the primal perturbation function \(p\), which records the best objective value at each constraint level \(u\), and its augmented landscape \(\Phi_{c,\lambda}\), obtained by adding a linear multiplier tilt and quadratic curvature. Minimizing the augmented Lagrangian in \(x\) is the same value-level operation as minimizing this tilted landscape in \(u\), subject to attainment.
assumptions_latex: The level-set infima defining \(p\) use the same local or global interpretation throughout.
The displayed equivalence of minimizers assumes the relevant infima are attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Augmented-Lagrangian minimization projects to minimization of \(p(u)+\lambda^\top u+\frac c2\|u\|^2\) in constraint-level space.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(p\) is differentiable at the minimizing level, stationarity is \(\nabla p(u_{c,\lambda})+\lambda+cu_{c,\lambda}=0\).
The multiplier update \(\lambda^+=\lambda+cu_{c,\lambda}\) converts this condition to \(-\lambda^+=\nabla p(u_{c,\lambda})\).
special_cases_latex: At feasibility, \(u=0\) and \(p(0)\) is the constrained optimal value.
For affine \(h(x)=Ax-b\) and convex \(f\), \(p\) is a convex perturbation function under standard closedness assumptions.
immediate_consequences_latex: The penalty parameter controls curvature in constraint-level space.
The multiplier supplies a linear tilt without changing the domain of \(p\).
boundary_notes: Differentiability of \(p\) is not part of the basic definition.
Local value functions can depend on the neighborhood used and should not be confused with a global perturbation function.

notation.meaning: Quadratically augmented and linearly tilted primal value landscape.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Geometry of the Multiplier Tilt and Quadratic Augmentation
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(p:U\subseteq\mathbb R^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be a primal perturbation value function, and let \(c>0\), \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-level geometry; differentiable relations are included only when differentiability at the selected level is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The augmented landscape associated with \((\lambda,c)\) is
\[\Phi_{c,\lambda}(u):=p(u)+\lambda^\top u+\frac c2\|u\|^2.\]
Its geometric minimizing level set is
\[U_c(\lambda):=\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in U}\Phi_{c,\lambda}(u).\]
Equivalently, \(u\in U_c(\lambda)\) exactly when
\[p(u)+\frac c2\|u\|^2+\lambda^\top u
\leq p(v)+\frac c2\|v\|^2+\lambda^\top v\quad\forall v\in U.\]
If \(p\) is differentiable at \(u\in U_c(\lambda)\), then
\[\nabla p(u)+\lambda+cu=0,\qquad \lambda^+:=\lambda+cu=-\nabla p(u).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Augmented-landscape geometry is the geometry of a value function after two transformations: the multiplier adds the affine tilt \(\lambda^\top u\), and augmentation adds the isotropic quadratic curvature \(c\|u\|^2/2\). A minimizing constraint level is characterized by global comparison of the transformed landscape; when differentiable, the updated multiplier is the negative slope of the original value function at that level.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is the effective constraint-level domain and \(p\) is finite at at least one point of \(U\).
The gradient identities require differentiability of \(p\) at the selected minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The multiplier tilt and quadratic term select \(U_c(\lambda)\), and differentiable selected levels satisfy \(\lambda+cu=-\nabla p(u)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Completing the square gives \(\lambda^\top u+\frac c2\|u\|^2=\frac c2\|u+\lambda/c\|^2-\frac1{2c}\|\lambda\|^2\).
Thus \(U_c(\lambda)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in U}\{p(u)+\frac c2\|u+\lambda/c\|^2\}\).
special_cases_latex: For \(\lambda=0\), augmentation is an untilted quadratic regularization around feasibility \(u=0\).
If \(p\) is convex, the quadratic term makes \(\Phi_{c,\lambda}\) strongly convex and its minimizer is unique whenever it exists.
immediate_consequences_latex: Increasing \(c\) strengthens the preference for levels near \(-\lambda/c\).
The additive constant \(-\|\lambda\|^2/(2c)\) does not affect the minimizing level.
boundary_notes: For nonconvex \(p\), the quadratic term need not make the landscape globally convex.
A stationary point of \(\Phi_{c,\lambda}\) need not be a global minimizer without convexity.

notation.meaning: Set of minimizing constraint levels of the augmented landscape.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbation value-function representation of the minimized augmented Lagrangian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), and define the perturbation value function \(p:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\cup\{\pm\infty\}\) by \[p(u)=\inf\{f(x):x\in\mathbb R^n,\ c(x)=u\},\] using \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\). Then, for every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(\rho>0\), \[\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\left(f(x)+\lambda^\top c(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert c(x)\rVert^2\right)=\inf_{u\in\mathbb R^m}\left(p(u)+\lambda^\top u+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert u\rVert^2\right).\] Thus minimizing the augmented Lagrangian is equivalent, at the level of infimal values, to minimizing a quadratically tilted primal perturbation function over possible constraint residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The infimum of the augmented Lagrangian equals the infimum of the primal perturbation value function after adding the corresponding linear and quadratic residual terms.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal Perturbation Functional for Multiplier Methods
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\). The reference constrained problem is \(\inf\{f(x):h(x)=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-function formulation, global unless a local neighborhood is explicitly selected around a reference minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The primal functional is the extended-real function
\[p(u):=\inf\{f(x):x\in\mathbb R^n,\ h(x)=u\},\qquad u\in\mathbb R^m,\]
with \(p(u)=+\infty\) when the level set is empty. For every \(c>0\) and \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\),
\[\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\left(f(x)+\lambda^\top h(x)+\frac c2\|h(x)\|^2\right)
=\inf_{u\in\mathbb R^m}\left(p(u)+\lambda^\top u+\frac c2\|u\|^2\right).\]
The feasible value of the original problem is \(p(0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal functional assigns to each right-hand-side perturbation \(u\) the best objective value attainable at constraint level \(h(x)=u\), using \(+\infty\) for unattainable levels. It converts augmented-Lagrangian minimization from decision space into minimization of a regularized value function in residual space, and the original constrained value is its value at \(u=0\).
assumptions_latex: The infimum convention is used, so attainment is not required to define \(p\).
The displayed identity uses the same global domain for both nested infima.
For a local version, all infima are restricted to a fixed neighborhood of the reference solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The augmented-Lagrangian value equals the infimum of the tilted, quadratically regularized primal functional, and the constrained optimal value is \(p(0)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(\psi_c(u)=p(u)+\frac c2\|u\|^2\), the augmented value is \(\inf_u\{\psi_c(u)+\lambda^\top u\}\).
If a minimizer \(x_{c,\lambda}\) exists, then \(h(x_{c,\lambda})\) minimizes the residual-space problem.
special_cases_latex: For affine constraints \(h(x)=Ax-b\) and convex \(f\), \(p\) is the standard convex perturbation function under appropriate regularity.
For \(u=0\), the level problem is exactly the original equality-constrained problem.
immediate_consequences_latex: Multiplier and penalty effects can be studied entirely through the transformed function \(p(u)+\lambda^\top u+c\|u\|^2/2\).
Empty constraint levels are excluded automatically by the value \(+\infty\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(q:\mathbb R^m\to[-\infty,+\infty)\) be a proper upper-semicontinuous concave dual function and let \(c>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex-duality regime; regularization is applied to the concave dual maximization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The quadratically regularized dual envelope centered at \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\) is
\[q_c(\lambda):=\max_{y\in\mathbb R^m}\left\{q(y)-\frac1{2c}\|y-\lambda\|^2\right\}.\]
Its proximal maximizer is
\[y_c(\lambda):=\operatorname*{argmax}_{y\in\mathbb R^m}\left\{q(y)-\frac1{2c}\|y-\lambda\|^2\right\}.\]
Because the objective is strongly concave on the effective domain, \(y_c(\lambda)\) is unique whenever the maximum exists. The regularized-dual viewpoint identifies
\[\nabla q_c(\lambda)=\frac{y_c(\lambda)-\lambda}{c},\qquad
\operatorname*{argmax}q_c=\operatorname*{argmax}q.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual regularization replaces a possibly nonsmooth concave dual function \(q\) by its quadratic upper envelope \(q_c\). Evaluation at \(\lambda\) selects the unique dual point \(y_c(\lambda)\) balancing dual value against squared distance from \(\lambda\). The displacement divided by \(c\) is the gradient of the envelope, and regularization preserves the dual maximizers.
assumptions_latex: \(q\) is proper, concave, and upper semicontinuous.
For every center under consideration, the displayed maximum is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Quadratic dual regularization defines \(q_c\), its proximal maximizer \(y_c\), and the gradient relation \(\nabla q_c(\lambda)=(y_c(\lambda)-\lambda)/c\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For the convex function \(F=-q\), \(-q_c(\lambda)=\min_y\{F(y)+\frac1{2c}\|y-\lambda\|^2\}\).
Thus \(y_c(\lambda)=\operatorname{prox}_{cF}(\lambda)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(q\) is already differentiable, \(q_c\) remains a smoothed dual objective with the same maximizers.
If \(q\) is polyhedral concave, the proximal maximizer remains well defined although \(q\) itself is nonsmooth.
immediate_consequences_latex: \(q_c(\lambda)\geq q(\lambda)\) by choosing \(y=\lambda\).
A fixed point \(y_c(\lambda)=\lambda\) is a maximizer of \(q\).
boundary_notes: This regularization is not the addition of \(-\|\lambda\|^2/(2c)\) directly to \(q(\lambda)\); it is a moving-center envelope.
Existence of a maximizer must be checked when the dual effective domain is not closed.

notation.meaning: Unique proximal maximizer of the regularized dual subproblem.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the concave dual function \(d\) is twice continuously differentiable near the unique proximal maximizer \(\mu_\rho(\lambda)\), and set \(Q=-\nabla^2d(\mu_\rho(\lambda))\succeq0\). For \[d_\rho(\lambda)=\sup_\mu\left\{d(\mu)-\frac{1}{2\rho}\|\mu-\lambda\|^2\right\},\] one has \[D\mu_\rho(\lambda)=(I+\rho Q)^{-1},\qquad \nabla^2d_\rho(\lambda)=-Q(I+\rho Q)^{-1}.\] Thus an eigenvalue \(-q\) is transformed into \(-q/(1+\rho q)\), whose magnitude is at most \(1/\rho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic dual regularization damps negative curvature and bounds the envelope curvature magnitude by the reciprocal penalty.
assumptions_latex: \(d\) is concave and twice continuously differentiable near the unique proximal maximizer.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global differentiability and Lipschitz-gradient properties of quadratic concave regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d:H\to[-\infty,+\infty)\) be proper, upper semicontinuous, and concave, let \(g=-d\), and for \(\rho>0\) define \[d_\rho(\lambda)=\sup_\mu\left\{d(\mu)-\frac{1}{2\rho}\|\mu-\lambda\|^2\right\},\qquad P_\rho(\lambda)=\operatorname*{argmax}_\mu\left\{d(\mu)-\frac{1}{2\rho}\|\mu-\lambda\|^2\right\}.\] Then \(P_\rho(\lambda)\) is unique, \(d_\rho\) is concave and Fréchet differentiable, and \[\nabla d_\rho(\lambda)=\frac{P_\rho(\lambda)-\lambda}{\rho}.\] Moreover, \(\nabla d_\rho\) is \(1/\rho\)-Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic regularization makes a proper closed concave dual function differentiable, with reciprocal-penalty Lipschitz gradient given by displacement to its proximal maximizer.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d\) be proper, upper-semicontinuous, and concave, and define \[d_\rho(\lambda)=\sup_\mu\left\{d(\mu)-\frac{1}{2\rho}\|\mu-\lambda\|^2\right\},\qquad\rho>0.\] With proximal maximizer \(P_\rho(\lambda)\), \[\nabla d_\rho(\lambda)=\rho^{-1}(P_\rho(\lambda)-\lambda).\] Consequently, \[\nabla d_\rho(\lambda)=0\iff P_\rho(\lambda)=\lambda\iff0\in\partial(-d)(\lambda)\iff\lambda\in\operatorname*{argmax}d.\]

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex equality case: the augmented dual is a concave proximal regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x f(x)\) subject to \(Ax=b\), where \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex, and define \(d(\mu)=\inf_x\{f(x)+\mu^\top(Ax-b)\}\). Under strong duality for the quadratic conjugate interchange, the augmented dual satisfies \[d_\rho(\lambda):=\inf_x\left\{f(x)+\lambda^\top(Ax-b)+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert Ax-b\rVert^2\right\}=\sup_\mu\left\{d(\mu)-\frac{1}{2\rho}\lVert\mu-\lambda\rVert^2\right\}.\] If the maximizing \(\mu_\rho(\lambda)\) is unique, then \(\nabla d_\rho(\lambda)=(\mu_\rho(\lambda)-\lambda)/\rho\), so \(\lambda^+=\lambda+\rho\nabla d_\rho(\lambda)\) is stabilized dual ascent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The augmented dual is the concave proximal envelope of the ordinary dual, so multiplier updating is gradient ascent on a regularized dual objective.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex, and the constraint is \(Ax=b\).
The minimax interchange defining the envelope is valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_\rho\) is the quadratic concave proximal envelope of \(d\), and its gradient step reaches its proximal maximizer when that maximizer is unique.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Multiplier Update as Ascent on the Regularized Dual
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For the convex problem \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)\) subject to \(Ax=b\), define \(q(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x)+\lambda^\top(Ax-b)\}\) and its regularized envelope \(q_c\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact augmented-subproblem regime with linear equality constraints and convex duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[x_c(\lambda)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\left\{f(x)+\lambda^\top(Ax-b)+\frac c2\|Ax-b\|^2\right\}.\]
Define \(r_c(\lambda):=Ax_c(\lambda)-b\). The regularized dual-ascent interpretation is
\[\nabla q_c(\lambda)=r_c(\lambda),\qquad
\lambda^+=\lambda+c\nabla q_c(\lambda)=\lambda+c(Ax_c(\lambda)-b).\]
Equivalently, \(\lambda^+=y_c(\lambda)\), where
\[y_c(\lambda)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{y}\left\{q(y)-\frac1{2c}\|y-\lambda\|^2\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The regularized dual-ascent view regards the exact augmented-Lagrangian residual as the gradient of the smoothed dual envelope. The familiar multiplier update is therefore a gradient-ascent step on \(q_c\) with step length \(c\); the resulting point is simultaneously the proximal maximizer of the original, possibly nonsmooth dual function.
assumptions_latex: The perturbation function is closed and proper and strong duality holds.
The augmented primal minimum is attained at \(x_c(\lambda)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method-of-multipliers update equals both \(\lambda+c\nabla q_c(\lambda)\) and the regularized-dual maximizer \(y_c(\lambda)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \((\lambda^+-\lambda)/c=Ax_c(\lambda)-b\).
The update is a unit step in the scaled gradient \(c\nabla q_c\), not ordinary ascent on the generally nonsmooth function \(q\).
special_cases_latex: If the constraint residual is zero, then \(\lambda^+=\lambda\), a fixed point of the dual proximal map.
With a constant \(c\), the same regularized envelope is used at every iteration.
immediate_consequences_latex: The ascent direction is well defined even when \(q\) is nondifferentiable.
Newton or quasi-Newton maximization of \(q_c\) gives distinct higher-order multiplier variants.
boundary_notes: With an inexact primal solution, the residual is generally only an approximate envelope gradient.
The equality is tied to the exact quadratic regularization and stated sign convention.

children.title: Dual Proximal-Point Equivalence
children.top_down_role: The proximal interpretation of convex multiplier methods.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(q\) be the concave dual function of \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)\) subject to \(Ax=b\), and set \(F=-q\), a proper closed convex function under the stated duality assumptions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact convex method of multipliers for linear equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(c_k>0\), the proximal-point iteration for minimizing \(F=-q\) is
\[\lambda_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^m}
\left\{-q(\lambda)+\frac1{2c_k}\|\lambda-\lambda_k\|^2\right\},\]
or equivalently
\[\lambda_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^m}
\left\{q(\lambda)-\frac1{2c_k}\|\lambda-\lambda_k\|^2\right\}.\]
If
\[x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\left(f(x)+\lambda_k^\top(Ax-b)+\frac{c_k}{2}\|Ax-b\|^2\right),\]
then the exact method-of-multipliers update
\[\lambda_{k+1}=\lambda_k+c_k(Ax_{k+1}-b)\]
is precisely that proximal-point iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual proximal-point equivalence means that an exact quadratic method-of-multipliers step in primal variables produces the same multiplier as a proximal-point step applied to the convex function \(-q\), or equivalently a proximal maximization step for the concave dual function \(q\). The equivalence is equality of the generated multiplier map, not merely a similarity of convergence behavior.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper convex, \(X\) is convex, and the perturbation function is closed and proper with finite value at zero.
The augmented primal minimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exact augmented-Lagrangian multiplier update equals \(\operatorname{prox}_{c_k(-q)}(\lambda_k)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The optimality inclusion is \(0\in-\partial q(\lambda_{k+1})+(\lambda_{k+1}-\lambda_k)/c_k\).
Equivalently, \((\lambda_k-\lambda_{k+1})/c_k\in\partial(-q)(\lambda_{k+1})\).
special_cases_latex: For constant \(c_k=c\), the same resolvent map is iterated.
If \(q\) is polyhedral concave, proximal steps may reach a dual maximizer in finitely many iterations under the cited setting.
immediate_consequences_latex: The multiplier map is single-valued because the proximal objective is strongly convex.
Classical proximal-point convergence theory applies to the dual sequence under its standard hypotheses.
boundary_notes: This exact equivalence does not cover an unspecified inexact augmented subproblem.
Nonlinear nonconvex constraints generally fall outside the convex dual proximal identity stated here.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d\) be proper, upper-semicontinuous, and concave, let \(\rho>0\), and define \[\lambda^+=\operatorname*{argmax}_\mu\left\{d(\mu)-\frac{1}{2\rho}\|\mu-\lambda\|^2\right\}.\] Then \[d(\lambda^+)\ge d(\lambda)+\frac{1}{2\rho}\|\lambda^+-\lambda\|^2.\] Moreover, \[\lambda^+=\lambda\iff0\in\partial(-d)(\lambda)\iff\lambda\in\operatorname*{argmax}d.\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fejer Descent of an Exact Dual Proximal Step
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step distance decrease toward the dual solution set for the exact proximal update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d:H\to[-\infty,+\infty)\) be proper, upper semicontinuous, and concave with \(S=\operatorname*{argmax}d\ne\varnothing\). For \(\rho>0\), let \[\lambda^+=\operatorname*{argmax}_\mu\left\{d(\mu)-\frac{1}{2\rho}\|\mu-\lambda\|^2\right\}.\] Then, for every \(z\in S\), \[\|\lambda^+-z\|^2+\|\lambda^+-\lambda\|^2\le\|\lambda-z\|^2.\] Thus an exact dual proximal step is Fejer monotone with respect to the dual solution set, and its displacement is square-summable along repeated exact steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every exact dual proximal update decreases squared distance to each dual optimizer by at least the squared update displacement.
assumptions_latex: \(d\) is proper, upper semicontinuous, and concave.

Exact Dual Proximal View
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact primal subproblem solves yield exact proximal-point steps on the concave dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the convex equality assumptions defining \(d(\mu)=\inf_x\{f(x)+\mu^\top(Ax-b)\}\), let \(x^{k+1}\) exactly minimize \(f(x)+(\lambda^k)^\top(Ax-b)+(\rho_k/2)\lVert Ax-b\rVert^2\), and set \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\rho_k(Ax^{k+1}-b)\). If primal-dual interchange is valid and the required minimizers exist, then \[\lambda^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{\mu\in\mathbb R^m}\left\{d(\mu)-\frac{1}{2\rho_k}\lVert\mu-\lambda^k\rVert^2\right\}.\] Thus one exact method-of-multipliers iteration is exactly one proximal-point iteration for maximizing the concave dual function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With an exact augmented-Lagrangian subproblem solve, the new multiplier is exactly the quadratic proximal maximizer of the ordinary dual function.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex, and the equality constraint is \(Ax=b\).
The augmented primal minimum and dual proximal maximum are attained.
The conjugate minimax interchange is valid.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider the convex linearly constrained problem \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)\) subject to \(Ax=b\), with dual function \(q(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x)+\lambda^\top(Ax-b)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact primal augmented minimization; this slot isolates the exactness condition distinguishing it from inexact proximal interpretations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(\lambda_k\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(c_k>0\). An exact dual proximal multiplier step is defined by selecting
\[x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}L_{c_k}(x,\lambda_k),\qquad
L_{c_k}(x,\lambda_k)=f(x)+\lambda_k^\top(Ax-b)+\frac{c_k}{2}\|Ax-b\|^2,\]
and setting
\[u_{k+1}:=Ax_{k+1}-b,
\qquad \lambda_{k+1}:=\lambda_k+c_ku_{k+1}.\]
Exactness means that \(x_{k+1}\) attains the full augmented subproblem minimum. Under the convex-duality assumptions,
\[\lambda_{k+1}=	ext{the unique }\operatorname*{argmax}_{\lambda}
\left\{q(\lambda)-\frac1{2c_k}\|\lambda-\lambda_k\|^2\right\},\]
and
\[u_{k+1}=\frac{\lambda_{k+1}-\lambda_k}{c_k}\in\partial q(\lambda_{k+1}).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact dual proximal view defines a multiplier step through an exactly solved augmented primal subproblem. Its residual is the scaled displacement from the old multiplier to the new one, and the new multiplier is exactly the unique proximal maximizer of the dual objective. The defining distinction is attainment of the complete augmented subproblem minimum, not merely a decrease or stationarity test.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper convex, \(X\) is convex, and the associated perturbation function is closed and proper with finite value at zero.
The minimum of \(L_{c_k}(\cdot,\lambda_k)\) over \(X\) is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact augmented minimization yields the exact dual proximal point \(\lambda_{k+1}\) and residual relation \(u_{k+1}=(\lambda_{k+1}-\lambda_k)/c_k\in\partial q(\lambda_{k+1})\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\lambda_{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{c_k(-q)}(\lambda_k)\).
\(0\in-\partial q(\lambda_{k+1})+(\lambda_{k+1}-\lambda_k)/c_k\).
In perturbation variables, \(u_{k+1}\in\arg\min_u\{p(u)+\lambda_k^\top u+c_k\|u\|^2/2\}\).
special_cases_latex: If \(u_{k+1}=0\), the multiplier is a fixed point and a dual maximizer.
When several primal minimizers exist but share the same residual, they generate the same unique proximal multiplier.
immediate_consequences_latex: The exact multiplier is independent of which exact primal minimizer is selected whenever the dual proximal maximizer is unique.
The subgradient relation provides the exact proximal certificate for the dual step.
boundary_notes: A merely stationary primal point does not establish the exact proximal identity.
For inexact subproblem solutions, an explicit error criterion is required and the equality becomes an approximate inclusion.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let d be a proper upper-semicontinuous concave dual function, set g=-d, and let \(P_\rho(\lambda)=\operatorname*{argmin}_\mu\{g(\mu)+(2\rho)^{-1}\|\mu-\lambda\|^2\}\). Then \[P_\rho=(I+\rho\,\partial g)^{-1},\qquad \frac{\lambda-P_\rho(\lambda)}{\rho}\in\partial g(P_\rho(\lambda)).\] Moreover, for all \(a,b\), \[\|P_\rho(a)-P_\rho(b)\|^2\le\langle P_\rho(a)-P_\rho(b),a-b\rangle.\] Thus the exact multiplier update, whenever identified with \(P_\rho\), is a single-valued firmly nonexpansive resolvent.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{f(x):Ax=b\}\), fix \(y^k\) and \(\rho>0\), and suppose \[h_k(x)=f(x)+\langle y^k,Ax-b\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax-b\|^2\] is differentiable and \(m\)-strongly convex. Let \(x_k^\star=\arg\min h_k\), \(y_k^\star=y^k+\rho(Ax_k^\star-b)\), and suppose \(\|\nabla h_k(x^{k+1})\|\le\eta_k\). For \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}-b)\), \[\|x^{k+1}-x_k^\star\|\le\frac{\eta_k}{m},\qquad \|y^{k+1}-y_k^\star\|\le\frac{\rho\|A\|}{m}\eta_k.\] Whenever exact ALM–proximal equivalence holds, \(y_k^\star\) is the exact dual proximal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity turns a computable primal stationarity residual into a bound on the induced dual proximal-point error.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequence convergence for additive optimality errors in proximal minimization of the negative concave dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(d:H\to[-\infty,+\infty)\) be proper, upper semicontinuous, and concave, let \(g=-d\), and suppose \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}g\ne\varnothing\). Let \(0<\underline\rho\le\rho_k\), and choose \(y^{k+1}\) and \(e^{k+1}\) such that
\[e^{k+1}\in\partial g(y^{k+1})+\rho_k^{-1}(y^{k+1}-y^k),\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\rho_k\|e^{k+1}\|<\infty.\]
Then \((y^k)\) is quasi-Fejér with respect to \(S\) and converges weakly to a point \(\bar y\in S\). In finite-dimensional spaces, the convergence is strong.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact dual proximal sequence with summable scaled additive optimality residuals converges weakly to a dual optimizer, and strongly in finite dimensions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonsmooth strongly convex conversion from certified inner value error to distance from the exact dual proximal update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{f(x):Ax=b\}\), fix \(y^k\) and \(\rho>0\), and let \[h_k(x)=f(x)+\langle y^k,Ax-b\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax-b\|^2\] be proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(m\)-strongly convex. Let \(x_k^\star=\arg\min h_k\), \(y_k^\star=y^k+\rho(Ax_k^\star-b)\), and suppose \(h_k(x^{k+1})-h_k(x_k^\star)\leq\delta_k\). With \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}-b)\), \[\|x^{k+1}-x_k^\star\|\leq\sqrt{\frac{2\delta_k}{m}},\qquad \|y^{k+1}-y_k^\star\|\leq\rho\|A\|\sqrt{\frac{2\delta_k}{m}}.\] Whenever exact ALM-proximal equivalence holds, this bounds the distance from the exact dual proximal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a possibly nonsmooth strongly convex augmented subproblem, a certified inner value gap bounds both primal minimizer error and the induced multiplier's distance from the exact dual proximal update.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of convergence when additive proximal residuals vanish but are not summable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=\mathbb R\), \(g\equiv0\), \(\rho_k=1\), and \(y^0=0\). Set \[y^{k+1}=y^k+\frac{1}{k+1},\qquad e^{k+1}=\frac{1}{k+1}.\] Then \[e^{k+1}\in\partial g(y^{k+1})+(y^{k+1}-y^k),\qquad e^{k+1}\to0,\] but \(y^k=\sum_{j=1}^k j^{-1}\to+\infty\). Thus vanishing additive proximal optimality residuals alone do not guarantee convergence; a summability or stronger relative-error condition is essential.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even for the zero objective, harmonic inexact proximal errors vanish while their accumulated iterates diverge, so pointwise error decay is insufficient for convergence.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower-semicontinuous, and convex with \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}g\ne\varnothing\). Let \(0<\underline\rho\le\rho_k\), set \(P_k=(I+\rho_k\partial g)^{-1}\), and generate \[y^{k+1}=P_k(y^k)+r^{k+1},\qquad\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|r^{k+1}\|<\infty.\] Then \((y^k)\) is quasi-Fejér with respect to \(S\) and converges weakly to a point of \(S\); in finite dimensions it converges strongly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If each inexact dual update stays a summable distance from the exact proximal point, the multiplier sequence converges to a dual optimizer.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal Inner Stationarity Error Is Not Automatically a Dual Proximal Residual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural limitation on converting an approximate augmented-subproblem stationarity test into an additive dual proximal inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[h_k(x)=f(x)+\langle y^k,Ax-b\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax-b\|^2,\qquad y^+=y^k+\rho(Ax-b),\] and let \(q(y)=\inf_u\{f(u)+\langle y,Au-b\rangle\}\). If \(v\in\partial h_k(x)\), then \[v\in\partial f(x)+A^{\mathsf T}y^+.\] Exact inner stationarity, together with attainment, gives \(Ax-b\in\partial^+q(y^+)\), where \(\partial^+q\) is the concave superdifferential. A bound \(\|v\|\leq\eta\) alone does not bound \[\operatorname{dist}\!\left(Ax-b,\partial^+q(y^+)\right)\] or an additive proximal optimality residual at \(y^+\) without an additional error bound, metric-regularity condition, or explicit primal-to-dual stability assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small primal augmented-subproblem stationarity residual does not by itself yield a small additive dual proximal residual; a stability or error-bound hypothesis is needed.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
Only \(\|v\|\leq\eta\) is assumed for some \(v\in\partial h_k(x)\).
review_flags: Quantitative transfer may hold under strong convexity, metric regularity, rank conditions, or another explicit error bound.

Inexact Dual Proximal View
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex equality-constrained ALM with approximate primal minimization represented as an inexact proximal dual step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the convex problem \(\inf_x\{f(x):Ax=b\}\), its dual function \(q(y)=\inf_x\{f(x)+\langle y,Ax-b\rangle\}\), and \(\rho_k>0\). If \(x^{k+1}\) approximately minimizes \(L_{\rho_k}(x,y^k)=f(x)+\langle y^k,Ax-b\rangle+\frac{\rho_k}{2}\|Ax-b\|^2\), set \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho_k(Ax^{k+1}-b)\). The induced dual step is an inexact solution of \[\max_y\left\{q(y)-\frac{1}{2\rho_k}\|y-y^k\|^2\right\}.\] For example, the inclusion \(e^{k+1}\in-\partial q(y^{k+1})+\rho_k^{-1}(y^{k+1}-y^k)\) quantifies its proximal residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate augmented-Lagrangian minimization induces an approximate proximal-point step on the concave dual function, with primal solution error represented by a dual optimality residual.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and the primal-dual values are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e^{k+1}\in-\partial q(y^{k+1})+\rho_k^{-1}(y^{k+1}-y^k)\), with \(e^{k+1}=0\) in the exact case.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inexact proximal interpretation of an augmented-Lagrangian multiplier step
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(d:\mathbb R^m\to[-\infty,+\infty)\) be a proper upper-semicontinuous concave dual function, let \(c_k>0\), and define \(\Phi_k(s)=d(s)-(2c_k)^{-1}\|s-\lambda^k\|^2\). For the equality-constrained primal problem, let \(L_{c_k}(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\langle\lambda,h(x)\rangle+(c_k/2)\|h(x)\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex dual interpretation with a quadratic proximal regularizer. The primal augmented-Lagrangian subproblem may be solved approximately; no convergence assertion is included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An inexact dual proximal step is a pair \((\lambda^{k+1},e^{k+1})\in\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^m\) satisfying \[e^{k+1}\in-\partial d(\lambda^{k+1})+c_k^{-1}(\lambda^{k+1}-\lambda^k).\] Equivalently, \[c_k^{-1}(\lambda^k-\lambda^{k+1})+e^{k+1}\in-\partial d(\lambda^{k+1}).\] For an augmented-Lagrangian realization, an approximate primal point \(x^k\) and the update \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+c_kh(x^k)\) define such an inexact proximal step when their subproblem error induces the displayed residual \(e^{k+1}\). Exact minimization corresponds to \(e^{k+1}=0\) and hence \(\lambda^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{s}\Phi_k(s)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The multiplier update is viewed as an approximate proximal maximization of the concave dual function. Its error is the residual in the proximal optimality inclusion. When that residual is zero, the new multiplier exactly maximizes the dual function minus the quadratic distance from the old multiplier; an approximate augmented-Lagrangian minimizer produces a nonzero residual.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(T=-\partial d\), the inclusion is \(e^{k+1}\in T(\lambda^{k+1})+c_k^{-1}(\lambda^{k+1}-\lambda^k)\).
If \(e^{k+1}=0\), then \(\lambda^{k+1}=(I+c_kT)^{-1}(\lambda^k)\).
special_cases_latex: For exact primal minimization and the quadratic augmented Lagrangian, \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+c_kh(x^k)\) is the exact dual proximal step.
immediate_consequences_latex: The norm \(\|e^{k+1}\|\) is a dual-proximal accuracy certificate distinct from primal feasibility \(\|h(x^k)\|\).
boundary_notes: The definition does not identify an arbitrary small primal gradient residual with a dual proximal residual without an additional error-transfer result.
For inequality multipliers, the proximal problem must include the nonnegative multiplier domain.

notation.meaning: Concave superdifferential, represented through the monotone operator \(-\partial d\).
Residual in the proximal optimality inclusion.

With \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}-b)\), \[\|x^{k+1}-x_k^\star\|\le\frac{\eta_k}{m},\qquad \|y^{k+1}-y_k^\star\|\le\frac{\rho\|A\|}{m}\eta_k.\] Whenever exact ALM-proximal equivalence holds, \(y_k^\star\) is the exact dual proximal point, so the second bound is an explicit inexact-proximal error estimate.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), let \(g:X\to\mathbb R^r\), and consider \(\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ g(x)\le0\}\). Let \(P_c(\cdot;\mu)\) be an admissible convex augmentation with \(c>0\), and set \(L_c(x,\mu)=f(x)+P_c(g(x);\mu)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A representation-level definition covering the augmented saddle inequality, augmented dual function, and its regularized ordinary-dual form. Global equality claims require the stated convex-duality hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The augmented saddle-duality viewpoint associated with \(L_c\) consists of the three linked objects \[d_c(\mu):=\inf_{x\in X}L_c(x,\mu),\qquad \sup_{\mu\in M}d_c(\mu),\] \[(x^*,\mu^*)\text{ is an augmented saddle point}\Longleftrightarrow L_c(x^*,\mu)\le L_c(x^*,\mu^*)\le L_c(x,\mu^*)\quad(\forall x\in X,\ \forall\mu\in M),\] and, when ordinary strong duality holds and \(P_c^*(\cdot;\mu)\) is the conjugate of the augmentation, \[d_c(\mu)=\max_{s\in M}\{d(s)-P_c^*(s;\mu)\}.\] Here \(M=\mathbb R_+^r\) for inequality multipliers unless the chosen augmentation admits an extension to all of \(\mathbb R^r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This viewpoint treats one augmented Lagrangian simultaneously as a primal–dual saddle function, as the generator of an augmented dual function obtained by minimizing over the primal variable, and as a regularization of the ordinary dual problem. The admissible multiplier domain is part of the definition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[d_c(\mu)=\inf_{x\in X}L_c(x,\mu),\qquad d_c(\mu)=\max_{s\in M}\{d(s)-P_c^*(s;\mu)\}\] whenever the regularized-dual identity's convex-duality hypotheses hold.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For quadratic equality augmentation, \(P_c^*(s;\lambda)=(2c)^{-1}\|s-\lambda\|^2\), so \(d_c\) is a Moreau-type regularization of \(d\).
special_cases_latex: If \(X=\mathbb R^n\) and the augmentation is defined for unrestricted multipliers, the saddle inequalities are unconstrained in both variables.
immediate_consequences_latex: An augmented saddle point simultaneously minimizes \(L_c(\cdot,\mu^*)\) and maximizes \(L_c(x^*,\cdot)\) over the specified domains.
boundary_notes: The regularized-dual identity is not asserted for arbitrary nonconvex data.
The multiplier domain cannot be omitted for inequality constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Augmented Saddle-Point Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global saddle geometry for the quadratic augmented Lagrangian of a convex affine equality-constrained problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L_\rho(x,y)=f(x)+\langle y,Ax-b\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax-b\|^2\), where \(\rho>0\). If \((x^\star,y^\star)\) is an ordinary primal-dual optimal pair, then \(Ax^\star=b\), and the KKT condition implies that \(x^\star\) globally minimizes \(L_\rho(\cdot,y^\star)\). Consequently, for every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\), \[L_\rho(x^\star,y)\le L_\rho(x^\star,y^\star)\le L_\rho(x,y^\star).\] Conversely, if a finite pair \((x^\star,y^\star)\) satisfies these inequalities for every such \(x\) and \(y\), then \(Ax^\star=b\), \(x^\star\) is primal optimal, and \(y^\star\) maximizes the augmented dual function \(q_\rho(y)=\inf_x L_\rho(x,y)\), with \(q_\rho(y^\star)=f(x^\star)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ordinary primal-dual solution forms a saddle point of the augmented Lagrangian. Conversely, a finite global augmented saddle point yields primal optimality and zero gap for the associated augmented dual function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The augmented saddle inequalities imply primal optimality and \(q_\rho(y^\star)=f(x^\star)\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(M\subseteq\mathbb R^r\), and let \(L_c:X\times M\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be an augmented Lagrangian for a fixed \(c>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global saddle geometry on the explicitly stated primal and multiplier domains. A local saddle notion would replace the universal quantifiers by neighborhood-restricted quantifiers and is not used here.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pair \((x^*,\mu^*)\in X\times M\) is a global augmented saddle point of \(L_c\) if \[L_c(x^*,\mu)\le L_c(x^*,\mu^*)\le L_c(x,\mu^*)\qquad\forall(x,\mu)\in X\times M.\] Equivalently, \[x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}L_c(x,\mu^*),\qquad \mu^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{\mu\in M}L_c(x^*,\mu).\] The associated saddle value is \(v_c=L_c(x^*,\mu^*)\); consequently \[\sup_{\mu\in M}\inf_{x\in X}L_c(x,\mu)=v_c=\inf_{x\in X}\sup_{\mu\in M}L_c(x,\mu)\] whenever the displayed saddle point exists and the extended-real expressions are well defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An augmented saddle point is a primal–dual pair at which the augmented Lagrangian cannot be decreased by changing the primal variable and cannot be increased by changing the multiplier. Its central value is simultaneously the max–min and min–max value.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[L_c(x^*,\mu^*)=\min_{x\in X}L_c(x,\mu^*)=\max_{\mu\in M}L_c(x^*,\mu).\]
special_cases_latex: For convex inequality programming with \(M=\mathbb R_+^r\) and an admissible augmentation, an optimal solution–multiplier pair is characterized by this saddle relation.
For an augmentation defined on all multipliers, one may take \(M=\mathbb R^r\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Existence of an augmented saddle point rules out a saddle-value gap for that augmented model.
boundary_notes: Stationarity of \(L_c\) alone is weaker than the global saddle inequalities.
The definition does not assert that every KKT pair is a global saddle point in a nonconvex problem.

knowledge_statements.title: Augmented Dual Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic augmented dual function obtained by globally minimizing the augmented Lagrangian over primal variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\rho>0\), define the augmented Lagrangian \(L_\rho(x,y)=f(x)+\langle y,Ax-b\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax-b\|^2\). Its augmented dual function is \[q_\rho(y):=\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}L_\rho(x,y),\qquad y\in\mathbb{R}^m.\] The function \(q_\rho\) is concave because it is a pointwise infimum of affine functions of \(y\). The associated augmented dual problem is \(\sup_{y\in\mathbb{R}^m}q_\rho(y)\), and weak duality gives \(q_\rho(y)\le p^\star\) whenever the primal optimum \(p^\star\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The augmented dual function is the primal infimum of the augmented Lagrangian. It is concave in the multiplier and supplies lower bounds on the primal optimum.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex, let \(q(z)=\inf_x\{f(x)+\langle z,Ax-b\rangle\}\), and suppose \(q\) is proper. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Augmentation Need Not Remove a Nonconvex Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar equality problem with a positive augmented-duality gap below a sharp penalty threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{(x^2-1)^2:x=0\}\), with \(p^\star=1\). For \(0<\rho<4\), let \(d_\rho=\sup_{y\in\mathbb R}\inf_{x\in\mathbb R}\{(x^2-1)^2+yx+(\rho/2)x^2\}\). The inner-value function is concave and even in \(y\), so it is maximized at \(y=0\), and \[d_\rho=1-\left(1-\frac{\rho}{4}\right)^2<p^\star.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scalar double-well problem retains a positive augmented-duality gap for every penalty below four.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Asymptotic Closure of the Augmented Duality Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global nonconvex augmented-dual values on a compact primal domain as the penalty diverges.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be compact, let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:X\to\mathbb R^m\) be continuous, and suppose \(F=\{x\in X:c(x)=0\}\neq\varnothing\). Define \(p^\star=\min_{x\in F}f(x)\) and \[d_\rho=\sup_y\inf_{x\in X}\left\{f(x)+\langle y,c(x)\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\|c(x)\|^2\right\}.\] Then \(d_\rho\le p^\star\), \(d_\rho\) is nondecreasing in \(\rho\), and \(d_\rho\to p^\star\) as \(\rho\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact domain with continuous data and a nonempty feasible set, increasing quadratic augmentation closes the nonconvex augmented-duality gap asymptotically.
knowledge_statements.title: Asymptotic Closure of the Augmented Duality Gap

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Augmented Exactness Does Not Close the Global Duality Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinction between local augmented minimization and the global minimization required by nonconvex augmented duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(d_\rho=\sup_y\inf_xL_\rho(x,y)\), zero gap depends on the global infimum of \(L_\rho(\cdot,y)\). If a feasible global primal optimizer \(x^\star\) is merely a strict local minimizer of \(L_\rho(\cdot,y^\star)\), only a neighborhood inequality follows. A remote point may have \(L_\rho(x,y^\star)<p^\star\), so local augmented exactness alone does not imply \(d_\rho=p^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strict local augmented minimum at a primal solution is insufficient for zero augmented-duality gap because the dual function uses a global primal infimum.
assumptions_latex: The primal problem and \(L_\rho\) may be nonconvex.
\(x^\star\) is feasible and globally primal optimal.
\(x^\star\) is assumed only to locally minimize \(L_\rho(\cdot,y^\star)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Local Augmented Exactness Does Not Close the Global Duality Gap

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sharp Finite-Penalty Threshold for the Double-Well Example
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completion of the sharp penalty boundary in the accepted scalar nonconvex augmented-duality example.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p^\star=\min\{(x^2-1)^2:x=0\}=1\), define \[d_\rho=\sup_{y\in\mathbb R}\inf_{x\in\mathbb R}\left\{(x^2-1)^2+yx+\frac{\rho}{2}x^2\right\}.\] For every \(\rho\geq4\), the inner-value function is concave and even in \(y\), hence is maximized at \(y=0\), and \(x=0\) globally minimizes the resulting augmented objective. Therefore \[d_\rho=1=p^\star.\] Together with the accepted formula for \(0<\rho<4\), the augmented-duality gap closes at the sharp threshold \(\rho=4\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In the scalar double-well example, the positive augmented-duality gap below four disappears exactly when the quadratic penalty reaches four.
assumptions_latex: The primal constraint is \(x=0\) and the objective is \((x^2-1)^2\).
knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Finite-Penalty Threshold for the Double-Well Example

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Noncompact Near-Feasible Escape Can Preserve the Augmented Duality Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of asymptotic nonconvex gap closure without compactness or comparable level-boundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{f(x):c(x)=0\}\) on \(\mathbb R\), where \[f(x)=-\frac{x^2}{1+x^2},\qquad c(x)=xe^{-x^2}.\] The feasible set is \(\{0\}\), so \(p^\star=f(0)=0\). For every \(\rho>0\), define \[d_\rho=\sup_{y\in\mathbb R}\inf_{x\in\mathbb R}\left\{f(x)+yc(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}c(x)^2\right\}.\] Since \(f(x)\to-1\) and \(c(x)\to0\) as \(x\to+\infty\), the inner infimum is at most \(-1\) for every \(y\) and \(\rho\). Hence \[d_\rho\le-1<p^\star\qquad(\rho>0),\] so the augmented-duality gap does not close as \(\rho\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unbounded sequence can become nearly feasible while retaining objective values below the feasible optimum, preventing quadratic augmentation from closing the nonconvex duality gap at any penalty.
knowledge_statements.title: Noncompact Near-Feasible Escape Can Preserve the Augmented Duality Gap
Nonconvex Augmented Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional zero-gap augmented duality for nonconvex equality-constrained optimization through a global augmented saddle point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(p^\star=\inf\{f(x):c(x)=0\}\) and \(L_\rho(x,y)=f(x)+\langle y,c(x)\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\|c(x)\|^2\). Without convexity, weak duality still gives \(d_\rho:=\sup_y\inf_x L_\rho(x,y)\le p^\star\). If there exist \(x^\star,y^\star\) and \(\rho>0\) such that \(c(x^\star)=0\), \(f(x^\star)=p^\star\), and \(x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_xL_\rho(x,y^\star)\), then \[d_\rho=\inf_xL_\rho(x,y^\star)=f(x^\star)=p^\star.\] Thus global augmented exactness closes the duality gap even though convexity is absent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a nonconvex problem, augmented weak duality always holds; a globally exact augmented Lagrangian multiplier is sufficient for zero augmented duality gap.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Augmented dual value and gap for a nonconvex equality problem
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), let \(h:X\to\mathbb R^m\), and define \(p^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ h(x)=0\}\). For \(c\ge0\), set \(L_c(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\langle\lambda,h(x)\rangle+(c/2)\|h(x)\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, possibly nonconvex global construction. The definition measures rather than presupposes exact duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The quadratic augmented dual function and augmented dual value are \[d_c(\lambda):=\inf_{x\in X}L_c(x,\lambda),\qquad v_c^{\mathrm D}:=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^m}d_c(\lambda).\] The augmented duality gap is \[\Delta_c:=p^*-v_c^{\mathrm D}\in[0,+\infty],\] because every feasible \(x\) satisfies \(L_c(x,\lambda)=f(x)\), and hence \(d_c(\lambda)\le p^*\). The model has exact augmented duality at parameter \(c\) precisely when \(\Delta_c=0\); it has attained exact augmented duality when, additionally, some \(\lambda^*\) satisfies \(d_c(\lambda^*)=p^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonconvex augmented duality is defined by taking the infimum of the augmented Lagrangian over the whole primal domain and then maximizing that lower bound over multipliers. The difference between the primal optimum and this augmented dual value is the augmented duality gap. Zero gap and attainment are separate properties, not automatic consequences of augmentation.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Exact augmented duality means \(p^*=\sup_{\lambda}\inf_{x\in X}L_c(x,\lambda)\).
special_cases_latex: At \(c=0\), \(d_c\) reduces to the classical Lagrangian dual function.
For convex problems satisfying a suitable constraint qualification, the classical gap may already vanish; augmentation then regularizes the dual representation rather than repairing a gap.
immediate_consequences_latex: Increasing \(c\) changes the family of global lower bounds but does not by definition guarantee \(\Delta_c=0\).
boundary_notes: Local augmented-Lagrangian dual functions based on a selected local minimizer are different objects.
No universal finite penalty threshold for zero gap is asserted.

notation.meaning: Global augmented duality gap at penalty parameter \(c\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(\min\{f(x):h(x)=0\}\), let \(L_{c_k}(x,\lambda^k)=f(x)+\langle\lambda^k,h(x)\rangle+(c_k/2)\|h(x)\|^2\), where \(c_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic finite-dimensional equality-constrained ALM. The definition describes the control organization and permits exact or residual-controlled inner solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nested ALM control architecture is a sequence \(\{(x^k,\lambda^k,c_k,\eta_k)\}_{k\ge0}\) in which each outer iteration first invokes an inner solver to return \(x^k\) satisfying a prescribed certificate \[\mathcal E_k(x^k;\lambda^k,c_k)\le\eta_k,\] then performs the multiplier update \[\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+c_kh(x^k),\] and finally selects \(c_{k+1}>0\) and \(\eta_{k+1}\ge0\) by an outer control rule. For a smooth unconstrained inner problem, the canonical certificate is \(\mathcal E_k=\|\nabla_xL_{c_k}(x^k,\lambda^k)\|\); exact minimization is represented by \(x^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_xL_{c_k}(x,\lambda^k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method has an inner level that approximately or exactly minimizes the current augmented Lagrangian and an outer level that updates multipliers, penalty parameters, and the requested inner accuracy. These quantities together, rather than the multiplier formula alone, constitute the nested control state.
special_cases_latex: The classical method of multipliers uses exact inner minimization and usually a nondecreasing penalty sequence.
An asymptotically exact architecture uses \(\eta_k\to0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Warm starting the inner solver from a preceding primal iterate changes implementation but not the mathematical architecture.
boundary_notes: Specific penalty-increase tests, multiplier projections, and safeguards are variants of the outer control rule.
This definition does not itself supply convergence conditions.

notation.meaning: Outer rule selecting penalty and accuracy controls.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Classification by explicitly retained inner constraints
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let the original feasible set be described by an augmented constraint block \(a(x)=0\) and a retained block \(x\in C\), where \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty. Define \(L_c^a(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\langle\lambda,a(x)\rangle+(c/2)\|a(x)\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional partial-elimination architecture. The retained set may encode no constraints, bounds, affine constraints, or a general lower-level feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A subproblem constraint architecture is the choice of a retained feasible set \(C\) in the inner problem \[x^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}L_{c_k}^a(x,\lambda^k),\qquad \lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+c_ka(x^k).\] It is classified as unconstrained when \(C=\mathbb R^n\), bound-constrained when \(C=[\ell,u]\), linearly constrained when \(C=\{x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le q\}\), and general lower-level when \(C\) is a prescribed nonlinear, conic, discrete, or otherwise structured set delegated to a constrained solver. Only the constraints in \(a(x)=0\) are augmented and receive the displayed multiplier update; constraints defining \(C\) remain explicit in every inner solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The architecture is determined by which constraints are absorbed into the augmented Lagrangian and which are deliberately retained as the feasible set of the inner optimization problem. Four standard classes result from taking that retained set to be the whole space, a box, a polyhedron, or a general structured set.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If retained equalities are \(b(x)=0\), then \(C=\{x:b(x)=0\}\) and the construction is the partial method of multipliers.
special_cases_latex: Taking \(C=\mathbb R^n\) recovers full elimination of the selected constraint block.
immediate_consequences_latex: Changing \(C\) changes the inner solver class without changing the multiplier update for the augmented block.
boundary_notes: A constraint must not simultaneously be counted as retained and augmented unless a separately defined splitting formulation duplicates it.

notation.meaning: Feasible set deliberately retained in each ALM subproblem.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matrix-free trust-region solution of a BCL inner subproblem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Describes the practical inner-solver architecture and permitted curvature approximations; it asserts neither convergence nor complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \begin{gathered}B_k:=\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda^k)+\mu_kA_k^TA_k,\\ \min_d\ \frac12d^TB_kd+\nabla_x\mathcal L_A(x_k,\lambda^k;\mu_k)^Td\\ \text{subject to }l\le x_k+d\le u,\qquad \|d\|_\infty\le\Delta.\end{gathered}
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a bound-constrained augmented-Lagrangian inner problem, form the stated box- and infinity-norm-constrained quadratic model. First use a projected-gradient line search to identify components fixed at their bounds; then apply conjugate gradients to the remaining free components. The conjugate-gradient stage uses matrix-vector products and does not require factorization of a KKT matrix or the constraint Jacobian. The Lagrangian Hessian may be replaced by a BFGS or SR1 approximation, and partially separable structure may be exploited.
assumptions_latex: \text{The displayed quadratic model and its required matrix-vector products are available.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The model can be treated by projected-gradient bound identification followed by conjugate gradients over the free variables, without KKT or constraint-Jacobian factorization.}
