knowledge_statements.title: Unconstrained ALM Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: All explicit constraints are absorbed into the augmented objective, leaving an unconstrained inner minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the equality-constrained problem \(\min_x f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), an unconstrained ALM subproblem at outer iterate \((y^k,\rho_k)\) is \[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{f(x)+\langle y^k,c(x)\rangle+\frac{\rho_k}{2}\|c(x)\|^2\right\}.\] No feasibility condition is imposed on inner trial points. After exact or prescribed inexact solution, the outer multiplier update is typically \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho_kc(x^{k+1})\); the penalty parameter is then retained or increased according to an outer feasibility test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All constraints enter the augmented objective, so each inner problem is unconstrained and can be delegated to a smooth or nonsmooth unconstrained optimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}\) is computed over the full domain \(\mathbb{R}^n\), with feasibility enforced only through \(L_{\rho_k}\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth first- and second-order tests for an unconstrained ALM inner problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Every local minimizer of a differentiable unconstrained augmented objective \(\phi(x)=L_ho(x,y)\) satisfies \(
abla\phi(x)=0\). If \(\phi\) is twice differentiable there, it also satisfies \(
abla^2\phi(x)\succeq0\). Conversely, \(
abla\phi(x)=0\) is sufficient for global optimality when \(\phi\) is convex, and \(
abla^2\phi(x)\succ0\) together with stationarity is sufficient for a strict local minimum. Without convexity, stationarity need not imply minimization: \(\phi(t)=-t^2\) has \(\phi'(0)=0\), but zero is a strict local maximum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ordinary gradient and Hessian provide the smooth optimality tests for a full-space ALM subproblem. Stationarity is globally sufficient under convexity but can identify a maximum in a nonconvex subproblem.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unconstrained proximal augmented-Lagrangian formulation for inequality constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-value and proximal-smoothed unconstrained representations of a smooth inequality-constrained problem with no equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x)\) subject to \(c_i(x)\ge 0\) for every \(i\in\mathcal I\), with no equality constraints. Its extended-value objective is
\[
F(x)=\max_{\lambda\ge0}\left\{f(x)-\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}\lambda_i c_i(x)\right\}=\begin{cases}f(x),&c_i(x)\ge0\ \forall i,\\+\infty,&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}
\]
so \(\min_xF(x)=\min_{x\text{ feasible}}f(x)\). Direct minimization of \(F\) is impractical because it changes from finite to infinite across the feasible-set boundary. Given \(\mu_k>0\) and \(\lambda^k\ge0\), the proximal surrogate
\[
\widehat F(x;\lambda^k,\mu_k)=\max_{\lambda\ge0}\left\{f(x)-\sum_i\lambda_i c_i(x)-\frac1{2\mu_k}\sum_i(\lambda_i-\lambda_i^k)^2\right\}
\]
has componentwise maximizer \(\lambda_i=[\lambda_i^k-\mu_kc_i(x)]_+\) and the unconstrained representation
\[
\widehat F(x;\lambda^k,\mu_k)=f(x)+\sum_i\psi(c_i(x),\lambda_i^k;\mu_k),\qquad
\psi(t,\sigma;\mu)=\begin{cases}-\sigma t+\frac\mu2t^2,&t\le\sigma/\mu,\\-\frac{\sigma^2}{2\mu},&t>\sigma/\mu.\end{cases}
\]
Thus an inequality-constrained augmented-Lagrangian step may minimize \(\widehat F\) over \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and then update each multiplier by \(\lambda_i^{k+1}=[\lambda_i^k-\mu_kc_i(x)]_+\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a problem minimizing f(x) subject only to inequalities c_i(x) ≥ 0, maximizing the ordinary Lagrangian over nonnegative multipliers produces an extended-value objective equal to f at feasible points and positive infinity elsewhere, hence an equivalent unconstrained problem that is unsuitable for direct smooth minimization. Adding a quadratic proximal term around the current nonnegative multiplier estimate yields a finite unconstrained augmented-Lagrangian surrogate. Its multiplier maximization is separable and explicit: each new multiplier is the positive part of λ_i^k − μ_k c_i(x). Substitution gives the stated piecewise penalty function, so the method minimizes this surrogate in x and applies the explicit multiplier update.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Constrained ALM Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The augmented model absorbs general constraints while retaining simple lower and upper bounds explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the primal problem contains box restrictions \(\ell\le x\le u\) and nonlinear equalities \(c(x)=0\). A bound-constrained ALM subproblem at \((y^k,\rho_k)\) is \[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\ell\le x\le u}\left\{f(x)+\langle y^k,c(x)\rangle+\frac{\rho_k}{2}\|c(x)\|^2\right\}.\] The box is not penalized: every inner iterate must remain in \(B=[\ell,u]\). A verifiable first-order termination measure is the projected-gradient residual \(\|x-P_B(x-\nabla_xL_{\rho_k}(x,y^k))\|\), when the augmented objective is differentiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonlinear constraints are augmented, but variable bounds remain explicit and are handled by a box-constrained inner solver using projected optimality measures.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are differentiable on a neighborhood of \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}\in B\) minimizes or approximately minimizes \(L_{\rho_k}(\cdot,y^k)\) over \(B\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in B=[\ell,u]\) and any \(\alpha>0\), \[x=P_B(x-\alpha
abla\phi(x))\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad0\in
abla\phi(x)+N_B(x).\] Componentwise, \(
abla_i\phi(x)=0\) in the strict interior, \(
abla_i\phi(x)\ge0\) at a lower bound that is not also an upper bound, and \(
abla_i\phi(x)\le0\) at an upper bound that is not also a lower bound; a fixed coordinate \(\ell_i=u_i\) imposes no gradient-sign restriction. Every local minimizer satisfies this condition. If \(\phi\) is convex on \(B\), the condition is also sufficient for global optimality; without convexity it is only stationary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero projected-gradient residual is equivalent to box KKT stationarity. It is necessary at a local minimum and sufficient for a global minimum when the augmented objective is convex.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B=[\ell,u]=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\ell_i\le x_i\le u_i\}\), allowing infinite endpoints, and let \(L_c^a(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\langle\lambda,a(x)\rangle+(c/2)\|a(x)\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional partial elimination in which box geometry is retained exactly and another constraint block is augmented.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A bound-constrained ALM subproblem at \((\lambda^k,c_k)\) is \[\min_{x\in B}L_{c_k}^a(x,\lambda^k),\qquad B=[\ell,u].\] The exact solution set is \(S_k^B=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in B}L_{c_k}^a(x,\lambda^k)\). For differentiable \(L_{c_k}^a\), a canonical first-order inexactness measure is the normal-cone residual \[\mathcal E_k^B(x)=\operatorname{dist}\bigl(0,\nabla_xL_{c_k}^a(x,\lambda^k)+N_B(x)\bigr),\] and an inexact inner solution satisfies \(x^k\in B\) and \(\mathcal E_k^B(x^k)\le\eta_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inner solver minimizes the augmented objective while enforcing lower and upper bounds exactly. Approximate optimality is naturally measured by distance from the box-constrained first-order inclusion, not merely by the ordinary gradient norm at a boundary point.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a closed convex box, exact first-order stationarity is \(0\in\nabla_xL_{c_k}^a(x^k,\lambda^k)+N_B(x^k)\).
special_cases_latex: One-sided bounds are represented by \(\ell_i=-\infty\) or \(u_i=+\infty\).
Nonnegativity corresponds to \(B=\mathbb R_+^n\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Projected-gradient or active-set methods can preserve box feasibility throughout the inner solve.
boundary_notes: General polyhedral constraints are not boxes unless they separate coordinatewise.
A small unconstrained gradient is not necessary at an active bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Linearly Constrained ALM Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonlinear constraints are augmented while affine constraints remain explicit in every inner problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x:Gx=h,\;Hx\le r\}\) be a nonempty polyhedron, and let \(c(x)=0\) denote constraints selected for augmentation. At outer state \((y^k,\rho_k)\), the linearly constrained ALM subproblem is \[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}\left\{f(x)+\langle y^k,c(x)\rangle+\frac{\rho_k}{2}\|c(x)\|^2\right\}.\] The affine constraints defining \(P\) remain exact throughout the inner solve, whereas violations of \(c(x)=0\) are controlled through the multiplier and penalty terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inner solver enforces selected affine equalities and inequalities exactly while treating the remaining constraints through the augmented Lagrangian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}\in P\) minimizes or approximately minimizes \(L_{\rho_k}(\cdot,y^k)\) over \(P\).

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The augmented objective is minimized over a fixed polyhedron. The retained affine constraints are enforced by the inner solver, whereas the separate augmented constraints drive the outer multiplier update.

special_cases_latex: A box-constrained subproblem is a polyhedral special case, but is normally separated because its projection and linear algebra are simpler.

knowledge_statements.title: General Lower-Level Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A chosen constraint block remains explicit and is handled by a specialized constrained inner solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{x:g(x)\le0,\;h(x)=0\}\) collect constraints assigned to the lower-level solver, and let \(c(x)=0\) collect constraints assigned to augmentation. At outer state \((y^k,\rho_k)\), the general lower-level subproblem is \[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\left\{f(x)+\langle y^k,c(x)\rangle+\frac{\rho_k}{2}\|c(x)\|^2\right\}.\] Thus the inner solver must return an \(X\)-feasible point satisfying the prescribed objective or stationarity accuracy; only the block \(c(x)=0\) is managed by the outer ALM updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Some constraints remain inside a specialized constrained subproblem, while the outer augmented-Lagrangian mechanism manages only the selected augmented constraint block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}\in X\) solves the current augmented objective subject to all retained lower-level constraints.

Let \(x\in X=\{x:g(x)\le0,\ h(x)=0\}\). If \(x\) locally minimizes \(\phi(x)=L_ho(x,y)\) over \(X\) and MFCQ holds at \(x\), then there exist \(\lambda\ge0\) and \(

abla\phi(x)+Jg(x)^	op\lambda+Jh(x)^	op
u=0,\qquad\lambda_i g_i(x)=0\quad	ext{for every }i.\] Conversely, if \(\phi\) and every \(g_i\) are convex, \(h\) is affine, and a feasible point satisfies these relations, then it is a global minimizer of the retained-constraint subproblem. knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty retained feasible set and let \(L_c^a(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\langle\lambda,a(x)\rangle+(c/2)\|a(x)\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional partial augmentation with an arbitrary explicitly retained feasible set. Convexity and smoothness are not imposed by the definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A general lower-level ALM subproblem at \((\lambda^k,c_k)\) is the constrained optimization problem \[\min_{x\in C}L_{c_k}^a(x,\lambda^k).\] An exact lower-level solution belongs to \(S_k^C=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}L_{c_k}^a(x,\lambda^k)\). An inexact solution is a feasible point \(x^k\in C\) satisfying a solver-compatible certificate \(\mathcal E_C(x^k;\lambda^k,c_k)\le\eta_k\). When \(C\) is closed and convex and the objective is differentiable, the canonical stationarity certificate is \[\mathcal E_C(x;\lambda,c)=\operatorname{dist}\bigl(0,\nabla_xL_c^a(x,\lambda)+N_C(x)\bigr).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A general lower-level architecture leaves a structured feasible set intact and delegates minimization of the current augmented objective over that set to an appropriate constrained solver. The admissible inexactness certificate must match the geometry and regularity of the retained set.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(C=\{x:b(x)=0\}\), this is the partial method-of-multipliers subproblem.
special_cases_latex: Boxes and polyhedra recover the bound-constrained and linearly constrained architectures.
A conic set, nonlinear feasible region, or discrete structured set may serve as \(C\), subject to an appropriate solver and certificate.
immediate_consequences_latex: Only the block \(a\) participates in the displayed outer multiplier update.
boundary_notes: For nonconvex \(C\), normal-cone stationarity and global lower-level minimization are distinct notions.
Solver failure is not an inexact solution unless a valid certificate is returned.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact, inexact, and asymptotically exact inner accuracy
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For each outer index \(k\), let \(F_k:C\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be the current augmented-Lagrangian subproblem objective, let \(F_k^*=\inf_{x\in C}F_k(x)\), and let \(\mathcal E_k:C\to[0,+\infty]\) be an optimality residual with \(\mathcal E_k(x)=0\) at exact solutions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract deterministic classification applicable to smooth or nonsmooth and constrained or unconstrained ALM subproblems once a valid residual is fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A subproblem accuracy regime specifies admissible inner outputs \(x^k\in C\) through one of the following conditions: exact minimization, \[F_k(x^k)=F_k^*;\] inexact minimization, \[\mathcal E_k(x^k)\le\eta_k\quad\text{for a prescribed }\eta_k\ge0;\] or asymptotically exact minimization, \[\mathcal E_k(x^k)\le\eta_k\quad\text{with }\eta_k\to0.\] A value-gap certificate \(F_k(x^k)-F_k^*\le\varepsilon_k\) is an alternative only when \(F_k^*\) is well defined and the gap is computable or bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The accuracy regime is the rule determining how close each inner output must be to solving the current augmented-Lagrangian subproblem. Exact minimization requires attaining the infimum; inexact minimization permits a stated residual; asymptotically exact minimization makes the permitted residual tend to zero.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a smooth unconstrained subproblem, one may take \(\mathcal E_k(x)=\|\nabla F_k(x)\|\).
For closed convex \(C\), one may take \(\mathcal E_k(x)=\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial(F_k+\delta_C)(x))\).
special_cases_latex: Setting \(\eta_k=0\) for every \(k\) recovers exact minimization when zero residual characterizes a minimizer.
immediate_consequences_latex: A vanishing tolerance is weaker than exact minimization at each finite iteration.
boundary_notes: A residual must be chosen so that small values have the intended optimization meaning.
Fixed nonzero tolerances are inexact but not asymptotically exact.

notation.meaning: Optimal value of the kth inner subproblem.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Subproblem Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ideal ALM regime in which every inner augmented-Lagrangian problem is solved globally without error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be the retained inner feasible set and \(L_{\rho_k}(\cdot,y^k)\) the augmented objective at outer iteration \(k\). Exact subproblem minimization means that an attained global minimizer is selected: \[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}L_{\rho_k}(x,y^k),\qquad L_{\rho_k}(x^{k+1},y^k)=\inf_{x\in X}L_{\rho_k}(x,y^k).\] Equivalently, the inner objective gap is zero at every outer iteration. This condition is stronger than merely finding a stationary point when the subproblem is nonconvex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every ALM inner problem is solved to an attained global minimum, so its objective gap is exactly zero before the outer variables are updated.
assumptions_latex: For every \(k\), the infimum of \(L_{\rho_k}(\cdot,y^k)\) over \(X\) is attained.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and let \(F_k(x)=L_{c_k}(x,\lambda^k)\) be the kth augmented-Lagrangian objective on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global exact minimization. Local exact minimization is a separate regime and must explicitly identify the neighborhood or selected local branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The kth ALM subproblem is minimized exactly when the inner output \(x^k\) satisfies \[x^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}F_k(x),\] equivalently, \[x^k\in C\quad\text{and}\quad F_k(x^k)\le F_k(x)\quad\forall x\in C.\] Thus its objective gap is zero: \(F_k(x^k)-\inf_{x\in C}F_k(x)=0\). If \(F_k+\delta_C\) is proper closed convex, exact minimization is also equivalent to \(0\in\partial(F_k+\delta_C)(x^k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact minimization means that the returned inner point globally attains the smallest current augmented-Lagrangian value over the retained feasible set. In convex settings this is equivalently a zero subdifferential residual; in nonconvex settings first-order stationarity alone is not enough.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[L_{c_k}(x^k,\lambda^k)=\inf_{x\in C}L_{c_k}(x,\lambda^k).\]
Under proper closed convexity, \(0\in\partial_x(L_{c_k}(\cdot,\lambda^k)+\delta_C)(x^k)\).
special_cases_latex: For \(C=\mathbb R^n\), the exact solve is unconstrained.
For a strictly convex subproblem, the exact minimizer is unique.
immediate_consequences_latex: There is no inner optimization error at iteration \(k\), although the outer iterate need not yet solve the original constrained problem.
boundary_notes: An exact stationary point of a nonconvex subproblem need not be its exact global minimizer.
The definition presumes the infimum is attained.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(F_k(x)=L_{c_k}(x,\lambda^k)\), and define \(\bar F_k=F_k+\delta_C\). Assume \(\partial\bar F_k(x)\) is nonempty at the candidate point.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic inner solve with an explicit first-order residual. In smooth unconstrained problems this becomes a gradient-norm test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The kth ALM subproblem is minimized inexactly to tolerance \(\eta_k\ge0\) when the returned point \(x^k\in C\) satisfies \[\mathcal E_k(x^k):=\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial\bar F_k(x^k))\le\eta_k.\] Equivalently, there exists \(v^k\in\partial\bar F_k(x^k)\) with \(\|v^k\|\le\eta_k\). If \(C=\mathbb R^n\) and \(F_k\) is differentiable, this reduces to \[\|\nabla_xL_{c_k}(x^k,\lambda^k)\|\le\eta_k.\] The tolerance sequence is part of the outer–inner method specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inner solve is inexact when the returned feasible point has a certified optimality residual no larger than a prescribed tolerance. For a smooth unconstrained augmented Lagrangian the residual is its gradient norm; with retained constraints it includes the feasible-set normal cone.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[\exists v^k\in\partial(L_{c_k}(\cdot,\lambda^k)+\delta_C)(x^k):\ \|v^k\|\le\eta_k.\]
special_cases_latex: For \(\eta_k=0\) in a convex subproblem, the condition characterizes exact minimization.
For a smooth unconstrained problem, \(v^k=\nabla_xL_{c_k}(x^k,\lambda^k)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The inner solver may terminate after finitely many iterations once the residual test is met.
boundary_notes: For nonconvex subproblems the residual certifies approximate stationarity, not a global value gap.
A small residual may require scaling when variables or constraints have disparate units.

children.title: Absolute-Accuracy Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Absolute-Accuracy Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inexact inner solves controlled by an externally prescribed, unscaled sequence of objective tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi_k(x)=L_{\rho_k}(x,y^k)\) on a retained feasible set \(X\), and let \(\varepsilon_k\ge0\) be prescribed independently of the current outer residual. An absolute objective-accuracy regime accepts \(x^{k+1}\in X\) whenever \[\phi_k(x^{k+1})-\inf_{x\in X}\phi_k(x)\le\varepsilon_k.\] A uniformly bounded absolute-accuracy regime imposes \(\varepsilon_k\le\bar\varepsilon\) for some \(\bar\varepsilon\ge0\), while an asymptotically exact absolute-accuracy regime imposes \(\varepsilon_k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inner solution satisfies absolute objective accuracy when its subproblem objective gap is bounded by a prescribed tolerance that is not scaled by current outer progress.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty and \(\inf_{x\in X}\phi_k(x)\) is finite.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal E_k(x)\ge0\) be an inner optimality residual for the kth augmented-Lagrangian subproblem, and let \(\varepsilon_k\ge0\) be prescribed independently of the magnitude of current outer residuals.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute, additively scaled stopping rule. The residual may be a gradient, subgradient, projected-gradient, or normal-cone residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An absolute-accuracy regime requires every accepted inner point \(x^k\) to satisfy \[\mathcal E_k(x^k)\le\varepsilon_k,\] where \(\varepsilon_k\) is an externally specified tolerance not multiplied by a current feasibility, step, or multiplier-progress measure. In the smooth unconstrained equality-constrained ALM, the canonical form is \[\|\nabla_xL_{c_k}(x^k,\lambda^k)\|\le\varepsilon_k.\] The regime is asymptotically exact when \(\varepsilon_k\to0\), and uniformly absolute when \(\varepsilon_k\equiv\bar\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Absolute accuracy compares the inner optimality residual directly with a prescribed tolerance. The threshold does not scale with the current outer step or constraint violation. If these absolute tolerances converge to zero, the inner solves become asymptotically exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal E_k(x^k)\le\varepsilon_k,\qquad \varepsilon_k\text{ independent of current outer progress measures}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For smooth unconstrained subproblems, \(\mathcal E_k(x)=\|\nabla_xL_{c_k}(x,\lambda^k)\|\).
special_cases_latex: \(\varepsilon_k=0\) gives zero-residual solves.
\(\varepsilon_k\downarrow0\) gives progressively refined absolute accuracy.
immediate_consequences_latex: The stopping threshold remains meaningful even when the current feasibility residual is zero.
boundary_notes: An absolute tolerance is sensitive to scaling of variables and objective units.
A rule proportional to \(\|h(x^k)\|\) is relative rather than purely absolute.

children.title: Relative-Accuracy Regimes
children.top_down_role: Inner accuracy scaled to current outer progress.

assumptions_latex: \(s_k\ge0\) is a declared, computable inner-solve error measure.
\(r_k\ge0\) is a declared, computable outer-progress scale.
The identity \(r_k=\|c(x^{k+1})\|\) for the multiplier-step scale assumes \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho_kc(x^{k+1})\) with \(\rho_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inner error scaled by a declared measure of current outer progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A relative-accuracy regime accepts an inner point when a declared inner error \(s_k\) satisfies \[s_k\le\eta_k r_k,\] where \(r_k\ge0\) measures current outer progress and \(\eta_k\ge0\) is a forcing parameter. Under the standard update \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho_kc(x^{k+1})\), one admissible scale is \[r_k=\frac{\|y^{k+1}-y^k\|}{\rho_k}=\|c(x^{k+1})\|.\] A uniformly relative regime bounds \(\eta_k\), while \(\eta_k\to0\) gives a strengthening relative regime. If \(r_k=0\), a purely relative rule forces \(s_k=0\); allowing nonzero error then requires an explicitly hybrid absolute-plus-relative criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative accuracy bounds a certified inner error by a forcing parameter times a declared outer-progress scale. The common multiplier-step and feasibility scales coincide only under the standard multiplier update.
knowledge_statements.title: Relative Inner-Accuracy Criterion
Relative-Accuracy Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inner error bounded relative to a computable scale measuring the current outer or proximal step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_k\ge0\) be a computable outer-progress scale, such as \(r_k=\|y^{k+1}-y^k\|/\rho_k=\|c(x^{k+1})\|\), and let \(s_k\ge0\) be a computable inner optimality residual for the current augmented subproblem. A relative-accuracy regime accepts the inner point when \[s_k\le\eta_k r_k,\qquad 0\le\eta_k\le\bar\eta<1.\] Thus the admissible inner error contracts automatically as feasibility or the multiplier step contracts. If \(r_k=0\), the criterion requires \(s_k=0\), unless an additional absolute tolerance is explicitly included.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The allowed inner optimality error is a fixed fraction of a current outer residual, so inner accuracy tightens as the outer iteration approaches feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(s_k\ge0\) is a computable inner optimality residual.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inner accuracy relative to outer progress
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal E_k(x)\) be the inner optimality residual and let \(R_k(x)\ge0\) measure current outer progress, such as \(R_k(x)=\|h(x)\|\) or \(R_k=\|\lambda^{k+1}-\lambda^k\|/c_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative deterministic stopping rule for a smooth equality-constrained ALM, with a general abstract formulation included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A relative-accuracy regime accepts \(x^k\) only if \[\mathcal E_k(x^k)\le\gamma_kR_k(x^k)\] for a prescribed factor \(\gamma_k\ge0\). A combined absolute-relative rule is \[\mathcal E_k(x^k)\le\min\{\varepsilon_k,\gamma_kR_k(x^k)\}.\] For the smooth equality-constrained augmented Lagrangian, the canonical choice is \[\|\nabla_xL_{c_k}(x^k,\lambda^k)\|\le\min\{\varepsilon_k,\gamma_k\|h(x^k)\|\}.\] Thus the permitted inner residual contracts automatically as the outer feasibility measure contracts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative accuracy scales the allowed inner optimality error by a current outer progress measure. A standard ALM rule compares the augmented-Lagrangian gradient with the constraint violation, optionally imposing an absolute cap at the same time.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Since \(\lambda^{k+1}-\lambda^k=c_kh(x^k)\), choosing \(R_k=\|h(x^k)\|\) is equivalent to scaling by \(\|\lambda^{k+1}-\lambda^k\|/c_k\).
special_cases_latex: Constant \(\gamma_k=\gamma\) gives a fixed relative factor.
If \(\gamma_k\to0\), inner error becomes negligible relative to the chosen outer residual.
immediate_consequences_latex: When \(R_k(x^k)=0\), the pure relative rule demands zero inner residual.
boundary_notes: A denominator-based ratio should not be used without specifying behavior when the outer residual vanishes.
The choice of \(R_k\) is part of the mathematical regime.

notation.meaning: Outer progress scale used to normalize inner accuracy.

children.title: Cumulative-Error Regimes
children.top_down_role: Inexactness controlled across the full outer sequence.

assumptions_latex: \(d_k\ge 0\) is a declared, certified error measure for the inner solve at iteration \(k\).

notation.meaning: certified error of the kth inner solve in the declared metric
summable upper budget for the kth error

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequence-wide inexactness control by a summable budget, independent of any particular dual sign convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cumulative-error regime declares a nonnegative inner-solve error measure \(d_k\) and accepts errors satisfying \[0\le d_k\le\varepsilon_k,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\varepsilon_k<\infty.\] Consequently the total certified error is finite and \(d_k\to0\). Canonical realizations include a subproblem objective gap or an inner optimality or proximal residual, but these realizations are not interchangeable without an additional error bound. Summability is strictly stronger than vanishing error: for example, \(d_k=1/(k+1)\) tends to zero but is not cumulative-error admissible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cumulative-error regime bounds each certified inner error by a summable budget. This forces finite total error and vanishing individual errors, while excluding vanishing but nonsummable sequences.
knowledge_statements.title: Summable Cumulative Error Budget
Cumulative-Error Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inexactness sequence constrained globally, typically by summability across all outer iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(e^{k+1}\) denote the residual in the inexact dual proximal inclusion \[e^{k+1}\in-\partial q(y^{k+1})+\rho_k^{-1}(y^{k+1}-y^k).\] A cumulative-error regime requires a nonnegative error budget \(\varepsilon_k\) satisfying \[\|e^{k+1}\|\le\varepsilon_k,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\varepsilon_k<\infty.\] Hence the total perturbation injected into the outer proximal sequence is finite. The condition implies \(\varepsilon_k\to0\), but is strictly stronger than asymptotic exactness alone; a nonsummable vanishing sequence does not satisfy this regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each inexact proximal residual is bounded by an error budget whose infinite sum is finite, limiting the total perturbation accumulated by the outer method.
assumptions_latex: \(q\) is a proper concave dual function with nonempty proximal subproblems.

notation.meaning: dual proximal residual induced by the inner solve

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(e^k\) denote an inner-solve error vector or let \(\eta_k\ge0\) bound a scalar inner residual at outer iteration \(k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic sequence-level accuracy definition. It controls the aggregate error budget rather than only each iteration separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cumulative-error regime is an inexact ALM regime for which the full outer sequence satisfies a finite aggregate error budget, canonically \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|e^k\|<\infty,\] or, when \(\|e^k\|\le\eta_k\), the sufficient prescribed condition \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\eta_k<\infty.\] A weighted cumulative regime replaces this by \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}w_k\|e^k\|<\infty\) for explicitly specified weights \(w_k>0\). The error object, norm, and weights are part of the definition and must match the inexact optimality or proximal inclusion used by the ALM formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cumulative-error control requires the total magnitude of inner inaccuracies across all outer iterations to be finite. It is stronger than merely requiring the individual errors to vanish. Weighted versions are valid only when the weights and the underlying residual are stated explicitly.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The tail budgets \(E_N=\sum_{k=N}^{\infty}\eta_k\) are finite and satisfy \(E_N\downarrow0\).
special_cases_latex: A geometric schedule \(\eta_k=\eta_0q^k\) with \(0<q<1\) is summable.
A harmonic schedule \(\eta_k=(k+1)^{-1}\) vanishes but is not summable.
immediate_consequences_latex: Summability implies \(\eta_k\to0\), so every cumulative-error regime of this form is asymptotically exact.
boundary_notes: Vanishing error alone does not imply finite cumulative error.
The supplied local source hints did not contain a directly inspectable statement of this summability definition for ALM; independent source support is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stationarity Does Not Imply Global Asymptotic Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of stationarity-based accuracy to imply global objective-value exactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\phi(x)=(x^2-1)^2\), the constant sequence \(x_k=0\) satisfies \(\nabla\phi(x_k)=0\) for every \(k\), but \[\phi(x_k)-\inf_x\phi(x)=1.\] Thus zero first-order residual does not imply asymptotically exact global minimization for nonconvex inner problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonoptimal stationary point can have zero inner stationarity residual forever while retaining a positive global objective gap.
knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity Does Not Imply Global Asymptotic Exactness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalence of Gap and Stationarity Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform unconstrained conditions under which objective-gap and gradient-residual notions agree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let every \(\phi_k:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable, \(\mu\)-strongly convex, and have an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, with fixed \(0<\mu\le L\). For \(x_k^*=\arg\min\phi_k\), \[\frac{1}{2L}\|\nabla\phi_k(x_k)\|^2\le\phi_k(x_k)-\phi_k(x_k^*)\le\frac{1}{2\mu}\|\nabla\phi_k(x_k)\|^2.\] Hence vanishing objective gaps and vanishing gradient residuals are equivalent under these uniform assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform strong convexity and smoothness make vanishing inner objective gaps equivalent to vanishing gradient residuals.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\phi_k\) is differentiable, \(\mu\)-strongly convex, and has an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient.
knowledge_statements.title: Equivalence of Gap and Stationarity Accuracy
Asymptotically Exact Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A vanishing first-order residual condition for equality-constrained augmented-Lagrangian subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed, let \(f\) and \(c\) be continuously differentiable, and define \(L_{\rho}(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}c(x)+(\rho/2)\lVert c(x)\rVert^2\). Inner minimization at outer iteration \(k\) is asymptotically exact if it returns \(x_{k+1}\in X\) satisfying
\[\operatorname{dist}\!\left(0,\nabla_x L_{\rho_k}(x_{k+1},\lambda_k)+N_X(x_{k+1})\right)\leq \varepsilon_k,\qquad \varepsilon_k\downarrow0.\]
For unconstrained inner problems, this reduces to \(\lVert\nabla_xL_{\rho_k}(x_{k+1},\lambda_k)\rVert\leq\varepsilon_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each inner solve has a stationarity residual bounded by a tolerance that converges to zero along the outer iterations.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty. At outer iteration \(k\), let \(\Phi_k:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be the augmented subproblem objective and let \(v_k:=\inf_{x\in X}\Phi_k(x)>-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is a value-gap definition for finite-dimensional, possibly nonconvex augmented subproblems. It does not require attainment of \(v_k\), differentiability, or exact minimization at any finite outer iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sequence \(\{x^{k+1}\}_{k\geq0}\subseteq X\) is an asymptotically exact minimization sequence for \(\{\Phi_k\}\) if there is a sequence \(\{\varepsilon_k\}\subseteq[0,\infty)\) such that \(\varepsilon_k\to0\) and, for every \(k\), \[0\leq \Phi_k(x^{k+1})-v_k\leq\varepsilon_k.\] Equivalently, \(\Phi_k(x^{k+1})-\inf_{x\in X}\Phi_k(x)\to0\). The definition compares each computed point with the global value of its own iteration-dependent subproblem; it does not compare values belonging to different outer iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each outer iteration, compare the computed inner point with the infimum of that iteration's augmented objective over its domain. The minimization is asymptotically exact when these nonnegative objective gaps are bounded by tolerances tending to zero. The subproblem infimum need not be attained, and no individual inner solve must be exact.
equivalent_formulations_latex: There exist \(\varepsilon_k\downarrow0\) after replacement by the monotone envelope \(\widehat\varepsilon_k:=\sup_{j\geq k}(\Phi_j(x^{j+1})-v_j)\), provided that envelope is finite.
The defining condition is \(\lim_{k\to\infty}[\Phi_k(x^{k+1})-v_k]=0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(x_k^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\Phi_k(x)\), the condition becomes \(\Phi_k(x^{k+1})-\Phi_k(x_k^\star)\leq\varepsilon_k\to0\).
Exact subproblem minimization is the special case \(\varepsilon_k=0\) for every \(k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: For any fixed \(\delta>0\), all sufficiently large \(k\) satisfy \(\Phi_k(x^{k+1})\leq v_k+\delta\).
boundary_notes: A vanishing gradient or subgradient residual is a different accuracy regime and is equivalent to a vanishing value gap only under additional regularity such as an error bound or strong convexity.
The local sources inspected describe vanishing stationarity tolerances for inexact augmented-Lagrangian minimization, but do not directly support this global value-gap definition.

children.title: Inner Solver Families
children.top_down_role: Solver families used for augmented subproblems.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal P\) be a class of subproblems \(P=(X,\Phi)\), where \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty and \(\Phi:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\). Let \(\mathcal A\) index solver architectures and let \(\eta\geq0\) be a requested inner accuracy.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition formalizes an interface shared by deterministic finite-dimensional inner solvers. It classifies solvers by the information and step mechanisms used while keeping the outer ALM independent of internal iteration details.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An inner-solver family for \(\mathcal P\) is a collection \(\{\mathcal S_{\alpha}\}_{\alpha\in\mathcal A}\) of maps which, for every admissible \((P,z^0,\eta)\), generate a finite inner sequence \(z^0,z^1,\ldots,z^J\in X\) and return \((z^J,C_P(z^J))\), where \(C_P:X\to[0,\infty]\) is a declared termination certificate and \(C_P(z^J)\leq\eta\). The family specification includes the admissible problem class, oracle used for \(\Phi\), step-generation rule, globalization rule when present, and certificate. Two members belong to distinct solver families when their permitted oracle or defining step model differs, rather than merely their numerical parameter values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inner-solver family is a parameterized collection of algorithms for augmented subproblems. Each member declares the subproblem class it accepts, the objective information it may query, its step and globalization mechanisms, and a nonnegative stopping certificate. Given admissible data and a requested tolerance, it returns an inner iterate whose declared certificate does not exceed that tolerance.
assumptions_latex: Every solver member declares a certificate \(C_P\) compatible with its admitted problem class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned point \(z^J\in X\) satisfies the family interface condition \(C_P(z^J)\leq\eta\).
special_cases_latex: A first-order family restricts its oracle to values, gradients, subgradients, projections, or proximal maps.
A second-order family permits Hessians or Hessian-vector products in its step model.
A quasi-Newton family replaces exact curvature with an updated secant metric.
immediate_consequences_latex: An outer ALM can invoke different family members while using the common pair \((z^J,C_P(z^J))\) as its inner-solve output.
boundary_notes: This interface does not assert that every member terminates on every mathematical objective; admissibility and termination guarantees must be stated separately.
No inspected source supplied a canonical definition of a solver family at this abstraction level.

notation.meaning: A member of the inner-solver family.

review_flags: The object is an interface-level taxonomy; an authoritative source supporting this exact formalization is required.

children.title: First-Order Inner Solvers
children.top_down_role: Gradient, projected, proximal, and accelerated inner-solver interfaces.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projected and Proximal Gradient Inner Iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order solution of a fixed smooth or composite augmented subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For fixed outer parameters, write the inner objective as \(F_k(x)=\phi_k(x)+h(x)\), with differentiable \(\phi_k\) and proximable \(h\). Given \(\alpha_j>0\), set
\[x^{j+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha_jh}\bigl(x^j-\alpha_j\nabla\phi_k(x^j)\bigr).
\]
For \(h=\delta_X\), this is projected gradient. Steps may use a Lipschitz-based value or backtracking, and the iteration stops when the proximal-gradient mapping meets the outer-supplied tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply projected or proximal gradient to the fixed augmented subproblem and stop using its gradient-mapping residual.
assumptions_latex: The outer multiplier and penalty remain fixed during the inner iteration.
\(h\) is proper, closed, convex, and has a computable proximal map.

notation.meaning: Smooth part of the fixed inner objective.
Convex proximable term, including an indicator of simple constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected and Proximal Gradient Inner Iteration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact first-order test for the composite inner problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\alpha>0\), define
\[G_\alpha(x)=\alpha^{-1}\left[x-\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha h}(x-\alpha\nabla\phi_k(x))\right].\]
Then
\[G_\alpha(x)=0\iff 0\in\nabla\phi_k(x)+\partial h(x).\]
For \(h=\delta_X\), this is the projected-gradient stationarity condition on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal-gradient mapping vanishes exactly at a first-order stationary point of the fixed composite subproblem.
knowledge_statements.title: Proximal-Gradient Stationarity Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-gap rates for convex composite augmented subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(\phi_k\) is convex with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, \(h\) is proper closed convex, and \(x^\star\) minimizes \(F_k\), proximal gradient with step \(1/L\) satisfies
\[F_k(x^N)-F_k(x^\star)\leq\frac{L\|x^0-x^\star\|^2}{2N}.\]
A standard accelerated proximal-gradient iteration satisfies
\[F_k(x^N)-F_k(x^\star)\leq\frac{2L\|x^0-x^\star\|^2}{(N+1)^2}.\]
If \(\phi_k\) is additionally \(\mu\)-strongly convex, proximal gradient has a geometric objective-gap rate with factor at most \(1-\mu/L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex proximal gradient has an inverse-linear objective-gap rate, acceleration gives an inverse-quadratic rate, and strong convexity yields linear convergence.
assumptions_latex: The geometric conclusion additionally assumes \(\mu\)-strong convexity of \(\phi_k\).
knowledge_statements.title: Convex and Accelerated Inner Rates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Baseline stationarity rate for a possibly nonconvex smooth augmented term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(\nabla\phi_k\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz, \(h\) is proper closed convex, and \(F_k=\phi_k+h\) is bounded below. Proximal gradient with step \(1/L\) satisfies
\[\min_{0\leq j<N}\|G_{1/L}(x^j)\|^2\leq\frac{2L(F_k(x^0)-\inf F_k)}{N}.\]
Hence an iterate with \(\|G_{1/L}\|\leq\varepsilon\) is obtained in \(O(\varepsilon^{-2})\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without convexity of the smooth augmented term, proximal gradient reaches an epsilon-stationary point in order epsilon to the minus two iterations.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Proximal-Gradient Stationarity Complexity
First-Order Inner Solvers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected-gradient interface for an augmented-Lagrangian subproblem with simple primal constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x^0\in X\), fixed outer parameters \((\lambda_k,\rho_k)\), stepsizes \(\alpha_j>0\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon_k>0\), generate
\[x^{j+1}=P_X\!\left(x^j-\alpha_j\nabla_xL_{\rho_k}(x^j,\lambda_k)\right).\]
Choose each \(\alpha_j\) by a rule ensuring sufficient decrease, or take \(0<\alpha_j<2/L_k\) when the inner gradient is \(L_k\)-Lipschitz. Stop at the first \(j\) for which \(\lVert x^j-P_X(x^j-\nabla_xL_{\rho_k}(x^j,\lambda_k))\rVert\leq\varepsilon_k\), and return \(x_{k+1}=x^j\). Proximal-gradient variants replace \(P_X\) by the relevant proximal map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply projected or proximal gradient steps to the fixed augmented-Lagrangian subproblem and stop when its gradient-mapping residual meets the outer tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(x\mapsto L_{\rho_k}(x,\lambda_k)\) is continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned point satisfies the prescribed first-order inner residual test.

notation.meaning: Augmented Lagrangian with outer parameters fixed.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: First-order solver interface for composite augmented subproblems
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and convex and let \(\Phi(x)=g(x)+r(x)\), where \(g\) is differentiable on a neighborhood of \(X\) and \(r:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, closed, and convex with \(\operatorname{dom}r\subseteq X\). For \(M\succ0\), define \(\operatorname{prox}_{r}^{M}(u):=\operatorname*{argmin}_z\{r(z)+\tfrac12\|z-u\|_M^2\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition covers smooth gradient, projected-gradient, proximal-gradient, and momentum or accelerated variants. It does not claim convexity of the smooth augmented term \(g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A first-order inner solver accesses the augmented subproblem through objective values, gradients, and any declared projection or proximal map, but not through Hessians. For a composite objective, its standard variable-metric step is a proximal-gradient step. The norm of the resulting generalized gradient mapping supplies the stopping certificate, and the inner solve ends when that norm is at most the requested tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(M_j\) is symmetric positive definite for every inner iteration \(j\).
The proximal subproblem defining \(\operatorname{prox}_{r}^{M_j}\) has a unique solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned iterate satisfies \(\|G_{M_J}(z^J)\|_{M_J^{-1}}\leq\eta\) using only the declared first-order oracle.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(G_M(z)=0\) if and only if \(0\in\nabla g(z)+\partial r(z)\).
special_cases_latex: For \(r=0\), \(G_M(z)=\nabla g(z)\) and the step is a scaled gradient step.
For \(r=\delta_X\), the proximal map is the \(M\)-metric projection onto \(X\), giving projected gradient.
An accelerated proximal-gradient member uses extrapolated oracle points but the same value-gradient-proximal information class.
immediate_consequences_latex: The certificate is meaningful for constrained and nonsmooth composite subproblems without forming a Hessian.
boundary_notes: A method using Hessian-vector products is classified here as second-order even if it never forms a dense Hessian.
For a nonconvex nonsmooth term \(r\), the proximal map can be set-valued and requires a different interface.
review_flags: The supplied source hints did not provide a locator jointly supporting the composite gradient, projected, proximal, and accelerated interface stated here.
knowledge_statements.title: First-order solver interface for composite augmented subproblems

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order certificate for projected or proximal solution of a fixed inner subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x)=\phi(x)+h(x)\), where \(\phi\) is differentiable and \(h\) is proper, closed, and convex. For \(\alpha>0\), define
\[G_\alpha(x)=\alpha^{-1}\bigl(x-\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha h}(x-\alpha\nabla\phi(x))\bigr).\]
Then \(G_\alpha(x)=0\) if and only if
\[0\in\nabla\phi(x)+\partial h(x).\]
For \(h=\delta_X\), this becomes the projected-gradient certificate for a closed convex set \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal gradient mapping vanishes exactly at a first-order stationary point of the composite inner problem.
knowledge_statements.title: Gradient-Mapping Stationarity Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Baseline objective complexity for a convex composite augmented subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=\phi+h\), where \(\phi\) is convex with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient and \(h\) is proper, closed, and convex. If \(x^\star\in\arg\min F\), proximal gradient with step \(1/L\),
\[x^{j+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{h/L}\bigl(x^j-L^{-1}\nabla\phi(x^j)\bigr),\]
satisfies
\[F(x^N)-F(x^\star)\leq \frac{L\|x^0-x^\star\|^2}{2N}.\]
Thus an inner objective gap at most \(\varepsilon\) is obtained within \(O(L\|x^0-x^\star\|^2/\varepsilon)\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex smooth-plus-proximable inner problem, proximal gradient has the standard inverse-linear objective-gap rate.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi\) is convex and has an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient.

notation.meaning: Gradient Lipschitz constant of the smooth part.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Proximal-Gradient Inner Complexity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accelerated first-order complexity for a convex composite inner subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the assumptions of convex proximal-gradient minimization, the standard Nesterov extrapolated proximal-gradient iteration can be chosen so that
\[F(x^N)-F(x^\star)\leq \frac{2L\|x^0-x^\star\|^2}{(N+1)^2}.\]
Consequently, an objective gap at most \(\varepsilon\) requires \(O(\sqrt{L/\varepsilon}\,\|x^0-x^\star\|)\) proximal-gradient evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Acceleration improves the convex inner objective-gap rate from order one over the iteration count to order one over its square.
assumptions_latex: A minimizer exists and the standard accelerated coefficients are used.
knowledge_statements.title: Accelerated Proximal-Gradient Variant

children.title: Second-Order Inner Solver Family
children.top_down_role: Second-order inner solution and globalization interfaces.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Phi:X\to\mathbb R\) be twice continuously differentiable on an open neighborhood of \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). At inner iterate \(z^j\), write \(g_j=\nabla\Phi(z^j)\) and \(H_j=\nabla^2\Phi(z^j)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition concerns deterministic smooth finite-dimensional inner minimization. It includes line-search Newton, trust-region Newton, regularized Newton, and truncated Newton implementations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A second-order inner solver is a method whose defining step uses the local quadratic model \[q_j(p)=\Phi(z^j)+g_j^Tp+\tfrac12p^TH_jp\] or the action \(v\mapsto H_jv\). It computes a trial step by approximately minimizing \(q_j\) on a declared domain, such as \(\|p\|\leq\Delta_j\), or by satisfying a regularized Newton equation \[(H_j+\sigma_jI)p_j=-g_j,\qquad \sigma_j\geq0.\] A globalization map accepts, shortens, or rejects \(p_j\) according to a line-search, trust-region, or regularization test and sets \(z^{j+1}=z^j+\alpha_jp_j\) or \(z^{j+1}=z^j+p_j\). The family is second-order because exact curvature or Hessian-vector products enter the defining model, irrespective of whether \(H_j\) is assembled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A second-order inner solver builds its step from the gradient and the exact Hessian, or from Hessian-vector products representing that Hessian. It approximately minimizes a quadratic model or solves a regularized Newton equation, then applies an explicit globalization mechanism such as a line search, trust region, or adaptive regularization before accepting the trial point.
assumptions_latex: \(\Phi\) is twice continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of the inner iterates.
Every accepted step remains in \(X\), or the quadratic model includes the constraints defining \(X\).
The globalization rule is defined whenever a trial step is produced.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each inner trial step is generated from \((g_j,H_j)\) or \((g_j,v\mapsto H_jv)\) and is accepted only through the declared globalization interface.
special_cases_latex: Pure Newton uses \(\sigma_j=0\), \(H_j\) nonsingular, and \(p_j=-H_j^{-1}g_j\).
Trust-region Newton minimizes the quadratic model over \(\|p\|\leq\Delta_j\).
Truncated Newton approximately solves the Newton system using Hessian-vector products.
immediate_consequences_latex: Matrix-free curvature products suffice for membership in the second-order family.
boundary_notes: A quasi-Newton method using only secant approximations belongs to the separate quasi-Newton family.
Positive definiteness of \(H_j\) is not part of the family definition; indefinite models require suitable globalization.

notation.meaning: Second-order Taylor model at the current inner iterate.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact, Modified, and Inexact Newton Inner Steps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Newton solution interface for one fixed smooth augmented subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \((\lambda_k,\rho_k)\), let \(g_j=\nabla_xL_{\rho_k}(x^j,\lambda_k)\), and let \(H_j=\nabla_{xx}^2L_{\rho_k}(x^j,\lambda_k)\). An exact step solves \(H_jp_j=-g_j\). An inexact step satisfies
\[\|H_jp_j+g_j\|\leq\eta_j\|g_j\|.
\]
When unmodified curvature does not yield an acceptable minimization direction, use a prescribed symmetric positive-definite modification. Pass the direction to the sibling globalization interface and stop when \(\|g_j\|\leq\varepsilon_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the fixed inner stationarity equation by exact or inexact Newton steps, modifying indefinite curvature when a minimization direction is required.
assumptions_latex: The fixed inner objective is twice continuously differentiable.
The subproblem is unconstrained or its explicit constraints have been eliminated.
A globalization and Hessian-modification policy is prescribed where needed.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact, Modified, and Inexact Newton Inner Steps

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Newton Stationarity Is Not a Minimization Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonconvex curvature boundary for unmodified inner Newton.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\phi(x)=-x^2\), Newton's equation gives \(p=-x\), so every full Newton step reaches \(x^+=0\). Although \(\nabla\phi(0)=0\), the point is a strict local maximum. Thus an inner gradient test or exact solution of the Newton equation does not certify minimization without curvature information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unmodified Newton may converge exactly to a strict maximum of a nonconvex augmented subproblem.
knowledge_statements.title: Newton Stationarity Is Not a Minimization Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact and Inexact Newton Local Rates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forcing-term characterization of local convergence on a fixed inner objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g=\nabla\phi_k\), let \(g(x^\star)=0\), and suppose \(H(x^\star)=\nabla g(x^\star)\) is nonsingular and \(H\) is locally Lipschitz. For sufficiently close iterates satisfying
\[\|H(x^j)p_j+g(x^j)\|\leq\eta_j\|g(x^j)\|,
\]
convergence is Q-linear if \(\eta_j\leq\bar\eta<1\), Q-superlinear if \(\eta_j\to0\), and Q-quadratic if \(\eta_j=O(\|g(x^j)\|)\). Exact Newton has \(\eta_j=0\) and is locally Q-quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The linear-solve forcing term determines linear, superlinear, or quadratic local convergence of the inner Newton iteration.
assumptions_latex: The inner Hessian is nonsingular at the stationary point and locally Lipschitz.
The initial iterate is sufficiently close.
The displayed relative linear-residual condition holds.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact and Inexact Newton Local Rates
Newton Inner Solvers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Damped Newton solution of a smooth augmented-Lagrangian subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \((\lambda_k,\rho_k)\) and initialize \(x^0\). At inner iteration \(j\), form \(g_j=\nabla_xL_{\rho_k}(x^j,\lambda_k)\) and \(H_j=\nabla_{xx}^2L_{\rho_k}(x^j,\lambda_k)\). Compute \(p_j\) from
\[H_jp_j=-g_j,\]
using a symmetric positive-definite modification of \(H_j\) when necessary. Select \(\alpha_j\in(0,1]\) by a globalization rule and set \(x^{j+1}=x^j+\alpha_jp_j\). Stop when \(\lVert g_j\rVert\leq\varepsilon_k\), and return \(x_{k+1}=x^j\). Near a nondegenerate local minimizer, the unmodified full Newton step is the local interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve each smooth augmented-Lagrangian subproblem by damped Newton steps, modifying curvature when needed and terminating at the requested stationarity tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The inner problem is unconstrained, or primal constraints have already been eliminated.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Newton Stationarity Does Not Imply Inner Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curvature boundary for an unmodified Newton inner solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the smooth inner objective \(\phi(x)=-x^2\), Newton's equation is \((-2)p=-(-2x)=2x\), hence \(p=-x\). From every starting point, the full Newton step reaches \(x^+=0\), where \(\nabla\phi(0)=0\), but \(0\) is a strict local maximum. Thus solving the gradient equation by unmodified Newton does not by itself ensure minimization of a nonconvex augmented subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unmodified Newton can converge in one step to a strict maximum, so an inner gradient tolerance alone does not certify local minimization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla\phi(x)=0\text{ is not a minimization certificate without curvature information}.
knowledge_statements.title: Newton Stationarity Does Not Imply Inner Minimization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-solve accuracy conditions for local inner Newton convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g(x)=\nabla\phi_k(x)\) and \(H(x)=\nabla^2\phi_k(x)\), and suppose \(H(x^\star)\) is nonsingular and locally Lipschitz near a root \(g(x^\star)=0\). If an inexact Newton step satisfies
\[\|H(x^j)p_j+g(x^j)\|\leq\eta_j\|g(x^j)\|,\qquad x^{j+1}=x^j+p_j,
\]
then sufficiently close iterates converge Q-linearly when \(\eta_j\leq\bar\eta<1\), Q-superlinearly when \(\eta_j\to0\), and Q-quadratically when \(\eta_j=O(\|g(x^j)\|)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The forcing term for the inner linear solve determines whether inexact Newton convergence is linear, superlinear, or quadratic.
assumptions_latex: The fixed inner gradient has a nonsingular locally Lipschitz Jacobian at its root.
The initial point is sufficiently close.
The displayed relative linear-residual test holds.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Newton Forcing-Term Rates

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Quadratic Convergence of Exact Inner Newton
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local rate for exact Newton solution of a fixed augmented subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x^\star\) satisfy \(
abla\phi_k(x^\star)=0\). If \(\phi_k\) is twice continuously differentiable near \(x^\star\), \(
abla^2\phi_k(x^\star)\) is nonsingular, and \(
abla^2\phi_k\) is locally Lipschitz, then for every sufficiently close \(x^0\) the full Newton iteration
\[x^{j+1}=x^j-
abla^2\phi_k(x^j)^{-1}
abla\phi_k(x^j)\]
is well defined and satisfies
\[\|x^{j+1}-x^\star\|\leq C\|x^j-x^\star\|^2.\]
If the limiting Hessian is positive definite, \(x^\star\) is a strict local minimizer of the inner objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact full Newton steps converge locally quadratically to a nondegenerate stationary point of the fixed inner objective; positive curvature identifies it as a local minimum.
assumptions_latex: The outer multiplier and penalty are fixed.
The limiting Hessian is nonsingular and locally Lipschitz.
The initial point is sufficiently close.

children.title: Trust-Region Inner Solvers

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Inner Solvers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trust-region globalization for a fixed smooth augmented-Lagrangian subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \((\lambda_k,\rho_k)\), define \(\phi_k(x)=L_{\rho_k}(x,\lambda_k)\), and initialize \(x^0\) and \(\Delta_0>0\). At inner iteration \(j\), let \(g_j=\nabla\phi_k(x^j)\), choose a symmetric Hessian model \(H_j\), and define
\[m_j(p)=\phi_k(x^j)+g_j^{\mathsf T}p+\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}H_jp.\]
Compute a step \(p_j\) satisfying \(\lVert p_j\rVert\leq\Delta_j\) and a prescribed model-decrease condition. When \(m_j(0)-m_j(p_j)>0\), form
\[r_j=\frac{\phi_k(x^j)-\phi_k(x^j+p_j)}{m_j(0)-m_j(p_j)}.\]
For a fixed \(\eta_1\in(0,1)\), set \(x^{j+1}=x^j+p_j\) if \(r_j\geq\eta_1\), and set \(x^{j+1}=x^j\) otherwise. Update \(\Delta_j\) by prescribed thresholds based on \(r_j\). Stop at an iterate \(x^j\) satisfying \(\lVert g_j\rVert\leq\varepsilon_k\), and return \(x_{k+1}=x^j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximately minimize a quadratic model of the fixed augmented-Lagrangian subproblem inside a trust region, accept a step according to actual versus predicted reduction, and stop when the inner gradient meets its tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(x\mapsto L_{\rho_k}(x,\lambda_k)\) is continuously differentiable on the relevant level set.
\(\Delta_j>0\), \(0<\eta_1<1\), and each computed step provides the prescribed positive model decrease.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When the stopping test is reached, the returned iterate satisfies \(\lVert\nabla_xL_{\rho_k}(x_{k+1},\lambda_k)\rVert\leq\varepsilon_k\).

notation.meaning: Ratio of actual reduction to predicted model reduction.

\]

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local fast regime of the exact-Hessian trust-region variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(x^\star\) is stationary, \(\nabla^2\phi_k(x^\star)\succ0\), and the Hessian is locally Lipschitz. If \(H_j=\nabla^2\phi_k(x^j)\), the unconstrained Newton step is selected whenever it lies within the radius, and highly successful steps do not shrink the radius, then sufficiently near \(x^\star\) the Newton step lies strictly inside the trust region, its reduction ratio tends to one, and it is accepted. The resulting iterates converge Q-quadratically.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a positive-definite inner minimizer, the exact-Hessian trust-region method eventually becomes the full quadratically convergent Newton method.
assumptions_latex: The exact locally Lipschitz Hessian is used.
The limiting Hessian is positive definite.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity guarantee for the fixed augmented-subproblem iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the fixed inner objective \(\phi_k\) be bounded below on the initial level set and have Lipschitz gradient there. Suppose \(\|H_j\|\leq\beta\), and each trial step satisfies a uniform fraction of Cauchy decrease,
\[m_j(0)-m_j(p_j)\geq\frac{\kappa}{2}\|g_j\|\min\left\{\frac{\|g_j\|}{1+\beta},\Delta_j\right\},
\]
with \(\kappa>0\). Under standard fixed-threshold ratio acceptance and bounded-factor radius updates, every infinite generated sequence satisfies \(\|g_j\|\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform Cauchy decrease and standard radius safeguards make the fixed inner trust-region iteration globally first-order convergent.
assumptions_latex: The inner objective is bounded below on the relevant level set and has Lipschitz gradient.
Every trial step achieves a uniform fraction of Cauchy decrease.
Acceptance thresholds and radius update factors obey the standard fixed safeguards.
knowledge_statements.title: Global First-Order Trust-Region Convergence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global First-Order Convergence under Cauchy Decrease
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global stationarity guarantee for the fixed inner trust-region iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\phi_k\) be bounded below on the initial level set with Lipschitz continuous gradient, and suppose \(\|H_j\|\leq\beta\). Assume each trust-region step gives a fixed fraction \(\kappa\in(0,1]\) of Cauchy decrease:
\[m_j(0)-m_j(p_j)\geq\frac{\kappa}{2}\|g_j\|\min\left\{\frac{\|g_j\|}{1+\beta},\Delta_j\right\}.
\]
With standard ratio-based acceptance and radius updates, every infinite sequence satisfies
\[\liminf_{j\to\infty}\|g_j\|=0.
\]
Under the usual additional rule preventing indefinite rejection at a fixed nonzero gradient, \(\|g_j\|\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trust-region method whose subproblem steps achieve uniform Cauchy decrease has globally stationary accumulation behavior on a bounded-below smooth inner objective.
assumptions_latex: The inner objective has a Lipschitz gradient and is bounded below on the relevant level set.
The model Hessians are uniformly bounded.
Steps achieve a uniform fraction of Cauchy decrease.
Standard ratio-based radius safeguards are used.
knowledge_statements.title: Global First-Order Convergence under Cauchy Decrease

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local fast convergence of the exact-Hessian trust-region variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(x^\star\) is a stationary point of the fixed inner objective, \(\nabla^2\phi_k(x^\star)\succ0\), and the Hessian is locally Lipschitz. If \(H_j=\nabla^2\phi_k(x^j)\) and the trust-region subproblem is solved so that the unconstrained Newton step is selected whenever it lies inside the radius, then for all sufficiently large \(j\) the Newton step lies strictly inside the trust region, its reduction ratio tends to one, it is accepted, and
\[\|x^{j+1}-x^\star\|\leq C\|x^j-x^\star\|^2.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a positive-definite inner minimizer, the exact-Hessian trust-region method eventually accepts interior full Newton steps and becomes quadratically convergent.
assumptions_latex: The exact Hessian is used and is locally Lipschitz.
The limiting Hessian is positive definite.
The radius update does not shrink after highly successful steps.
knowledge_statements.title: Eventual Full Newton Trust-Region Steps

knowledge_statements.title: Newton Globalization Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Line-search and trust-region interfaces for globalizing Newton-type steps on a fixed augmented-Lagrangian subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the fixed inner objective \(\phi_k(x)=L_{\rho_k}(x,\lambda_k)\), a line-search interface computes a Newton or modified-Newton descent direction \(p_j\) and chooses \(\alpha_j\in(0,1]\) until
\[\phi_k(x^j+\alpha_jp_j)\leq\phi_k(x^j)+\sigma\alpha_j\nabla\phi_k(x^j)^{\mathsf T}p_j,\]
where \(0<\sigma<1\). It then sets \(x^{j+1}=x^j+\alpha_jp_j\). Alternatively, a trust-region interface forms a quadratic Newton model and computes a step \(p_j\) subject to \(\lVert p_j\rVert\leq\Delta_j\); it accepts the trial point only when the ratio of actual to predicted reduction meets the prescribed threshold and updates \(\Delta_j\) accordingly. In either interface, terminate when the outer-supplied inner stationarity tolerance is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Globalize Newton-type inner iterations either by an Armijo line search along a descent direction or by a radius-constrained quadratic model whose trial step is tested using actual versus predicted reduction.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi_k\) is continuously differentiable and bounded below on the relevant level set.
For the line-search interface, \(p_j\) satisfies \(\nabla\phi_k(x^j)^{\mathsf T}p_j<0\).
For the trust-region interface, the computed radius-constrained step provides positive predicted model reduction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each accepted inner step satisfies the acceptance test of the selected globalization interface.

notation.meaning: Line-search direction or trust-region model step, according to the selected interface.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global stationarity and local full-step behavior for the line-search interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\phi\) be bounded below on the initial level set and have a Lipschitz gradient there. Suppose directions satisfy, for constants \(c_1,c_2>0\),
\[-
abla\phi(x^j)^{\mathsf T}p_j\geq c_1\|
abla\phi(x^j)\|^2,\qquad \|p_j\|\leq c_2\|
abla\phi(x^j)\|,
\]
and backtracking chooses an Armijo step with fixed parameters. Then \(\|
abla\phi(x^j)\|	o0\). If additionally \(p_j\) is the exact Newton direction near a limit point \(x^\star\), \(
abla^2\phi(x^\star)\succ0\), and the Hessian is locally Lipschitz, then the unit step satisfies the Armijo test for all sufficiently large \(j\), and the subsequent convergence is quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly gradient-related Newton-type directions with Armijo backtracking drive the inner gradient to zero; near a positive-definite solution, full Newton steps are eventually accepted and converge quadratically.

knowledge_statements.title: Quasi-Newton Inner Solvers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Secant approximation of augmented-Lagrangian curvature within a fixed outer iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \((\lambda_k,\rho_k)\), define \(\phi_k(x)=L_{\rho_k}(x,\lambda_k)\), and initialize \(x^0\) and a symmetric positive-definite matrix \(B_0\). At iteration \(j\), let \(g_j=\nabla\phi_k(x^j)\), solve \(B_jp_j=-g_j\), globalize the step, and set \(x^{j+1}=x^j+\alpha_jp_j\). With \(s_j=x^{j+1}-x^j\) and \(y_j=g_{j+1}-g_j\), perform the BFGS update
\[B_{j+1}=B_j-\frac{B_js_js_j^{\mathsf T}B_j}{s_j^{\mathsf T}B_js_j}+\frac{y_jy_j^{\mathsf T}}{y_j^{\mathsf T}s_j}\]
when \(y_j^{\mathsf T}s_j>0\), using a prescribed damped or skipped update otherwise. Stop when \(\lVert g_j\rVert\leq\varepsilon_k\), and return \(x_{k+1}=x^j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate the fixed augmented-Lagrangian objective's curvature by safeguarded BFGS secant updates, globalize each step, and stop at the required inner stationarity tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The step-globalization and update-safeguard rules are prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(B_j\) is symmetric positive definite and \(y_j^{\mathsf T}s_j>0\), then the displayed BFGS update is symmetric positive definite and satisfies \(B_{j+1}s_j=y_j\).

abla\phi_{k+1}(x)-y=\Delta_k(x+s)-\Delta_k(x).
\]
Thus a pair formed for \(\phi_k\) is not generally a secant pair for \(\phi_{k+1}\); uncontrolled reuse can also lose positive curvature and does not inherit fixed-objective superlinear theory.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing ALM outer parameters generally invalidates the exact secant interpretation of stored inner curvature pairs.
assumptions_latex: The multiplier or penalty may change between the two inner objectives.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Cross-outer pair reuse requires an explicit reset, damping, or change-control rule.}

notation.meaning: Change in the inner gradient caused by the outer update.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Outer Secant-Pair Mismatch

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local rate for BFGS on one fixed smooth augmented subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x^\star\) minimize the fixed \(\phi_k\). Suppose \(\phi_k\) is twice continuously differentiable near \(x^\star\), its Hessian is locally Lipschitz, and \(\nabla^2\phi_k(x^\star)\succ0\). If BFGS iterates converge to \(x^\star\), unit steps are eventually accepted, and
\[\frac{\|(B_j-\nabla^2\phi_k(x^\star))s_j\|}{\|s_j\|}\to0,
\]
then \(\|x^{j+1}-x^\star\|/\|x^j-x^\star\|\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Dennis–Moré condition and eventual unit steps give local Q-superlinear BFGS convergence on a fixed strongly convex local model.
assumptions_latex: The limiting Hessian is positive definite and locally Lipschitz.
The iterates converge, unit steps are eventually accepted, and the Dennis–Moré condition holds.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Superlinear BFGS Inner Convergence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Secant-metric solver for an augmented subproblem
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Phi:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable. For successive inner iterates define \(s_j=z^{j+1}-z^j\) and \(y_j=\nabla\Phi(z^{j+1})-\nabla\Phi(z^j)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition covers smooth unconstrained augmented subproblems and line-search or trust-region variable-metric implementations. Limited-memory variants are included through implicit metric representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A quasi-Newton inner solver maintains a symmetric matrix \(B_j\) approximating \(
abla^2\Phi(z^j)\), or an inverse approximation \(D_j\), and computes a trial direction from \[B_jp_j=-
abla\Phi(z^j)\qquad	ext{or}\qquad p_j=-D_j
abla\Phi(z^j).\] After an accepted displacement, the metric is updated from \((s_j,y_j)\) so that the secant relation \[B_{j+1}s_j=y_j\qquad	ext{or}\qquad D_{j+1}y_j=s_j\] holds whenever the update is accepted. A line search, trust region, damping, or update-skipping rule controls descent and metric definiteness. The method treats augmented curvature through secant information rather than a newly evaluated exact Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quasi-Newton inner solver replaces the exact Hessian of the augmented objective with a symmetric variable metric. Its direction solves the corresponding approximate Newton system. After an accepted step, gradient differences and displacements update the metric to satisfy a secant equation, subject to the method's damping, safeguarding, or update-skipping rule.
assumptions_latex: \(\Phi\) is continuously differentiable at all inner iterates.
The accepted update has well-defined vectors \(s_j\) and \(y_j\).
When positive definiteness is required, the update enforces or tests an appropriate curvature condition such as \(s_j^Ty_j>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inner direction uses a secant curvature approximation and each accepted metric update satisfies the declared secant relation.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The inverse and direct secant relations are equivalent when \(B_{j+1}=D_{j+1}^{-1}\) is nonsingular.
special_cases_latex: BFGS and DFP are full-memory secant updates.
Limited-memory BFGS stores a finite collection of recent \((s_j,y_j)\) pairs and applies \(D_j\) implicitly.
immediate_consequences_latex: No exact augmented-objective Hessian need be formed.
An inverse approximation can also estimate curvature entering a multiplier-space second-order update.
boundary_notes: The secant equation alone does not guarantee global convergence or positive definiteness.
If \(y_j\) is formed from a changing outer subproblem rather than one fixed inner objective, additional consistency conditions are needed.

notation.meaning: Direct quasi-Newton approximation to augmented curvature.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Outer-Parameter Changes Break the Inner Secant Relation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on carrying curvature pairs between changing ALM subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\phi_k(x)=L_{ho_k}(x,\lambda_k)\). A pair formed at outer iteration \(k\),
\[y=
abla\phi_k(x+s)-
abla\phi_k(x),\]
satisfies the secant relation for \(\phi_k\), not generally for \(\phi_{k+1}\). Indeed,
\[
abla\phi_{k+1}(x+s)-
abla\phi_{k+1}(x)-y
=\Delta_k(x+s)-\Delta_k(x),\]
where \(\Delta_k=
abla\phi_{k+1}-
abla\phi_k\). Unless this difference vanishes or is controlled, reusing the pair can violate positive curvature and invalidate fixed-objective superlinear theory.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A curvature pair generated for one multiplier and penalty generally is not a secant pair for the next augmented subproblem.
assumptions_latex: The multiplier or penalty may change between outer iterations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Uncontrolled cross-outer reuse of secant pairs has no exact secant guarantee.}

notation.meaning: Change in inner gradients caused by the outer-parameter update.
