knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partial Elimination by a Basic Constraint Block
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implicit null-space reduction without constructing a general basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Partition \(A=[A_B\ A_N]\) and \(p=(p_B,p_N)\), with square nonsingular \(A_B\). The constraint equation gives
\[p_B=-A_B^{-1}(r+A_Np_N).
\]
Substitution into the quadratic model produces a reduced problem in \(p_N\); solving it and applying the displayed recovery equation yields the full feasible step. This is the null-space representation with
\[Z=\begin{bmatrix}-A_B^{-1}A_N\\I\end{bmatrix}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular basic constraint block permits direct elimination of dependent step variables and an implicit null-space solve.
assumptions_latex: A square nonsingular block \(A_B\) is available.
The quadratic model is expressed in the conforming variable partition.

notation.meaning: Independent reduced variables in this partition.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial Elimination by a Basic Constraint Block

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity and minimization tests for the reduced quadratic model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume \(A\) has full row rank. A feasible \(p\) is stationary if and only if
\[Z^{\mathsf T}(g+Hp)=0,
\]
equivalently if and only if there is a unique \(\nu\) with \(Hp+g+A^{\mathsf T}\nu=0\). If \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\succ0\), the stationary step is the unique global minimizer. If \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\) has a negative eigenvalue, the quadratic model is unbounded below along a feasible tangent ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced-gradient vanishing is equivalent to full KKT stationarity; reduced curvature classifies uniqueness or exposes unbounded negative curvature.

notation.meaning: Multiplier for the explicit linear constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced KKT and Curvature Certificates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of primal reduction and multiplier recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(A\) is rank deficient but \(-r\in\operatorname{range}(A)\), a null-space basis still parameterizes every feasible step, but a multiplier in \(Hp+g+A^{\mathsf T}\nu=0\) need not be unique. If \(-r\notin\operatorname{range}(A)\), no particular feasible step exists and the stated reduction cannot be formed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consistency is required for primal reduction, whereas full row rank is required for the usual multiplier-uniqueness claim.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: -r\in\operatorname{range}(A)\ \text{controls feasibility; full row rank controls multiplier uniqueness}.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank and Consistency Boundaries

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal-plus-tangent reduction of an equality-constrained quadratic inner model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[\min_p\ g^{\mathsf T}p+\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}Hp\quad\text{s.t. }Ap=-r.
\]
If \(p_N\) satisfies \(Ap_N=-r\) and the full-column-rank matrix \(Z\) spans \(\ker A\), every feasible step has the unique form \(p=p_N+Zq\). The reduced problem is
\[\min_q\ (Z^{\mathsf T}(g+Hp_N))^{\mathsf T}q+\tfrac12q^{\mathsf T}(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ)q.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A particular constraint-correcting step plus null-space coordinates converts the constrained quadratic model into an unconstrained reduced-Hessian problem.
assumptions_latex: The affine step equations are consistent.
The columns of \(Z\) form a basis of \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p=p_N+Zq\ \text{gives a one-to-one parameterization of feasible steps}.
knowledge_statements.title: Null-Space Reduced Inner Model
Reduced-Space Inner Solvers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Null-space reduction of equality-constrained quadratic inner models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the quadratic inner model
\[\min_p\; g^{\mathsf T}p+\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}Hp\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ap=-r,\]
where \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) has full row rank. Let \(Z\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times(n-m)}\) satisfy \(AZ=0\) and have full column rank, and choose \(p_N\) with \(Ap_N=-r\). Every feasible step has the unique form \(p=p_N+Zq\), and the model reduces to
\[\min_q\;(Z^{\mathsf T}(g+Hp_N))^{\mathsf T}q+\tfrac12q^{\mathsf T}(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ)q.\]
After solving for \(q\), recover the full inner step as \(p=p_N+Zq\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent every linearized-feasible step by a particular normal step plus a null-space step, then solve the smaller reduced-Hessian problem.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) is a full-column-rank basis matrix for \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constrained quadratic model is equivalent to the displayed unconstrained reduced problem in \(q\).

notation.meaning: Null-space basis for the linearized constraints.
Particular step satisfying the linearized constraints.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Null-space reduced solver for a partially constrained augmented subproblem
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider minimizing a smooth augmented objective \(\Phi:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) while retaining constraints \(a(x)=0\), where \(a:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\) is differentiable and \(A(x):=\nabla a(x)^T\) has full row rank near the inner iterates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition is local and finite-dimensional. It covers null-space, reduced-Hessian, and partial-elimination architectures for augmented subproblems with explicitly retained constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At an inner iterate \(z\), a reduced-space solver selects \(Z(z)\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-q)}\) with full column rank and \[A(z)Z(z)=0.\] It decomposes a trial step as \(p=p_N+Z(z)p_R\), where the normal component \(p_N\) addresses the linearized retained constraints and the reduced component \(p_R\) is computed in \(\mathbb R^{n-q}\). For a curvature model \(H\), the reduced model uses \[g_R=Z^T\nabla\Phi(z),\qquad H_R=Z^THZ,\] and determines \(p_R\) from a reduced gradient, Newton, quasi-Newton, or trust-region subproblem. A partial-elimination realization is equivalent at the interface level when dependent variables are locally expressed as functions of free variables and the inner objective is minimized over those free variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduced-space inner solver preserves explicitly retained constraints by splitting each step into a normal component and a component in the null space of the linearized constraints. Optimization occurs in null-space coordinates using the reduced gradient and reduced curvature. Local elimination of dependent variables is another realization of the same reduced-coordinate architecture.
assumptions_latex: \(A(z)\) has full row rank, so a full-column-rank null-space basis \(Z(z)\) exists.
The normal step is chosen so that \(A(z)p_N=-a(z)\) exactly or to the declared normal-step tolerance.
The reduced subproblem is well-defined in \(\mathbb R^{n-q}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The tangential component satisfies \(A(z)Z(z)p_R=0\), and its optimization model is expressed through \((Z^T\nabla\Phi(z),Z^THZ)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: A local variable elimination \(x=\chi(u)\) with \(a(\chi(u))=0\) yields the reduced objective \(u\mapsto\Phi(\chi(u))\).
special_cases_latex: If \(q=0\), then \(Z=I\) and the reduced solver is an ordinary full-space solver.
A matrix-free implementation applies \(H_Rv=Z^TH(Zv)\) without assembling \(H_R\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The reduced linear-algebra dimension is \(n-q\).
Tangential reduced steps preserve the linearized retained constraints.
boundary_notes: The definition does not cover rank-deficient retained constraints without a generalized null-space construction.
Partial elimination of penalized constraints is different from retaining those constraints explicitly.

notation.meaning: Basis for the null space of the retained-constraint Jacobian.

review_flags: The inspected partial-elimination source did not directly state the combined null-space and reduced-Hessian definition used here.
knowledge_statements.title: Null-space reduced solver for a partially constrained augmented subproblem

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of uniqueness claims when the explicit constraint Jacobian lacks full row rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(A\) is rank deficient, a null-space basis still parameterizes feasible displacements whenever \(Ap=-r\) is consistent, but the constraint multiplier solving \(Hp+g+A^{\mathsf T}\nu=0\) need not be unique. If \(-r\notin\operatorname{range}(A)\), no particular feasible step exists and the reduced parameterization of the stated constrained model cannot be formed. Thus full row rank is unnecessary for primal null-space reduction itself but is necessary for the usual uniqueness claim for multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank deficiency does not prevent a consistent primal null-space reduction, but it destroys multiplier uniqueness; inconsistency prevents the reduction entirely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Consistency controls primal parameterization; full row rank controls multiplier uniqueness.}

notation.meaning: Range of the explicit linearized constraint operator.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Deficient Reduction Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Safeguarded outer control system for equality-constrained ALM
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(\min\{f(x):h(x)=0\}\), let \(L_\rho(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^Th(x)+\tfrac\rho2\|h(x)\|^2\). At outer iteration \(k\), an inner solver returns \(x^{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This deterministic finite-dimensional definition coordinates multiplier protection, progress-based penalty management, inner accuracy, and termination. It is an outer control interface rather than an inner minimization method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An outer-iteration safeguard system is a tuple \(\mathfrak S=(\mathcal M,S_\lambda,U_\rho,U_\eta,T)\), where \(\mathcal M\subset\mathbb R^m\) is a prescribed bounded multiplier region, \(S_\lambda:\mathbb R^m\to\mathcal M\) is a safeguard map, \(U_\rho\) updates the positive penalty, \(U_\eta\) updates the inner tolerance, and \(T\) is a primal-dual stopping predicate. With \(\widehat\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\rho_kh(x^{k+1})\), the controlled update has the form \[\lambda^{k+1}=S_\lambda(\widehat\lambda^{k+1}),\qquad \rho_{k+1}=U_\rho(\rho_k,r_k,r_{k-1}),\qquad \eta_{k+1}=U_\eta(\eta_k,r_k),\] where \(r_k\) is a declared progress residual. The outer process stops exactly when \(T(x^{k+1},\lambda^{k+1};\epsilon)=\mathrm{true}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An outer safeguard system consists of a bounded admissible multiplier region, a rule that safeguards tentative multiplier updates, a progress-dependent penalty rule, an inner-tolerance rule, and a primal-dual stopping predicate. These maps jointly transform the current residual information into the next multiplier, penalty, tolerance, or a termination decision.
assumptions_latex: The safeguard map has range contained in the bounded set \(\mathcal M\).
The progress residual \(r_k\geq0\) and all update maps are defined on the states they receive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every controlled state satisfies \(\lambda^{k+1}\in\mathcal M\), \(\rho_{k+1}>0\), and either proceeds with a declared next inner tolerance or terminates through \(T\).
special_cases_latex: A rejection safeguard keeps \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k\) when the tentative update leaves \(\mathcal M\).
A progress test increases \(\rho_k\) only when feasibility fails to contract by a prescribed factor.
immediate_consequences_latex: Boundedness of safeguarded multiplier estimates is enforced by construction.
Penalty growth can be decoupled from iterations exhibiting satisfactory feasibility progress.
boundary_notes: The definition does not itself guarantee convergence; the safeguard region and update maps must satisfy the hypotheses of a convergence result.
Projection, clipping, and rejection are different safeguard realizations.

children.top_down_role: Protective treatment of multiplier estimates in practical outer iterations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exclusion Bias of a Fixed Safeguard
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary containment condition for a fixed multiplier safeguard.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a fixed closed safeguard set \(Y\) excludes a target multiplier \(\lambda_*\), then every safeguarded sequence \(\lambda_k\in Y\) satisfies \[\|\lambda_k-\lambda_*\|_2\ge\operatorname{dist}(\lambda_*,Y)>0.\] Thus convergence to \(\lambda_*\) is impossible; an adaptive safeguard must eventually cease excluding it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed safeguard that excludes the correct multiplier makes convergence to that multiplier impossible.

notation.meaning: target multiplier excluded by the safeguard

knowledge_statements.title: Exclusion Bias of a Fixed Safeguard

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Eventual Inactivity of a Valid Multiplier Safeguard
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient containment condition for a fixed or expanding projection safeguard to become inactive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\lambda_{k+1}=P_{Y_k}(\widehat\lambda_{k+1})\). If \(\widehat\lambda_{k+1}\to\lambda_*\) and there exist \(\delta>0\) and \(K\) such that \(B(\lambda_*,\delta)\subseteq Y_k\) for every \(k\ge K\), then \(\widehat\lambda_{k+1}\in Y_k\) eventually and hence \(\lambda_{k+1}=\widehat\lambda_{k+1}\) eventually.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projection safeguard becomes permanently inactive when its sets eventually contain a neighborhood of the limiting raw multiplier.
assumptions_latex: Each \(Y_k\) is nonempty and closed so the displayed projection is defined; convexity ensures uniqueness.
There exist \(\delta>0\) and \(K\) with \(B(\lambda_*,\delta)\subseteq Y_k\) for all \(k\ge K\).
knowledge_statements.title: Eventual Inactivity of a Valid Multiplier Safeguard

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete expanding safeguard for a convergent raw multiplier sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y_k=[-R_k,R_k]^m\), where \(R_k\to\infty\), and set \(\lambda_{k+1}=P_{Y_k}(\widehat\lambda_{k+1})\). If \(\widehat\lambda_{k+1}\to\lambda_*\in\mathbb R^m\), then \(\widehat\lambda_{k+1}\in Y_k\) and \(\lambda_{k+1}=\widehat\lambda_{k+1}\) for all sufficiently large \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection onto boxes with diverging radii eventually leaves every convergent raw multiplier sequence unchanged.
knowledge_statements.title: Eventual Inactivity of Expanding-Box Safeguards

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projected Multiplier Safeguard with Expanding Boxes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-multiplier safeguard with a precise adaptive nonexclusion policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_{k+1}\), \(\lambda_k\), and \(\rho_k>0\), form
\[
\widehat\lambda_{k+1}=\lambda_k+\rho_k c(x_{k+1}).
\]
Choose prescribed radii \(0<R_k\uparrow\infty\), set \(Y_k=[-R_k,R_k]^m\), and define
\[
\lambda_{k+1}=P_{Y_k}(\widehat\lambda_{k+1}).
\]
Use \(\lambda_{k+1}\) in the next augmented-Lagrangian subproblem. Componentwise,
\[
(\lambda_{k+1})_i=\min\{R_k,\max\{-R_k,(\widehat\lambda_{k+1})_i\}\}.
\]
Each accepted estimate is bounded by the current radius and every finite target multiplier is eventually contained, although the diverging radii do not by themselves make the entire multiplier sequence bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project each equality-multiplier estimate onto a box with diverging prescribed radius, bounding each accepted update without permanently excluding any finite multiplier.
assumptions_latex: \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is the equality residual.
\(0<R_k\uparrow\infty\) is prescribed independently of the projection calculation.

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the safeguard box

knowledge_statements.title: Projected Multiplier Safeguard with Expanding Boxes

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convergence and Rate Inheritance after Safeguard Inactivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional preservation of an underlying ALM result once the safeguard stops modifying updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a safeguarded ALM with \(\lambda_{k+1}=P_{Y_k}(\widehat\lambda_{k+1})\). Suppose there is \(K\) such that \(\widehat\lambda_{k+1}\in Y_k\) for every \(k\ge K\), and the corresponding unsafeguarded ALM, initialized at the iteration-\(K\) state, satisfies a stated convergence theorem with limit \((x_*,\lambda_*)\) and asymptotic rate class \(\mathcal R\). If all other updates coincide, the safeguarded and unsafeguarded iterations have identical tails and hence the safeguarded iteration has the same limit and asymptotic rate class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Once projection is permanently inactive, the safeguarded ALM is identical to its underlying ALM and inherits every applicable tail convergence and rate result.
assumptions_latex: All primal, penalty, and acceptance updates other than multiplier projection coincide with the specified unsafeguarded ALM.
The underlying ALM theorem applies from the iteration-K state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x_k,\lambda_k)\to(x_*,\lambda_*)\) with the same tail rate class \(\mathcal R\) as the underlying unsafeguarded ALM.

notation.meaning: asymptotic rate class supplied by the underlying ALM theorem

knowledge_statements.title: Convergence and Rate Inheritance after Safeguard Inactivity
Multiplier Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection safeguard for equality-constraint multiplier estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Y=[\ell,u]\subset\mathbb{R}^m\) be a nonempty bounded box, with componentwise bounds \(\ell_i<u_i\). Given \(x_{k+1}\), \(\lambda_k\), and \(\rho_k>0\), form the raw multiplier estimate
\[\widehat\lambda_{k+1}=\lambda_k+\rho_k c(x_{k+1}),\]
and set
\[\lambda_{k+1}=P_Y(\widehat\lambda_{k+1}).\]
The projected multiplier is used in the next augmented-Lagrangian subproblem. The bounds may be fixed or enlarged by a prescribed outer rule, but they are not altered during the projection itself. This safeguard prevents unbounded multiplier estimates without changing any raw estimate already lying in \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project each raw multiplier update onto a prescribed bounded box, leaving estimates inside the box unchanged and preventing uncontrolled dual growth.
assumptions_latex: \(Y=[\ell,u]\) is a nonempty closed bounded box.

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the safeguard box.

review_flags: no supplied locator identifies this projection safeguard or its intended bound-update policy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Projection onto a bounded box has the stated elementary consequences, but no source supports this particular multiplier safeguard, its use in the next ALM subproblem, or the proposed bound-enlargement policy.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic metric property of convex projection proposed for a multiplier safeguard.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty closed convex set \(Y\), \(\|P_Y(a)-P_Y(b)\|_2^2\le\langle P_Y(a)-P_Y(b),a-b\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection onto a closed convex set is firmly nonexpansive.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonexpansiveness of Multiplier Projection

Penalty updates and stopping tests are excluded to siblings; generic firm nonexpansiveness is deferred to convex projection theory. Because the safeguard algorithm itself remains only in a deferred seed, expansion is required.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For an equality-constrained ALM, let \(\widehat\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\rho_kh(x^{k+1})\) be the tentative multiplier update, with \(\rho_k>0\). Let \(\mathcal M\subset\mathbb R^m\) be a prescribed nonempty bounded set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition treats protective multiplier handling in deterministic outer iterations. The safeguard may reject or map a tentative update, but its essential property is bounded range.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A multiplier safeguard is a map \(S_{\mathcal M}:\mathbb R^m\to\mathcal M\) satisfying \(S_{\mathcal M}(\lambda)=\lambda\) for admissible \(\lambda\) in a declared invariant subset of \(\mathcal M\). The safeguarded ALM update is \[\lambda^{k+1}=S_{\mathcal M}\!\left(\lambda^k+\rho_kh(x^{k+1})\right).\] A rejection safeguard is defined by \[S_{\mathcal M}(u;\lambda^k)=\begin{cases}u,&u\in\mathcal M,\\ \lambda^k,&u\notin\mathcal M,\end{cases}\] while a projection safeguard uses \(S_{\mathcal M}(u)=\Pi_{\mathcal M}(u)\) when \(\mathcal M\) is closed and convex. In either realization, the defining invariant is \(\lambda^{k+1}\in\mathcal M\) for every \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiplier safeguard maps every tentative multiplier update into a prescribed bounded admissible region. It may accept admissible updates and reject the others by retaining the previous multiplier, or it may project onto a closed convex region. In all cases, the multiplier sequence remains in the safeguard region.
assumptions_latex: The current multiplier belongs to \(\mathcal M\).
For the projection realization, \(\mathcal M\) is also closed and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda^{k+1}\in\mathcal M\) for every safeguarded outer iteration, hence \(\{\lambda^k\}\) is bounded.

Update rejection leaves \(\lambda^k\) unchanged whenever \(\widehat\lambda^{k+1}\notin\mathcal M\).

The bounded-multiplier hypothesis used in local ALM convergence analysis holds by construction.

children.title: Penalty-Update Controls
children.top_down_role: Progress-based and safeguarded penalty-management families.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite escalation count for a capped multiplicative penalty rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(0<\rho_0\le\rho_{\max}\), every strict increase is \(\rho^+=\min\{\gamma\rho,\rho_{\max}\}\) with \(\gamma>1\), and all other updates retain \(\rho\). Then \(\rho_k\) is nondecreasing, remains in \([\rho_0,\rho_{\max}]\), and increases strictly at most \[\left\lceil\frac{\log(\rho_{\max}/\rho_0)}{\log\gamma}\right\rceil\] times.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A correctly initialized capped multiplicative penalty rule can increase only logarithmically many times before saturation.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Capped Penalty Escalation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Penalty-Cap Stagnation Is Not an Infeasibility Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interpretation boundary for repeated failure at the maximum allowed penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\rho_k=\rho_{\max}<\infty\) repeatedly while the measured violation does not approach zero, the control has exhausted its permitted response but has not certified infeasibility. The observation is also compatible with inadequate inner solves, poor multiplier estimates, an unsuitable progress measure, or a cap below that needed by the local regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Persistent violation at the penalty cap is an algorithmic failure diagnostic, not an infeasibility certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho_k=\rho_{\max}<\infty\) on an infinite set of iterations.
The measured constraint violation is bounded away from zero there.
knowledge_statements.title: Penalty-Cap Stagnation Is Not an Infeasibility Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step and windowed variants of a capped monotone penalty controller.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(0<\rho_0\le\rho_{\max}\), \(\gamma>1\), \(q\in\mathbb N\), and \(\tau\in(0,1)\). Once \(k+1\ge q\), set \[\rho_{k+1}=\begin{cases}\rho_k,&v_{k+1}\le\tau v_{k+1-q},\\\min\{\gamma\rho_k,\rho_{\max}\},&v_{k+1}>\tau v_{k+1-q}.\end{cases}\] Retain \(\rho_k\) before a complete window is available. The choice \(q=1\) is the canonical one-step retain-or-increase rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retain the penalty after sufficient feasibility contraction over a declared window; otherwise apply a capped multiplicative increase.
knowledge_statements.title: Windowed Feasibility-Progress Penalty Control
Penalty-Update Controls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility-progress rule for safeguarded penalty growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose \(\rho_0>0\), a growth factor \(\gamma>1\), a required progress factor \(\tau\in(0,1)\), and bounds \(0<\rho_{\min}\leq\rho_{max}<\infty\). Let \(v_k=\lVert c(x_k)\rVert\). After computing \(x_{k+1}\), update
\[\rho_{k+1}=\begin{cases}
\max\{\rho_{\min},\rho_k\},&v_{k+1}\leq\tau v_k,\\
\min\{\gamma\rho_k,\rho_{max}\},&v_{k+1}>\tau v_k.
\end{cases}\]
Thus the penalty remains unchanged when feasibility improves sufficiently and increases only after inadequate progress. The caps prevent illegal or excessive penalty values; a practical implementation reports failure if \(\rho_k=\rho_{max}\) repeatedly without feasibility improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keep the penalty after sufficient feasibility reduction; otherwise increase it by a bounded factor and flag persistent failure at the cap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{k+1}\in[\rho_{\min},\rho_{max}]\), and penalty growth occurs only when \(v_{k+1}>\tau v_k\).
review_flags: no supplied locator supports the selected progress test, caps, or failure policy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the selected feasibility-progress rule, caps, or failure policy. In addition, the stated assumption rho_0>0 does not ensure rho_0 lies in the declared interval, so the claimed bounded invariant need not hold under the displayed sufficient-progress branch.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(r_k:=\|h(x^{k+1})\|\) measure equality-constraint violation after the kth augmented subproblem. Let \(\rho_k>0\), choose a required contraction factor \(\gamma\in(0,1)\), and choose an increase factor \(\beta>1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is the standard two-branch progress rule for scalar quadratic-augmentation parameters. Componentwise penalties are a related specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A progress-based penalty-update control is the map \[\rho_{k+1}=\begin{cases}\rho_k,&r_k\leq\gamma r_{k-1},\\ \beta\rho_k,&r_k>\gamma r_{k-1}.\end{cases}\] Thus the penalty is retained when the declared feasibility residual contracts sufficiently and is increased only when the contraction test fails. A safeguarded variant additionally imposes \(0<\rho_{\min}\leq\rho_k\leq\rho_{\max}\leq+\infty\) and replaces the second branch by \(\min\{\beta\rho_k,\rho_{\max}\}\). The defining information is the current penalty and a comparison of consecutive feasibility residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A progress-based penalty control keeps the current penalty when constraint violation has decreased by at least a prescribed factor. Otherwise it multiplies the penalty by a factor greater than one. Optional lower and upper safeguards restrict the admissible penalty interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{k+1}\geq\rho_k>0\), with strict increase precisely when the progress test fails and the upper safeguard is inactive.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The failure branch is selected when \(r_k/r_{k-1}>\gamma\) for \(r_{k-1}>0\).
special_cases_latex: With \(\rho_{\max}=+\infty\), the penalty is nondecreasing and uncapped.
Separate penalties \(\rho_{i,k}\) may be increased only for constraints whose componentwise violations fail their progress tests.
immediate_consequences_latex: A successful feasibility reduction does not worsen penalty-induced conditioning at the next outer iteration.
Repeated failed progress tests produce geometric penalty growth until a cap is reached.
boundary_notes: When \(r_{k-1}=0\), the ratio form is undefined, but the displayed inequality remains meaningful.
The update rule alone does not ensure that the inner subproblem is solved accurately enough for the residual comparison to be reliable.

notation.meaning: Feasibility residual used by the progress test.

children.title: Primal–Dual Stopping Controls
children.top_down_role: Termination interfaces coordinating feasibility, stationarity, and complementarity.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Penalty-normalized raw multiplier increment as an equality-feasibility stopping quantity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the raw equality-multiplier update \(\widehat\lambda_{k+1}=\lambda_k+\rho_k c(x_{k+1})\), \(\rho_k>0\), \[\|c(x_{k+1})\|=\frac{\|\widehat\lambda_{k+1}-\lambda_k\|}{\rho_k}.\] Thus \(\|c(x_{k+1})\|\le\varepsilon_p\) is equivalent to \(\|\widehat\lambda_{k+1}-\lambda_k\|\le\rho_k\varepsilon_p\). The identity generally fails for a projected multiplier increment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a raw ALM update, equality violation equals the multiplier increment divided by the penalty; projection or omission of that normalization destroys the equivalence.
knowledge_statements.title: Penalty-Normalized Multiplier-Increment Test
Primal–Dual Stopping Controls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate KKT termination certificate for smooth nonlinear programs with equalities and inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[\min_x f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad c(x)=0,\qquad g(x)\leq0,\]
a tuple \((x,\lambda,\mu)\) is an \((\varepsilon_d,\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_c)\)-stopping certificate if \(\mu\geq0\) and
\[\left\lVert\nabla f(x)+J_c(x)^{\mathsf T}\lambda+J_g(x)^{\mathsf T}\mu\right\rVert\leq\varepsilon_d,\]
\[\lVert c(x)\rVert\leq\varepsilon_p,\qquad \lVert[g(x)]_+\rVert\leq\varepsilon_p,\qquad \lVert\mu\odot g(x)\rVert\leq\varepsilon_c.\]
An outer ALM iteration may terminate only when all displayed tests hold, thereby coordinating stationarity, primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Terminate only when approximate KKT stationarity, primal feasibility, nonnegative inequality multipliers, and complementarity all meet their assigned tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed residuals provide a directly checkable approximate KKT termination certificate.

notation.meaning: Componentwise positive part of the inequality residual.

review_flags: no supplied locator specifically supports this combined approximate-KKT stopping convention

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual collection is a plausible approximate-KKT certificate and the certificate kind fits the leaf, but no citation supports this exact combination of norms, tolerances, exact multiplier nonnegativity, and complementarity convention as an ALM stopping control.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\leq0\), with differentiable data, equality multiplier \(\lambda\), inequality multiplier \(\mu\geq0\), and Lagrangian \(\mathcal L(x,\lambda,\mu)=f(x)+\lambda^Th(x)+\mu^Tg(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition gives an absolute-residual stopping interface for smooth finite-dimensional nonlinear programming. Scaling or relative tolerances require an explicitly modified residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the stationarity, primal-feasibility, dual-feasibility, and complementarity residuals by \[r_s=\|\nabla_x\mathcal L(x,\lambda,\mu)\|,\quad r_p=\max\{\|h(x)\|,\|[g(x)]_+\|\},\] \[r_d=\|[-\mu]_+\|,\qquad r_c=\|\mu\odot g(x)\|.\] Given tolerances \(\epsilon_s,\epsilon_p,\epsilon_d,\epsilon_c\geq0\), a primal–dual stopping control accepts \((x,\lambda,\mu)\) exactly when \[r_s\leq\epsilon_s,\quad r_p\leq\epsilon_p,\quad r_d\leq\epsilon_d,\quad r_c\leq\epsilon_c.\] A single-tolerance implementation uses \(\max\{r_s,r_p,r_d,r_c\}\leq\epsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-dual stopping control evaluates four parts of the KKT system: stationarity, primal feasibility, nonnegativity of inequality multipliers, and complementarity. It terminates only when every residual is below its assigned tolerance, or equivalently when their maximum is below one common tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(f,h,g\) are differentiable at the candidate point.
The norms used in the residuals are declared consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An accepted point is an \((\epsilon_s,\epsilon_p,\epsilon_d,\epsilon_c)\)-approximate KKT point under the displayed residual convention.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With one tolerance, acceptance is \(\|R_{\mathrm{KKT}}(x,\lambda,\mu)\|_\infty\leq\epsilon\), where \(R_{\mathrm{KKT}}\) stacks the four residual blocks.
special_cases_latex: For equality constraints only, \(r_d\) and \(r_c\) are absent.
For an unconstrained problem, the test reduces to \(\|\nabla f(x)\|\leq\epsilon_s\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Zero tolerances recover the classical first-order KKT equalities and inequalities.
Separate tolerances permit feasibility and stationarity to be scaled independently.
boundary_notes: The product residual \(\mu\odot g(x)\) is not scale invariant.
For nonsmooth objectives or constraints, stationarity must use an appropriate generalized derivative or proximal residual.
No inspected source hint supplied this exact four-block stopping convention.
review_flags: A precise source locator for the combined stationarity, feasibility, dual-feasibility, and complementarity stopping interface is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Curvature and operator interface induced by quadratic augmentation
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be twice continuously differentiable, and define \(L_\rho(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^Th(x)+\tfrac\rho2\|h(x)\|^2\) for \(\rho>0\). Let \(J(x)=\nabla h(x)^T\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This exact finite-dimensional interface concerns equality constraints with Euclidean quadratic augmentation. Weighted augmentation replaces \(J^TJ\) by \(J^TWJ\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The augmentation linear-algebra interface at \((x,\lambda,ho)\) is the symmetric operator \[H_ho(x,\lambda):=
abla_{xx}^2L_ho(x,\lambda)=
abla^2f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m(\lambda_i+ho h_i(x))
abla^2h_i(x)+ho J(x)^TJ(x).\] An admissible inner linear solver may access this operator either as an assembled matrix or through products \[v\longmapsto H_ho v=
abla^2f(x)v+\sum_i(\lambda_i+ho h_i(x))
abla^2h_i(x)v+ho J(x)^T(J(x)v).\] Thus quadratic augmentation contributes a positive-semidefinite normal-curvature term \(ho J^TJ\), while nonlinear constraints also modify the Lagrangian-curvature coefficients through \(\lambda+ho h(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The linear-algebra object supplied by quadratic augmentation is the Hessian of the augmented Lagrangian. It consists of objective curvature, constraint Hessians weighted by the shifted multiplier, and the positive-semidefinite term rho times the Jacobian Gram matrix. Inner solvers may use the assembled matrix or only its action on vectors.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and every component of \(h\) are twice continuously differentiable at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exact augmented-curvature operator is \(H_\rho=\nabla^2f+\sum_i(\lambda_i+\rho h_i)\nabla^2h_i+\rho J^TJ\), with the stated matrix-free product.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(\widetilde\lambda=\lambda+\rho h(x)\), one has \(H_\rho=\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x,\widetilde\lambda)+\rho J^TJ\).
special_cases_latex: For affine constraints, \(\nabla^2h_i=0\), so \(H_\rho=\nabla^2f+\rho J^TJ\).
At a feasible point, \(h(x)=0\), so the constraint-Hessian coefficients equal \(\lambda_i\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The augmentation term increases curvature only in directions detected by \(J\).
A matrix-free implementation requires products with \(J\), \(J^T\), and the unaugmented Lagrangian Hessian.
boundary_notes: The term \(\rho J^TJ\) does not regularize directions in \(\ker J\).
For inequality augmented Lagrangians with projections or positive parts, twice differentiability may fail at active-set transitions.

notation.meaning: Constraint Jacobian with constraints in rows.

children.title: Penalty-Induced Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Curvature imbalance associated with increasing augmentation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counter-regime to unconditional condition-number growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(H_0=0\) and \(J\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is nonsingular, then
\[H_\rho=\rho J^{\mathsf T}J,\qquad \kappa_2(H_\rho)=\kappa_2(J)^2,
\]
independently of \(\rho\). In particular, \(J=I\) gives \(H_\rho=\rho I\) and \(\kappa_2(H_\rho)=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Penalty-scaled eigenvalues can all diverge while the condition number remains constant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Eigenvalue growth alone does not imply condition-number growth.}
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Penalty Curvature without Ill-Conditioning

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal-versus-tangent curvature added by quadratic equality augmentation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[L_\rho(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}c(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|c(x)\|^2,\]
\[\nabla_{xx}^2L_\rho=\nabla^2f+\sum_i(\lambda_i+\rho c_i)\nabla^2c_i+\rho J_c^{\mathsf T}J_c.\]
At a feasible point, \(\rho J_c^{\mathsf T}J_c\) vanishes on \(\ker J_c\) and has eigenvalues \(\rho\sigma_i(J_c)^2\) on its nonzero singular directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic augmentation adds penalty-scaled curvature in linearized normal directions but none in tangent directions.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and every \(c_i\) are twice continuously differentiable.
The tangent–normal interpretation is applied at a feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d\in\ker J_c\Rightarrow d^{\mathsf T}(\rho J_c^{\mathsf T}J_c)d=0.
knowledge_statements.title: Augmented-Hessian Curvature Decomposition

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear Conditioning Growth under Tangent–Normal Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient spectral regime for penalty-linear condition-number growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T=\ker J\) and \(N=T^\perp\), with both nonzero, and let \(H_\rho=H_0+\rho J^{\mathsf T}J\). Suppose \(T,N\) are invariant under \(H_0\),
\[aI\preceq H_0|_T\preceq bI,\quad 0\preceq H_0|_N\preceq BI,\quad \sigma^2I\preceq(J^{\mathsf T}J)|_N\preceq\Sigma^2I,
\]
where \(a,\sigma>0\). Then \(H_\rho\succ0\), and for all sufficiently large \(\rho\),
\[\frac{\rho\sigma^2}{b}\leq\kappa_2(H_\rho)\leq\frac{B+\rho\Sigma^2}{a}.\]
Consequently \(\kappa_2(H_\rho)=\Theta(\rho)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With bounded positive tangent curvature and uniformly nonzero normal singular values, the augmented Hessian condition number grows linearly with the penalty.
assumptions_latex: The nonzero tangent and normal subspaces are invariant under \(H_0\).
Tangent curvature is bounded above and uniformly positive.
Nonzero singular values of \(J\) are bounded above and away from zero.
Normal base curvature is positive semidefinite and bounded.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear Conditioning Growth under Tangent–Normal Separation
Penalty-Induced Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral curvature growth caused by the quadratic augmentation term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For equality constraints and
\[L_\rho(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}c(x)+\tfrac{\rho}{2}\lVert c(x)\rVert^2,\]
the Hessian satisfies
\[\nabla_{xx}^2L_\rho(x,\lambda)=\nabla^2 f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m(\lambda_i+\rho c_i(x))\nabla^2c_i(x)+\rho J_c(x)^{\mathsf T}J_c(x).\]
At a feasible point, the final term adds curvature of order \(\rho\) on directions having nonzero linearized constraint violation, but vanishes on \(\ker J_c(x)\). Consequently, if tangent-space curvature remains of order one while \(\rho\to\infty\), the Hessian condition number generally grows at least proportionally to \(\rho\), absent compensating scaling or preconditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Large penalties add strong normal-space curvature but no tangent-space curvature, commonly producing a condition number that grows with the penalty.
assumptions_latex: The point \(x\) is feasible when the spectral interpretation is applied.
Tangent-space curvature is uniformly positive and bounded independently of \(\rho\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The augmentation creates an increasing normal-versus-tangent curvature imbalance as \(\rho\to\infty\).
review_flags: the Hessian identity is standard, but no supplied locator supports the stated conditioning consequence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Hessian identity is standard, but the asserted at-least-linear condition-number growth requires additional spectral hypotheses, including positive definiteness and uniform bounds on nonzero normal-space singular values and on tangent curvature. No source is supplied to fix or support the precise conditioning claim.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H_\rho\succ0\) be the symmetric augmented-subproblem curvature used by a local inner method, and let its Euclidean spectral condition number be \(\kappa_2(H_\rho)=\lambda_{\max}(H_\rho)/\lambda_{\min}(H_\rho)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition applies where the relevant curvature is positive definite. For indefinite Hessians, singular-value conditioning or inertia-aware measures must be used instead.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A family \(\{H_\rho\}_{\rho>0}\) exhibits penalty-induced ill-conditioning on a penalty sequence \(\rho_k\to\infty\) if \[\kappa_2(H_{\rho_k})\to\infty.\] More generally, its penalty-induced conditioning profile is the map \(\rho\mapsto\kappa_2(H_\rho)\). For affine equality constraints and quadratic local curvature, \[H_\rho=H_0+\rho J^TJ.\] The profile records the imbalance between the \(O(\rho)\) curvature introduced in \(\operatorname{range}(J^T)\) and the curvature retained in directions weakly affected or unaffected by \(J\). The term denotes this spectral imbalance, not merely the numerical magnitude of \(\rho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Penalty-induced conditioning is the dependence of the augmented curvature's spectral condition number on the penalty. Ill-conditioning occurs along an increasing penalty sequence when that condition number diverges. For affine constraints, the added Jacobian Gram term can make normal directions increasingly stiff while leaving tangent directions comparatively unchanged.
assumptions_latex: Eigenvalues are measured in the declared Euclidean coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Penalty-induced ill-conditioning is present exactly when \(\lambda_{\max}(H_{\rho_k})/\lambda_{\min}(H_{\rho_k})\to\infty\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For symmetric positive-definite \(H_\rho\), \(\kappa_2(H_\rho)=\|H_\rho\|_2\|H_\rho^{-1}\|_2\).
special_cases_latex: If \(H_0=I\) and \(J=(1,0)\), then \(H_\rho=\operatorname{diag}(1+\rho,1)\) and \(\kappa_2(H_\rho)=1+\rho\).
If \(J\) has full column rank and all eigenvalues scale comparably with \(\rho\), divergence is not automatic.
immediate_consequences_latex: Large penalties can increase the difficulty of unpreconditioned first-order and iterative linear solvers.
A condition number is coordinate dependent, so scaling can change the observed profile.
boundary_notes: A large penalty does not by itself imply a large condition number.
The definition excludes singular and indefinite curvature without an alternative conditioning convention.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Large Penalties Need Not Cause Ill-Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary excluding unconditional condition-number growth claims.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Take \(H_0=0\) and an invertible \(J\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\). Then \(H_\rho=\rho J^{\mathsf T}J\) and
\[\kappa_2(H_\rho)=\kappa_2(J^{\mathsf T}J)=\kappa_2(J)^2\]
for every \(\rho>0\). In particular, if \(J=I\), then \(H_\rho=\rho I\) and \(\kappa_2(H_\rho)=1\), although every eigenvalue diverges linearly with \(\rho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A large penalty does not itself imply a large condition number: if it scales every direction uniformly, the condition number remains constant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Penalty-induced eigenvalue growth does not imply penalty-induced condition-number growth.
knowledge_statements.title: Large Penalties Need Not Cause Ill-Conditioning

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear Condition-Number Growth in an Orthogonal Tangent–Normal Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Precise spectral regime in which increasing augmentation causes linear ill-conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H_0\in\mathbb S^n\), \(J\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(T=\ker J\), and \(N=T^\perp\). Assume \(T\) and \(N\) are invariant under \(H_0\), \(aI\preceq H_0|_T\preceq bI\), \(0\preceq H_0|_N\preceq BI\), and \(\sigma^2 I\preceq (J^{\mathsf T}J)|_N\preceq \Sigma^2I\), where \(a,\sigma>0\). Then for \(H_\rho=H_0+\rho J^{\mathsf T}J\),
\[\min\{a,\rho\sigma^2\}\leq\lambda_{\min}(H_\rho),\qquad \lambda_{\max}(H_\rho)\leq\max\{b,B+\rho\Sigma^2\}.\]
Moreover, for all sufficiently large \(\rho\), \(\lambda_{\min}(H_\rho)\leq b\) and \(\lambda_{\max}(H_\rho)\geq\rho\sigma^2\), so \(\kappa_2(H_\rho)\geq \rho\sigma^2/b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When tangent curvature stays bounded while uniformly nonzero normal singular values are penalized, the augmented Hessian's condition number grows at least linearly with the penalty.
assumptions_latex: The tangent and normal subspaces are invariant under \(H_0\).
Tangent curvature is uniformly positive and bounded.
The nonzero singular values of \(J\) are bounded above and away from zero.

notation.meaning: Lower and upper nonzero singular-value bounds for the constraint Jacobian.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Metric condition number for scaled augmented curvature
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H_\rho\succ0\) be an augmented-curvature matrix and let \(M\succ0\) define the primal metric \(\|v\|_M^2=v^TMv\). Let \(W\succ0\) be an optional constraint-space metric in the quadratic term \(\tfrac\rho2\|h(x)\|_W^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This finite-dimensional definition separates constraint scaling through \(W\) from primal preconditioning through \(M\). Both matrices are symmetric positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The metric-conditioned augmented curvature is \[\widehat H_{\rho,M}:=M^{-1/2}H_\rho M^{-1/2},\] and its metric condition number is \[\kappa_M(H_\rho):=\kappa_2(\widehat H_{\rho,M})=\frac{\lambda_{\max}(M^{-1/2}H_\rho M^{-1/2})}{\lambda_{\min}(M^{-1/2}H_\rho M^{-1/2})}.\] With constraint metric \(W\), the augmentation contribution is \(\rho J^TWJ\). A metric conditioning calculus is the comparison of \(\kappa_M(H_\rho)\) under admissible choices of \(M\) and \(W\), including coordinate changes, constraint scaling, and preconditioner updates. The ideal relation \(M=H_\rho\) gives \(\kappa_M(H_\rho)=1\), while practical metrics approximate this balance at lower cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Metric conditioning measures augmented curvature after transforming it by a positive-definite primal metric. Constraint scaling changes the Jacobian Gram term through a separate positive-definite constraint metric. The calculus compares the resulting condition numbers across scalings and preconditioners.
assumptions_latex: \(H_\rho\), \(M\), and \(W\) are symmetric positive definite where their condition numbers or norms are used.
Square roots and inverse square roots are the symmetric positive-definite ones.
The Jacobian convention is fixed across compared metrics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conditioned spectrum is the spectrum of \(M^{-1/2}H_\rho M^{-1/2}\), and augmentation in constraint metric \(W\) contributes \(\rho J^TWJ\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\kappa_M(H_\rho)\) is the ratio of the largest to smallest generalized eigenvalues in \(H_\rho v=\theta Mv\).
special_cases_latex: For \(M=I\), \(\kappa_M(H_\rho)=\kappa_2(H_\rho)\).
Diagonal \(W\) gives independent scaling weights to constraint residuals.
A change of variables \(x=Sy\) corresponds to transformed curvature \(S^TH_\rho S\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Preconditioning quality is assessed by clustering generalized eigenvalues rather than by the unscaled Hessian alone.
Constraint scaling and primal preconditioning affect different sides of the augmented operator.
boundary_notes: An excellent condition number may still be computationally useless if applying \(M^{-1}\) is too expensive.
No inspected locator directly supported the full two-metric calculus stated here.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of equivalence when the penalty metric is not transported.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\widetilde c=Dc\), \(\tfrac\rho2\|\widetilde c\|^2=\tfrac12c^{\mathsf T}(\rho D^{\mathsf T}D)c\), which equals \(\tfrac\rho2\|c\|^2\) for all \(c\) iff \(D^{\mathsf T}D=I\). A general metric is invariant precisely under \(\widetilde W=D^{-\mathsf T}WD^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed scalar penalty is not invariant under general constraint scaling; the residual metric must be transported contragrediently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (Dc)^{\mathsf T}\widetilde W(Dc)=c^{\mathsf T}Wc\ \forall c\iff \widetilde W=D^{-\mathsf T}WD^{-1}.

notation.meaning: penalty metrics before and after scaling

knowledge_statements.title: Scalar-Penalty Noninvariance Under Constraint Scaling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transformation law for residual-based ALM termination tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonsingular \(D\), \[\sigma_{\min}(D)\|c(x)\|_2\le\|Dc(x)\|_2\le\sigma_{\max}(D)\|c(x)\|_2.\] Thus exact feasibility is invariant, whereas an absolute residual tolerance is not invariant unless its norm or threshold is transported.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint scaling preserves exact feasibility but changes absolute feasibility tolerances according to the scaling singular values.

notation.meaning: extreme singular values of the scaling

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling of Feasibility Residual Certificates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covariance of a metric ALM multiplier update under constraint-coordinate scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\lambda^+=\lambda+\rho Wc(x^+)\). Under \(\widetilde c=Dc\), set \(\widetilde\lambda=D^{-\mathsf T}\lambda\) and \(\widetilde W=D^{-\mathsf T}WD^{-1}\). Then \[\widetilde\lambda^+=\widetilde\lambda+\rho\widetilde W\widetilde c(x^+)=D^{-\mathsf T}\lambda^+.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transporting multipliers and the penalty metric contragrediently makes the scaled ALM multiplier update exactly covariant.

notation.meaning: penalty metrics in original and scaled coordinates
multipliers in original and scaled coordinates

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier-Update Covariance Under Scaling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral effect of constraint-coordinate scaling on augmented Gauss–Newton curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonsingular \(D\), \(W\in\mathbb S_{++}^m\), and every \(z\), \[\lambda_{\min}(D^{\mathsf T}WD)\|Jz\|_2^2\le z^{\mathsf T}J^{\mathsf T}D^{\mathsf T}WDJz\le\lambda_{\max}(D^{\mathsf T}WD)\|Jz\|_2^2.\] If \(J\) has full column rank, then \[\kappa_2(J^{\mathsf T}D^{\mathsf T}WDJ)\le\kappa_2(D^{\mathsf T}WD)\,\kappa_2(J^{\mathsf T}J).\] Nonsingularity of the scaling alone therefore gives no conditioning improvement guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint scaling changes augmented curvature within spectral bounds determined by the transported residual metric and can improve or worsen conditioning.
assumptions_latex: Full column rank of \(J\) is required for the finite condition-number bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \kappa_2(J^{\mathsf T}D^{\mathsf T}WDJ)\le\kappa_2(D^{\mathsf T}WD)\kappa_2(J^{\mathsf T}J)\quad\text{when }J\text{ has full column rank}.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaled Augmented-Curvature Bounds
Constraint Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal rescaling of equality constraints and its effect on augmented curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\) be nonsingular and diagonal, and replace \(c(x)=0\) by \(\widetilde c(x)=Dc(x)=0\). With scaled multiplier \(\widetilde\lambda=D^{-\mathsf T}\lambda\), the linear Lagrangian term is invariant:
\[\widetilde\lambda^{\mathsf T}\widetilde c(x)=\lambda^{\mathsf T}c(x).\]
The quadratic augmentation becomes
\[\tfrac{\rho}{2}\lVert\widetilde c(x)\rVert^2=\tfrac12c(x)^{\mathsf T}(\rho D^{\mathsf T}D)c(x),\]
and its Gauss–Newton curvature contribution is \(\rho J_c(x)^{\mathsf T}D^{\mathsf T}DJ_c(x)\). Thus constraint scaling is equivalent to choosing a positive diagonal penalty metric and changes conditioning without changing the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonsingular diagonal constraint scaling preserves feasibility and the linear multiplier term while replacing the scalar penalty by a diagonal metric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x:Dc(x)=0\}=\{x:c(x)=0\}\), while augmented curvature is weighted by \(D^{\mathsf T}D\).

children.title: Metric Preconditioning

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spectral-Equivalence Criterion for an Inner Preconditioner
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition ensuring uniform conditioning of an augmented-curvature solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H,P\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\). If \(0<\alpha\le\beta\) satisfy \(\alpha P\preceq H\preceq\beta P\), then \[\sigma(P^{-1/2}HP^{-1/2})\subseteq[\alpha,\beta],\qquad \kappa_2(P^{-1/2}HP^{-1/2})\le\beta/\alpha.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inner preconditioner is uniformly effective when it is spectrally equivalent to augmented curvature.
knowledge_statements.title: Spectral-Equivalence Criterion for an Inner Preconditioner

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of uniform inner conditioning when equivalence constants deteriorate with the penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(H_\rho,P_\rho\succ0\), pointwise invertibility of \(P_\rho\) does not imply penalty-robust preconditioning. Uniform spectral control requires constants independent of \(\rho\) with \(\alpha P_\rho\preceq H_\rho\preceq\beta P_\rho\). If the best ratio \(\beta_\rho/\alpha_\rho\) is unbounded, no uniform condition-number guarantee follows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A preconditioner is penalty robust only when its spectral equivalence with augmented curvature remains uniform.
knowledge_statements.title: Penalty-Robustness Boundary
Metric Preconditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variable-metric representation of the equality-constrained augmented-Lagrangian penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^m\), \(\rho>0\), and let \(W\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^m\). The metric augmented Lagrangian is
\[\mathcal L_{\rho,W}(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}c(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}c(x)^{\mathsf T}Wc(x).\]
Writing \(R^{\mathsf T}R=W\), its penalty equals \(\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert Rc(x)\rVert_2^2\). At a point where \(J(x)=Dc(x)\), the Gauss–Newton penalty curvature is \(\rho J(x)^{\mathsf T}WJ(x)\); hence choosing \(W\) preconditions constraint-space directions without changing the feasible set \(c(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite constraint metric weights residual directions and contributes the curvature term rho times J-transpose W J while preserving the original feasible set.

notation.meaning: A factor satisfying R-transpose R equals W.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is mathematically coherent: the displayed term is the Gauss–Newton part of the penalty Hessian, and a positive-definite residual metric preserves the zero set of c. However, the record supplies no source or explicit standard-field rationale for this nontrivial metric-ALM formulation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic PCG theorem rather than a preconditioner construction local to this leaf.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\alpha P\preceq H\preceq\beta P\), exact-arithmetic PCG satisfies the standard energy-norm bound with condition number at most \(\beta/\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Spectral equivalence implies the standard square-root-condition-number PCG rate.

children.title: Scaling–Preconditioner Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility between normalization choices and preconditioned inner solution.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient transport laws for equality-constraint residual coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\widetilde c=Sc\), where \(S\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) is nonsingular. Requiring
\[\widetilde\lambda^{\mathsf T}Sr+\frac{\rho}{2}(Sr)^{\mathsf T}\widetilde W(Sr)=\lambda^{\mathsf T}r+\frac{\rho}{2}r^{\mathsf T}Wr\quad\forall r\in\mathbb R^m\]
is equivalent to
\[\widetilde\lambda=S^{-\mathsf T}\lambda,\qquad \widetilde W=S^{-\mathsf T}WS^{-1}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact invariance under nonsingular constraint scaling requires inverse-transpose transport of the multiplier and congruence transport of the residual metric.
assumptions_latex: Invariance is required for every residual vector, not merely residuals attained by one constraint map.

notation.meaning: Residual metrics in the original and scaled coordinates.
Multiplier coordinates before and after scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Scaling–Metric Compatibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for retaining the same residual metric after scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(W\) is kept fixed after \(r\mapsto Sr\), then
\[(Sr)^{\mathsf T}W(Sr)=r^{\mathsf T}Wr\quad\forall r\]
if and only if \(S^{\mathsf T}WS=W\). If this identity fails, some residual vector has a changed penalty value and normal-curvature quadratic form.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An untransported metric is compatible only with scalings that are isometries of that metric.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Metric Isometry Boundary
Scaling–Preconditioner Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact invariance condition for nonsingular constraint scaling and residual metrics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\) be nonsingular and define the scaled constraints \(\widetilde c(x)=Sc(x)\). The scaled multiplier and metric are compatible with the original augmented Lagrangian precisely when
\[\widetilde\lambda=S^{-\mathsf T}\lambda,\qquad \widetilde W=S^{-\mathsf T}WS^{-1}.\]
Indeed, compatibility means that for every \(x\),
\[\widetilde\lambda^{\mathsf T}\widetilde c(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\widetilde c(x)^{\mathsf T}\widetilde W\widetilde c(x)=\lambda^{\mathsf T}c(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}c(x)^{\mathsf T}Wc(x).\]
Thus scaling and metric preconditioning commute only after applying the corresponding contragredient transformations to both multiplier and metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint scaling preserves the augmented Lagrangian exactly when multipliers and the residual metric undergo the corresponding inverse-transpose transformations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widetilde\lambda=S^{-\mathsf T}\lambda\) and \(\widetilde W=S^{-\mathsf T}WS^{-1}\) are necessary and sufficient for exact invariance for all residual vectors.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The contragredient transformations give invariance for every residual vector. If equality is required only for every x, necessity need not follow unless the range of c is sufficiently rich. A source is needed to determine and support the intended exact formulation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary showing when constraint scaling and a fixed residual metric do not represent the same augmented model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) be nonsingular, \(W\in\mathbb S_{++}^m\), and \(\widetilde c=Sc\). If the same matrix \(W\) is used before and after scaling, then the quadratic penalty is invariant for every residual \(r\in\mathbb R^m\) if and only if \(S^{\mathsf T}WS=W\). Otherwise there exists \(r\) such that \((Sr)^{\mathsf T}W(Sr)\ne r^{\mathsf T}Wr\); hence fixed-metric scaling changes the augmented objective and its normal curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keeping the residual metric fixed under a general constraint scaling changes the penalty unless the scaling is an isometry of that metric.
assumptions_latex: Invariance is required for every residual vector.

notation.meaning: Residual-space metric kept fixed in both representations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Assembled and matrix-free representations of augmented curvature
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H_\rho\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be the symmetric curvature operator of an augmented subproblem, with decomposition \(H_\rho=H_L+\rho J^TJ\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition concerns large-scale smooth subproblems for which either sparse assembly or operator products are computationally meaningful.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A large-scale subproblem representation pair for \(H_\rho\) consists of: (i) an assembled representation storing sparse factors or entries sufficient to apply and factor \(H_\rho\); and (ii) a matrix-free representation supplying the linear map \[\mathcal H_\rho(v):=H_Lv+\rho J^T(Jv)\] without forming \(H_\rho\). The pair is consistent if \(\mathcal H_\rho(v)=H_\rho v\) for every \(v\in\mathbb R^n\). An inner solver may select the assembled member for sparse direct factorization or the operator member for Krylov iteration, but both represent the same quadratic model \(q(p)=g^Tp+\tfrac12p^TH_\rho p\). Optional preconditioners are auxiliary operators and are not part of the equality defining consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The representation pair consists of a sparse assembled matrix and a matrix-free operator for the same augmented curvature. They are consistent when both produce the same matrix-vector product for every vector. The assembled form supports sparse factorization, while the operator form supports Krylov methods through products with the Lagrangian Hessian, Jacobian, and transpose Jacobian.
assumptions_latex: \(H_\rho\) is a well-defined linear operator on \(\mathbb R^n\).
The assembled and operator representations use the same iterate, multiplier, penalty, and derivative data.
The operator products \(H_Lv\), \(Jv\), and \(J^Tw\) are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For all \(v\in\mathbb R^n\), the consistency condition is \(\mathcal H_\rho(v)=H_\rho v\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The quadratic forms agree for every \(v\): \(v^T\mathcal H_\rho(v)=v^TH_\rho v\), provided both operators are symmetric and equality is interpreted through polarization.
special_cases_latex: If \(J\) is sparse and explicitly stored, both representations may share the same Jacobian data.
A Gauss–Newton model uses \(H_L\) equal to an objective or residual-model curvature approximation.
immediate_consequences_latex: Matrix-free storage avoids explicitly forming \(J^TJ\).
The same preconditioned Krylov algorithm can be validated against an assembled representation on smaller instances.
boundary_notes: Equality of quadratic forms alone does not identify a nonsymmetric operator.
Finite-precision implementations may satisfy consistency only to numerical tolerance.
No exact source locator for this named representation pair was found.
review_flags: The mathematical pair is standard in large-scale numerical optimization, but the supplied sources did not directly support this exact named definition.

children.title: Sparse Subproblem Algebra
children.top_down_role: Augmented-subproblem representations that preserve or exploit sparse algebraic structure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Structural Fill Pattern of Augmented Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparsity graph induced by a diagonal residual metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(W=\operatorname{diag}(w_1,\ldots,w_m)\), \[(J^{\mathsf T}WJ)_{pq}=\sum_i w_iJ_{ip}J_{iq}.\] Absent cancellation, variables \(p\) and \(q\) are structurally coupled whenever a row with nonzero weight contains both columns; each such row support therefore induces a clique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forming the augmented normal matrix couples every pair of variables appearing in a common constraint row.
assumptions_latex: structural nonzeros ignore accidental numerical cancellation
knowledge_statements.title: Structural Fill Pattern of Augmented Curvature

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordering-qualified comparison of assembled augmented-normal and saddle-point formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L_N\) and \(L_K\) be symbolic factors, under specified admissible orderings and pivoting rules, of \(N=B+\rho J^{\mathsf T}WJ\) and \(K=\begin{pmatrix}B&J^{\mathsf T}\\J&-(\rho W)^{-1}\end{pmatrix}\). Storage and direct-factorization work depend on the resulting elimination graphs and fronts. Neither formulation uniformly minimizes them: forming \(N\) can create row-support cliques, while the larger indefinite block system \(K\) can incur its own fill and pivoting costs. Any comparison therefore requires the matrix patterns, orderings, and pivoting restrictions to be specified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Neither formulation is uniformly sparser or cheaper to factor; the comparison depends on sparsity graphs, ordering, and pivoting.
assumptions_latex: A sparse ordering and compatible direct-factorization strategy are specified for each formulation.
Cost is assessed from the resulting symbolic or pivoted factors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{nnz}(L_N)\lessgtr\operatorname{nnz}(L_K)\text{ and corresponding factorization-work comparisons can reverse across instances and admissible orderings}.

notation.meaning: factor of the augmented normal matrix

knowledge_statements.title: No Uniform Sparse-Factorization Dominance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact block-elimination equivalence for an assembled sparse augmented Newton system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb S^n\), \(J\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(W\in\mathbb S_{++}^m\), and \(\rho>0\). Then \((d,y)\) solves \[\begin{pmatrix}B&J^{\mathsf T}\\J&-(\rho W)^{-1}\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}d\\y\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}-g\\0\end{pmatrix}\] if and only if \[(B+\rho J^{\mathsf T}WJ)d=-g,\qquad y=\rho WJd.\] Consequently, nonsingularity of \(B+\rho J^{\mathsf T}WJ\) makes the primal step unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The augmented normal equation and sparse saddle-point system have exactly the same primal solutions, with the auxiliary variable recovered explicitly.
assumptions_latex: Nonsingularity is required only for uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (d,y)\text{ solves the block system}\iff (B+\rho J^{\mathsf T}WJ)d=-g\text{ and }y=\rho WJd.
knowledge_statements.title: Augmented Normal and Saddle-Point Equivalence
Sparse Subproblem Algebra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse normal-equation and saddle-point forms for an augmented-Lagrangian Newton step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B\in\mathbb{S}^n\), \(J\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(W\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^m\), \(\rho>0\), and \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\). The augmented quadratic step satisfies
\[(B+\rho J^{\mathsf T}WJ)d=-g.\]
When \(B\), \(J\), and \(W\) are stored sparsely, the same step is obtained from the sparse saddle-point system
\[\begin{pmatrix}B&J^{\mathsf T}\\J&-(\rho W)^{-1}\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}d\\y\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}-g\\0\end{pmatrix}.\]
Eliminating \(y\) gives the normal equation above. The saddle-point form avoids explicitly forming \(J^{\mathsf T}WJ\), whose fill-in may exceed that of the block factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An augmented Newton equation can be represented as a sparse saddle-point system, avoiding explicit formation and possible fill-in of J-transpose W J.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The first block component of the saddle-point solution is the unique solution of \((B+\rho J^{\mathsf T}WJ)d=-g\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The block elimination and signs are correct, and representation is the appropriate knowledge kind for this leaf. The sparse-factorization and fill-in claim is nontrivial and has no cited source or standard-field rationale.

children.title: Matrix-Free Operator Products
children.top_down_role: Inner solution based on derivative or curvature products without explicit matrix assembly.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for symmetric Krylov use with operator-only augmented curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(K\) replaces \(J^*\), the implemented operator \(\widehat H=B+\rho KWJ\) has skew-adjoint part \[\tfrac12(\widehat H-\widehat H^*)=\tfrac\rho2(KWJ-J^*WK^*).\] Hence symmetric Krylov recurrences require this term to vanish, in particular when \(K=J^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reverse product that is not the true adjoint can destroy symmetry.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact-Adjoint Symmetry Failure

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Symmetry and Positivity of the Augmentation Product
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic properties required by symmetric matrix-free inner solvers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For self-adjoint \(B\) and \(W\), \(H=B+\rho J^*WJ\) is self-adjoint. If \(B\succeq0\), \(W\succeq0\), and \(\rho\ge0\), then \[v^{\mathsf T}Hv=v^{\mathsf T}Bv+\rho\|W^{1/2}Jv\|^2\ge0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact adjoint products preserve symmetry, and positive-semidefinite components preserve positive semidefiniteness.

notation.meaning: Euclidean adjoint of the Jacobian action

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry and Positivity of the Augmentation Product

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local operation and storage count for the direct matrix-free evaluation of one augmented-curvature product.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[
Hv=Bv+\rho J^*WJv,
\]
the direct composition evaluates \(u=Jv\), \(z=Wu\), \(t=J^*z\), and \(Hv=Bv+\rho t\). It uses one call to each of the \(B\), \(J\), \(W\), and \(J^*\) product oracles. Excluding the input vector, final output, operator-internal storage, and any Krylov basis, a conventional implementation needs at most one additional primal-space vector and two constraint-space vectors; overwrite-capable or fused oracles may use less. No entries of \(J^*WJ\) are formed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A direct augmented-curvature action uses one call to each constituent operator and at most one extra primal vector plus two constraint-space temporaries, excluding input, output, solver-basis, and operator storage.
assumptions_latex: \(B:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), \(J:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), \(W:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^m\), and \(J^*:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^n\) are available as product oracles.
The count refers to the displayed direct composition and permits reuse after an intermediate vector's final use.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_B=N_J=N_W=N_{J^*}=1\) for the displayed evaluation, and \(S_{\mathrm{temp}}\le n+2m\) scalar slots excluding input and final output.

notation.meaning: numbers of constituent oracle calls in one direct product evaluation
temporary storage excluding input, final output, operator storage, and Krylov-basis storage

knowledge_statements.title: Per-Application Oracle and Temporary-Storage Cost

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Foundational operator interface for applying augmented-subproblem curvature without assembly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), \(J:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), \(W:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^m\), and let \(J^*:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^n\) be the Euclidean adjoint. For \(\rho\ge0\), the augmented-curvature operator
\[
H=B+\rho J^*WJ
\]
is applied to \(v\in\mathbb R^n\) by
\[
u=Jv,\qquad z=Wu,\qquad Hv=Bv+\rho J^*z.
\]
This composition is algebraically identical to multiplication by an assembled \(H\) and requires no assembly of \(J^*WJ\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successive forward-Jacobian, metric, adjoint-Jacobian, and base-curvature products apply augmented curvature exactly without assembling the composite matrix.
assumptions_latex: The four displayed operator actions are available with the stated domains.
The reverse Jacobian action is the Euclidean adjoint \(J^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v\mapsto Bv+\rho J^*(W(Jv))\) equals multiplication by \(B+\rho J^*WJ\).
knowledge_statements.title: Dimensioned Matrix-Free Augmented-Curvature Action
Matrix-Free Operator Products
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator-only application of augmented-subproblem curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(H=B+\rho J^{\mathsf T}WJ\), a Krylov method need not assemble \(H\). Given \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\), compute successively
\[u=Jv,\qquad z=Wu,\qquad Hv=Bv+\rho J^{\mathsf T}z.\]
If products with \(B\), \(J\), \(J^{\mathsf T}\), and \(W\) are available as operators, this procedure is algebraically identical to multiplication by the assembled augmented curvature. Its working storage, excluding the operators and Krylov basis, is one primal vector and at most two constraint-space vectors; no entries of \(J^{\mathsf T}WJ\) are required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Augmented curvature products are computed by successive Jacobian, metric, adjoint-Jacobian, and Hessian products without assembling the augmented matrix.
assumptions_latex: The linear operators \(B\), \(J\), \(J^{\mathsf T}\), and \(W\) are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The operator sequence returns exactly \(Hv=(B+\rho J^{\mathsf T}WJ)v\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The operator sequence is algebraically correct and fits the matrix-free representation leaf. The domains of B, J, J-transpose, and W are not stated explicitly, and neither the representation nor its storage bound has supporting evidence.

children.top_down_role: Large-scale regimes combining partial sparse assembly with matrix-free products.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral effect of using the assembled sparse block as a preconditioner for the operator remainder.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=P+K\), where \(P\succ0\), \(K\succeq0\), and \(K\preceq\gamma P\). Then \[1\le\lambda(P^{-1/2}HP^{-1/2})\le1+\gamma,\qquad \kappa_2(P^{-1/2}HP^{-1/2})\le1+\gamma.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spectrally dominant assembled block provides an explicit preconditioning bound for the matrix-free remainder.
knowledge_statements.title: Assembled-Block Preconditioning Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp mixed-metric boundary for an additive assembled–operator curvature split.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(J=(J_s^{\mathsf T},J_o^{\mathsf T})^{\mathsf T}\) and \(W=\begin{psmallmatrix}W_{ss}&W_{so}\\W_{os}&W_{oo}\end{psmallmatrix}\), \[J^{\mathsf T}WJ=J_s^{\mathsf T}W_{ss}J_s+J_s^{\mathsf T}W_{so}J_o+J_o^{\mathsf T}W_{os}J_s+J_o^{\mathsf T}W_{oo}J_o.\] Hence the diagonal-block split is exact if and only if the two mixed terms sum to zero. Block diagonality of \(W\) is sufficient but not necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A general residual metric creates two cross terms between assembled and operator blocks; the additive hybrid split is exact exactly when their sum vanishes.
assumptions_latex: \(J_s\in\mathbb R^{m_s\times n}\), \(J_o\in\mathbb R^{m_o\times n}\), and \(J=(J_s^{\mathsf T},J_o^{\mathsf T})^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: J^{\mathsf T}WJ=J_s^{\mathsf T}W_{ss}J_s+J_o^{\mathsf T}W_{oo}J_o\iff J_s^{\mathsf T}W_{so}J_o+J_o^{\mathsf T}W_{os}J_s=0.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Metric Cross-Term Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact augmented-curvature action combining an assembled sparse block with an operator-only block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), \(J_s:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_s}\), \(J_o:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_o}\), \(W_s:\mathbb R^{m_s}\to\mathbb R^{m_s}\), and \(W_o:\mathbb R^{m_o}\to\mathbb R^{m_o}\). With \(Jv=(J_sv,J_ov)\), \(W=\operatorname{diag}(W_s,W_o)\), and \(\rho>0\),
\[
Hv=(B+\rho J_s^*W_sJ_s)v+\rho J_o^*W_o(J_ov).
\]
The first parenthesized operator may be assembled sparsely and the final term evaluated through forward, metric, and adjoint products. This equals \((B+\rho J^*WJ)v\) exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint-row partition and block-diagonal residual metric give an exact curvature action with one sparse assembled component and one matrix-free component.
assumptions_latex: The displayed operators have the stated finite-dimensional domains and codomains.
\(\rho>0\), and the required adjoint actions are available.
knowledge_statements.title: Dimensioned Hybrid Assembled–Operator Curvature Interface
Hybrid Sparse–Operator Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixed assembled and matrix-free decomposition of augmented curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Partition the constraint Jacobian by rows as \(J=\begin{pmatrix}J_s\\J_o\end{pmatrix}\) and take \(W=\operatorname{diag}(W_s,W_o)\), where the sparse block \(J_s\) is assembled and \(J_o\) is available only through products. Then
\[Hv=(B+\rho J_s^{\mathsf T}W_sJ_s)v+\rho J_o^{\mathsf T}W_o(J_ov).\]
The first term may be assembled and factored or used as a preconditioner, while the second is evaluated operator-wise. This hybrid representation is exact provided that the row partition and block-diagonal metric introduce no omitted cross terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A row-partitioned Jacobian permits sparse assembly for one constraint block and matrix-free products for another, with exactness under a compatible block-diagonal metric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H=B+\rho J_s^{\mathsf T}W_sJ_s+\rho J_o^{\mathsf T}W_oJ_o\) admits an exact assembled–operator split.

notation.meaning: Jacobian block accessed through operator products.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The split is exact under a conforming row partition and block-diagonal metric, and representation is the correct content kind. The spaces and operator domains are implicit, while no source or explicit standard-field rationale supports the hybrid-regime claim.
