knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convergence specification for an augmented-Lagrangian iteration
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let an ALM generate states \(s_k=(x^k,\lambda^k,\rho_k,\eta_k)\) for a constrained problem, and let \(\mathcal S^\star\) denote a target primal-dual solution set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The source node names a body of theory rather than a single classical mathematical object. This record formalizes the local sidecar object as a convergence specification containing hypotheses, conclusions, and rate regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An augmented-Lagrangian convergence specification is a tuple \(\mathfrak C=(\mathcal H,\mathcal W,\mathcal G,\mathcal R,\mathcal E)\), where \(\mathcal H\) is a stated set of problem and algorithm hypotheses; \(\mathcal W\) asserts that each required augmented subproblem has an admissible solution; \(\mathcal G\) states a global or subsequential conclusion such as \[\operatorname{dist}((x^k,\lambda^k),\mathcal S^\star)\to0;\] \(\mathcal R\) records any local rate under strengthened hypotheses; and \(\mathcal E\) specifies allowable inexactness and whether \(\{\rho_k\}\) may remain bounded. The specification is complete only when every convergence conclusion explicitly identifies its hypotheses, quantifiers, solution concept, and exact or inexact inner-solve regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An augmented-Lagrangian convergence specification packages five mathematically distinct components: hypotheses, well-posedness of subproblems, a global or subsequential convergence conclusion, any stronger local rate, and the permitted inexactness and penalty behavior. It is complete only when each conclusion states its own assumptions and target solution set.
assumptions_latex: The ALM state sequence and target solution set \(\mathcal S^\star\) are explicitly defined.
Every component of \(\mathfrak C\) states the regime to which it applies.
Any rate statement declares the norm or distance used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A complete specification associates each asserted limit or rate with explicit problem, penalty, multiplier, and inner-accuracy hypotheses.
special_cases_latex: A global-convergence specification may assert only that every accumulation point is a KKT point.
A local specification may assert linear or superlinear convergence near an isolated primal-dual solution.
A finite-penalty specification permits \(\sup_k\rho_k<\infty\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Global convergence, local rate, inexactness, and finite-penalty behavior cannot be inferred from one another without additional hypotheses.
boundary_notes: This is a formal taxonomy of convergence claims, not itself a convergence result.
The supplied node title does not designate a universally standardized mathematical object with one canonical definition.
review_flags: The slot requests a canonical definition for a theory-level aggregation node; human review should confirm that an interface definition is intended rather than a theorem slot.
No authoritative source defines the five-component tuple used here.

children.title: Augmented-Subproblem Well-Posedness
children.top_down_role: Existence, localization, and stability families for augmented subproblem solutions.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\), let \((x^\star,\lambda^\star)\) be a local primal-multiplier pair and let \(L_\rho(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^Th(x)+\tfrac\rho2\|h(x)\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is a local smooth finite-dimensional notion. It combines existence, local uniqueness, localization, and stability of the augmented-subproblem solution map near a regular second-order solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The augmented subproblems are locally well posed at \((x^\star,\lambda^\star)\) if there exist \(\bar\rho>0\), \(\delta>0\), \(\epsilon>0\), and \(M>0\) such that, for every \[D:=\{(\lambda,\rho):\rho\geq\bar\rho,\ \|\lambda-\lambda^\star\|<\delta\rho\},\] the localized problem \[\min_{\|x-x^\star\|<\epsilon}L_\rho(x,\lambda)\] has a unique solution \(x(\lambda,\rho)\), the solution map is continuous on \(D\) and continuously differentiable in its interior, and \[\|x(\lambda,\rho)-x^\star\|\leq M\frac{\|\lambda-\lambda^\star\|}{\rho}.\] Strong local well-posedness additionally requires \(\nabla_{xx}^2L_\rho(x(\lambda,\rho),\lambda)\succ0\) throughout \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Augmented subproblems are locally well posed when every sufficiently large penalty and appropriately scaled nearby multiplier defines one unique local minimizer near the target solution. That minimizer varies continuously, is differentiable in the interior of the parameter region, remains quantitatively close to the target, and has positive-definite augmented curvature in the strong form.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(h\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(x^\star\).
\(x^\star\) is regular and \((x^\star,\lambda^\star)\) satisfies a second-order sufficient condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \((\lambda,\rho)\in D\), the localized augmented subproblem has the unique stable solution \(x(\lambda,\rho)\) satisfying \(\|x(\lambda,\rho)-x^\star\|\leq M\|\lambda-\lambda^\star\|/\rho\).
special_cases_latex: For fixed \(\lambda\), every sufficiently large \(\rho\) belongs to \(D\).
At \(\lambda=\lambda^\star\), the localization bound forces \(x(\lambda^\star,\rho)=x^\star\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The local augmented minimizer cannot bifurcate within the stated parameter region.
Bounded multiplier sequences eventually satisfy the scaled-neighborhood condition when \(\rho_k\to\infty\).
boundary_notes: The definition is local and does not assert existence or uniqueness of a global minimizer.
Rank deficiency or failure of second-order sufficiency can destroy single-valuedness or stability.
The parameter region permits multiplier distance to grow proportionally to the penalty.

notation.meaning: Multiplier-penalty region in which local well-posedness holds.

children.title: Local-Minimizer Existence
children.top_down_role: Existence theory for nearby augmented-Lagrangian minimizers.

knowledge_statements.title: Local-Minimizer Existence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical smooth equality-constrained local existence theorem for quadratic augmentation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be twice continuously differentiable near \(x^*\), and define \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}c(x)\) and \(\mathcal L_\rho(x,\lambda)=L(x,\lambda)+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert c(x)\rVert_2^2\). Suppose \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) satisfies the KKT equations, \(J(x^*)=Dc(x^*)\) has full row rank, and
\[d^{\mathsf T}\nabla_{xx}^2L(x^*,\lambda^*)d>0\]
for every nonzero \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfying \(J(x^*)d=0\). Then there exist neighborhoods \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) of \(x^*\) and \(V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) of \(\lambda^*\), and \(\bar\rho>0\), such that for every \(\lambda\in V\) and \(\rho\geq\bar\rho\), the function \(\mathcal L_\rho(\cdot,\lambda)\) has a strict local minimizer in \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a twice continuously differentiable equality-constrained problem, LICQ and the strong second-order sufficient condition ensure that the quadratic augmented Lagrangian has a nearby strict local minimizer for every nearby multiplier and every sufficiently large penalty.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(x^*\).
\((x^*,\lambda^*)\) satisfies the KKT equations and \(J(x^*)\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For all \(\lambda\) sufficiently near \(\lambda^*\) and all sufficiently large \(\rho\), \(\mathcal L_\rho(\cdot,\lambda)\) has a strict local minimizer near \(x^*\).

notation.meaning: Ordinary Lagrangian f(x) plus lambda-transpose c(x).
Jacobian Dc(x) of the equality-constraint mapping.
Quadratic augmented Lagrangian with penalty parameter rho.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be twice continuously differentiable, and consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\). Define \(L_c(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^T h(x)+(c/2)\|h(x)\|^2\). Let \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) satisfy the KKT conditions and the second-order sufficient condition with \(\nabla h(x^*)\) of full column rank.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, smooth equality-constrained problems near a regular strict local solution; the definition concerns existence in a prescribed neighborhood, not global minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The augmented subproblem has the local-minimizer existence property at \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) if there are \(\bar c,\delta,\varepsilon>0\) such that, for every \(c\geq\bar c\) and \(\|\lambda-\lambda^*\|<\delta c\), the restricted problem \[\min_{\|x-x^*\|<\varepsilon}L_c(x,\lambda)\] has a solution \(x(\lambda,c)\), and this solution is an unconstrained local minimizer of \(L_c(\cdot,\lambda)\). The strong local-existence property additionally requires uniqueness in the neighborhood and \(\nabla_{xx}^2L_c(x(\lambda,c),\lambda)\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the smooth equality-constrained problem, local-minimizer existence means that one neighborhood of the reference solution and one sufficiently large penalty threshold work uniformly: whenever \(c\) exceeds the threshold and the scaled multiplier discrepancy \(\|\lambda-\lambda^*\|/c\) is small, the augmented Lagrangian possesses a local minimizer inside that neighborhood. Strong local existence includes uniqueness there and positive definiteness of the augmented Hessian.
assumptions_latex: \(\nabla h(x^*)\) has rank \(m\), and the Lagrangian Hessian is positive definite on \(\{d:\nabla h(x^*)^Td=0\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Under the stated smooth regularity, the strong property is equivalently represented by a locally defined branch \(x(\lambda,c)\) satisfying \(\nabla_xL_c(x(\lambda,c),\lambda)=0\) and \(\nabla_{xx}^2L_c(x(\lambda,c),\lambda)\succ0\).
special_cases_latex: For \(\lambda=\lambda^*\), \(x^*\) itself is a strict local minimizer of \(L_c(\cdot,\lambda^*)\) for every sufficiently large \(c\).
immediate_consequences_latex: For each fixed \(\lambda\), the condition \(\|\lambda-\lambda^*\|<\delta c\) holds for all sufficiently large \(c\).
boundary_notes: The property does not assert that the augmented Lagrangian is bounded below or has a global minimizer.
Without regularity and second-order sufficiency, a nearby stationary point need not be a local minimizer.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stable tracking of an augmented minimizer
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(L_c(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^Th(x)+(c/2)\|h(x)\|^2\), let \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) be a regular local solution–multiplier pair satisfying second-order sufficiency. Let \(x(\lambda,c)\) denote the unique minimizer of \(L_c(\cdot,\lambda)\) in a fixed neighborhood of \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local, smooth, finite-dimensional stability of a selected isolated minimizer branch with respect to multiplier and penalty parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The augmented minimizer is stable at \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) if there exist \(\bar c,\delta,\varepsilon,M>0\) such that \(x(\lambda,c)\) is uniquely defined whenever \(c\geq\bar c\) and \(\|\lambda-\lambda^*\|<\delta c\), is continuously differentiable on the interior of this parameter region, and satisfies \[\|x(\lambda,c)-x^*\|\leq M\frac{\|\lambda-\lambda^*\|}{c}.\] Isolation means that no other local minimizer of \(L_c(\cdot,\lambda)\) lies in \(B_\varepsilon(x^*)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stability means that the nearby augmented minimizer is a uniquely selected, isolated branch that varies continuously differentiably with the multiplier and penalty. Its displacement from the reference solution is uniformly bounded by a constant times the scaled multiplier error \(\|\lambda-\lambda^*\|/c\). Thus larger augmentation suppresses the primal displacement caused by a fixed multiplier perturbation.
assumptions_latex: \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) satisfies KKT, full-rank equality-constraint regularity, and second-order sufficiency.
\(\bar c\) is chosen so that \(\nabla_{xx}^2L_{\bar c}(x^*,\lambda^*)\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x(\cdot,\cdot)\in C^1(\operatorname{int}D)\) and \(\|x(\lambda,c)-x^*\|\leq M\|\lambda-\lambda^*\|/c\) for \(D=\{(\lambda,c):c\geq\bar c,\ \|\lambda-\lambda^*\|<\delta c\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(t=(\lambda-\lambda^*)/c\), stability is a local Lipschitz estimate \(\|x(t,c)-x^*\|\leq M\|t\|\), uniform over \(c\geq\bar c\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\lambda=\lambda^*\), the estimate forces \(x(\lambda^*,c)=x^*\) throughout the stability region.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every parameter sequence in the stability region with \(\|\lambda_k-\lambda^*\|/c_k\to0\) satisfies \(x(\lambda_k,c_k)\to x^*\).
boundary_notes: Stability applies to the selected local branch and does not exclude remote local minimizers.
The estimate does not by itself guarantee convergence of an algorithm that selects a different minimizer branch.

notation.meaning: Open Euclidean ball centered at the reference solution.

children.title: Augmented-Minimizer Localization
children.top_down_role: Local tracking of augmented minimizers near a reference solution.

assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(x^*\).
LICQ and the strong second-order sufficient condition hold at \((x^*,\lambda^*)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists U,V,\bar\rho:\ \forall\lambda\in V,\ \rho\geq\bar\rho,\ \exists!x(\lambda,\rho)\in U\text{ stationary, and it is a strict local minimizer};\quad x(\lambda,\rho)\to x^*.

notation.meaning: localized stationary point and strict local minimizer

review_flags: The theorem states qualitative localization only; quantitative rates are intentionally left to their canonical sibling nodes.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform local selection of the smooth augmented-subproblem minimizer near a regular strongly sufficient KKT pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal L_\rho(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\langle\lambda,c(x)\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\|c(x)\|^2\). If \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) is an equality-constrained KKT pair, \(f\) and \(c\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(x^*\), and LICQ and the strong second-order sufficient condition hold there, then there exist neighborhoods \(U\) of \(x^*\) and \(V\) of \(\lambda^*\) and \(\bar\rho>0\) such that, for every \(\lambda\in V\) and \(\rho\geq\bar\rho\), \(\mathcal L_\rho(\cdot,\lambda)\) has a unique stationary point \(x(\lambda,\rho)\) in \(U\). This point is a strict local minimizer, and \(x(\lambda,ho)\to x^*\) whenever \(\lambda\to\lambda^*\) and \(\rho\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a KKT pair satisfying LICQ and strong second-order sufficiency, every nearby multiplier and sufficiently large penalty determine one nearby strict augmented minimizer, which localizes at the primal solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Augmented-Minimizer Localization
Augmented-Minimizer Localization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Localization of the smooth augmented-subproblem minimizer near a regular KKT point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under LICQ and the strong second-order sufficient condition at \((x^*,\lambda^*)\), there exist neighborhoods \(U\) of \(x^*\) and \(V\) of \(\lambda^*\), and constants \(\bar\rho,C>0\), such that each \(\lambda\in V\) and \(\rho\geq\bar\rho\) determine a unique stationary point \(x(\lambda,\rho)\in U\) of \(\mathcal L_\rho(\cdot,\lambda)\). This point is a strict local minimizer and satisfies
\[\lVert x(\lambda,\rho)-x^*\rVert\leq C\bigl(\lVert\lambda-\lambda^*\rVert/\rho+1/\rho\bigr).\]
Consequently, \(x(\lambda_k,\rho_k)\to x^*\) whenever \(\lambda_k\to\lambda^*\) and \(\rho_k\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a regular strongly sufficient KKT point, the unique nearby augmented minimizer remains localized and converges to the primal solution as the penalty grows.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(x^*\).
LICQ and the strong second-order sufficient condition hold at \((x^*,\lambda^*)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The nearby augmented minimizer is unique in \(U\) and converges to \(x^*\) as \((\lambda,1/\rho)\to(\lambda^*,0)\).

children.title: Isolated Augmented Minimizers
children.top_down_role: Regimes in which relevant augmented minimizers remain locally separated.

knowledge_statements.title: Isolated Augmented Minimizers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local isolation for a fixed multiplier and penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^m\) and \(\rho>0\), and let \(B_r(\bar x)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\lVert x-\bar x\rVert<r\}\). A point \(\bar x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) is an isolated local minimizer of \(\mathcal L_\rho(\cdot,\lambda)\) if there exists \(r>0\) such that
\[\mathcal L_\rho(x,\lambda)>\mathcal L_\rho(\bar x,\lambda)\quad\text{for every }x\in B_r(\bar x)\setminus\{\bar x\}.\]
It has local quadratic growth if there exist \(\alpha>0\) and \(r>0\) such that
\[\mathcal L_\rho(x,\lambda)\geq\mathcal L_\rho(\bar x,\lambda)+\alpha\lVert x-\bar x\rVert^2\quad\text{for every }x\in B_r(\bar x).\]
Local quadratic growth implies that \(\bar x\) is an isolated local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An augmented minimizer is isolated when it is the unique minimizer of the augmented Lagrangian in some neighborhood. A local positive quadratic-growth bound is a stronger sufficient property for isolation.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal L_\rho(\cdot,\lambda)\) is defined on a neighborhood of \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Isolation means that \(\bar x\) is the unique minimizer on some ball about itself; local quadratic growth supplies the bound \(\mathcal L_\rho(x,\lambda)\geq\mathcal L_\rho(\bar x,\lambda)+\alpha\lVert x-\bar x\rVert^2\).

notation.meaning: Open Euclidean ball of radius r centered at bar x.

notation.meaning: Hessian of the fixed augmented Lagrangian with respect to the primal variable

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order sufficient certificate for quadratic growth of a fixed smooth augmented subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \((\lambda,\rho)\). Suppose \(x\mapsto\mathcal L_\rho(x,\lambda)\) is twice continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\), \(\nabla_x\mathcal L_\rho(\bar x,\lambda)=0\), and \(\nabla^2_{xx}\mathcal L_\rho(\bar x,\lambda)\succ0\). Then there exist \(r>0\) and \(\alpha>0\) such that \[\mathcal L_\rho(x,\lambda)\geq\mathcal L_\rho(\bar x,\lambda)+\alpha\|x-\bar x\|^2\qquad(x\in B_r(\bar x)).\] Hence \(\bar x\) is an isolated strict local minimizer of the fixed augmented subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stationary point with positive-definite augmented-Lagrangian Hessian has local quadratic growth and is therefore an isolated strict local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Definite Hessian Certificate for Isolation

assumptions_latex: \(f(x)=x^4\) and the constraint mapping is identically zero, so the augmented subproblem objective is \(\mathcal L_\rho(x,\lambda)=x^4\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\text{ is an isolated strict local minimizer, but }\nexists\alpha,r>0\text{ such that }x^4\geq\alpha x^2\text{ for all }|x|<r.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp converse boundary for the seed's quadratic-growth implication.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Take the unconstrained instance \(f(x)=x^4\), equivalently an augmented-Lagrangian model with constraint mapping identically zero. Then \(\mathcal L_\rho(x,\lambda)=x^4\) for every fixed \((\lambda,\rho)\). The point \(0\) is an isolated strict local minimizer, but there are no \(\alpha>0\) and \(r>0\) such that \(x^4\geq\alpha x^2\) for every \(|x|<r\). Thus isolation does not imply local quadratic growth without additional curvature assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The fourth-power augmented subproblem has an isolated strict minimizer at zero but no positive quadratic-growth modulus.

children.title: Loss of Local Isolation
children.top_down_role: Boundaries where nearby augmented minimizers cease to be locally distinguishable.

knowledge_statements.title: Loss of Local Isolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Flat tangent directions can destroy isolation even with positive penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(f(x_1,x_2)=0\) and the equality constraint \(c(x_1,x_2)=x_1=0\). For \(\lambda=0\) and every \(\rho>0\),
\[\mathcal L_\rho(x_1,x_2,0)=\frac{\rho}{2}x_1^2.\]
Every point \((0,t)\), with \(t\in\mathbb{R}\), is a global minimizer. Hence no such point is an isolated augmented minimizer. The failure is caused by the unconstrained flat direction \((0,1)\): the Lagrangian Hessian has zero curvature on the tangent space, so the strong second-order sufficient condition is absent and increasing \(\rho\) cannot create tangent curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive penalty cannot isolate minimizers along a flat feasible direction; a simple two-variable example has an entire line of augmented minimizers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The minimizer set is \(\{(0,t):t\in\mathbb{R}\}\), so every augmented minimizer loses local isolation.

notation.meaning: Free coordinate along the feasible line.

children.title: Solution-Mapping Stability
children.top_down_role: Stability of primal solutions under multiplier and penalty changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Mapping Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local Lipschitz stability with respect to multiplier and reciprocal penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be twice continuously differentiable near \(x^*\), and define \(\mathcal L_\rho(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}c(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert c(x)\rVert_2^2\). Suppose \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) satisfies the equality-constrained KKT conditions, LICQ, and the strong second-order sufficient condition. Then there exist neighborhoods \(V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) of \(\lambda^*\) and \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) of \(x^*\), a number \(\bar\tau>0\), and a single-valued mapping \(x:V\times[0,\bar\tau)\to U\) with \(x(\lambda,0)=x^*\), such that for every \(\lambda\in V\) and \(0<\tau<\bar\tau\), the point \(x(\lambda,\tau)\) is the unique nearby stationary point and a strict local minimizer of \(\mathcal L_{1/\tau}(\cdot,\lambda)\). Moreover, there is \(K>0\) such that
\[\lVert x(\lambda_1,\tau_1)-x(\lambda_2,\tau_2)\rVert\leq K\bigl(\lVert\lambda_1-\lambda_2\rVert+|\tau_1-\tau_2|\bigr)\]
whenever \((\lambda_i,\tau_i)\in V\times[0,\bar\tau)\) for \(i\in\{1,2\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under LICQ and strong second-order sufficiency, the localized augmented-Lagrangian minimizer extends to reciprocal penalty zero and varies locally Lipschitz-continuously with the multiplier and reciprocal penalty.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(x^*\).
\((x^*,\lambda^*)\) satisfies KKT, LICQ, and the strong second-order sufficient condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The localized mapping \((\lambda,\tau)\mapsto x(\lambda,\tau)\), with \(\tau=1/\rho\) for positive \(\tau\), is single-valued and locally Lipschitz on its stated domain.

notation.meaning: Reciprocal penalty parameter, extended to zero.
Localized augmented-subproblem solution, with value x-star at reciprocal penalty zero.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stability of the augmented-subproblem solution mapping
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(S(\lambda,c)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in B_\varepsilon(x^*)}L_c(x,\lambda)\), where \(L_c\) is the quadratic augmented Lagrangian of a smooth equality-constrained problem and \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) is a regular strict local solution–multiplier pair.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parametric stability of a local primal solution mapping; this is distinct from stability of an entire algorithmic sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The local solution mapping \(S\) is single-valued stable at the reference branch if there are \(\bar c,\delta,\varepsilon,M>0\) such that \[S(\lambda,c)=\{x(\lambda,c)\}\quad\text{for }c\geq\bar c,\ \|\lambda-\lambda^*\|<\delta c,\] the selection \(x\) is continuous on this region and continuously differentiable in its interior, and \[\operatorname{dist}(S(\lambda,c),x^*)=\|x(\lambda,c)-x^*\|\leq M\|\lambda-\lambda^*\|/c.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The solution mapping assigns to each multiplier–penalty pair the minimizers of the augmented subproblem in a fixed neighborhood. It is stable when this localized mapping is single-valued, continuous, differentiable away from the parameter-region boundary, and uniformly Lipschitz in the scaled perturbation \((\lambda-\lambda^*)/c\).
assumptions_latex: \(f,h\in C^2\) near \(x^*\), and \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) satisfies regularity and second-order sufficiency.
The localization radius \(\varepsilon\) is fixed independently of \((\lambda,c)\) in the stated parameter region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S(\lambda,c)=\{x(\lambda,c)\}\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(S(\lambda,c),x^*)\leq M\|\lambda-\lambda^*\|/c\) throughout the local parameter region.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(t=(\lambda-\lambda^*)/c\), the localized mapping admits a single-valued \(C^1\) selection near \(t=0\), uniformly for \(c\geq\bar c\).
special_cases_latex: At \(\lambda=\lambda^*\), the localized solution set is \(S(\lambda^*,c)=\{x^*\}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \((\lambda_k,c_k)\) remains admissible and \((\lambda_k-\lambda^*)/c_k\to0\), every selected solution converges to \(x^*\).
boundary_notes: The definition localizes the argmin mapping; global argmin mappings may be empty or set-valued.
Continuity of the selected primal solution does not imply boundedness of arbitrary multiplier sequences.

children.title: Global Convergence Principles
children.top_down_role: Global convergence organized by convexity, regularity, and penalty behavior.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global convergence of an augmented-Lagrangian process
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min\{f(x):x\in X,\ h(x)=0\}\), with closed \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and an augmented-Lagrangian process producing \((x^k,\lambda^k,c^k)\). Let \(\Omega\) denote the prescribed target set, such as the global primal solution set or the KKT set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequence-level global convergence from arbitrary admissible initialization; the target set must be specified by the convex or nonconvex regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The process is globally convergent to \(\Omega\) if every generated sequence satisfying its stated safeguards obeys \[\operatorname{Limsup}_{k\to\infty}\{(x^k,\lambda^k)\}\subseteq\Omega,\] equivalently, every convergent subsequence has its limit in \(\Omega\). Primal global convergence uses \(\operatorname{Limsup}\{x^k\}\subseteq X^*\); feasibility recovery additionally requires \(\operatorname{dist}(x^k,F)\to0\), where \(F=\{x\in X:h(x)=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global convergence is the property that every accumulation point produced from any admissible starting point belongs to the regime’s target set. For globally solved augmented subproblems with bounded multipliers and increasing penalties, the canonical target is the set of global primal solutions. In stationary nonconvex analyses, the target is instead a suitable KKT or generalized-stationary set.
assumptions_latex: The algorithmic class, admissible starts, subproblem accuracy, multiplier safeguard, and penalty behavior are fixed before asserting global convergence.
The target set \(\Omega\) is nonempty and is stated explicitly.
equivalent_formulations_latex: When the generated sequence is bounded, global convergence to a closed \(\Omega\) is equivalent to \(\operatorname{dist}((x^k,\lambda^k),\Omega)\to0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(x^k\) globally minimizes \(L_{c^k}(\cdot,\lambda^k)\), \(\{\lambda^k\}\) is bounded, and \(c^k\uparrow\infty\), the canonical conclusion is that every primal limit point is globally optimal.
immediate_consequences_latex: If the sequence is bounded and has a unique limit point in \(\Omega\), then the entire sequence converges to that point.
boundary_notes: Global convergence does not mean convergence to a global minimizer in every nonconvex method; the target may only be stationary.
A limit-point statement is vacuous for an unbounded sequence with no accumulation point unless boundedness or existence of limit points is also established.

notation.meaning: Outer limit, or set of subsequential limits, of a sequence.

children.title: Convex Global Convergence
children.top_down_role: Primal, dual, and saddle convergence families for convex programs.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\) be closed proper convex, let the equality constraints be affine, and suppose the primal–dual solution set \(\mathcal S^*\) is nonempty. For the exact method of multipliers, \(x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x L_{c_k}(x,\lambda^k)\) and \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+c_k h(x^{k+1})\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex programs with exact augmented-subproblem minimization and an existing saddle point; nonsmooth convex objectives are allowed when the argmin is well defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Convex global convergence means that, from every initial multiplier, the multiplier sequence approaches the dual solution set, primal residuals vanish, objective values approach the common primal–dual value, and every primal cluster point is optimal: \[\operatorname{dist}(\lambda^k,\Lambda^*)\to0,\qquad h(x^k)\to0,\qquad f(x^k)\to f^*,\qquad\operatorname{Limsup}\{x^k\}\subseteq X^*.\] If \(X^*\) or \(\Lambda^*\) is a singleton and the corresponding sequence is bounded, set convergence strengthens to point convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In the convex regime, global convergence couples four objects: multiplier convergence to the dual solution set, recovery of primal feasibility, convergence of objective values to the common optimal value, and optimality of every primal accumulation point. The method-of-multipliers update is also a proximal maximization step for the concave dual function, which supplies the canonical dual interpretation.
assumptions_latex: The primal problem is convex, the equality constraint is affine, and a primal–dual saddle point exists.
Each augmented subproblem is solved exactly, and \(c_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(\lambda^k,\Lambda^*)\to0\), \(h(x^k)\to0\), \(f(x^k)\to f^*\), and every primal cluster point lies in \(X^*\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The multiplier update is the proximal dual step \(\lambda^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{\lambda}\{q(\lambda)-(2c_k)^{-1}\|\lambda-\lambda^k\|^2\}\) for equality constraints.
special_cases_latex: If the primal solution is unique and \(\{x^k\}\) is bounded, then \(x^k\to x^*\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Any convergent primal–dual subsequence converges to a saddle point and has zero duality gap.
boundary_notes: Without uniqueness, the primal iterates need not converge to one point even when all cluster points are optimal.
The statement does not cover nonconvex objectives or merely local augmented-subproblem solutions.

children.title: Primal-Solution Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence behavior of primal sequences and solution sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Solution Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact convex ALM convergence for linearly constrained problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex, let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and suppose \(\min\{f(x):Ax=b\}\) has a primal-dual solution with optimal value \(p^*\). Fix \(\rho>0\) and \(\lambda^0\in\mathbb{R}^m\). For every integer \(k\geq0\), choose an attained exact minimizer
\[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left(f(x)+(\lambda^k)^{\mathsf T}(Ax-b)+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert Ax-b\rVert_2^2\right)\]
and set
\[\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}-b).\]
Then \(Ax^{k+1}-b\to0\), \(f(x^{k+1})\to p^*\), and every cluster point of \(\{x^k\}\) is primal optimal. If the primal solution is unique and \(\{x^k\}\) is bounded, then \(x^k\to x^*\), where \(x^*\) is the unique primal solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For exact convex augmented-Lagrangian iterations with linear equality constraints, feasibility residuals vanish, objective values approach the optimum, and all primal cluster points are optimal. If the primal solution is unique and the primal sequence is bounded, the entire sequence converges to that solution.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and a primal-dual solution exists.
Every augmented subproblem is solved exactly and attains its minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax^k-b\to0\), \(f(x^k)\to p^*\), and every cluster point of \(\{x^k\}\) is primal optimal; uniqueness together with boundedness implies \(x^k\to x^*\).

children.title: Dual-Value Convergence Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Convergence behavior of multipliers and associated values.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Correspondence between multiplier and value convergence
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For the equality-constrained problem, let \(q(\lambda)=\inf_x\{f(x)+\lambda^Th(x)\}\) be the dual function, let \(\Lambda^*=\operatorname*{argmax}q\), and define the augmented multiplier estimate \(\widetilde\lambda^k=\lambda^k+c_kh(x^k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional multiplier estimates and associated dual values; the definition distinguishes convergence of multipliers from convergence of scalar values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Dual-value convergence correspondence holds along an index set \(K\) if there exists \(\lambda^*\in\Lambda^*\) such that \[\widetilde\lambda^k\to\lambda^*\quad(k\in K),\qquad q(\widetilde\lambda^k)\to q(\lambda^*)=f^*.\] In a smooth regular local regime, the corresponding KKT relation is \[\nabla f(x^*)+\nabla h(x^*)\lambda^*=0,\qquad h(x^*)=0,\] where \(x^k\to x^*\) along \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The correspondence couples convergence of the augmented multiplier estimate with convergence of its dual value. Under regularity, a convergent primal subsequence and vanishing augmented-subproblem gradient determine a multiplier limit satisfying KKT. In a convex strong-duality regime, convergence to a dual-optimal multiplier associates that limit with the common primal–dual value.
assumptions_latex: \(\nabla h(x^*)\) has rank \(m\); for the value identity, strong duality and continuity of \(q\) at \(\lambda^*\) are assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widetilde\lambda^k\to\lambda^*\), the limit pair satisfies KKT, and in the convex strong-duality case \(q(\widetilde\lambda^k)\to f^*\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The multiplier estimate satisfies \(\nabla_xL_0(x^k,\widetilde\lambda^k)=\nabla_xL_{c_k}(x^k,\lambda^k)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\lambda^*\) is the unique dual solution, every convergent multiplier-estimate subsequence has the same limit.
immediate_consequences_latex: When \(\{\lambda^k\}\) and \(\{\widetilde\lambda^k\}\) are bounded while \(c_k\to\infty\), one has \(h(x^k)\to0\) along the convergent subsequence.
boundary_notes: Convergence of dual values alone does not imply convergence of multipliers when the dual solution set is not a singleton.
The KKT multiplier conclusion requires a constraint-regularity condition or an appropriate weaker substitute.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Sequence Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual convergence of exact convex ALM as a proximal-point iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex, let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and suppose \(\min\{f(x):Ax=b\}\) has a primal-dual solution. Let \(D^*\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) be the nonempty set of dual maximizers. Fix \(\rho>0\) and \(\lambda^0\in\mathbb{R}^m\), solve every augmented subproblem exactly, and update
\[\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}-b).\]
The multiplier update is a proximal-point iteration for the concave dual problem. Consequently, there exists \(\bar\lambda\in D^*\) such that \(\lambda^k\to\bar\lambda\), and
\[\operatorname{dist}(\lambda^k,D^*)\to0,\qquad \lVert\lambda^{k+1}-\lambda^k\rVert_2=\rho\lVert Ax^{k+1}-b\rVert_2\to0.\]
The dual values converge to the optimal dual value whenever the dual function is finite at the multiplier iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For exact convex augmented-Lagrangian iterations with a fixed positive penalty, the multiplier sequence is a dual proximal-point sequence and converges to a dual optimizer; its increments and the primal feasibility residuals vanish.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and a primal-dual solution exists.
Every augmented subproblem is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(\bar\lambda\in D^*\) such that \(\lambda^k\to\bar\lambda\) and \(\lambda^{k+1}-\lambda^k\to0\).

notation.meaning: Nonempty set of dual optimal multipliers.
Euclidean distance from a multiplier to the dual solution set.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Cumulative Proximal Progress Can Miss the Dual Solution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of exact variable-step proximal convergence when the positive step sizes have finite total mass.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T=I\) on \(\mathbb{R}\), so \(T^{-1}(0)=\{0\}\), and let \(\rho_k>0\) satisfy \(\sum_k\rho_k<\infty\). The exact iteration \[y^{k+1}=J_{\rho_kT}(y^k)=\frac{y^k}{1+\rho_k}\] converges to a nonzero point whenever \(y^0\neq0\). Thus positivity of variable penalties alone does not ensure convergence to a dual solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact proximal iterates can converge to a nonoptimal point when variable penalties provide only finite cumulative progress.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Cumulative Proximal Progress Can Miss the Dual Solution

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact convex affine ALM with variable positive penalties uniformly bounded away from zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex, and suppose \(\min\{f(x):Ax=b\}\) has a primal-dual solution with dual solution set \(D^*\neq\varnothing\). Let every augmented subproblem be solved to an attained global minimum and update \[y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho_k(Ax^{k+1}-b),\qquad \rho_k\geq\underline\rho>0.\] Equivalently, \(y^{k+1}=J_{\rho_kT}(y^k)\) for the maximal-monotone dual optimality operator \(T\). Then, in finite dimensions, \[y^k\to y^*\in D^*,\qquad y^{k+1}-y^k\to0,\qquad Ax^{k+1}-b\to0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact convex ALM retains multiplier convergence under variable penalties that remain uniformly positive.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex, and a primal-dual solution exists.
Every augmented subproblem has an attained exact minimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Penalty Dual-Sequence Convergence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of dual convergence to an optimizer when proximal parameters have finite total mass.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T=I\) on \(\mathbb{R}\), so \(T^{-1}(0)=\{0\}\), and let \(\rho_k>0\) satisfy \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\rho_k<\infty\). The exact proximal iteration \[y^{k+1}=J_{\rho_kT}(y^k)=\frac{y^k}{1+\rho_k}\] obeys \[y^k=y^0\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}(1+\rho_j)^{-1}\longrightarrow y^0\prod_{j=0}^{\infty}(1+\rho_j)^{-1}\neq0\] whenever \(y^0\neq0\). Thus positive penalties alone do not ensure convergence to a dual solution; a condition such as \(\inf_k\rho_k>0\), or another condition forcing sufficient cumulative proximal progress, is essential.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If variable penalties have finite total mass, even an exact proximal sequence can converge to a nonoptimal point.

notation.meaning: nonoptimal limit of the exact proximal sequence

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex, let \(c(x)=Ax-b\), and suppose the primal problem has value \(p^*\) and a primal-dual solution. children.top_down_role: Consistency between limiting dual sequences and limiting value quantities.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual–Value Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency between inexact augmented-subproblem values and the augmented dual-value sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a nonempty set, let \(m\in\mathbb{N}\), fix \(\rho>0\), and let \(L_\rho:X\times\mathbb{R}^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\). Define \(q_\rho(y)=\inf_{x\in X}L_\rho(x,y)\). Suppose \(y^k\in\mathbb{R}^m\), \(x^{k+1}\in X\), \(p^*\in\mathbb{R}\), and \(\varepsilon_k\geq0\) satisfy \[0\leq L_\rho(x^{k+1},y^k)-q_\rho(y^k)\leq\varepsilon_k.\] If \(\varepsilon_k\to0\) and \(q_\rho(y^k)\to p^*\), then \[L_\rho(x^{k+1},y^k)-q_\rho(y^k)\to0,\qquad L_\rho(x^{k+1},y^k)\to p^*.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed augmented-value function, vanishing subproblem value error makes the computed augmented values asymptotically equal to the augmented dual values; consequently, convergence of the latter to a finite value implies convergence of the former to the same value.

notation.meaning: augmented dual-value function obtained by minimizing over the primal domain

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Persistent Value Error Does Not Transfer Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for transferring augmented-dual value convergence to computed inexact subproblem values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{0,1\}\), with \(L_\rho(0,y)=0\) and \(L_\rho(1,y)=1\) for every \(y\), and choose \(x^{k+1}=1\). Then \(q_\rho(y^k)=0\to0\) and \[0\leq L_\rho(x^{k+1},y^k)-q_\rho(y^k)=1\leq\varepsilon_k\quad\text{for }\varepsilon_k=1,\] while \(L_\rho(x^{k+1},y^k)=1\not\to0\). Hence bounded, nonvanishing value errors do not transfer the augmented-dual limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded but persistent inner value error does not force computed augmented values to share the augmented-dual limit.

notation.meaning: infimum of the augmented-value function over the primal domain

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonconvex global convergence to feasible stationary points
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f,h\in C^1\) and consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\). An augmented-Lagrangian process generates \((x^k,\lambda^k,c_k)\), with stationarity residual \(r_k=\nabla_xL_{c_k}(x^k,\lambda^k)\) and estimate \(\widetilde\lambda^k=\lambda^k+c_kh(x^k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional nonconvex programs; the global conclusion concerns all regular accumulation points and is stationarity-based rather than global optimality-based.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The process is nonconvex globally convergent in the regular-limit sense if, from every admissible start, every accumulation point \(x^*\) satisfying \(\operatorname{rank}
abla h(x^*)=m\) is feasible and admits a multiplier \(\lambda^*\) such that \[h(x^*)=0,\qquad 
abla f(x^*)+
abla h(x^*)\lambda^*=0,\] and along the corresponding subsequence \(\widetilde\lambda^k	o\lambda^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonconvex problem, global convergence normally means that every regular accumulation point generated from any admissible start is a first-order constrained stationary point. It does not mean that the accumulation point is a global or even local minimizer. The augmented multiplier estimates must converge along the same subsequence to a KKT multiplier.
assumptions_latex: The considered subsequence satisfies \(x^k\to x^*\) and \(\nabla h(x^*)\) has rank \(m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every regular primal accumulation point \(x^*\) is feasible and forms a KKT pair with the subsequential limit of \(\widetilde\lambda^k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The conclusion is \(\operatorname{Limsup}\{(x^k,\widetilde\lambda^k)\}\subseteq\{(x,\lambda):h(x)=0,\ \nabla f(x)+\nabla h(x)\lambda=0\}\), restricted to regular primal limits.
special_cases_latex: If every accumulation point is regular and the generated sequence is bounded, all accumulation points are KKT points.
immediate_consequences_latex: If the KKT pair is unique and the sequence is bounded, the entire primal–estimate sequence converges to it.
boundary_notes: Singular accumulation points are not covered by the full-rank formulation.
KKT stationarity alone does not establish second-order stationarity or local optimality.

children.title: Feasibility-Recovery Regimes
children.top_down_role: Global regimes supporting recovery of primal feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Recovery Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonconvex feasibility recovery through globally controlled augmented subproblems and diverging penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty and compact, let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(c:X\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be continuous, and suppose \(c(\bar x)=0\) for some \(\bar x\in X\). For \(x\in X\), define \(L_{\rho_k}(x,y^k)=f(x)+\langle y^k,c(x)\rangle+\frac{\rho_k}{2}\|c(x)\|^2\). Suppose \(x^{k+1}\in X\), \(\{y^k\}\subset\mathbb{R}^m\) is bounded, \(\rho_k>0\) with \(\rho_k\to\infty\), and \[L_{\rho_k}(x^{k+1},y^k)\leq L_{\rho_k}(\bar x,y^k)+\varepsilon_k\] for a bounded sequence \(\varepsilon_k\geq0\). Then \(\|c(x^{k+1})\|=O(\rho_k^{-1/2})\), so \(c(x^{k+1})\to0\) and every accumulation point of \(\{x^{k+1}\}\) is feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact primal domain containing a feasible point, bounded multipliers and uniformly controlled augmented-subproblem values make a diverging quadratic penalty drive the constraint violation to zero at order at most the inverse square root of the penalty.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty and compact, and \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(c:X\to\mathbb{R}^m\) are continuous.
There is \(\bar x\in X\) with \(c(\bar x)=0\), and every \(x^{k+1}\) lies in \(X\).
\(\{y^k\}\) and \(\{\varepsilon_k\}\) are bounded, \(\varepsilon_k\geq0\), \(\rho_k\to\infty\), and the displayed comparison holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|c(x^{k+1})\|=O(\rho_k^{-1/2})\to0\), and every accumulation point of \(\{x^{k+1}\}\) is feasible.

notation.meaning: equality-constraint mapping on the compact primal domain

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Penalty-Scale Multipliers Can Defeat Feasibility Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of diverging-penalty feasibility recovery without multiplier control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[0,1]\), \(f(x)=0\), \(c(x)=x\), \(\bar x=0\), \(\rho_k=k\), \(y^k=-k\), and \(x^{k+1}=1\). Then \[L_{\rho_k}(x^{k+1},y^k)=-k/2\leq0=L_{\rho_k}(\bar x,y^k),\] but \(c(x^{k+1})=1\) for every \(k\). Thus a diverging quadratic penalty and global value comparison need not recover feasibility when multipliers grow on the penalty scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Penalty-scale multipliers can cancel the quadratic feasibility term, so diverging penalties alone do not force feasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Penalty-Scale Multipliers Can Defeat Feasibility Recovery

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F=\{x\in X:h(x)=0\}\neq\varnothing\), and let \(\{x^k\}\subseteq X\) be generated by minimizing or approximately minimizing quadratic augmented Lagrangians with penalties \(c_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained finite-dimensional problems; recovery may be expressed through residuals or distance to the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sequence is in a feasibility-recovery regime if \[\|h(x^k)\|\to0.\] It has strong feasibility recovery if additionally \(\operatorname{dist}(x^k,F)\to0\). For continuous \(h\), every convergent subsequence with vanishing residual has a feasible limit; if \(\{x^k\}\) is bounded and \(F\) is closed, residual recovery plus an error bound \(\operatorname{dist}(x,F)\leq\kappa\|h(x)\|\) implies strong recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasibility recovery is the asymptotic disappearance of the constraint violation. Strong recovery asks that the iterates themselves approach the feasible set. For exact global augmented-subproblem minimizers, bounded multipliers and penalties increasing without bound form a canonical recovery regime. For approximate stationary subproblems, regularity is needed to rule out convergence to infeasible stationary points of the squared violation.
assumptions_latex: For the canonical global-minimizer regime, \(x^k\) globally minimizes \(L_{c_k}(\cdot,\lambda^k)\), \(\{\lambda^k\}\) is bounded, and \(c_k\uparrow\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|h(x^k)\|\to0\); under a local or global error bound, \(\operatorname{dist}(x^k,F)\to0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(h\) is continuous, \(\|h(x^k)\|\to0\) is equivalent to every existing primal limit point being feasible, provided the residual sequence itself converges to zero.
special_cases_latex: For affine constraints \(h(x)=Ax-b\), a Hoffman-type bound converts residual convergence into distance-to-feasibility convergence.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every primal cluster point lies in \(F\) when \(h\) is continuous.
boundary_notes: Stationarity of \(\|h\|^2\) does not imply feasibility at rank-deficient points.
Feasibility recovery alone says nothing about objective optimality.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unbounded Multipliers Can Defeat Penalty Feasibility Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failure of the seed's diverging-penalty comparison argument without bounded multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[0,1]\), \(f(x)=0\), \(c(x)=x\), \(\bar x=0\), \(\rho_k=k\), and \(y^k=-k\). Choose \(x^{k+1}=1\). Then \[L_{\rho_k}(1,y^k)=-k+\frac{k}{2}=-\frac{k}{2}\leq0=L_{\rho_k}(0,y^k),\] so the augmented-value comparison holds with \(\varepsilon_k=0\), although \(c(x^{k+1})=1\) for every \(k\). Thus a diverging quadratic penalty and global value comparison do not recover feasibility when multipliers can grow on the penalty scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multipliers growing with the penalty can cancel the quadratic feasibility term, so diverging penalties alone do not force feasibility.

children.title: Stationary Limit-Point Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Stationary Limit-Point Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT stationarity of feasible limit points generated by approximate augmented-Lagrangian stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be continuously differentiable. Suppose \(x^{k+1}\to x^*\), \(c(x^{k+1})\to0\), and define \(\lambda^{k+1}=y^k+\rho_kc(x^{k+1})\), where \(y^k\in\mathbb{R}^m\) and \(\rho_k>0\). If \(\lambda^{k+1}\to\lambda^*\) and \[\|\nabla f(x^{k+1})+Dc(x^{k+1})^\top\lambda^{k+1}\|\to0,\] then \[c(x^*)=0,\qquad \nabla f(x^*)+Dc(x^*)^\top\lambda^*=0.\] Thus \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) satisfies the first-order KKT equations for minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a smooth equality-constrained problem, a convergent primal sequence with vanishing feasibility and stationarity residuals and convergent effective multipliers converges to a primal-multiplier pair satisfying the KKT equations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasible Stationary Approximations Can Lack a Finite KKT Multiplier
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating feasible primal limits from finite KKT-pair conclusions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{x:x^2=0\}\), let \(x^k=1/k\) and \(\lambda^k=-k/2\). Then \(x^k\to0\), \((x^k)^2\to0\), and \[1+2x^k\lambda^k=0,\] but \(|\lambda^k|\to\infty\). At the feasible limit, the KKT stationarity equation is \(1+2(0)\lambda=0\), which has no finite solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible, exactly stationary approximating sequence can have diverging multipliers and converge to a point with no KKT multiplier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^k\to0\) with zero stationarity residual, but no finite KKT multiplier exists at \(x=0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Feasible Stationary Approximations Can Lack a Finite KKT Multiplier

knowledge_statements.statement_title: KKT Characterization of Every Finite Residual Cluster Pair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subsequence form of nonconvex augmented-Lagrangian stationarity convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) and \(c\) be continuously differentiable. Suppose \(c(x^k)\to0\), define \(\lambda^k=y^{k-1}+\rho_{k-1}c(x^k)\), and assume \[\|\nabla f(x^k)+Dc(x^k)^\top\lambda^k\|\to0.\] If, along a subsequence \(K\), \((x^k,\lambda^k)\to(\bar x,\bar\lambda)\), then \[c(\bar x)=0,\qquad \nabla f(\bar x)+Dc(\bar x)^\top\bar\lambda=0.\] Hence every finite primal-effective-multiplier cluster pair is a KKT pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every finite cluster pair of a feasible, asymptotically stationary augmented-Lagrangian sequence satisfies the equality-constrained KKT equations.
assumptions_latex: \(c(x^k)\to0\) and the effective-multiplier stationarity residual tends to zero.
A subsequence of \((x^k,\lambda^k)\) converges to a finite pair.

notation.meaning: index set of a convergent subsequence

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(f,h\in C^1\), let \(r_k=\nabla_xL_{c_k}(x^k,\lambda^k)\) and \(\widetilde\lambda^k=\lambda^k+c_kh(x^k)\). Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb N\) be infinite with \(x^k\to x^*\) for \(k\in K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth nonconvex equality constraints and first-order stationarity of regular limit points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The subsequence lies in a stationary limit-point regime if \(r_k\to0\), \(h(x^*)=0\), and there exists \(\lambda^*\) such that \[\widetilde\lambda^k\to\lambda^*\quad(k\in K),\qquad \nabla f(x^*)+\nabla h(x^*)\lambda^*=0.\] A method has the stationary limit-point property if every accumulation point satisfying its stated constraint regularity admits such a multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stationary limit-point regime is one in which approximate augmented-subproblem stationarity passes to constrained KKT stationarity at every relevant accumulation point. The multiplier attached to the limit is obtained from the augmented estimates, not necessarily from the uncorrected multiplier sequence.
assumptions_latex: \(x^k\to x^*\) along \(K\), \(r_k\to0\), and \(\nabla h(x^*)\) has rank \(m\).
\(\{\lambda^k\}\) is bounded and \(c_k\to\infty\), ensuring feasibility once \(\{\widetilde\lambda^k\}_K\) is bounded.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\nabla_xL_0(x^k,\widetilde\lambda^k)=r_k\to0\), so any convergent pair \((x^k,\widetilde\lambda^k)\) has a stationary limit.
special_cases_latex: If \(m=0\), the condition reduces to unconstrained stationarity \(\nabla f(x^*)=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: When all accumulation points are regular, boundedness of the primal sequence guarantees existence of at least one KKT accumulation point.
boundary_notes: The definition excludes rank-deficient limits unless another constraint qualification supplies bounded multipliers.
It is a first-order property and does not classify the limit as a minimum, maximum, or saddle point.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal Convergence Without Multiplier Control Is Insufficient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating feasible primal limits from KKT-pair conclusions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Feasibility of a primal limit and vanishing augmented-Lagrangian stationarity residual do not by themselves yield a finite KKT multiplier. For \(\min\{x:x^2=0\}\), take \(x^k=1/k\) and \(\lambda^k=-k/2\). Then \(x^k\to0\), \(c(x^k)=(x^k)^2\to0\), and \[\nabla f(x^k)+c'(x^k)\lambda^k=1+2(1/k)(-k/2)=0,\] but \(|\lambda^k|\to\infty\). At the feasible limit, \(c'(0)=0\), so the KKT stationarity equation \(1+c'(0)\lambda=0\) has no finite solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible, exactly stationary approximating sequence can have diverging multipliers and converge to a point with no KKT multiplier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^k\to0\) and the stationarity residual is zero, but no finite KKT multiplier exists at \(x=0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Constraint-Qualification Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer from approximate KKT sequences to KKT limits under a weak sequential constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing a continuously differentiable \(f\) subject to continuously differentiable equalities \(h(x)=0\) and inequalities \(g(x)\leq0\). Let \(x^k\to x^*\) be feasible in the limit and suppose there are \(\lambda^k\) and \(\mu^k\geq0\) such that the Lagrangian stationarity residual tends to zero and \(\mu_i^k g_i(x^k)\to0\). If a weak sequential constraint qualification at \(x^*\), such as relaxed constant positive linear dependence, guarantees a bounded equivalent multiplier subsequence, then a subsequential limit \((\lambda^*,\mu^*)\) satisfies stationarity, dual feasibility, and complementarity. Thus \(x^*\) is a KKT point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weak sequential constraint qualification turns an approximate-KKT limit into a KKT point by ensuring that suitable multipliers remain bounded.
assumptions_latex: The iterates and multipliers form an approximate-KKT sequence converging primally to \(x^*\).
A weak sequential constraint qualification provides a bounded equivalent multiplier subsequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exist \(\lambda^*\) and \(\mu^*\ge0\) satisfying the KKT conditions at \(x^*\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(f,h\in C^1\), consider a feasible point \(x^*\) and sequences \(x^k\to x^*\), residuals \(r_k\to0\), and multiplier estimates \(\mu^k\) satisfying \(\nabla f(x^k)+\nabla h(x^k)\mu^k=r_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sequential, multiplier-boundedness formulation intended for singular nonconvex limit points; it is weaker in use than full-rank LICQ but is not identified here with one named modern constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A weak constraint-qualification regime at \(x^*\) is a regime in which every algorithmically admissible approximate-stationarity sequence \[(x^k,\mu^k,r_k)	o(x^*,\cdot,0),\qquad 
abla f(x^k)+
abla h(x^k)\mu^k=r_k,\] admits a subsequence for which \(\{\mu^k\}\) is bounded. Consequently, some subsequential limit \(\mu^*\) satisfies \[
abla f(x^*)+
abla h(x^*)\mu^*=0.\] Feasibility \(h(x^*)=0\) is required separately or supplied by the algorithm’s recovery property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The regime replaces full-rank constraint regularity by the exact property needed to pass approximate stationarity to a finite KKT multiplier: admissible multiplier estimates cannot escape to infinity without a bounded subsequence. Once feasibility is known, continuity yields a KKT multiplier at the limit.
assumptions_latex: \(x^*\) is feasible, \(f,h\in C^1\), and the admissible sequence class is specified by the augmented-Lagrangian method.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every admissible approximate-stationarity sequence has a subsequence \(K\) with \(\mu^k\to\mu^*\) and \(\nabla f(x^*)+\nabla h(x^*)\mu^*=0\).
special_cases_latex: Full column rank of \(\nabla h(x^*)\) implies local boundedness and uniqueness of equality-constraint multiplier estimates, hence satisfies this sequential requirement.
immediate_consequences_latex: Combined with feasibility recovery, the property makes every admissible limit point a KKT point.
boundary_notes: The source inspected establishes the stronger full-rank case but does not provide this sequential weak-CQ definition under a standard name.

children.title: Augmentation Boundedness Regimes
children.top_down_role: The interaction between multiplier control, constraint regularity, and finite augmentation.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(c_k>0\) be the penalty or augmentation parameters of an augmented-Lagrangian method, and let \(\lambda^k\) be its multiplier sequence.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification of an ALM run by asymptotic penalty behavior, with multiplier control recorded separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The run is in a bounded-augmentation regime if \[\sup_k c_k<\infty.\] It is eventually constant if \(\exists\bar k,\bar c>0\) such that \(c_k=\bar c\) for all \(k\geq\bar k\). It is in an unbounded-augmentation regime if \(\sup_kc_k=\infty\), and in a divergent-augmentation regime if \(c_k\to\infty\). A controlled augmentation regime additionally specifies \(\sup_k\|\lambda^k\|<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Augmentation boundedness classifies an augmented-Lagrangian run according to whether the penalty parameters remain below a finite ceiling, stabilize at a finite value, become merely unbounded, or actually diverge to infinity. Multiplier boundedness is a separate condition and must be stated rather than inferred from penalty behavior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Bounded augmentation is \(\sup_kc_k<\infty\); divergent augmentation is \(c_k\to\infty\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(\{c_k\}\) is nondecreasing, \(\sup_kc_k<\infty\) is equivalent to convergence to a finite \(c_\infty\), while \(\sup_kc_k=\infty\) is equivalent to \(c_k\to\infty\).
special_cases_latex: An eventually constant penalty sequence is bounded but need not be small; it may lie above a local convergence threshold.
immediate_consequences_latex: For nondecreasing update rules, every run falls into exactly one of the finite-limit and divergent-penalty regimes.
boundary_notes: Bounded penalty parameters do not alone imply bounded multipliers or convergence.
An oscillatory positive sequence can be unbounded without converging to infinity unless monotonicity is imposed.

notation.meaning: Finite limiting augmentation parameter when it exists.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Multiplier Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A compactness condition enabling extraction of limiting multipliers in global convergence arguments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For equality constraints \(c(x)=0\), define effective multipliers by \[\lambda^{k+1}=y^k+\rho_k c(x^{k+1}).\] The iteration is in a bounded-multiplier regime when there is a compact set \(Y\subset\mathbb{R}^m\) and an index \(k_0\) such that \(\lambda^{k+1}\in Y\) for every \(k\geq k_0\). Equivalently in finite dimensions, \(\sup_{k\geq k_0}\|\lambda^{k+1}\|<\infty\). Every subsequence of primal iterates then admits a further subsequence along which the corresponding effective multipliers converge, permitting passage from vanishing first-order residuals to limiting stationarity equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The regime requires effective multipliers to remain in a compact set, ensuring convergent multiplier subsequences for stationarity analysis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_k\|\lambda^{k+1}\|<\infty\), and every multiplier subsequence has a convergent further subsequence.

notation.meaning: effective multiplier at the new primal iterate

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\lambda^k\in\mathbb R^m\) be the multiplier iterates and \(\widetilde\lambda^k=\lambda^k+c_kh(x^k)\) the corrected multiplier estimates of an augmented-Lagrangian process.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional equality-constrained ALM sequences; raw and corrected multipliers are distinguished.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The process is in a bounded-multiplier regime if \[\sup_{k\geq0}\|\lambda^k\|<\infty.\] It is in a bounded-estimate regime if \(\sup_k\|\widetilde\lambda^k\|<\infty\), and in a jointly bounded regime if both bounds hold. A safeguard realizes the first regime when all iterates are constrained to a fixed bounded set \(B\subset\mathbb R^m\) containing at least one target multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplier boundedness means that all raw multiplier iterates stay in one bounded subset of multiplier space. This must be distinguished from boundedness of the corrected estimates \(\lambda^k+c_kh(x^k)\). Many convergence statements need one or both bounds, and a projection or rejection safeguard can enforce boundedness of the raw sequence.
assumptions_latex: The multiplier space is finite-dimensional and a fixed norm is used.
For a safeguarded regime, the safeguard set is bounded and contains a relevant solution multiplier.
equivalent_formulations_latex: In finite dimensions, boundedness is equivalent to relative compactness, so every multiplier subsequence has a convergent further subsequence.
special_cases_latex: If \(\lambda^{k+1}\) is left unchanged whenever a proposed update exits a prescribed bounded open set, the raw multiplier sequence remains bounded.
immediate_consequences_latex: If both multiplier sequences are bounded and \(c_k\to\infty\), then \(h(x^k)=(\widetilde\lambda^k-\lambda^k)/c_k\to0\).
boundary_notes: Bounded raw multipliers do not imply bounded corrected estimates when constraint residuals are large.
Boundedness does not imply convergence to a multiplier unless the limit set is further controlled.

children.title: Bounded-Penalty Regimes
children.top_down_role: Settings in which finite augmentation suffices for outer convergence.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Penalty Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility consequence when the penalty stabilizes at a positive finite value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the equality-constrained multiplier update \[y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho_k c(x^{k+1}).\] Suppose that for some \(\bar\rho>0\) and \(k_0\), \(\rho_k=\bar\rho\) whenever \(k\geq k_0\). If the multiplier increments satisfy \(\|y^{k+1}-y^k\|\to0\), then \[\|c(x^{k+1})\|=\bar\rho^{-1}\|y^{k+1}-y^k\|\longrightarrow0.\] Thus a finite stabilized augmentation parameter suffices to recover primal feasibility whenever the multiplier sequence is asymptotically regular; no divergence of the penalty is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Once a positive penalty stabilizes, vanishing multiplier increments imply vanishing constraint violation, so finite augmentation can recover feasibility.

notation.meaning: a bounded-above penalty sequence tending to zero

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity of a positive lower penalty bound for the increment-based feasibility test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Boundedness of the penalty from above is insufficient if the penalty can vanish. For example, let \(\rho_k=1/(k+1)\) and \(c(x^{k+1})=1\). The update identity gives \(y^{k+1}-y^k=1/(k+1)\to0\), although the feasibility residual remains equal to one. Thus vanishing multiplier increments imply feasibility only with an eventual positive lower bound on \(\rho_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A penalty tending to zero can make multiplier increments vanish while the constraint violation stays nonzero.
knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing-Penalty Failure Boundary

notation.meaning: uniform positive lower and finite upper penalty bounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility consequence for variable penalties confined to a compact positive interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the update \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho_kc(x^{k+1})\), suppose \(0<\underline\rho\leq\rho_k\leq\bar\rho<\infty\) for all sufficiently large \(k\). Then \[\|c(x^{k+1})\|=\rho_k^{-1}\|y^{k+1}-y^k\|\leq\underline\rho^{-1}\|y^{k+1}-y^k\|.\] Hence vanishing multiplier increments imply primal feasibility even when the bounded penalty varies and never becomes exactly constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eventual constancy is unnecessary: any penalty sequence bounded away from zero converts vanishing multiplier increments into vanishing feasibility residuals.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniformly Positive Variable-Penalty Variant

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(c_k>0\) be a nondecreasing penalty sequence in an augmented-Lagrangian method, and let \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) be a regular local solution–multiplier pair. Let \(\bar c\) denote a threshold above which the local augmented Hessian and multiplier iteration have the required stability properties.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local multiplier-method regime in which a finite penalty level is sufficient; this is not the pure quadratic penalty method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A run is in a bounded-penalty regime if \[0<c_k\leq C<\infty\quad\text{for all }k.\] For a nondecreasing sequence this is equivalent to \(c_k\to c_\infty<\infty\). It is a finite-sufficient-augmentation regime at \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) if, additionally, \(c_k\geq\bar c\) eventually and the selected local minimizers and multiplier updates converge to \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) without requiring \(c_k\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded-penalty regime keeps every augmentation parameter below a finite ceiling. In local multiplier methods, boundedness can coexist with convergence when the eventual penalty lies above a problem-dependent threshold and the algorithm tracks the correct nearby minimizer branch. This finite-augmentation behavior distinguishes multiplier methods from pure penalty methods, which generally require penalties tending to infinity.
assumptions_latex: For finite-sufficient augmentation, local regularity, second-order sufficiency, bounded multipliers, and correct local-minimizer selection hold after some index.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c_k\to c_\infty\in[\bar c,\infty)\) and convergence is obtained while \(\sup_kc_k<\infty\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For nondecreasing \(\{c_k\}\), boundedness is equivalent to convergence to a finite limit.
special_cases_latex: The constant-penalty choice \(c_k\equiv c\geq\bar c\) is the canonical bounded-penalty case.
immediate_consequences_latex: Finite augmentation avoids the necessity of progressively increasing the quadratic curvature contributed by \(c_k\nabla h\nabla h^T\).
boundary_notes: A bounded penalty below the convergence threshold need not stabilize the multiplier iteration.
The conclusion is local and depends on selecting the minimizer branch near \(x^*\).

children.title: Unbounded-Penalty Regimes
children.top_down_role: Convergence behavior when augmentation grows without stabilization.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded-Penalty Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility may survive diverging penalties while multiplier and stationarity convergence need not.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty and compact, let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(c:X\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be continuous, and let \(\bar x\in X\) satisfy \(c(\bar x)=0\). For \(x\in X\), define \(L_{\rho_k}(x,y^k)=f(x)+\langle y^k,c(x)\rangle+\frac{\rho_k}{2}\|c(x)\|^2\). Suppose \(x^{k+1}\in X\), \(\rho_k>0\) with \(\rho_k\to\infty\), \(\{y^k\}\subset\mathbb{R}^m\) is bounded, and \[L_{\rho_k}(x^{k+1},y^k)\leq L_{\rho_k}(\bar x,y^k)+\varepsilon_k\] for a bounded sequence \(\varepsilon_k\geq0\). These hypotheses imply \(c(x^{k+1})\to0\), but they alone imply neither boundedness of \(y^k+\rho_kc(x^{k+1})\) nor convergence of a first-order stationarity residual to zero. Consequently, KKT stationarity requires additional stationarity and multiplier-control hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact domain, a diverging penalty together with bounded multipliers and a uniform augmented-value comparison forces feasibility, but those value hypotheses alone do not control effective multipliers or guarantee KKT stationarity.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty and compact; \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(c:X\to\mathbb{R}^m\) are continuous; and \(c(\bar x)=0\) for some \(\bar x\in X\).
The displayed augmented-value comparison holds for a bounded sequence \(\varepsilon_k\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c(x^{k+1})\to0\), but boundedness of \(y^k+\rho_kc(x^{k+1})\) and KKT stationarity do not follow without additional hypotheses.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit failure of effective-multiplier and stationarity control under a bounded augmented-value comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[-1,1]\), \(f(x)=0\), \(c(x)=x\), \(y^k=0\), and \(\rho_k\to\infty\). Choose \(x^{k+1}=\rho_k^{-1/2}\) once this point lies in \(X\). With the feasible comparison point \(\bar x=0\), \[\mathcal L_{\rho_k}(x^{k+1},0)=\tfrac12=\mathcal L_{\rho_k}(0,0)+\tfrac12,\qquad c(x^{k+1})=\rho_k^{-1/2}\to0.\] Nevertheless, the effective multiplier and the derivative of the augmented subproblem at \(x^{k+1}\) both equal \(\rho_kx^{k+1}=\sqrt{\rho_k}\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded augmented-value error can force feasibility at the inverse-square-root penalty scale while effective multipliers and stationarity residuals diverge.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Without Effective-Multiplier Control

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(c_k>0\) be the augmentation sequence for \(L_{c_k}(x,\lambda^k)=f(x)+(\lambda^k)^Th(x)+(c_k/2)\|h(x)\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Penalty or augmented-Lagrangian processes whose penalty parameter grows without bound; exact global-minimizer and approximate-stationary variants have different conclusions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A run is in the divergent-penalty regime if \[c_k\to\infty.\] In the canonical exact global-subproblem regime, \(\{\lambda^k\}\) is bounded and \(x^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}L_{c_k}(x,\lambda^k)\); then the intended limit property is that every primal accumulation point is feasible and globally optimal. In an approximate-stationary regime, one instead requires \(\|\nabla_xL_{c_k}(x^k,\lambda^k)\|\to0\), and regular accumulation points are required to be KKT points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unbounded-penalty regime is one in which the augmentation tends to infinity, not merely one having occasional large values. With exact global augmented-subproblem solutions and bounded multipliers, this is the classical regime for recovering global primal solutions. With only approximate stationarity, divergence of the penalty does not itself ensure optimality; regularity and multiplier-estimate control lead only to KKT conclusions.
assumptions_latex: Either exact global subproblem minimization is imposed, or the approximate-stationarity and regular-limit assumptions are stated explicitly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining condition is \(c_k\to\infty\); its canonical exact-minimization consequence is \(\operatorname{Limsup}\{x^k\}\subseteq X^*\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a nondecreasing positive sequence, \(c_k\to\infty\iff\sup_kc_k=\infty\).
special_cases_latex: The pure quadratic penalty method has \(\lambda^k\equiv0\) and ordinarily uses \(c_k\uparrow\infty\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If both \(\lambda^k\) and \(\lambda^k+c_kh(x^k)\) remain bounded, then \(h(x^k)\to0\).
boundary_notes: Growing penalties may make augmented subproblems increasingly ill-conditioned.
Penalty divergence does not prevent convergence to an infeasible stationary point when constraint regularity fails and only subproblem stationarity is enforced.

notation.meaning: Nondecreasing penalty sequence diverging to infinity.
