knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local primal–dual linear and superlinear rates
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(z^k=(x^k,\lambda^k)\) converge to a regular local solution–multiplier pair \(z^*=(x^*,\lambda^*)\). Define \(e_k=\|z^k-z^*\|\), or separate primal and dual errors \(e_k^x=\|x^k-x^*\|\) and \(e_k^\lambda=\|\lambda^k-\lambda^*\|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local asymptotic rates for smooth equality-constrained multiplier methods that track the stable augmented-minimizer branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The primal–dual sequence converges Q-linearly if there are \(q\in(0,1)\) and \(k_0\) such that \[e_{k+1}\leq q e_k\quad(k\geq k_0).\] It converges Q-superlinearly if \[\frac{e_{k+1}}{e_k}\to0.\] Separate primal and dual rates are defined by replacing \(e_k\) with \(e_k^x\) or \(e_k^\lambda\). In the local method-of-multipliers regime, a sufficiently large bounded penalty yields linear convergence, while \(c_k\to\infty\) yields superlinear convergence under the stated regularity and correct branch-selection assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local primal–dual rate theory measures how rapidly the combined primal and multiplier error shrinks once the iterates are near a regular solution pair. A uniform contraction gives Q-linear convergence; a contraction factor tending to zero gives Q-superlinear convergence. For the classical local multiplier method, a sufficiently large finite augmentation supports a linear rate, while increasing augmentation without bound supports a superlinear rate.
assumptions_latex: \(f,h\in C^2\), \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) satisfies full-rank regularity and second-order sufficiency, and the initial pair lies in the local attraction region.
Each augmented subproblem selects the stable local minimizer nearest \(x^*\), and the multiplier update is \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+c_kh(x^k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For sufficiently large bounded \(c_k\), \(e_{k+1}\leq q e_k\) eventually for some \(q<1\); if \(c_k\to\infty\), then \(e_{k+1}/e_k\to0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Q-superlinear convergence is equivalent to the existence of factors \(q_k\to0\) with \(e_{k+1}\leq q_ke_k\) eventually.
special_cases_latex: With a constant penalty \(c_k\equiv c\) above the local threshold, the asymptotic rate is linear.
If \(\lambda^k=\lambda^*\), augmented-minimizer stability gives zero local primal displacement for the exact selected branch.
immediate_consequences_latex: Q-linear convergence implies R-linear convergence of both component errors under any equivalent product norm.
Q-superlinear convergence of the combined error implies superlinear convergence of each nonzero component error along indices where that component is defined.
boundary_notes: The rate statement is local and does not establish entry into the attraction neighborhood.
Increasing \(c_k\) can improve the outer asymptotic rate while worsening conditioning of the inner augmented subproblem.
Inexact subproblem solutions require additional forcing conditions not included in this definition.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Local-Rate Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local primal sensitivity rate for exact augmented-Lagrangian minimizers near a regular solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), where \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) are twice continuously differentiable near a KKT pair \((x^*,y^*)\). Define \(L_\rho(x,y)=f(x)+\langle y,c(x)\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\|c(x)\|^2\). Assume LICQ and the strong second-order sufficient condition at \((x^*,y^*)\). Then there exist \(C>0\), \(\rho_0>0\), and neighborhoods of \(x^*\) and \(y^*\) such that, for every \(\rho\geq\rho_0\) and every admissible \(y\) in the multiplier neighborhood, the local minimizer \(x(y,\rho)\) of \(L_\rho(\cdot,y)\) in the primal neighborhood satisfies \[\|x(y,\rho)-x^*\|\leq\frac{C}{\rho}\|y-y^*\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a regular KKT pair satisfying strong second-order sufficiency, the exact local augmented-Lagrangian minimizer has primal error bounded by a penalty-independent constant times the multiplier error divided by the penalty.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) are twice continuously differentiable near \((x^*,y^*)\).
LICQ and the strong second-order sufficient condition hold at the KKT pair \((x^*,y^*)\).
\(x(y,\rho)\) is the local minimizer of \(L_\rho(\cdot,y)\) on the asserted local branch, and \(\rho\geq\rho_0\).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local primal-rate family for augmented-Lagrangian iterates
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), let \(x^*\) solve \(\min\{f(x):h(x)=0\}\), and let \(x^k\) be the primal points produced by augmented-Lagrangian subproblems with multipliers \(\lambda^k\) and penalties \(c_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional equality-constrained smooth ALM; the definition concerns asymptotic local behavior after the iterates enter a neighborhood of one designated solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A primal local-rate family is specified by a nonnegative error functional \(E_x:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R_+\), with \(E_x(x^*)=0\), and a comparison function \(\varphi:\mathbb R_+\times\mathbb R_+\to\mathbb R_+\), such that for some \(k_0\), \[E_x(x^{k+1})\leq \varphi(E_x(x^k),c_k),\qquad k\geq k_0.\] The canonical distance member uses \(E_x(x)=\|x-x^*\|\). It is locally Q-linear when \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}E_x(x^{k+1})/E_x(x^k)<1\), Q-superlinear when that limit superior is zero, and of Q-order at least \(p>1\) when \(E_x(x^{k+1})\leq C E_x(x^k)^p\) eventually.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The family measures the asymptotic error of augmented primal points relative to a fixed solution. An error functional vanishing at that solution is chosen, normally \(E_x(x)=\|x-x^*\|\), and the tail errors must satisfy \(E_x(x^{k+1})\leq\varphi(E_x(x^k),c_k)\). A ratio strictly below one defines local Q-linear behavior, a ratio tending to zero defines Q-superlinear behavior, and an eventual bound by \(C E_x(x^k)^p\) defines Q-order at least \(p>1\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For the canonical error, local Q-linear convergence is equivalently certified by \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}\|x^{k+1}-x^*\|/\|x^k-x^*\|\leq q\) for some \(q<1\).
special_cases_latex: The ALM sensitivity estimate \(\|x^k-x^*\|\leq M\|\lambda^k-\lambda^*\|/c_k\) couples the primal family to multiplier error and penalty size.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(\|x^k-x^*\|\leq M\|\lambda^k-\lambda^*\|/c_k\) and the right-hand side tends to zero, then the primal sequence converges to \(x^*\).
boundary_notes: The definition does not assert that a particular ALM enters the local neighborhood or selects the intended local augmented minimizer.
R-linear bounds on an auxiliary sequence are not identical to Q-linear contraction of consecutive primal errors.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local multiplier-rate family for the method of multipliers
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(\min\{f(x):h(x)=0\}\), let \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) be a regular local primal–dual solution and consider \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+c_kh(x^k)\), where \(x^k\) locally minimizes \(L_{c_k}(x,\lambda^k)=f(x)+(\lambda^k)^Th(x)+(c_k/2)\|h(x)\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth equality-constrained method of multipliers near a regular solution satisfying a second-order sufficient condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A multiplier local-rate family is a collection of asymptotic bounds for \(e_k^\lambda=\|\lambda^k-\lambda^*\|\) of the form \[e_{k+1}^\lambda\leq \psi_k(e_k^\lambda),\qquad k\geq k_0,\] where \(\psi_k(0)=0\). Its Q-linear members satisfy \(e_{k+1}^\lambda\leq q e_k^\lambda\) eventually for some \(q\in(0,1)\); its Q-superlinear members satisfy \(e_{k+1}^\lambda/e_k^\lambda\to0\), with the ratio taken only where \(e_k^\lambda>0\). A penalty-explicit member has \(e_{k+1}^\lambda\leq (M/c_k)e_k^\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The object classified is the multiplier error \(e_k^\lambda=\|\lambda^k-\lambda^*\|\) generated by the method-of-multipliers update. A local-rate member is an eventual recursion \(e_{k+1}^\lambda\leq\psi_k(e_k^\lambda)\). Uniform contraction by a factor below one is Q-linear; a consecutive-error ratio tending to zero is Q-superlinear. ALM sensitivity theory supplies the important penalty-dependent member \(e_{k+1}^\lambda\leq(M/c_k)e_k^\lambda\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Q-superlinear multiplier convergence is equivalently \(\|\lambda^{k+1}-\lambda^*\|=o(\|\lambda^k-\lambda^*\|)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(c_k\equiv c>M\), the penalty-explicit estimate gives Q-linear contraction factor at most \(M/c\).
If \(c_k\to\infty\), the same estimate gives Q-superlinear multiplier convergence.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every Q-linear or Q-superlinear member implies \(\lambda^k\to\lambda^*\) once the defining recursion holds and the initial local error is finite.
boundary_notes: The definition concerns convergence to one selected multiplier; nonunique multiplier sets require a distance-to-set error instead.
Multiplier convergence alone does not specify the cost of solving each augmented subproblem.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Merit-Function Descent of the Primal-Dual Newton Step
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the Newton iteration quantities \(H^k\) and \(N^k\) defined outside the extracted proposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^*\) be a regular local minimum and let \(\lambda^*\) be a corresponding multiplier such that \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) satisfies the second-order sufficient conditions. There is a neighborhood \(S\) of \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) such that, whenever \((x^k,\lambda^k)\in S\) and \(x^k\ne x^*\), the next primal-dual Newton iterate is well defined and: (a) there exists \(\bar c\) such that, for every \(c\ge\bar c\), \(x^{k+1}-x^k\) is a descent direction for \(f(x)+c\max_{1\le i\le m}|h_i(x)|\) at \(x^k\); (b) \((x^{k+1}-x^k,\lambda^{k+1}-\lambda^k)\) is a descent direction for \(P(x,\lambda)=\tfrac12\|\nabla L(x,\lambda)\|^2\), and for every \(r>0\) there exists \(\delta>0\) such that \(\|(x^k-x^*,\lambda^k-\lambda^*)\|<\delta\) implies \(P(x^{k+1},\lambda^{k+1})\le rP(x^k,\lambda^k)\); and (c) whenever \(H^k+cN^k(N^k)'\succ0\), \(x^{k+1}-x^k\) is a descent direction for \(L_c(\cdot,\lambda^{k+1})\) at \(x^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a regular solution satisfying second-order sufficiency, the primal-dual Newton step is well defined. It descends a sufficiently heavily weighted exact constraint penalty, descends the squared KKT-residual merit function with an arbitrarily small local contraction factor, and descends the augmented Lagrangian whenever the stated augmented Hessian is positive definite.
assumptions_latex: x^*\text{ is a regular local minimum}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The Newton iterate is well defined and satisfies the exact-penalty descent, residual-merit descent and local contraction, and conditional augmented-Lagrangian descent properties stated above.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Superlinear Convergence of the Primal-Dual Newton Iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies to the Newton iteration denoted by equations (4.96)–(4.97) in the extract and to the equality-constrained second-order sufficiency conditions referenced there.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^*\) be a regular strict local minimum and let \(\lambda^*\) be a corresponding Lagrange multiplier such that \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) satisfies the second-order sufficient conditions. Then \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) is a point of attraction of the primal-dual Newton iteration (4.96)–(4.97). Whenever the generated sequence converges to \((x^*,\lambda^*)\), \(\|(x^k,\lambda^k)-(x^*,\lambda^*)\|\) converges superlinearly. If \(\nabla^2f\) and every \(\nabla^2h_i\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), are Lipschitz continuous near \(x^*\), the order is at least two.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regular strict local solution satisfying the second-order sufficient conditions is locally attracting for the specified primal-dual Newton iteration. Convergence is superlinear, and is at least quadratic when the objective and constraint Hessians are locally Lipschitz.
assumptions_latex: x^*\text{ is a regular strict local minimum}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x^*,\lambda^*)\text{ is attracting and }\|(x^k,\lambda^k)-(x^*,\lambda^*)\|\text{ converges superlinearly; if the relevant Hessians are locally Lipschitz, the order is at least }2.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Linear Convergence of the Lagrangian Primal-Dual Iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies to the specific iteration denoted by equations (4.87)–(4.88) in the extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) and \(h\) be twice continuously differentiable, and let \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) be a local-minimum–Lagrange-multiplier pair. If \(x^*\) is regular and \(\nabla_{xx}^2L(x^*,\lambda^*)\succ0\), then there exists \(\bar\alpha>0\) such that, for every \(\alpha\in(0,\bar\alpha]\), \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) is a point of attraction of the Lagrangian primal-dual iteration (4.87)–(4.88). Whenever the generated sequence converges to \((x^*,\lambda^*)\), both \(\|x^k-x^*\|\) and \(\|\lambda^k-\lambda^*\|\) converge linearly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a regular local solution with a positive-definite Lagrangian Hessian, all sufficiently small positive step parameters make the specified Lagrangian primal-dual iteration locally attracting. Convergent primal and multiplier sequences then have linear rates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\bar\alpha>0\ \forall\alpha\in(0,\bar\alpha]:\ (x^*,\lambda^*)\text{ is attracting, and convergence implies linear rates for both }x^k\text{ and }\lambda^k.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Multiplier Rates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local Q-linear convergence for exact multiplier iterations with a sufficiently large fixed penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), where \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) are twice continuously differentiable near a KKT pair \((x^*,y^*)\). Define \(L_\rho(x,y)=f(x)+\langle y,c(x)\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\|c(x)\|^2\), assume LICQ and the strong second-order sufficient condition at \((x^*,y^*)\), let \(x^{k+1}\) be the local minimizer of \(L_\rho(\cdot,y^k)\) on the stable branch near \(x^*\), and set \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho c(x^{k+1})\). Then there exist \(C>0\), \(\rho_0>0\), and a neighborhood of \(y^*\) such that, for fixed \(\rho\geq\rho_0\) and multiplier iterates in that neighborhood, \[\|y^{k+1}-y^*\|\leq\frac{C}{\rho}\|y^k-y^*\|.\] If additionally \(\rho>C\), the multiplier sequence converges locally Q-linearly with contraction factor at most \(C/\rho<1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For exact local augmented-Lagrangian minimization near a regular strongly stable KKT pair, a sufficiently large fixed penalty gives local Q-linear convergence of the multiplier iterates.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) are twice continuously differentiable, and LICQ plus the strong second-order sufficient condition hold at \((x^*,y^*)\).
Each augmented subproblem selects the local minimizer on the stable branch near \(x^*\).
The penalty is fixed with \(\rho\geq\rho_0\) and \(\rho>C\), and the multiplier iterates remain in the asserted neighborhood.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Q-linear local convergence of ALM multipliers
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\lambda^k\to\lambda^*\) be a multiplier sequence in \(\mathbb R^m\) generated locally by \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+c_kh(x^k)\), and set \(e_k=\|\lambda^k-\lambda^*\|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic pointwise multiplier convergence in a fixed finite-dimensional norm; the definition is Q-linear rather than merely R-linear.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The multiplier sequence has a local Q-linear rate if there exist \(q\in(0,1)\) and \(k_0\in\mathbb N\) such that \[\|\lambda^{k+1}-\lambda^*\|\leq q\|\lambda^k-\lambda^*\|,\qquad k\geq k_0.\] Equivalently, it is enough that \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}e_{k+1}/e_k<1\), with zero errors omitted or interpreted as finite termination. A penalty-uniform linear family consists of bounds \(e_{k+1}\leq q(c_k)e_k\) with \(\sup_{k\geq k_0}q(c_k)<1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local Q-linear multiplier convergence means that, after some index, every multiplier error is at most a fixed fraction \(q<1\) of the preceding error. The equivalent asymptotic ratio test requires the upper limit of consecutive error ratios to be below one. When the contraction depends on the penalty, linearity requires the tail contraction factors to remain uniformly below one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\exists q\in(0,1),\ \exists k_0,\ \forall k\geq k_0:\ e_{k+1}\leq q e_k.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[\limsup_{k\to\infty}\frac{\|\lambda^{k+1}-\lambda^*\|}{\|\lambda^k-\lambda^*\|}<1.\]
There exist \(C>0\) and \(q\in(0,1)\) such that \(e_k\leq Cq^{k-k_0}\) for every \(k\geq k_0\).
special_cases_latex: Under \(e_{k+1}\leq(M/c_k)e_k\), any fixed or bounded-below penalty tail satisfying \(\inf_{k\geq k_0}c_k>M\) yields a linear contraction.
immediate_consequences_latex: The tail satisfies \(e_{k_0+j}\leq q^j e_{k_0}\), hence \(\lambda^k\to\lambda^*\).
boundary_notes: A bound on \(\limsup e_k^{1/k}\) below one gives R-linear convergence and need not give the displayed consecutive-error contraction.
The contraction factor is local and need not describe iterations before \(k_0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Superlinear Multiplier Rates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local Q-superlinear multiplier convergence obtained by increasing the penalty within the stable local branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\{y^k\}\subset\mathbb{R}^m\), let \(y^*\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and let \(\rho_k>0\). Suppose there are constants \(C>0\) and \(\rho_0>0\) and a neighborhood of \(y^*\) such that the exact augmented-Lagrangian iteration remains on its stable local-minimizer branch in that neighborhood and satisfies \[\|y^{k+1}-y^*\|\leq\frac{C}{\rho_k}\|y^k-y^*\|\] whenever \(\rho_k\geq\rho_0\). If \(\rho_k\to\infty\), then, for every sufficiently large index with \(y^k\neq y^*\), \[\frac{\|y^{k+1}-y^*\|}{\|y^k-y^*\|}\leq\frac{C}{\rho_k}\longrightarrow0.\] Thus either the multiplier iteration reaches \(y^*\) finitely or it converges locally Q-superlinearly to \(y^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the exact local multiplier contraction factor is bounded by a uniform constant divided by the penalty, increasing the penalty without bound gives Q-superlinear convergence unless the limiting multiplier is reached finitely.
assumptions_latex: The local estimate \(\|y^{k+1}-y^*\|\leq C\rho_k^{-1}\|y^k-y^*\|\) holds with a uniform \(C>0\).
The iterates remain on the stable local augmented-minimizer branch and \(\rho_k\to\infty\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Q-superlinear local convergence of ALM multipliers
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\lambda^k\to\lambda^*\) in \(\mathbb R^m\) under a method-of-multipliers update and define \(e_k=\|\lambda^k-\lambda^*\|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic multiplier convergence to a designated multiplier; finite termination is included as a degenerate faster case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The multiplier sequence converges locally Q-superlinearly to \(\lambda^*\) if \[\lim_{k\to\infty,\ e_k>0}\frac{\|\lambda^{k+1}-\lambda^*\|}{\|\lambda^k-\lambda^*\|}=0.\] Equivalently, \(e_{k+1}=o(e_k)\). A penalty-driven superlinear member is present when \(e_{k+1}\leq(M/c_k)e_k\) eventually and \(c_k\to\infty\). Q-order at least \(p>1\) is the stronger condition \(e_{k+1}\leq C e_k^p\) eventually.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiplier sequence is locally Q-superlinear when its next error is negligible relative to its current error: \(e_{k+1}/e_k\to0\). The condition is stronger than contraction by one fixed factor. In standard local ALM estimates, a bound \(e_{k+1}\leq(M/c_k)e_k\) becomes superlinear when the penalty tends to infinity. An order-\(p\) bound \(e_{k+1}\leq Ce_k^p\), with \(p>1\), is a stronger quantified member of this family.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For every \(q\in(0,1)\), there is \(k_q\) such that \(e_{k+1}\leq q e_k\) for all \(k\geq k_q\).
special_cases_latex: If \(e_{k+1}\leq(M/c_k)e_k\) and \(c_k\to\infty\), then \(e_{k+1}/e_k\leq M/c_k\to0\).
If an iterate equals \(\lambda^*\) and all later iterates remain there, convergence is finite and satisfies the superlinear convention.
immediate_consequences_latex: Q-superlinear convergence is eventually Q-linear with every prescribed contraction factor \(q\in(0,1)\).
boundary_notes: Increasing penalties can worsen conditioning of inner subproblems; the definition measures only the outer multiplier sequence.
Superlinear convergence does not by itself establish a particular polynomial order \(p>1\).

notation.meaning: optional quantified order greater than one

knowledge_statements.title: Penalty-Dependent Rate Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unified local rate classification by the asymptotic size of the penalty parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\{y^k\}\subset\mathbb{R}^m\), let \(y^*\in\mathbb{R}^m\), define \(e_k=\|y^k-y^*\|\), and let \(\rho_k\geq\rho_0>0\) and \(\eta_k\geq0\). Suppose a locally convergent augmented-Lagrangian iteration remains in the neighborhood where, for all sufficiently large \(k\), \[e_{k+1}\leq\left(\frac{C}{\rho_k}+\eta_k\right)e_k,\] with \(C>0\) and \(\eta_k\to0\). If \(\rho_k\equiv\bar\rho\) eventually and \(C/\bar\rho<1\), then the convergence is Q-linear. If \(\rho_k\to\infty\), then either \(e_k=0\) for some finite \(k\) or \(e_{k+1}/e_k\to0\) along the nonzero errors, so the convergence is Q-superlinear.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated local error recursion and vanishing normalized subproblem error, an eventually fixed penalty whose limiting contraction is below one gives Q-linear convergence, whereas a diverging penalty gives Q-superlinear convergence unless the limiting multiplier is reached finitely.
assumptions_latex: For all sufficiently large \(k\), \(e_{k+1}\leq(C/\rho_k+\eta_k)e_k\), where \(C>0\), \(\rho_k\geq\rho_0>0\), \(\eta_k\geq0\), and \(\eta_k\to0\).
The iterates remain in the neighborhood where the recursion is valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\rho_k\equiv\bar\rho\) eventually with \(C/\bar\rho<1\), convergence is Q-linear; if \(\rho_k\to\infty\), convergence is Q-superlinear unless finite termination occurs.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed- and increasing-penalty ALM rate regimes
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let local ALM errors satisfy \(e_{k+1}^\lambda\leq(M/c_k)e_k^\lambda\) and \(e_k^x\leq(M/c_k)e_k^\lambda\), where \(e_k^\lambda=\|\lambda^k-\lambda^*\|\) and \(e_k^x=\|x^k-x^*\|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local smooth equality-constrained ALM under regularity and second-order sufficiency; the classification is based on the penalty tail.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A penalty-dependent rate regime is the equivalence class of penalty sequences \(\{c_k\}\subset(0,\infty)\) having the same asymptotic implication in the error bounds. The fixed-penalty regime is \(c_k\equiv c\) eventually with \(c>M\), yielding the uniform factor \(q=M/c<1\). The bounded-variable regime has \(\inf_{k\geq k_0}c_k>M\) and yields at least Q-linear multiplier contraction. The increasing-penalty regime has \(c_k\to\infty\), yielding \(e_{k+1}^\lambda/e_k^\lambda\to0\) and hence Q-superlinear multiplier convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Penalty sequences are grouped by the rate consequences they induce in local ALM error estimates. An eventually fixed penalty above the sensitivity threshold yields a fixed linear contraction. A variable penalty uniformly bounded above the threshold also yields linear contraction. If the penalty diverges, the multiplier contraction factor \(M/c_k\) tends to zero and the multiplier rate is superlinear; the primal estimate receives the same direct improvement from division by \(c_k\).
special_cases_latex: A constant penalty need not be large in an absolute sense; it must exceed the local problem-dependent threshold.
A nonmonotone penalty sequence belongs to the linear regime if its tail infimum exceeds \(M\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Penalty growth is sufficient for superlinear outer multiplier convergence under the stated local estimate, but is not necessary if another mechanism makes the error ratio vanish.
boundary_notes: If \(c_k\) falls below the local well-posedness threshold, the augmented subproblem may lack the required local minimizer.
The classification does not account for the increasing numerical cost or ill-conditioning of inner solves as \(c_k\) grows.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inexact augmented-Lagrangian iteration and convergence family
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(\min\{f(x):h(x)=0\}\), define \(L_c(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^Th(x)+(c/2)\|h(x)\|^2\), with \(f,h\) continuously differentiable.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth equality-constrained ALM with approximate first-order solution of each unconstrained augmented subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An inexact ALM sequence is a triple \(\{(x^k,\lambda^k,c_k)\}\) for which \[\|\nabla_xL_{c_k}(x^k,\lambda^k)\|\leq\eta_k,\qquad \lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+c_kh(x^k),\] with prescribed tolerances \(\eta_k\geq0\). An inexact-convergence family is determined by an admissible condition on \(\{\eta_k\}\)—such as vanishing, summable, or progress-relative error—together with the resulting convergence target \((x^k,\lambda^k)\to(x^*,\lambda^*)\) or convergence of its residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact ALM iteration does not require exact minimization of the augmented Lagrangian. Instead, the chosen primal point has augmented-gradient residual at most \(\eta_k\), after which the standard multiplier update is applied. Different requirements on the tolerance sequence—vanishing, cumulative, or relative to current constraint progress—define distinct convergence families. The convergence target must state whether the iterates themselves or only feasibility and stationarity residuals converge.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Introducing \(r_k=\nabla_xL_{c_k}(x^k,\lambda^k)\), inexactness is equivalently \(\nabla_xL_{c_k}(x^k,\lambda^k)=r_k\) with \(\|r_k\|\leq\eta_k\).
special_cases_latex: Exact ALM is recovered by \(\eta_k=0\) for every \(k\).
The relative stopping rule \(\eta_k\leq\min\{\epsilon_k,\gamma_k\|h(x^k)\|\}\) couples inner stationarity to outer feasibility.
immediate_consequences_latex: Because \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+c_kh(x^k)\), primal feasibility can also be measured by \(\|h(x^k)\|=\|\lambda^{k+1}-\lambda^k\|/c_k\).
boundary_notes: The definition alone does not guarantee convergence; admissible error conditions and standard regularity or boundedness hypotheses are additional requirements.
For nonsmooth subproblems, the gradient residual must be replaced by an appropriate subdifferential-distance residual.

children.title: Vanishing-Error Convergence
children.top_down_role: Theory for progressively diminishing inner inaccuracies.

knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing-Error Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cluster-point convergence for convex equality-constrained ALM with vanishing first-order inner residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex, and consider \(\min\{f(x):Ax=b\}\). Suppose a primal-dual solution exists, \(\rho>0\), and the bounded sequence \((x^{k+1},y^{k+1})\) satisfies \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}-b)\) and \(e^{k+1}\in\partial f(x^{k+1})+A^{\mathsf T}y^{k+1}\), where \(e^{k+1}\to0\). If additionally \(y^{k+1}-y^k\to0\), then every cluster point \((\bar x,\bar y)\) satisfies \(A\bar x=b\) and \(0\in\partial f(\bar x)+A^{\mathsf T}\bar y\); hence \(\bar x\) is primal optimal and \(\bar y\) is dual optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing inner stationarity error and vanishing multiplier increments make every bounded primal-dual cluster point satisfy the KKT system.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex, and the primal-dual solution set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\bar x,\bar y)\) is a primal-dual solution for every cluster point.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vanishing absolute inner-error regime for ALM
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(r_k=\nabla_xL_{c_k}(x^k,\lambda^k)\) be the first-order residual of the \(k\)-th augmented subproblem and let \(\|r_k\|\leq\eta_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth equality-constrained inexact ALM; this is an absolute-error regime and does not impose summability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An inexact ALM sequence is in the vanishing-error regime when \[\eta_k\geq0,\qquad \|\nabla_xL_{c_k}(x^k,\lambda^k)\|\leq\eta_k,\qquad \eta_k\to0.\] Thus the augmented subproblems are solved to progressively tighter absolute first-order accuracy. Vanishing-error convergence means that, under the accompanying ALM regularity and boundedness hypotheses, the outer primal–dual residuals converge to zero or the iterates converge to a KKT pair while the displayed tolerance condition holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The vanishing-error regime requires the absolute augmented-gradient tolerance \(\eta_k\) to tend to zero. Each subproblem may remain inexact, but its first-order residual must eventually be arbitrarily small. This differs from cumulative-error convergence because \(\eta_k\to0\) does not imply \(\sum_k\eta_k<\infty\), and it differs from relative-error convergence because the tolerance need not track feasibility or a step norm.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For every \(\varepsilon>0\), there exists \(k_\varepsilon\) such that \(\|\nabla_xL_{c_k}(x^k,\lambda^k)\|\leq\varepsilon\) for all \(k\geq k_\varepsilon\).
special_cases_latex: Any summable nonnegative error sequence is vanishing.
The exact regime \(\eta_k\equiv0\) is a special case.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every accumulation point at which the remaining ALM feasibility and multiplier conditions pass to the limit satisfies augmented first-order stationarity.
boundary_notes: The sequence \(\eta_k=1/(k+1)\) vanishes but is not summable, so conclusions requiring cumulative control do not follow automatically.
Vanishing inner residuals do not alone prevent unbounded primal or multiplier sequences.

knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing Inner-Error ALM Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cluster-point convergence for convex equality-constrained ALM with vanishing first-order inner residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex, and consider \(\min\{f(x):Ax=b\}\). Suppose a primal-dual solution exists, \(\rho>0\), and the bounded sequence \((x^{k+1},y^{k+1})\) satisfies \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}-b)\) and \(e^{k+1}\in\partial f(x^{k+1})+A^{\mathsf T}y^{k+1}\), where \(e^{k+1}\to0\). If additionally \(y^{k+1}-y^k\to0\), then every cluster point \((\bar x,\bar y)\) satisfies \(A\bar x=b\) and \(0\in\partial f(\bar x)+A^{\mathsf T}\bar y\); hence \(\bar x\) is primal optimal and \(\bar y\) is dual optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing inner stationarity error and vanishing multiplier increments make every bounded primal-dual cluster point satisfy the KKT system.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex, and the primal-dual solution set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\bar x,\bar y)\) is a primal-dual solution for every cluster point.

children.top_down_role: Theory controlling aggregate inner error over outer iterations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonsummable Vanishing Errors Can Destroy Iterate Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of full-sequence proximal convergence when additive errors vanish but are not summable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\mathbb{R}\times\{0\}\), let \(T=N_C\), and use fixed \(\rho>0\), so \(J_{\rho T}=P_C\) and \(T^{-1}(0)=C\). Starting from \(y^0=(0,0)\), set \[e^k=((k+1)^{-1},0),\qquad y^{k+1}=P_C(y^k)+e^k.\] Then \(e^k\to0\) but \(\sum_k\|e^k\|=\infty\), and the first coordinate of \(y^k\) diverges. Thus merely vanishing additive errors do not guarantee convergence of the inexact proximal sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing but nonsummable errors can accumulate along a flat solution set and destroy convergence of the multiplier iterates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e^k\to0\), but \(y^k\) is unbounded and does not converge.

notation.meaning: normal-cone operator of the closed convex set C

knowledge_statements.title: Nonsummable Vanishing Errors Can Destroy Iterate Convergence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cumulative-error model for the dual proximal representation of inexact convex ALM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be a maximal monotone dual optimality operator and \(\rho>0\). An inexact dual proximal sequence has summable additive resolvent error when \[y^{k+1}=J_{\rho T}(y^k)+e^k,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|e^k\|<\infty,\] where \(J_{\rho T}=(I+\rho T)^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cumulative resolvent error is summable when the norms of the additive deviations from exact dual proximal steps have finite total sum.
assumptions_latex: The inexact update is measured by additive error after the resolvent evaluation.
knowledge_statements.title: Summable Additive Resolvent Error

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional summable-error convergence of the dual proximal form of convex ALM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be maximal monotone on a finite-dimensional Euclidean space with \(T^{-1}(0)\neq\varnothing\), fix \(\rho>0\), and suppose \[y^{k+1}=J_{\rho T}(y^k)+e^k,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|e^k\|<\infty.\] Then \(y^k\to y^*\in T^{-1}(0)\) and \(y^{k+1}-y^k\to0\). If these are ALM multipliers satisfying \(y^{k+1}-y^k=\rho(Ax^{k+1}-b)\), then \(Ax^{k+1}-b\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Summable additive errors in dual proximal steps preserve multiplier convergence and, under the ALM multiplier identity, drive affine infeasibility to zero.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is maximal monotone on a finite-dimensional Euclidean space and \(T^{-1}(0)\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y^k\to y^*\in T^{-1}(0)\), \(y^{k+1}-y^k\to0\), and, under the ALM update identity, \(Ax^{k+1}-b\to0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Cumulative-Error Dual Convergence
Cumulative-Error Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Summable-error convergence of the dual proximal-point form of convex ALM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the convex equality-constrained problem \(\min\{f(x):Ax=b\}\), let \(T\) be the maximal monotone dual optimality operator and suppose \(T^{-1}(0)\ne\varnothing\). Fix \(\rho>0\), write \(J_{\rho T}=(I+\rho T)^{-1}\), and generate multipliers satisfying \(\|y^{k+1}-J_{\rho T}(y^k)\|\le\varepsilon_k\). If \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\varepsilon_k<\infty\), then \((y^k)\) converges to some \(y^\star\in T^{-1}(0)\), and \(\|y^{k+1}-y^k\|\to0\). For ALM primal iterates obeying \(y^{k+1}-y^k=\rho(Ax^{k+1}-b)\), this also gives \(Ax^{k+1}-b\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A summable aggregate error in the dual proximal steps preserves multiplier convergence and drives the ALM feasibility residual to zero.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Step-Relative Additive Resolvent Error Need Not Converge
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the deferred additive-resolvent criterion with an arbitrary constant below one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathbb R\), let \(T=I\), \(\rho=1\), and hence \(J_{\rho T}(y)=y/2\). Define \(y^{k+1}=-4y^k\) and \(d^k=y^{k+1}-J_{\rho T}(y^k)=-(9/2)y^k\). Then \(\lvert d^k\rvert=0.9\lvert y^{k+1}-y^k\rvert\), although \(0.9<1\), while \(\lvert y^k\rvert=4^k\lvert y^0\rvert\) for \(y^0\ne0\). Thus the displayed additive-error condition with only \(\sigma<1\) does not imply convergence to \(T^{-1}(0)=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even for the identity monotone operator, an additive resolvent error equal to 90 percent of the resulting step can generate a multiplier sequence whose magnitude quadruples at every iteration.
assumptions_latex: \(T=I\) on \(\mathbb R\), so \(T\) is maximal monotone and \(T^{-1}(0)=\{0\}\).

notation.meaning: resolvent of the maximal monotone operator

knowledge_statements.title: Step-Relative Additive Resolvent Error Need Not Converge
Relative-Error Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative-error convergence for the dual proximal-point form of convex ALM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be a maximal monotone dual optimality operator on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space with \(T^{-1}(0)\ne\varnothing\), and fix \(\rho>0\). Suppose \(y^{k+1}=J_{\rho T}(y^k)+d^k\), where \(J_{\rho T}=(I+\rho T)^{-1}\), and \(\|d^k\|\le\sigma\|y^{k+1}-y^k\|\) for a constant \(0\le\sigma<1\). Then \((y^k)\) converges to a point of \(T^{-1}(0)\) and \(y^{k+1}-y^k\to0\). If these multipliers arise from ALM through \(y^{k+1}-y^k=\rho(Ax^{k+1}-b)\), then the primal feasibility residual converges to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If each inner error is uniformly smaller than the current multiplier step, the inexact dual proximal iteration converges and feasibility is recovered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y^k\to y^\star\in T^{-1}(0)\), and the associated ALM residual satisfies \(Ax^{k+1}-b\to0\).
review_flags: relative criterion may require a strengthened enlargement-based formulation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem uses a particular additive resolvent error measured relative to the resulting inexact step. Relative-error proximal methods have several inequivalent formulations, including enlargement-based criteria, so an authoritative source is required to confirm that the stated condition with only sigma less than one yields the claimed convergence.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(r_k=\nabla_xL_{c_k}(x^k,\lambda^k)\) and let \(h(x^k)\) be the current equality-constraint residual.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth equality-constrained inexact ALM with inner stationarity accuracy tied to current outer feasibility progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An inexact ALM sequence satisfies the feasibility-relative error condition if there are sequences \(\epsilon_k\downarrow0\) and \(\gamma_k\downarrow0\) such that \[\|\nabla_xL_{c_k}(x^k,\lambda^k)\|\leq\min\{\epsilon_k,\gamma_k\|h(x^k)\|\}.\] More generally, a relative-error family replaces \(\|h(x^k)\|\) by a nonnegative outer progress measure \(P_k\) and requires \(\|r_k\|\leq\gamma_kP_k\), with \(\gamma_k\to0\). The canonical ALM member uses \(P_k=\|h(x^k)\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative-error convergence couples inner accuracy to outer progress. In the canonical method-of-multipliers rule, the augmented-gradient residual is bounded both by a vanishing absolute tolerance and by \(\gamma_k\) times the current feasibility residual. Since \(\gamma_k\to0\), inner stationarity becomes negligible relative to constraint violation whenever that violation is nonzero.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Where \(h(x^k)\neq0\), the relative part is \(\|r_k\|/\|h(x^k)\|\leq\gamma_k\to0\).
Using the multiplier update, \(\|r_k\|\leq(\gamma_k/c_k)\|\lambda^{k+1}-\lambda^k\|\).
special_cases_latex: If \(h(x^k)=0\), the canonical relative rule forces \(r_k=0\) at that iteration.
The additional absolute cap \(\epsilon_k\) ensures vanishing inner residual even when feasibility does not yet improve.
immediate_consequences_latex: The inner stationarity perturbation is asymptotically lower order than the chosen outer progress measure.
boundary_notes: A fixed relative constant \(\gamma_k\equiv\gamma>0\) is a weaker regime than the canonical rule with \(\gamma_k\to0\).
The rule is undefined as a ratio at zero feasibility, so the product inequality is the primary formulation.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F=\{x\in X:c_E(x)=0,\ c_I(x)\geq0\}\), let \(S^*=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)\), and let \(A_\rho:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be an augmented or penalty objective with finite parameter \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General finite-dimensional penalty or augmented construction; local and global exactness are distinguished explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The family \(\{A_\rho\}_{\rho>0}\) is locally exact at \(x^*\in S^*\) if there exist \(\bar\rho<\infty\) and a neighborhood \(U\) of \(x^*\) such that, for every \(\rho\geq\bar\rho\), \[x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in U}A_\rho(x).\] It is strongly locally exact when the local minimizers of \(A_\rho\) in a smaller neighborhood coincide with the constrained local minimizers. It is globally exact if some finite \(\bar\rho\) satisfies \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}A_\rho(x)=S^*,\qquad \rho\geq\bar\rho.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-penalty exactness means that an infinite penalty limit is unnecessary. Above a finite threshold, a constrained solution is also a local minimizer of the augmented objective; strong local exactness additionally excludes nearby spurious minimizers. Global exactness requires the complete set of global minimizers of the augmented objective to equal the constrained solution set for every parameter beyond the threshold.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If only equality of optimal values and inclusion \(S^*\subseteq\operatorname*{argmin}A_\rho\) are known, equality of minimizer sets additionally requires exclusion of infeasible minimizers.
special_cases_latex: For the nonsmooth \(\ell_1\) penalty, a strict local KKT solution is locally exact for every \(\rho>\|\lambda^*\|_\infty\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Under global exactness, any global minimizer of one augmented problem with \(\rho\geq\bar\rho\) solves the original constrained problem.
boundary_notes: The ordinary quadratic penalty is generally not exact at any finite positive parameter.
Exactness of \(L_c(\cdot,\lambda^*)\) with the correct multiplier is distinct from exactness of a multiplier-free penalty function.

children.title: Local Augmented Exactness

knowledge_statements.title: Local Augmented Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth equality-constrained local exactness at a KKT pair under LICQ and second-order sufficiency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\), with \(f,h\) twice continuously differentiable near \(x^\star\). Let \((x^\star,y^\star)\) satisfy \(h(x^\star)=0\) and \(\nabla f(x^\star)+Dh(x^\star)^{\mathsf T}y^\star=0\). If \(Dh(x^\star)\) has full row rank and \(d^{\mathsf T}\nabla_{xx}^2L(x^\star,y^\star)d>0\) for every nonzero \(d\in\ker Dh(x^\star)\), then there exists \(\bar\rho<\infty\) such that, for every \(\rho>\bar\rho\), \(x^\star\) is a strict local minimizer of \(L_\rho(x,y^\star)=f(x)+\langle y^\star,h(x)\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\|h(x)\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LICQ and second-order sufficiency make a KKT point a strict local minimizer of the augmented Lagrangian for every sufficiently large finite penalty.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(h\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(x^\star\).
\((x^\star,y^\star)\) satisfies the KKT equations and LICQ.
The Lagrangian Hessian is positive definite on \(\ker Dh(x^\star)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\bar\rho<\infty\;\forall\rho>\bar\rho:\ x^\star\) is a strict local minimizer of \(L_\rho(\cdot,y^\star)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-parameter local exactness for a fixed feasible primal-multiplier pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a feasible point \(x^\star\), fixed multiplier \(y^\star\), and augmented family \(L_\rho(\cdot,y^\star)\), pointwise local augmented exactness means that there exists a finite \(\bar\rho\ge0\) such that \(x^\star\) is a local minimizer of \(L_\rho(\cdot,y^\star)\) for every \(\rho>\bar\rho\). Strict local augmented exactness requires strict local minimality for every such \(\rho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One finite threshold must preserve the fixed feasible point as a local augmented-Lagrangian minimizer for every larger penalty at the fixed multiplier; strict exactness requires strict local minimality.
assumptions_latex: The multiplier \(y^\star\) is fixed across the penalty family.

children.title: Global Augmented Exactness
children.top_down_role: Exactness connecting global augmented minimizers and constrained solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Augmented Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global exactness for convex affine constraints when the multiplier is dual optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex, let \(h(x)=Ax-b\), and suppose \((x^\star,y^\star)\) is a saddle point of \(L(x,y)=f(x)+\langle y,h(x)\rangle\) with optimal value \(f^\star\). For every \(\rho>0\), define \(L_\rho(x,y^\star)=L(x,y^\star)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|h(x)\|^2\). Then \(\inf_xL_\rho(x,y^\star)=f^\star\), and \(x\) globally minimizes \(L_\rho(\cdot,y^\star)\) if and only if \(h(x)=0\) and \(f(x)=f^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a dual-optimal multiplier, every positive quadratic penalty makes the global augmented minimizers exactly the globally optimal feasible points.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex, and \(h(x)=Ax-b\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Negative Tangent Curvature Cannot Be Penalized Away
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic augmentation changes normal curvature but leaves the Lagrangian Hessian unchanged on the linearized tangent space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume \(f,h\) are twice differentiable near a feasible KKT pair \((x^\star,y^\star)\). Set \(H=
abla_{xx}^2L(x^\star,y^\star)\) and \(J=Dh(x^\star)\). Then \(
abla_{xx}^2L_ho(x^\star,y^\star)=H+ho J^{\mathsf T}J\), so every \(d\in\ker J\) satisfies \(d^{\mathsf T}
abla_{xx}^2L_ho(x^\star,y^\star)d=d^{\mathsf T}Hd\). If this value is negative for some \(d\), then \(x^\star\) is not a local minimizer for any finite \(ho\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: No penalty size can remove negative Lagrangian curvature along a linearized feasible direction.

Constraint Jacobian at the feasible point.

knowledge_statements.title: Negative Tangent Curvature Cannot Be Penalized Away

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A finite quadratic penalty cannot repair first-order stationarity at a feasible point when the fixed multiplier is incompatible with KKT stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be differentiable at a feasible point \(x^\star\), and define \(L_\rho(x,y)=f(x)+\langle y,h(x)\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\|h(x)\|^2\). For any fixed \(y\), \(\nabla_xL_\rho(x^\star,y)=\nabla f(x^\star)+Dh(x^\star)^{\mathsf T}y\), independently of \(\rho\). Therefore, if this vector is nonzero, \(x^\star\) is not a local minimizer of \(L_\rho(\cdot,y)\) for any finite \(\rho\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At feasibility the quadratic penalty has zero gradient, so increasing its finite coefficient cannot repair an incompatible multiplier.

notation.meaning: Quadratic augmented Lagrangian at fixed multiplier y.

knowledge_statements.title: Wrong-Multiplier Obstruction to Finite Exactness
Exactness Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degenerate equality constraint showing failure of every finite quadratic augmentation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R}x\) subject to \(h(x)=x^2=0\). The unique feasible point \(x^\star=0\) is therefore the constrained global minimizer, but \(Dh(0)=0\), so no multiplier satisfies the first-order KKT equation. For arbitrary \(y\in\mathbb R\) and finite \(\rho\ge0\), the quadratic augmented Lagrangian is \(L_\rho(x,y)=x+yx^2+\frac{\rho}{2}x^4\), and \(L_\rho'(0)=1\). Consequently, \(0\) is not even a stationary point, hence not a local minimizer, of \(L_\rho(\cdot,y)\) for any finite \((y,\rho)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When constraint degeneracy prevents any KKT multiplier, no finite quadratic augmentation need reproduce even a unique constrained minimizer.
assumptions_latex: The augmentation parameter \(\rho\) and multiplier \(y\) are finite.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Parameter and structural boundary of finite exactness
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A_\rho\) be an augmented objective for a constrained problem with solution set \(S^*\), and let \(\mathcal P\) denote the class of admissible problem data and augmentations.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-valued definition covering local or global exactness failure; it records failure rather than asserting a universal cause.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed instance \(P\in\mathcal P\), the global exactness-failure set is \[\mathcal F(P)=\{\rho>0:\operatorname*{argmin}A_\rho\neq S^*\},\] where inequality includes nonattainment, infeasible augmented minimizers, or loss of an original solution. The finite-exactness boundary is \[\rho_{\mathrm{ex}}(P)=\inf\{\bar\rho>0:\mathcal F(P)\cap[\bar\rho,\infty)=\varnothing\},\] with \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\). Thus finite exactness fails precisely when \(\rho_{\mathrm{ex}}(P)=+\infty\). A local version replaces global argmin sets by minimizers in a neighborhood of a designated solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The failure boundary records the parameters for which the augmented and constrained solution sets do not agree. Failure includes lack of an augmented minimizer, an infeasible augmented minimizer, or disappearance of an original constrained solution. The exactness threshold is the smallest tail threshold beyond which failure never occurs. If no finite tail is failure-free, the threshold is infinite and finite-parameter exactness fails.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Finite exactness fails if and only if the failure set \(\mathcal F(P)\) is unbounded above.
special_cases_latex: For a standard quadratic penalty, constrained minimizers are generally approached only as the penalty tends to infinity, so finite exactness can fail.
For the \(\ell_1\) penalty at a strict local KKT solution, parameters above \(\|\lambda^*\|_\infty\) lie outside the local failure set.
immediate_consequences_latex: A finite parameter below a sufficient exactness threshold may still be exact for a particular instance; the threshold definition concerns an entire parameter tail.
boundary_notes: Failure of a stated sufficient regularity condition does not itself prove exactness failure.
Local failure and global failure are different: an augmented objective may be locally exact at one solution while possessing an infeasible global minimizer.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Penalty Threshold Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral characterization of strict second-order sufficient local penalty thresholds for smooth equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\), where \(f\) and \(h\) are twice continuously differentiable near a KKT pair \((x^\star,y^\star)\). Set \(H=\nabla_{xx}^2L(x^\star,y^\star)\), \(J=Dh(x^\star)\), and \(\mathcal S=\{\rho\ge0:H+\rho J^{\mathsf T}J\succ0\}\). Every \(\rho\in\mathcal S\) places the augmented Lagrangian in the strict second-order sufficient regime at \(x^\star\), so \(x^\star\) is a strict local minimizer of \(L_\rho(\cdot,y^\star)\). Define \(\rho_{\min}=\inf\mathcal S\). If \(J\) has full row rank and \(d^{\mathsf T}Hd>0\) for every nonzero \(d\in\ker J\), then \(\mathcal S\ne\varnothing\), \(\rho_{\min}<\infty\), and every \(\rho>\rho_{\min}\) belongs to \(\mathcal S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sufficient finite-penalty regime begins when the normal-space penalty curvature makes the augmented-Lagrangian Hessian positive definite; under LICQ and tangent-space second-order sufficiency, this occurs above a finite infimal threshold.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(h\) are twice continuously differentiable near the KKT pair \((x^\star,y^\star)\).
\(d^{\mathsf T}Hd>0\) for every nonzero \(d\in\ker J\), where \(H=\nabla_{xx}^2L(x^\star,y^\star)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{\min}<\infty\), and every \(\rho>\rho_{\min}\) satisfies \(H+\rho J^{\mathsf T}J\succ0\), which is sufficient for \(x^\star\) to be a strict local minimizer of \(L_\rho(\cdot,y^\star)\).

children.title: Exactness–Penalty Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Relationships between augmented exactness families and finite penalty levels.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strictly Above the Global Deficit Threshold
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clarifies endpoint equality and the exact existence criterion for a finite global quadratic-augmentation parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(y\), let the finite constrained optimum \(f^\star\) be attained, and define \(L(x,y)=f(x)+\langle y,h(x)\rangle\) and \(\rho_\star=\sup_{h(x)\ne0}2[f^\star-L(x,y)]_+/\|h(x)\|^2\). If \(\rho_\star<\infty\), then every \(\rho>\rho_\star\) satisfies \(L(x,y)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|h(x)\|^2>f^\star\) at every infeasible \(x\), while feasible global solutions attain \(f^\star\). Hence every \(\rho>\rho_\star\) is globally exact. At \(\rho=\rho_\star\), exactness additionally requires exclusion of infeasible equality points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finiteness of the normalized global deficit is exactly what permits some finite exact penalty; strict inequality above the threshold automatically excludes infeasible minimizers, while the endpoint needs a separate equality check.
assumptions_latex: The constrained optimal value \(f^\star\) is finite and attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho_\star<\infty\iff\exists\rho<\infty\text{ giving global exactness};\quad \rho>\rho_\star\text{ is always exact, while }\rho=\rho_\star\text{ requires equality exclusion}.
knowledge_statements.title: Strictly Above the Global Deficit Threshold
Exactness–Penalty Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global exactness threshold represented by the worst infeasible augmented-value deficit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a multiplier \(y\) for \(\min\{f(x):h(x)=0\}\), let \(f^\star\) be its attained constrained optimum, and write \(L(x,y)=f(x)+\langle y,h(x)\rangle\). Define \(\rho_\star=\sup_{h(x)\ne0}\frac{2[f^\star-L(x,y)]_+}{\|h(x)\|^2}\), with \(\sup\varnothing=0\). Then \(L_\rho(x,y)=L(x,y)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|h(x)\|^2\ge f^\star\) for all \(x\) if and only if \(\rho\ge\rho_\star\). If, additionally, equality can occur only at feasible global solutions, those solutions are exactly the global minimizers of \(L_\rho(\cdot,y)\). Finite global exactness is therefore equivalent to \(\rho_\star<\infty\) together with this equality condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The least global penalty is the supremum of the infeasible Lagrangian-value deficit divided by squared constraint violation, plus an equality-exclusion condition.
assumptions_latex: The constrained optimal value \(f^\star\) is finite and attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_\rho(\cdot,y)\ge f^\star\) globally exactly when \(\rho\ge\rho_\star\); exactness additionally requires equality only at constrained optima.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Outer, inner, and total ALM complexity certificate
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(R(z)\in\mathbb R_+^s\) be a residual vector for a primal–dual candidate \(z=(x,\lambda)\), let \(\varepsilon\in\mathbb R_{++}^s\), and let an ALM use outer iterations with inner subproblem work.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic worst-case accounting for a specified problem class, initialization set, residual certificate, and elementary-work model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An \(\varepsilon\)-approximate-solution complexity certificate is a quadruple \((R,\varepsilon,N_{\mathrm{out}},N_{\mathrm{tot}})\) such that every admitted run produces an index \(k\leq N_{\mathrm{out}}(\varepsilon)\) satisfying \[R_i(x^k,\lambda^k)\leq\varepsilon_i,\qquad i=1,\ldots,s,\] and the cumulative inner work obeys \[\sum_{j=0}^{k}N_{\mathrm{in},j}\leq N_{\mathrm{tot}}(\varepsilon).\] An inner-level certificate additionally specifies \(N_{\mathrm{in},j}\) sufficient to meet the prescribed augmented-subproblem stopping rule. The certificate is valid only relative to its declared oracle or elementary-operation model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complexity certificate combines a mathematically checkable approximate-solution target with resource bounds. It gives a worst-case number of outer ALM iterations by which all residual tolerances are met, and a bound on the accumulated inner work needed to obtain that iterate. If inner complexity is reported separately, the subproblem stopping rule and the unit of inner work must also be specified.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A scalar residual certificate uses \(\mathcal R(z)=\max_i R_i(z)/\varepsilon_i\) and requires \(\mathcal R(z^k)\leq1\).
special_cases_latex: Outer-iteration complexity ignores inner work by reporting only \(N_{\mathrm{out}}\).
Gradient-evaluation complexity takes each evaluation used by the inner solver as one elementary unit.
immediate_consequences_latex: Two complexity bounds are comparable only when their residual targets, problem classes, initialization conditions, and work units coincide.
boundary_notes: An asymptotic convergence rate is not by itself a finite-accuracy complexity certificate.
A certificate for feasibility alone is not an approximate KKT certificate unless stationarity and, where relevant, complementarity are also controlled.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual-based families of approximate optimality certificates
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Z\) be a primal–dual candidate space, let \(\mathcal S\subseteq Z\) be the exact solution or KKT set, and let \(R:Z\to\mathbb R_+^s\) collect nonnegative residual components.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional constrained optimization; certificates are mathematical predicates, independent of the algorithm producing the candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A certificate family is a parameterized collection \[\mathfrak C=\{C_\varepsilon:\varepsilon\in\mathbb R_{++}^s\},\qquad C_\varepsilon=\{z\in Z:R_i(z)\leq\varepsilon_i\ \forall i\},\] satisfying exact consistency \(R(z)=0\) for every \(z\in\mathcal S\). It is exact-set identifying when \(R(z)=0\) if and only if \(z\in\mathcal S\). Standard subfamilies select feasibility, stationarity, complementarity, second-order curvature, or primal–dual gap components. Componentwise tolerances preserve the distinct physical scales of these conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certificate family consists of residual sublevel sets indexed by accuracy tolerances. A candidate is certified when every selected residual lies below its corresponding tolerance. Exact solutions must have zero residual; a stronger identifying family has zero residual only at exact solutions. Feasibility, first-order stationarity, complementarity, curvature, and primal–dual gap are different members or components rather than interchangeable notions.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With weights \(w_i>0\), the componentwise certificate is equivalent to \(\max_i R_i(z)/(w_i\varepsilon_i)\leq1\) after rescaling tolerances.
special_cases_latex: A feasibility-only family takes \(R(z)=\operatorname{dist}(x,F)\).
A KKT family collects primal feasibility, dual feasibility, stationarity, and complementarity residuals.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(\varepsilon^{j}\to0\), \(z^j\in C_{\varepsilon^j}\), and \(R\) is continuous, every convergent subsequence has a zero-residual limit.
boundary_notes: Zero residual need not imply global optimality for a nonconvex problem.
Residual norms and scalings must be declared; numerical values from differently scaled certificates are not directly comparable.

children.title: First-Order Primal–Dual Certificates
children.top_down_role: First-order certificate families for feasibility, stationarity, and complementarity.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c_i(x)=0\) for \(i\in\mathcal E\) and \(c_i(x)\geq0\) for \(i\in\mathcal I\), with \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)-\sum_{i\in\mathcal E\cup\mathcal I}\lambda_ic_i(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuously differentiable finite-dimensional nonlinear programming using the source's sign convention \(c_i(x)\geq0\) for inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pair \((x,\lambda)\) is an \((\varepsilon_s,\varepsilon_f,\varepsilon_d,\varepsilon_c)\)-first-order primal–dual certificate if \[\|\nabla_xL(x,\lambda)\|\leq\varepsilon_s,\quad \|c_{\mathcal E}(x)\|\leq\varepsilon_f,\quad \|[c_{\mathcal I}(x)]_-\|\leq\varepsilon_f,\] \[\|[\lambda_{\mathcal I}]_-\|\leq\varepsilon_d,\qquad \|\lambda_{\mathcal I}\odot c_{\mathcal I}(x)\|\leq\varepsilon_c,\] where \([t]_- =\max\{0,-t\}\) componentwise. At zero tolerances these conditions reduce to stationarity, primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementarity in the KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The certificate separately controls the four first-order KKT blocks: Lagrangian stationarity, equality and inequality feasibility, nonnegativity of inequality multipliers, and complementarity products. The sign convention is that feasible inequalities satisfy \(c_i(x)\geq0\). Setting all tolerances to zero yields the exact KKT conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[R_{\mathrm{KKT}}(x,\lambda)=\bigl(\|\nabla_xL\|,\|c_{\mathcal E}\|,\|[c_{\mathcal I}]_-\|,\|[\lambda_{\mathcal I}]_-\|,\|\lambda_{\mathcal I}\odot c_{\mathcal I}\|\bigr)\leq\varepsilon.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A scalar certificate may use the maximum of the five normalized residual blocks.
With inequalities written \(g_i(x)\leq0\), replace \(c_i=-g_i\) while retaining nonnegative multipliers.
special_cases_latex: For equality constraints only, dual feasibility and complementarity blocks disappear.
For a feasible pair with \(\lambda_{\mathcal I}\geq0\), only stationarity and complementarity need additional certification.
immediate_consequences_latex: A sequence of certified pairs with tolerances tending to zero has KKT accumulation points whenever the sequence is bounded and the derivatives are continuous.
boundary_notes: Approximate KKT conditions do not imply approximate global optimality in a nonconvex problem.
Complementarity products can be small because either the multiplier or the slack is small; both primal and dual feasibility must be checked separately.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F=\{x:h(x)=0,\ g(x)\le0\}. Small r_{\mathrm{feas}}(x) directly certifies small constraint violations, but does not generally imply \operatorname{dist}(x,F)\le C r_{\mathrm{feas}}(x). For example, h_p(x)=x^p with p>1 has F=\{0\}, residual |x|^p, and distance |x|, so no such local linear bound holds near zero. If an error bound \operatorname{dist}(z,F)\le\kappa r_{\mathrm{feas}}(z) holds on the relevant region, then r_{\mathrm{feas}}(x)\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}} implies \operatorname{dist}(x,F)\le\kappa\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}.

The positive conclusion assumes \operatorname{dist}(z,F)\le\kappa r_{\mathrm{feas}}(z) on the relevant region.

Primal Feasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm-based certificate for approximate equality and inequality feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For constraints \(h(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\le0\), a point \(x\) carries an \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\)-primal-feasibility certificate when \(r_{\mathrm{feas}}(x)=\max\{\|h(x)\|,\|[g(x)]_+\|\}\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\). The displayed residual is directly computable from constraint values. It certifies that every equality residual is controlled in the chosen norm and that every positive inequality violation is controlled in the same norm. When \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}=0\), the certificate is equivalent to exact primal feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint values certify approximate feasibility when equality residuals and positive inequality violations are jointly below the stated tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p\) and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) are evaluable.
A norm and tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\ge0\) are fixed.

children.title: Stationarity-Complementarity Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Certificates for approximate first-order primal–dual consistency.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For inequalities \(c_{\mathcal I}(x)\geq0\), let \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)-\sum_i\lambda_ic_i(x)\), with equality multipliers unrestricted and inequality multipliers nonnegative in the exact KKT system.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order primal–dual consistency excluding the separate primal feasibility block, which may be supplied by a sibling feasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pair \((x,\lambda)\) satisfies an \((\varepsilon_s,\varepsilon_d,\varepsilon_c)\) stationarity–complementarity certificate when \[\|\nabla_xL(x,\lambda)\|\leq\varepsilon_s,\qquad \|[\lambda_{\mathcal I}]_-\|\leq\varepsilon_d,\qquad \|\lambda_{\mathcal I}\odot c_{\mathcal I}(x)\|\leq\varepsilon_c.\] The three blocks respectively measure first-order force balance, violation of multiplier sign, and failure of complementary slackness. Combined with a primal feasibility certificate, zero tolerances reproduce the complete KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The system certifies approximate Lagrangian stationarity, approximate nonnegativity of inequality multipliers, and approximate complementary slackness. These conditions are intentionally separated from primal feasibility. Their conjunction with a feasibility certificate produces an approximate first-order KKT certificate; at zero tolerance it produces the exact KKT conditions.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Componentwise complementarity may be stated as \(|\lambda_i c_i(x)|\leq\varepsilon_{c,i}\) for every inequality index.
For \(g_i(x)\leq0\), the same system uses \(L=f+\lambda^Tg\), \(\lambda\geq0\), and products \(\lambda_i g_i(x)\).
special_cases_latex: For equality-only problems, the certificate reduces to \(\|\nabla_xL(x,\lambda)\|\leq\varepsilon_s\).
If primal and dual feasibility are exact, the complementarity residual is zero precisely when every positive multiplier corresponds to an active constraint.
immediate_consequences_latex: Together with vanishing primal feasibility residuals, vanishing stationarity, dual-feasibility, and complementarity residuals yield KKT accumulation points under continuity.
boundary_notes: Small complementarity products do not enforce primal or dual feasibility.
Stationarity may hold at maxima, saddles, or nonoptimal feasible points in nonconvex problems.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection-based exact-equivalent stationarity representation for a closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let X be nonempty, closed, and convex, let d=\nabla f(x)+Dh(x)^{\mathsf T}\lambda+Dg(x)^{\mathsf T}\mu, and fix \alpha>0. Define G_\alpha(x,\lambda,\mu)=\alpha^{-1}(x-\Pi_X(x-\alpha d)). Then G_\alpha(x,\lambda,\mu)=0 if and only if 0\in d+N_X(x). Hence \|G_\alpha\| is a computable projected-gradient stationarity measure. Away from zero, its numerical tolerance depends on the stepsize, metric, and representation and is not automatically identical to \operatorname{dist}(0,d+N_X(x)).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projected-gradient fixed-point residual vanishes exactly at normal-cone stationarity, although nonzero tolerances are representation dependent.
assumptions_latex: X\subseteq\mathbb R^n is nonempty, closed, and convex.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected-Gradient Stationarity Certificate
Stationarity Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order Lagrangian stationarity certificate for smooth constraints and a closed convex simple set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\le0\), where \(f,h,g\) are continuously differentiable and \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is closed and convex. For multipliers \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^p\) and \(\mu\in\mathbb R_+^m\), define \(r_{\mathrm{stat}}(x,\lambda,\mu)=\operatorname{dist}(0,\nabla f(x)+Dh(x)^{\mathsf T}\lambda+Dg(x)^{\mathsf T}\mu+N_X(x))\). A computable vector \(v\in N_X(x)\) satisfying \(\|\nabla f(x)+Dh(x)^{\mathsf T}\lambda+Dg(x)^{\mathsf T}\mu+v\|\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{stat}}\) certifies \(r_{\mathrm{stat}}\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{stat}}\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v\in N_X(x)\) with residual norm at most \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{stat}}\) certifies approximate first-order stationarity.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent residual representation for slack–multiplier complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Put s=-g(x). Componentwise complementarity satisfies 0\le s\perp\mu\ge0 if and only if \min\{s,\mu\}=0, where the minimum is componentwise. Thus \|\min\{-g(x),\mu\}\| is an exact-equivalent complementarity residual at zero. At nonzero tolerance it controls sign violations and the smaller member of each pair, but it need not control the product residual without magnitude bounds: s_i=\varepsilon and \mu_i=M has minimum residual \varepsilon while s_i\mu_i=\varepsilon M.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The componentwise minimum is zero exactly for nonnegative complementary slack–multiplier pairs, but its approximate value does not uniformly control the product residual without bounds.
assumptions_latex: A fixed vector norm is used for an approximate residual.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sign-aware residual certificate for approximate inequality complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For inequality constraints \(g(x)\le0\) and candidate multipliers \(\mu\in\mathbb R^m\), define \(r_{\mathrm{comp}}(x,\mu)=\max\{\|[-\mu]_+\|,\|[g(x)]_+\|,\|\mu\odot g(x)\|\}\). If \(r_{\mathrm{comp}}(x,\mu)\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{comp}}\), then multiplier nonnegativity, inequality feasibility, and complementary slackness all hold to tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{comp}}\) in the selected norm. At zero tolerance, the certificate is equivalent to \(\mu\ge0\), \(g(x)\le0\), and \(\mu_i g_i(x)=0\) for every \(i\).

assumptions_latex: A norm and tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{comp}}\ge0\) are fixed.

children.top_down_role: Combined certificate regimes linking stationarity with complementarity quality.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized aggregation of component residuals with distinct tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For positive tolerances \varepsilon_f,\varepsilon_s,\varepsilon_c, define \widehat R(x,\lambda,\mu)=\max\{r_{\mathrm{feas}}(x)/\varepsilon_f,\ r_{\mathrm{stat}}(x,\lambda,\mu)/\varepsilon_s,\ r_{\mathrm{comp}}(x,\mu)/\varepsilon_c\}. Then \widehat R\le1 if and only if the three residuals satisfy their respective tolerances. A zero component tolerance must instead be imposed as an exact condition and cannot be used as a divisor.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unified maximum-residual certificate for approximate KKT conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the smooth problem \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\le0\), define the feasibility, stationarity, and complementarity residuals \(r_{\mathrm{feas}}\), \(r_{\mathrm{stat}}\), and \(r_{\mathrm{comp}}\) as in their component certificates. The joint residual is \(R_{\mathrm{KKT}}(x,\lambda,\mu)=\max\{r_{\mathrm{feas}}(x),r_{\mathrm{stat}}(x,\lambda,\mu),r_{\mathrm{comp}}(x,\mu)\}\). A tuple \((x,\lambda,\mu)\) with \(R_{\mathrm{KKT}}\le\varepsilon\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-KKT certificate. For \(\varepsilon=0\), it is equivalent to the exact KKT system.

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Stationarity Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate second-order KKT certificate for smooth equality-constrained optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), where \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) are twice continuously differentiable. For \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), let \(L(x,y)=f(x)+y^{\mathsf T}c(x)\), and let the columns of \(Z(x)\) form an orthonormal basis of \(\ker Jc(x)\). A pair \((x,y)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\) is an \((\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_H)\)-second-order stationarity certificate when
\[\|c(x)\|\leq\varepsilon_p,\qquad \|\nabla_xL(x,y)\|\leq\varepsilon_g,\qquad \lambda_{\min}\!\left(Z(x)^{\mathsf T}\nabla_{xx}^2L(x,y)Z(x)\right)\geq-\varepsilon_H.\]
The last inequality certifies approximate nonnegative curvature along linearized feasible directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The certificate bounds constraint infeasibility and the Lagrangian gradient and permits negative reduced-Lagrangian curvature no smaller than minus the prescribed curvature tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x,y)\) satisfies approximate feasibility, first-order KKT stationarity, and second-order stationarity on the linearized tangent space.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At an exact feasible KKT pair satisfying LICQ, positive semidefiniteness of the reduced Lagrangian Hessian is necessary for a local minimum but is not sufficient. The unconstrained example f(t)=t^3 at t=0 has zero gradient and zero Hessian but is not a local minimum. Positive definiteness on the tangent space, together with exact KKT conditions and standard smoothness, is sufficient for a strict local minimum. Approximate residual and curvature inequalities certify approximate second-order stationarity, not local optimality.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Gap Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-based certificate for convex problems with affine coupling constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) and \(g:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper closed convex functions, let \(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) and \(B:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R^m\) be linear maps, and let \(b\in\mathbb R^m\). Define \(P(x,z)=f(x)+g(z)\) and consider \(P^\star=\inf\{P(x,z):Ax+Bz=b\}\). For \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), define
\[q(y)=\inf_{u\in\mathbb R^n,\,v\in\mathbb R^p}\bigl(f(u)+g(v)+\langle y,Au+Bv-b\rangle\bigr).\]
For tolerances \(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d\geq0\), a triple \((x,z,y)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^p\times\mathbb R^m\) with \(q(y)>-\infty\) is a primal–dual gap certificate when
\[\|Ax+Bz-b\|\leq\varepsilon_p,\qquad P(x,z)-q(y)\leq\varepsilon_d.\]
If \(\varepsilon_p=0\), weak duality yields \(0\leq P(x,z)-P^\star\leq\varepsilon_d\) and \(0\leq P^\star-q(y)\leq\varepsilon_d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal point with bounded affine infeasibility and a finite dual point form a certificate when the difference between their primal and dual values is at most the prescribed gap; under exact feasibility, this also bounds both primal and dual objective errors.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|Ax+Bz-b\|\leq\varepsilon_p\) and \(P(x,z)-q(y)\leq\varepsilon_d\), with the displayed objective-error bounds when \(\varepsilon_p=0\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Why a dual-value difference at an infeasible point need not certify primal objective error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every y with q(y)>-\infty, weak duality gives q(y)\le P^\star. If (x,z) is infeasible, however, P(x,z) need not be at least P^\star, so P(x,z)-q(y) need not bound a nonnegative primal objective error. For example, minimizing u subject to u=0 has P^\star=0; at the infeasible point u=-\delta and dual multiplier y=-1, q(y)=0 while P(u)-q(y)=-\delta. Therefore a small gap together with nonzero feasibility residual requires an additional perturbation or error bound before it yields a primal suboptimality estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an infeasible primal point, a small primal–dual value difference need not bound primal suboptimality without a perturbation estimate.
assumptions_latex: q(y)>-\infty is a valid dual lower bound.
The failure concerns a primal candidate with nonzero affine infeasibility.
