knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal–Dual Gap Certificate for a Convex Conic Program
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces, let \(K\subseteq Y\) be a nonempty closed convex cone, and consider \(p^\star=\inf\{F(x):x\in X_0,\ Ax-b\in-K\}\), where \(X_0\subseteq X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex and \(F:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, closed, and convex. For \(y\in K^\ast\), set \(L(x,y)=F(x)+\langle y,Ax-b\rangle\) and \(d(y)=\inf_{u\in X_0}L(u,y)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex conic optimization with an exactly primal-feasible point and a dual-cone multiplier; the definition is value based and does not assert that such a pair is produced by a particular augmented-Lagrangian method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\varepsilon\ge0\), a pair \((x,y)\in X_0\times K^\ast\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-primal–dual gap certificate when \(Ax-b\in-K\), \(d(y)>-\infty\), and the computable gap \(\mathcal G(x,y):=F(x)-d(y)\) satisfies \(0\le\mathcal G(x,y)\le\varepsilon\). The certified interval is \([d(y),F(x)]\): weak duality gives \(d(y)\le p^\star\le F(x)\), so its width equals \(\mathcal G(x,y)\). A relative gap certificate with scale \(s(x,y)>0\) instead requires \(\mathcal G(x,y)/s(x,y)\le\varepsilon\), with the scale declared as part of the certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex conic problem, a primal–dual gap certificate consists of a feasible primal point and a dual-cone multiplier having a finite dual value. Its gap is the primal objective value minus the dual value. It is an epsilon certificate when this nonnegative difference is at most epsilon. The dual and primal values then bracket the optimal value, and the gap is exactly the width of that certified interval. A relative certificate uses the same gap divided by a separately declared positive scale.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is proper, closed, and convex, and \(X_0\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(K\) is a nonempty closed convex cone and \(K^\ast=\{y:\langle y,v\rangle\ge0\ \forall v\in K\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x,y)\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-primal–dual gap certificate exactly when \(\mathcal G(x,y)=F(x)-d(y)\le\varepsilon\), in which case \(d(y)\le p^\star\le F(x)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: If strong duality holds and the optimum is attained, then \(\mathcal G(x,y)=(F(x)-p^\star)+(p^\star-d(y))\), the sum of primal and dual value errors.
The absolute certificate is equivalently the interval enclosure \(p^\star\in[d(y),F(x)]\) with interval width at most \(\varepsilon\).
special_cases_latex: For equality constraints \(Ax=b\), take \(K=\{0\}\), so \(K^\ast=Y\) and the multiplier is unrestricted.
At \(\varepsilon=0\), any certificate has \(F(x)=d(y)=p^\star\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The certificate implies \(F(x)-p^\star\le\varepsilon\) and \(p^\star-d(y)\le\varepsilon\).
The reported pair supplies both an approximate solution and a numerical lower bound on the optimal value.
boundary_notes: An infeasible primal point does not satisfy this definition merely because a Lagrangian value difference is small; feasibility residuals must be added in a different certificate.
Without convexity and weak duality, the quantity \(F(x)-d(y)\) need not provide the stated global optimality enclosure.
A normalized gap is ambiguous until its positive normalization scale is specified.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Three-Level Complexity Account for an Inexact Augmented-Lagrangian Method
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Fix a problem class \(\mathfrak P\), an augmented-Lagrangian algorithm \(\mathcal A\), and a nonnegative certificate map \(C_P(z)\) for each \(P\in\mathfrak P\). Outer iteration \(k\) produces state \(z_k\), invokes an inner solver for \(n_k\in\mathbb N_0\) iterations, and incurs primitive-operation counts \(q_{k,r}\in\mathbb N_0\) for resource types \(r\in\mathcal R\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic worst-case accounting for a nested method; it defines measurement levels but does not supply an asymptotic rate for any particular algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\varepsilon\ge0\), define the stopping index \(K_P(\varepsilon)=\inf\{k\in\mathbb N_0:C_P(z_k)\le\varepsilon\}\), with \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\). The outer, inner, and primitive computational accounts are respectively \(N_{\rm out}(P,\varepsilon)=K_P(\varepsilon)\), \(N_{\rm in}(P,\varepsilon)=\sum_{k=0}^{K_P(\varepsilon)}n_k\), and \(Q_r(P,\varepsilon)=\sum_{k=0}^{K_P(\varepsilon)}q_{k,r}\). Their worst-case versions are the suprema over \(P\in\mathfrak P\). A complexity claim is level-complete only when it identifies which of these quantities is bounded, the certificate \(C_P\), the tolerance convention, and the unit-cost model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complexity accounting for a nested augmented-Lagrangian method has three distinct levels. Outer complexity counts multiplier or penalty cycles until the declared certificate reaches tolerance. Inner complexity sums all iterations used to solve the augmented subproblems through that cycle. Primitive computational complexity separately totals each declared resource, such as derivative evaluations or matrix–vector products. Worst-case complexity takes the supremum of the relevant count over the stated problem class. A bound is unambiguous only when it names the level, certificate, tolerance, and cost model.
assumptions_latex: For every \(P\in\mathfrak P\), the sequence \((z_k,n_k,(q_{k,r})_{r\in\mathcal R})\) is well defined until termination.
Counts \(n_k\) and \(q_{k,r}\) are nonnegative integers under a fixed accounting convention.
If \(K_P(\varepsilon)=+\infty\), all corresponding cumulative accounts are defined as \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The complexity profile is the tuple \(\bigl(N_{\rm out},N_{\rm in},(Q_r)_{r\in\mathcal R}\bigr)\), with worst-case profile obtained componentwise by \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For finite \(K_P(\varepsilon)\), the inner account is the cumulative work \(N_{\rm in}=n_0+\cdots+n_{K_P(\varepsilon)}\).
Given nonnegative unit costs \(w_r\), a scalar computational account is \(W(P,varepsilon)=\sum_{r\in\mathcal R}w_rQ_r(P,\varepsilon)\).
special_cases_latex: If every outer cycle uses at most \(\bar n\) inner iterations, then the bookkeeping identity gives \(N_{\rm in}\le\bar n\bigl(N_{\rm out}+1\bigr)\).
If one inner iteration uses exactly one counted oracle call, then \(N_{\rm in}\) and that oracle count coincide.
immediate_consequences_latex: Two bounds with the same asymptotic exponent need not be comparable when they count different levels or use different certificates.
Reporting only \(N_{\rm out}\) leaves the potentially dominant subproblem-solution cost unspecified.
boundary_notes: Wall-clock time, parallel depth, storage, and bit complexity are excluded unless included explicitly among the resource types.
The definition does not equate an outer update with one derivative evaluation.
Expected or high-probability stochastic accounts require an additional probabilistic convention.

notation.meaning: First outer index attaining the certificate tolerance.
Number of inner iterations in outer cycle k.
Cumulative count of primitive resource r.

knowledge_statements.title: Outer-Iteration Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of an outer residual rate into multiplier-and-penalty iteration complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(R_k\geq0\) be the certificate residual after outer iteration \(k\), where one outer iteration comprises one augmented-subproblem solve followed by multiplier and, if required, penalty updates. Define \(K_{\mathrm{out}}(\varepsilon)=\min\{K\geq0:\min_{0\leq k\leq K}R_k\leq\varepsilon\}\). If constants \(C>0\) and \(\alpha>0\) satisfy
\[\min_{0\leq k\leq K}R_k\leq \frac{C}{(K+1)^\alpha}\qquad(K\geq0),\]
then, for every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[K_{\mathrm{out}}(\varepsilon)\leq\max\!\left\{0,\left\lceil(C/\varepsilon)^{1/\alpha}\right\rceil-1\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An outer residual decaying as the negative alpha power of the iteration count gives an epsilon-complexity of order epsilon to the negative reciprocal alpha.

notation.meaning: outer iterations required for tolerance epsilon

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Outer-Iteration Complexity of an Augmented-Lagrangian Scheme
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal A\) generate outer states \(z_k=(x_k,y_k,\rho_k)\) for problems \(P\) in a class \(\mathfrak P\). Completing outer cycle \(k\) means accepting an approximate augmented-subproblem solution and then executing the prescribed multiplier update, penalty decision, and stopping test. Let \(C_P(z_k)\ge0\) be the declared final certificate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts only accepted multiplier–penalty cycles; all work performed inside a cycle is intentionally excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), the outer-iteration count on \(P\) is \(N_{\rm out}(P,\varepsilon)=\inf\{k\in\mathbb N_0:C_P(z_k)\le\varepsilon\}\), with value \(+\infty\) if the set is empty. The worst-case outer complexity of \(\mathcal A\) over \(\mathfrak P\) is \(N_{\rm out}^{\mathcal A}(\varepsilon;\mathfrak P)=\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P}N_{\rm out}(P,\varepsilon)\). A function \(B_{\rm out}\) is an outer-complexity bound when \(N_{\rm out}^{\mathcal A}(\varepsilon;\mathfrak P)\le B_{\rm out}(\varepsilon,\Theta)\) for every admitted tolerance and every instance whose declared parameters are \(\Theta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outer-iteration complexity counts the accepted augmented-Lagrangian cycles required before a specified certificate meets tolerance. A cycle includes acceptance of an approximate subproblem solution followed by the method's multiplier update, penalty decision, and stopping test, but it is counted as one regardless of its internal cost. The worst-case count is the supremum over the declared problem class. An outer-complexity bound must state the certificate, tolerance range, problem class, and parameters on which the bound depends.
assumptions_latex: The algorithm defines an outer state \(z_k\) and certificate \(C_P(z_k)\) at every completed cycle before termination.
The indexing convention starts with \(k=0\), and the initial state may itself satisfy the stopping test.
The problem class \(\mathfrak P\) and parameter vector \(\Theta\) are fixed before the supremum is taken.
Failed or repeated inner trials do not create new outer indices unless the algorithm accepts them as outer cycles.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Outer complexity is the worst-case stopping index \(N_{\rm out}^{\mathcal A}(\varepsilon;\mathfrak P)=\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P}\inf\{k:C_P(z_k)\le\varepsilon\}\).

special_cases_latex: If the initial state is certified, then \(N_{\rm out}(P,\varepsilon)=0\).
For a fixed penalty method without multiplier changes, each accepted penalty-stage transition may be designated as the outer cycle if that convention is stated.
immediate_consequences_latex: An outer bound alone provides no bound on the number of gradient, proximal, or linear-algebra operations.
Penalty increases and multiplier updates may be counted separately only by refining the outer-state accounting convention.
boundary_notes: Rejected trial subproblems and line-search evaluations are inner or computational work, not outer iterations under this definition.
The definition does not imply convergence or finiteness of the count.
Changing the certificate changes the complexity quantity even if the iterates are unchanged.

knowledge_statements.title: Inner-Iteration Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Total iterations used by solvers of the augmented-Lagrangian subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose outer iteration \(k\) requires an augmented-subproblem accuracy \(\delta_k>0\), and the chosen inner method returns that accuracy within
\[T_k\leq C_k\delta_k^{-p}\]
inner iterations, where \(p>0\). Through outer index \(K\), the aggregate inner-iteration complexity is
\[T_{\mathrm{in}}(K)=\sum_{k=0}^{K}T_k\leq\sum_{k=0}^{K}C_k\delta_k^{-p}.\]
In particular, if \(C_k\leq C\) and \(\delta_k\geq\underline\delta_K>0\) for \(0\leq k\leq K\), then
\[T_{\mathrm{in}}(K)\leq C(K+1)\underline\delta_K^{-p}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Total inner complexity is the sum of all subproblem-solver iterations and depends jointly on the number of outer steps and their requested accuracies.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At outer state \((y_k,\rho_k)\), let an inner algorithm generate iterates \(u_{k,0},u_{k,1},\ldots\) for the augmented subproblem \(\inf_{x\in X}\Phi_k(x)\), where \(\Phi_k(x)=\mathcal L_{\rho_k}(x,y_k)\) possibly includes nonsmooth terms. Let \(R_k(u)\ge0\) be the prescribed subproblem residual and \(\eta_k\ge0\) its target.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic cumulative work measured in iterations of a declared inner solver; an inner iteration need not have uniform primitive cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The inner stopping count in outer cycle \(k\) is \(n_k=\inf\{j\in\mathbb N_0:R_k(u_{k,j})\le\eta_k\}\), with \(n_k=+\infty\) if the target is never reached. If the final outer certificate is first attained at cycle \(K(\varepsilon)\), the cumulative inner-iteration complexity is \(N_{\rm in}(P,\varepsilon)=\sum_{k=0}^{K(\varepsilon)}n_k\). Its worst-case version over \(\mathfrak P\) is \(N_{\rm in}^{\mathcal A}(\varepsilon;\mathfrak P)=\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P}N_{\rm in}(P,\varepsilon)\). The definition includes the accuracy schedule \((\eta_k)\) and residuals \((R_k)\) as part of the algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inner-iteration complexity totals the iterations used to meet every augmented-subproblem accuracy target through the outer cycle that first attains the final certificate. The count in a cycle is the first inner index at which its declared residual is no larger than its declared tolerance. The worst-case cumulative count is the supremum over the problem class. Because changing either the residual or the accuracy schedule changes the required work, both are part of the complexity specification.
assumptions_latex: Each augmented subproblem \(\Phi_k\), inner sequence \((u_{k,j})_j\), residual \(R_k\), and target \(\eta_k\) is specified.
The final outer stopping index \(K(\varepsilon)\) is defined using an independently declared solution certificate.
Warm-start initialization \(u_{k,0}\) is counted consistently; it may satisfy the target with \(n_k=0\).
Any infinite cycle count makes the cumulative count \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inner complexity is \(N_{\rm in}(P,\varepsilon)=\sum_{k=0}^{K(\varepsilon)}\inf\{j:R_k(u_{k,j})\le\eta_k\}\), with worst case obtained by supremum over \(P\in\mathfrak P\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(n_k\le B_k(\eta_k,\rho_k)\) for every completed cycle, then the corresponding cumulative accounting bound is \(N_{\rm in}\le\sum_{k=0}^{K(\varepsilon)}B_k(\eta_k,\rho_k)\).
special_cases_latex: For exact subproblem solution, \(R_k(u)=0\) may be required; the inner count can then be infinite for iterative solvers.
For a fixed budget \(n_k\equiv n\), the cumulative count is \(n(K(\varepsilon)+1)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: An outer method with few cycles can still have large inner complexity when \(\eta_k\) becomes stringent or \(\rho_k\) causes poor conditioning.
Warm starts affect the numerical values of \(n_k\) and must remain part of the algorithm specification.
boundary_notes: The count does not distinguish cheap from expensive inner iterations.
Function evaluations used by a line search may exceed the inner-iteration count.
Random inner solvers require expected, almost-sure, or high-probability variants not specified here.

children.title: Computational Complexity Accounting
children.top_down_role: Aggregate derivative, proximal, matrix-vector, and linear-algebra work.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal R\) be a finite set of declared computational resources, such as objective or constraint evaluations, gradient or Jacobian products, Hessian–vector products, proximal mappings, projections, factorizations, triangular solves, and matrix–vector products. Let \(q_{k,j,r}\in\mathbb N_0\) count uses of resource \(r\) during inner step \(j\) of outer cycle \(k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An oracle and linear-algebra accounting model for finite-dimensional algorithms; bit complexity, communication, and memory are excluded unless declared as resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If certification occurs after outer cycle \(K(\varepsilon)\) and cycle \(k\) executes inner indices \(0\le j<n_k\), the resource vector is \(Q(P,\varepsilon)=(Q_r(P,\varepsilon))_{r\in\mathcal R}\), where \(Q_r(P,\varepsilon)=\sum_{k=0}^{K(\varepsilon)}\sum_{j=0}^{n_k-1}q_{k,j,r}+q^{\rm out}_{k,r}\). For nonnegative weights \(w_r\), the scalar weighted work is \(W_w(P,\varepsilon)=\sum_{r\in\mathcal R}w_rQ_r(P,\varepsilon)\). Worst-case computational complexity is the componentwise supremum of \(Q\), or the supremum of \(W_w\), over the declared problem class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Computational complexity accounting records the total number of uses of each declared primitive resource through certification. It includes resources consumed inside subproblem solves and in outer multiplier, penalty, and stopping operations. The primary account is a vector because derivative evaluations, proximal calls, products, and factorizations are not intrinsically interchangeable. A scalar cost is obtained only after assigning nonnegative weights. Worst-case complexity takes the appropriate supremum over the specified problem class.
assumptions_latex: The resource set \(\mathcal R\) and the rule for charging every operation are fixed before execution.
All counts \(q_{k,j,r}\) and outer overheads \(q^{\rm out}_{k,r}\) are nonnegative integers.
The certificate and terminal cycle \(K(\varepsilon)\) are specified independently of the accounting units.
Weights \(w_r\ge0\) are fixed if a scalar work measure is reported.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Computational complexity is represented by \(Q(P,\varepsilon)\), or by the explicitly weighted scalar \(W_w(P,\varepsilon)=\langle w,Q(P,\varepsilon)\rangle\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The vector inequality \(Q(P,\varepsilon)\le B(\varepsilon)\) means \(Q_r(P,\varepsilon)\le B_r(\varepsilon)\) for every \(r\in\mathcal R\).
A uniform unit-cost model is the special weighting \(w_r=1\) for all \(r\).
special_cases_latex: For a first-order oracle model, \(\mathcal R\) may contain only joint evaluations of values, gradients, and Jacobian products.
For factorization-based subproblem solvers, factorizations and triangular solves should be separate resources because their dimension dependence differs.
immediate_consequences_latex: A bound on inner iterations converts to an oracle bound only when per-iteration resource use is bounded.
Two algorithms can have identical iteration counts and different computational accounts.
boundary_notes: Arithmetic-operation counts require dimension-dependent charges rather than bare unit weights.
The account does not automatically measure numerical precision or conditioning effects.
Parallel operations are summed unless a parallel-depth model is declared.

notation.meaning: Finite set of charged computational resources.
Total uses of resource r through certification.

assumptions_latex: Each oracle interface specifies exactly what information one query returns.

notation.meaning: number of queries to oracle i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on comparing augmented-Lagrangian oracle counts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Oracle complexities are comparable only after fixing the information returned by one query. A bound \(N_{\mathcal O_1}=O(N_{\mathcal O_2})\) requires a uniform bound on the number of \(\mathcal O_2\)-queries needed to simulate each \(\mathcal O_1\)-query; two-sided equivalence requires bounded simulations in both directions. Without the relevant simulation bounds, \(N_{\mathcal O_1}\) and \(N_{\mathcal O_2}\) measure different resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Query counts for different oracle interfaces are not intrinsically comparable; each claimed conversion requires an explicit bounded-cost simulation in the corresponding direction.
knowledge_statements.title: Oracle-Model Dependence of Complexity Counts
Oracle Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accounting for evaluations requested by outer and inner augmented-Lagrangian routines.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix an oracle that, on a query point, returns a specified collection such as objective values, constraint values, gradients, Jacobian products, or Hessian-vector products. If outer iteration \(k\) makes \(q_k^{\mathrm{out}}\) direct oracle calls and its inner solver makes \(T_k\) iterations with at most \(q_k^{\mathrm{in}}\) calls per iteration, then the calls through outer index \(K\) satisfy
\[N_{\mathrm{orc}}(K)\leq\sum_{k=0}^{K}\left(q_k^{\mathrm{out}}+q_k^{\mathrm{in}}T_k\right).\]
If both call counts are bounded respectively by \(q_{\mathrm{out}}\) and \(q_{\mathrm{in}}\), then \(N_{\mathrm{orc}}(K)\leq(K+1)q_{\mathrm{out}}+q_{\mathrm{in}}T_{\mathrm{in}}(K)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oracle complexity counts specified function or derivative queries, summing direct outer calls and calls made during all inner iterations.
assumptions_latex: The oracle's returned information is fixed before counting.
Every inner iteration at stage \(k\) uses at most \(q_k^{\mathrm{in}}\) calls.

children.title: Operation Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity accounting based on matrix-vector products, factorizations, and related numerical work.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of a weighted arithmetic-operation model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A weighted count W=\sum_iw_in_i is an arithmetic-operation complexity under its declared unit-cost model. It is not automatically a bit-complexity bound: when operand precision or coefficient bit length grows, additions, multiplications, comparisons, and factorizations need not have uniformly bounded bit cost. A bit-complexity conclusion requires an encoding model, precision requirements, and bounds on intermediate bit lengths or numerical accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Counting arithmetic primitives does not itself bound bit operations when precision or operand size can grow.
assumptions_latex: The primitive weights describe arithmetic work rather than an explicit bit-level implementation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W\text{ yields a bit-complexity bound only after explicit assumptions convert every charged primitive into bit work.}
review_flags: standard_field_rationale:unit-cost arithmetic complexity and bit complexity are distinct models

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Treatment of primitive costs that vary with instance size.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For instances with size parameter d, primitive costs may depend on d: W(K,d)=\sum_iw_i(d)n_i(K,d). Replacing w_i(d) by constants is valid only when the relevant dimensions and implementation costs are uniformly bounded. Thus an iteration bound K(\varepsilon) becomes an operation bound only after charging all derivative evaluations, matrix actions, solves, factorizations, rejected trials, and setup operations performed through termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Operation complexity must retain size-dependent primitive costs; an iteration count alone is not an arithmetic-work bound.
assumptions_latex: A fixed computational model assigns each primitive its size-dependent cost.
Every performed primitive is counted with its multiplicity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W(K,d)=\sum_iw_i(d)n_i(K,d),\qquad\text{and constant-cost simplification requires uniform bounds on }w_i(d).

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension-Parameterized Operation Accounting
Operation Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic work obtained by weighting the algorithm's primitive computational tasks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose primitive operations indexed by \(i=1,\ldots,s\), assign each operation a cost \(w_i\geq0\), and let \(n_i(K)\) be the number of its occurrences through outer iteration \(K\). The operation complexity is
\[W(K)=\sum_{i=1}^{s}w_i n_i(K).\]
If each outer iteration costs at most \(w_{\mathrm{out}}\), each inner iteration costs at most \(w_{\mathrm{in}}\), and factorization or preconditioning work at stage \(k\) costs \(F_k\), then
\[W(K)\leq (K+1)w_{\mathrm{out}}+w_{\mathrm{in}}T_{\mathrm{in}}(K)+\sum_{k=0}^{K}F_k.\]
Thus costly linear-algebra setup must be counted separately unless it is already included in an iteration cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Operation complexity weights primitive tasks and includes outer overhead, inner iterations, and any separate factorization or preconditioning costs.
assumptions_latex: The primitive-operation model and the weights \(w_i\) are fixed.
Repeated operations are counted with their multiplicities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W(K)=\sum_{i=1}^{s}w_i n_i(K)\), with the displayed outer-inner decomposition under the stated uniform cost bounds.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: weighted sum definition of computational work

Complexity Accounting Equivalences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which oracle, iteration, and operation counts differ only by constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(N(K)\) be an iteration count, \(Q(K)\) the corresponding oracle-call count, and \(W(K)\) its operation count. Suppose constants \(0<a\leq b<\infty\) and \(0<c\leq d<\infty\), independent of \(K\) and the target tolerance, satisfy
\[aN(K)\leq Q(K)\leq bN(K),\qquad cQ(K)\leq W(K)\leq dQ(K).\]
Then
\[N(K)=\Theta(Q(K))=\Theta(W(K)).\]
If any uniform lower or upper comparison fails—for example, because linear-system dimensions or conditioning-dependent solve costs grow—these accounting measures need not be asymptotically equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Iteration, oracle, and operation complexities are equivalent only when their per-step conversion costs have uniform positive upper and lower bounds.
assumptions_latex: The comparison constants are independent of \(K\) and accuracy.
All three counts refer to the same execution prefix.

children.title: Complexity by Problem Regime
children.top_down_role: Complexity families separated by convexity, constraint structure, and stationarity target.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Sigma\) be a set of regime descriptors. Each \(\sigma\in\Sigma\) specifies a problem subclass \(\mathfrak P_\sigma\), a certificate \(C_\sigma\), an algorithmic resource count \(Q_\sigma\), and admitted parameters \(\Theta_\sigma\). Descriptors may encode convexity, smoothness, affine or cone-valued constraints, composite structure, and first- or second-order stationarity targets.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A taxonomy of worst-case complexity statements; it does not assert that a single algorithm or rate applies uniformly across all regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an algorithm \(\mathcal A_\sigma\) valid on \(\mathfrak P_\sigma\), define \(N_\sigma(\varepsilon;\Theta_\sigma)=\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_\sigma}Q_\sigma\bigl(\mathcal A_\sigma,P,\inf\{k:C_{\sigma,P}(z_k)\le\varepsilon\}\bigr)\). A complexity-by-regime family is the indexed collection \(\mathfrak C=\{(\mathfrak P_\sigma,C_\sigma,Q_\sigma,N_\sigma):\sigma\in\Sigma\}\). Two entries are comparable only after aligning their instance classes, certificates, tolerance parametrizations, and cost units. Refinement \(\mathfrak P_\tau\subseteq\mathfrak P_\sigma\) does not by itself preserve a rate when the algorithm or certificate changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complexity by problem regime is an indexed family of complete complexity specifications. Each regime identifies its problem class, target certificate, counted resource, algorithm, and parameters. Typical regime coordinates include convexity, smoothness, constraint geometry, composite structure, and the requested order of stationarity. The worst-case count is taken only over the corresponding subclass. Rates from different entries are directly comparable only when their classes, certificates, tolerance scales, and cost units agree.
assumptions_latex: Every descriptor \(\sigma\) determines a nonempty instance class \(\mathfrak P_\sigma\).
The algorithm \(\mathcal A_\sigma\) and certificate \(C_\sigma\) are well defined on that class.
The count \(Q_\sigma\) uses a fixed outer, inner, or primitive-operation convention.
The tolerance domain and parameter vector \(\Theta_\sigma\) are declared for each regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A regime-indexed complexity object is \(\mathfrak C=\{(\mathfrak P_\sigma,C_\sigma,Q_\sigma,N_\sigma)\}_{\sigma\in\Sigma}\), not an unqualified scalar rate.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The descriptor may be represented as \(\sigma=(\text{geometry},\text{smoothness},\text{constraint type},\text{target order},\text{cost model})\).
special_cases_latex: A convex affine regime may use a primal–dual gap certificate, whereas a smooth nonconvex regime may use an approximate KKT residual.
A second-order regime includes a curvature tolerance in addition to first-order feasibility and stationarity tolerances.
immediate_consequences_latex: A complexity exponent cannot be transferred between regimes solely because both methods are called augmented-Lagrangian methods.
A table of rates is meaningful only when every row reports the defining regime data.
boundary_notes: Problem dimension and conditioning may be regime parameters rather than separate regimes.
Average-case and stochastic regimes require probability laws and probabilistic quantifiers.
This definition classifies complexity claims; it does not supply their bounds.

Problem class associated with regime sigma.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Penalty Local Linear Convergence Boundary for an Equality Augmented-Lagrangian Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded local statement for the equality-constrained case of the referenced augmented-Lagrangian iteration; it is not a global iteration-complexity guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the equality-constrained case and suppose that $x_k\to x^*$, where $x^*$ solves the constrained problem, and that $A(x^*)$ and every $A(x_k)$ have full column rank $m$. With $g(x)=\nabla f(x)$, define $\lambda(x)=A(x)^+g(x)$ and $W(x)=\nabla^2f(x)-\sum_{i=1}^m[\lambda(x)]_i\nabla^2c_i(x)$. Then the generated multiplier satisfies $\lambda^{(k+1)}=\lambda(x_{k+1})$ and $\lambda(x_{k+1})+D_kc(x_{k+1})=\lambda(x_k)$, where $D_k=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_1^{(k)},\ldots,\sigma_m^{(k)})$. Locally,
\[
\bigl[D_kA(x^*)^T+A(x^*)^+W(x^*)\bigr](x_{k+1}-x^*)\approx A(x^*)^+W(x^*)(x_k-x^*).
\]
Thus, unless the penalty parameters tend to $+\infty$, the primal sequence is generically linearly convergent. The augmented-Lagrangian function under discussion is only once continuously differentiable, which can cause numerical difficulty when solving its subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the equality-constrained augmented-Lagrangian iteration, assume the primal iterates converge to a solution and the constraint-derivative matrix has full column rank at the solution and at every iterate. The multiplier is then the pseudoinverse-based multiplier mapping, and its update yields the displayed local error recurrence. Unless the penalty parameters diverge to infinity, this recurrence indicates generic linear convergence of the primal iterates. The augmented-Lagrangian function used in the method is only continuously differentiable once, which may make its subproblems numerically difficult.
assumptions_latex: x_k\to x^*\text{ and }x^*\text{ solves the equality-constrained problem}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda^{(k+1)}=A(x_{k+1})^+\nabla f(x_{k+1}),\quad \bigl[D_kA(x^*)^T+A(x^*)^+W(x^*)\bigr](x_{k+1}-x^*)\approx A(x^*)^+W(x^*)(x_k-x^*);\ \text{unless the penalties tend to }+\infty,\ \{x_k\}\text{ is generically linearly convergent, and the discussed augmented Lagrangian is only }C^1.

children.title: Convex Constraint-Regime Complexity
children.top_down_role: First-order complexity for convex programs with affine or cone-valued constraints.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: First-Order Complexity Profile for Convex Constraint Regimes
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X,Y\) be finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces and \(K\subseteq Y\) a closed convex cone. Consider \(\min_{x\in X_0}F(x)\) subject to \(G(x)\in-K\), where \(X_0\) is closed and convex, \(F\) is proper closed convex, and \(G\) is affine or \(K\)-convex. Let \(\mathcal O_1\) be a declared first-order oracle.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex programs with affine or cone-ordered convex constraints, measured by a value-and-feasibility certificate and first-order resource counts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a problem class \(\mathfrak P_{\rm cvx}\) of such instances and a first-order augmented-Lagrangian algorithm \(\mathcal A\), convex constraint-regime complexity is the profile \(N_{\rm cvx}(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_f;\Theta)=\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_{\rm cvx}}\inf\{Q_{\mathcal O_1}(k):F(x_k)-p_P^\star\le\varepsilon_p,\ \operatorname{dist}(G(x_k),-K)\le\varepsilon_f\}\). When a dual value is computable, the objective condition may be replaced by a primal–dual gap bound. The profile is defined only after fixing whether affine and nonlinear \(K\)-convex constraints share one class or form separate subclasses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex constraint-regime complexity is the worst-case first-order work needed to obtain a point whose objective error and cone-feasibility residual satisfy declared tolerances. The instances have a convex objective over a convex simple set and either affine or cone-ordered convex constraints. The objective error may be certified by a primal–dual gap when an admissible dual value is available. The definition must state the oracle, problem parameters, and whether affine and nonlinear convex constraints are combined or treated separately.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(X_0\) are convex, and the feasible set determined by \(G(x)\in-K\) is convex.
Each instance has finite optimal value \(p_P^\star\).
\(Q_{\mathcal O_1}(k)\) consistently counts first-order oracle work through iterate \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regime complexity is the worst-case oracle count required for \(F(x_k)-p_P^\star\le\varepsilon_p\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(G(x_k),-K)\le\varepsilon_f\).

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Affine-Constraint Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact augmented-Lagrangian iterations viewed as proximal-point steps on the convex dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a proper closed convex objective subject to \(Ax=b\), assume a primal-dual saddle point exists, and apply exact augmented-Lagrangian minimization with fixed penalty \(\rho>0\) and multiplier update \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}-b)\). Let \(d\) be the concave dual objective and \(y^\star\) a dual solution. The proximal-point interpretation gives
\[d(y^\star)-d(y^K)\leq\frac{\|y^0-y^\star\|^2}{2\rho K}\qquad(K\geq1).\]
Consequently, a dual objective error at most \(\varepsilon>0\) is obtained after at most
\[K=\left\lceil\frac{\|y^0-y^\star\|^2}{2\rho\varepsilon}\right\rceil\]
outer iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For exact convex affine augmented-Lagrangian steps, the dual objective error decreases at order one over the number of outer iterations.
assumptions_latex: The convex affine problem has a primal-dual saddle point.
Every augmented-Lagrangian subproblem is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d(y^\star)-d(y^K)=O(K^{-1})\), hence the dual-value outer complexity is \(O(\varepsilon^{-1})\).

knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Conic Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional dual proximal-point rate for exact convex-conic augmented-Lagrangian steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider minimizing a proper closed convex function subject to \(Gx-g\in-K\), where \(K\) is a closed convex cone, and assume a primal-dual saddle point exists. If an exact conic augmented-Lagrangian update with fixed penalty \(\rho>0\) induces the dual proximal-point step
\[y^{k+1}\in\mathop{\arg\max}_{y\in K^*}\left\{d(y)-\frac{1}{2\rho}\|y-y^k\|^2\right\},\]
then for any dual solution \(y^\star\) and \(K_0\geq1\),
\[d(y^\star)-d(y^{K_0})\leq\frac{\|y^0-y^\star\|^2}{2\rho K_0}.\]
Thus dual-value accuracy \(\varepsilon>0\) requires at most \(\left\lceil\|y^0-y^\star\|^2/(2\rho\varepsilon)\right\rceil\) outer steps.

Smooth Nonconvex Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual complexity derived from a uniform merit-descent inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Phi_k\) be the merit value generated by a smooth nonconvex augmented-Lagrangian scheme, and let \(R_k\geq0\) combine its feasibility and first-order stationarity residuals. Suppose \(\Phi_k\geq\Phi_{\inf}>-\infty\) and, for some \(\sigma>0\),
\[\Phi_k-\Phi_{k+1}\geq\sigma R_{k+1}^2\qquad(k\geq0).\]
Then for every \(K\geq1\),
\[\min_{1\leq j\leq K}R_j\leq\sqrt{\frac{\Phi_0-\Phi_{\inf}}{\sigma K}}.\]
Hence an iterate with \(R_j\leq\varepsilon\) occurs within \(\left\lceil(\Phi_0-\Phi_{\inf})/(\sigma\varepsilon^2)\right\rceil\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A squared-residual decrease in a lower-bounded merit function yields an order epsilon-minus-two bound for first-order nonconvex stationarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{1\leq j\leq K}R_j=O(K^{-1/2})\) and the iteration bound is \(O(\varepsilon^{-2})\).

Nonconvex Composite Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal-stationarity complexity under composite augmented-merit descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(k\geq0\), let the augmented subproblem on \(\mathbb R^n\) have composite form \(F_k(x)=h_k(x)+r(x)\), where \(h_k:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable and \(r:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, closed, and convex. Let \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be the constraint-residual map. For a fixed \(\gamma>0\), define
\[G_{\gamma,k}(x)=\gamma^{-1}\left(x-\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma r}(x-\gamma\nabla h_k(x))\right).\]
Suppose iterates \(x^{k+1}\in\mathbb R^n\) and a merit sequence \((\Phi_k)_{k\geq0}\) satisfy \(\Phi_k\geq\Phi_{\inf}>-\infty\) and
\[\Phi_k-\Phi_{k+1}\geq\sigma\left(\|G_{\gamma,k}(x^{k+1})\|^2+\|c(x^{k+1})\|^2\right)\]
for every \(k\geq0\), where \(\sigma>0\). Then, for every integer \(K\geq1\),
\[\min_{1\leq j\leq K}\sqrt{\|G_{\gamma,j-1}(x^j)\|^2+\|c(x^j)\|^2}\leq\sqrt{\frac{\Phi_0-\Phi_{\inf}}{\sigma K}}.\]
Consequently, the conditional iteration complexity for this combined residual to be at most \(\varepsilon>0\) is \(O(\varepsilon^{-2})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a lower-bounded composite augmented merit decreases by at least a fixed multiple of the squared proximal-stationarity and feasibility residuals, one of the first K iterates has combined residual of order one over the square root of K, giving conditional epsilon-minus-two iteration complexity.

\(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is the constraint-residual map.
The displayed decrease inequality holds for every \(k\geq0\) with \(\gamma>0\) and \(\sigma>0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Nonconvex Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional iteration bound for reaching approximate first- and second-order constrained stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Phi_k\geq\Phi_{\inf}\) be a merit sequence, and let \(g_k\) and \(H_k\) denote respectively the Lagrangian gradient residual and reduced Lagrangian Hessian at an accepted iterate. Fix \(\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_H>0\). Suppose every nonterminal iteration—one for which \(\|g_k\|>\varepsilon_g\) or \(\lambda_{\min}(H_k)<-\varepsilon_H\)—satisfies
\[\Phi_k-\Phi_{k+1}\geq\sigma\min\{\varepsilon_g^{3/2},\varepsilon_H^3\}\]
for some \(\sigma>0\). Then the number of nonterminal accepted iterations is at most
\[\left\lfloor\frac{\Phi_0-\Phi_{\inf}}{\sigma\min\{\varepsilon_g^{3/2},\varepsilon_H^3\}}\right\rfloor.\]

assumptions_latex: Every nonterminal accepted step satisfies the displayed decrease.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N=O\!\left(\max\{\varepsilon_g^{-3/2},\varepsilon_H^{-3}\}\right)\) accepted iterations suffice for the stated second-order tolerances.

children.title: Penalty-Dependent Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity distinctions induced by bounded, increasing, or regularized penalties.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Complexity Profile Parameterized by the Penalty Trajectory
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let an augmented-Lagrangian algorithm generate penalties \(\rho_k>0\), outer states \(z_k\), and a certificate \(C(z_k)\). Let \(K(\varepsilon)=\inf\{k:C(z_k)\le\varepsilon\}\), \(\rho_{\max}(\varepsilon)=\max_{0\le k\le K(\varepsilon)}\rho_k\), and let \(Q(k)\) be a declared cumulative work measure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic complexity in which conditioning and work may depend explicitly on the realized penalty sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A penalty-dependent complexity bound is a function \(B(\varepsilon;\rho_0,\ldots,\rho_{K(\varepsilon)},\Theta)\) satisfying \(Q(K(\varepsilon))\le B\) for every admitted instance and run. A compressed profile may depend on summaries such as \(K(\varepsilon)\), \(\rho_{\max}(\varepsilon)\), \(\sum_{k\le K}\rho_k^a\), or \(\sum_{k\le K}\kappa(\rho_k,\eta_k)\), provided the summary is declared. The bounded-penalty, unbounded-penalty, and regularized-penalty regimes are distinct restrictions on this profile rather than interchangeable rate statements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Penalty-dependent complexity is a work bound that retains explicit dependence on the penalty trajectory used by the augmented-Lagrangian method. The dependence may use the full sequence or a declared summary such as the largest penalty, a power sum, or accumulated condition-dependent inner costs. Bounded penalties, increasing unbounded penalties, and proximally regularized subproblems define different restricted profiles. A bound that hides these quantities in an unspecified constant is not a complete penalty-dependent account.
assumptions_latex: The penalty sequence satisfies \(\rho_k>0\) and is defined through the terminal cycle.
The stopping certificate \(C\), cumulative work \(Q\), and inner accuracy sequence are fixed.
Every sequence summary appearing in \(B\) is explicitly defined.
Uniform problem and algorithm parameters are collected in \(\Theta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Penalty-dependent complexity is the inequality \(Q(K(\varepsilon))\le B(\varepsilon;\rho_{0:K(\varepsilon)},\Theta)\) with declared trajectory dependence.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(B\) is monotone in every \(\rho_k\), it may be upper-bounded by a profile using \(\rho_{\max}(\varepsilon)\), but that produces a different, coarser account.
special_cases_latex: Uniformly bounded penalties impose \(\rho_{\max}(\varepsilon)\le\bar\rho\).
A geometric update has \(\rho_k=\rho_0\tau^{u_k}\) for update count \(u_k\) and factor \(\tau>1\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Penalty growth can affect both outer progress and inner conditioning.
Rates cannot be compared fairly when one treats \(\rho_{\max}\) as constant and another exposes it.
boundary_notes: Dependence on a penalty parameter is not itself a convergence guarantee.
The profile must distinguish algorithmic penalties from regularization coefficients.
A worst-case bound over all positive penalty sequences is generally different from a bound for a fixed update rule.

notation.meaning: Penalty trajectory through outer cycle K.

review_flags: No inspected source establishes this trajectory-functional definition as canonical.
Specific admissible penalty summaries require authoritative support.

children.title: Bounded-Penalty Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity theory under uniformly controlled augmentation.

assumptions_latex: \(K(\varepsilon)<\infty\) outer iterations produce the declared \(\varepsilon\)-approximate solution.
For the polynomial specialization, \(C,c>0\), \(p\geq0\), \(N(\eta)\leq C\eta^{-p}\), and \(\varepsilon_k\geq c\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: augmentation parameter at outer iteration k
inner-oracle cost at outer iteration k
outer iterations needed for the declared epsilon-accuracy target

review_flags: This is a conditional complexity decomposition, not an end-to-end theorem for an unspecified ALM.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Penalty-uniform aggregation of inner work when augmentation remains in a compact positive interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an augmented-Lagrangian method reaches its declared \(\varepsilon\)-approximate solution after \(K(\varepsilon)\) outer iterations. Let \(N_k\) be the inner-oracle calls used at iteration \(k\). If \(0<\underline\rho\leq\rho_k\leq\bar\rho<\infty\) and \(N_k\leq N(\varepsilon_k)\) uniformly for every penalty in this interval, then \[N_{\mathrm{tot}}(\varepsilon)\leq\sum_{k=0}^{K(\varepsilon)-1}N(\varepsilon_k).\] If additionally \(N(\eta)\leq C\eta^{-p}\), where \(C>0\) and \(p\geq0\), and \(\varepsilon_k\geq c\varepsilon\) with \(c>0\), then \[N_{\mathrm{tot}}(\varepsilon)\leq Cc^{-p}K(\varepsilon)\varepsilon^{-p}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With penalties confined to a compact positive interval and a penalty-uniform inner-cost bound, total work is the sum of the tolerance-dependent subproblem costs and has no additional penalty-growth factor.
knowledge_statements.title: Penalty-Uniform Work Decomposition

assumptions_latex: Only boundedness of \(\{\rho_k\}\) is assumed; no uniform bounds on the remaining subproblem data or conditioning moduli are imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_k\rho_k<\infty\ \not\Rightarrow\ \sup_k N_k(\varepsilon_k)<\infty\text{ after removal of tolerance dependence}.

notation.meaning: smoothness and strong-convexity moduli of the kth inner problem when they exist

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating bounded augmentation from uniformly controlled inner complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Bounded penalties alone do not give a penalty-uniform inner complexity bound. Other subproblem data may vary so that \(L_k\to\infty\), \(\mu_k\downarrow0\), or another solver-dependent regularity constant degenerates while \(\rho_k\in[\underline\rho,\bar\rho]\). Consequently, a complexity estimate that replaces all penalty-dependent inner costs by one iteration-independent function requires explicit uniform conditioning or oracle assumptions in addition to boundedness of \(\{\rho_k\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keeping penalties bounded does not by itself keep inner problems uniformly conditioned; uniform inner-complexity constants require additional assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded Penalty Is Not Uniform Conditioning
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Penalty Is Not Uniform Conditioning
Bounded-Penalty Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional outer–inner work bound when all augmentation parameters remain uniformly bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an augmented-Lagrangian method producing an \(\varepsilon\)-KKT point after \(K(\varepsilon)\) outer iterations. Let \(N_k(\varepsilon_k,\rho_k)\) be the number of inner oracle calls needed to meet tolerance \(\varepsilon_k\) at iteration \(k\). If \(0<\rho_k\leq \bar\rho\), and \(N_k(\varepsilon_k,\rho)\leq N(\varepsilon_k,\bar\rho)\) for every \(\rho\leq\bar\rho\), then the total inner work satisfies \[N_{\mathrm{tot}}(\varepsilon)\leq\sum_{k=0}^{K(\varepsilon)-1}N(\varepsilon_k,\bar\rho).\] In particular, if \(N(\varepsilon_k,\bar\rho)\leq C\varepsilon_k^{-p}\) and \(\varepsilon_k\geq c\varepsilon\), then \(N_{\mathrm{tot}}(\varepsilon)\leq Cc^{-p}K(\varepsilon)\varepsilon^{-p}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly bounded penalties prevent penalty growth from entering the inner-work bound; total work is the sum of bounded-parameter subproblem costs.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon_k\geq c\varepsilon\) when the polynomial specialization is used
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathrm{tot}}(\varepsilon)\leq Cc^{-p}K(\varepsilon)\varepsilon^{-p}\) under the polynomial inner bound.

notation.meaning: augmentation parameter at outer iteration k
inner-oracle cost of the kth subproblem
outer iterations required for an epsilon-KKT point

However, no inspectable source identifies an ALM, an epsilon-KKT criterion, or a penalty-uniform inner-oracle model supporting this as an ALM complexity result. knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal A\) be an augmented-Lagrangian algorithm with penalties \(\rho_k>0\), certificate \(C_P(z_k)\), terminal cycle \(K_P(\varepsilon)\), and cumulative resource count \(Q_P(K)\) on instances \(P\in\mathfrak P\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity conditional on a uniform finite upper bound for every penalty used before certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0<\underline\rho\le\bar\rho<\infty\), define the bounded-penalty run class \(\mathfrak R_{[\underline\rho,\bar\rho]}=\{(P,\text{run}):P\in\mathfrak P,\ \underline\rho\le\rho_k\le\bar\rho\text{ for all }0\le k\le K_P(\varepsilon)\}\). The bounded-penalty complexity is \(N_{\rm bp}^{\mathcal A}(\varepsilon;\underline\rho,\bar\rho,\Theta)=\sup_{(P,\text{run})\in\mathfrak R_{[\underline\rho,\bar\rho]}}Q_P(K_P(\varepsilon))\). A bound is uniform only if its constants depend on \(\underline\rho,\bar\rho,\Theta\) but not on the realized terminal index or any larger hidden penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded-penalty complexity is the worst-case work over runs whose augmentation parameter remains between fixed positive lower and finite upper bounds through certification. The bounds are part of the regime parameters. A complexity estimate is uniform in this regime only when its constants do not depend on a later penalty value, the realized terminal cycle, or another unreported upper bound. The definition is conditional unless the algorithm's theory separately guarantees bounded penalties.
assumptions_latex: Every counted run satisfies \(\underline\rho\le\rho_k\le\bar\rho\) through its terminal cycle.
The certificate, resource count, problem class, and remaining parameter vector \(\Theta\) are fixed.
Runs failing to reach certification have complexity \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\rm bp}^{\mathcal A}\) is the supremal work over the uniformly bounded-penalty run class \(\mathfrak R_{[\underline\rho,\bar\rho]}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The upper-bound condition is \(\sup_{0\le k\le K_P(\varepsilon)}\rho_k\le\bar\rho\), together with the stated positive lower bound.
special_cases_latex: A fixed-penalty method has \(\underline\rho=\bar\rho=\rho\).
An adaptive method belongs to this regime when its update rule caps penalties at \(\bar\rho\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Penalty-dependent factors can be replaced by functions of \(\bar\rho\) in a uniform bound.
Bounded penalties do not imply bounded multipliers or bounded inner work without additional assumptions.
boundary_notes: An eventual bound after certification is irrelevant; the restriction concerns all penalties used before certification.
Conditional bounded-penalty complexity does not prove that the algorithm enforces the bound.
Allowing \(\bar\rho\) to depend on \(\varepsilon\) produces a penalty-dependent rather than uniformly bounded regime.

notation.meaning: Class of runs satisfying uniform penalty bounds.
Worst-case work in the bounded-penalty regime.

children.title: Unbounded-Penalty Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity behavior associated with increasing penalties.

assumptions_latex: \(0<\rho_k\leq\rho_{k+1}\) and the relevant trajectory is not uniformly bounded.
For the simplified epsilon bounds, \(\varepsilon_k\geq c\varepsilon\) with \(c>0\).
The geometric specialization uses \(\rho_k=\rho_0\gamma^k\) with \(\rho_0>0\) and \(\gamma>1\).

notation.meaning: largest penalty used before the declared termination horizon

review_flags: This is conditional work accounting; an end-to-end bound additionally requires a named method to bound the outer horizon and largest attained penalty.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Penalty-dependent inner-work aggregation and trajectory specializations for increasing augmentation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an augmented-Lagrangian method uses nondecreasing penalties \(\rho_k>0\), reaches its declared \(\varepsilon\)-approximate solution after \(K(\varepsilon)\) outer iterations, and incurs inner cost \(N_k\leq C\rho_k^q\varepsilon_k^{-p}\), where \(C>0\) and \(p,q\geq0\). Then \[N_{\mathrm{tot}}(\varepsilon)\leq C\sum_{k=0}^{K(\varepsilon)-1}\rho_k^q\varepsilon_k^{-p}.\] If \(\varepsilon_k\geq c\varepsilon\), then \[N_{\mathrm{tot}}(\varepsilon)\leq Cc^{-p}\varepsilon^{-p}\sum_{k<K(\varepsilon)}\rho_k^q.\] For \(q>0\) and geometric growth \(\rho_k=\rho_0\gamma^k\), \(\gamma>1\), the sum is \(O(\rho_{K(\varepsilon)-1}^q)\). Hence a bound \(\rho_{\max}(\varepsilon)=O(\varepsilon^{-s})\) gives \(N_{\mathrm{tot}}=O(\varepsilon^{-(p+sq)})\); without an accuracy-dependent bound on \(\rho_{\max}\), the sum does not yield an epsilon-only complexity bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When inner cost grows as a power of the penalty, increasing penalties contribute an explicit penalty-power sum; geometric growth is governed by the largest attained penalty, whose accuracy dependence is essential for an epsilon-only bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Increasing-Penalty Work Decomposition
Unbounded-Penalty Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional work accounting when augmentation parameters increase without a uniform bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an augmented-Lagrangian method uses nondecreasing penalties \(\rho_k\) and reaches an \(\varepsilon\)-KKT point after \(K(\varepsilon)\) outer iterations. If solving the \(k\)-th augmented subproblem to tolerance \(\varepsilon_k\) costs at most \(C\rho_k^{q}\varepsilon_k^{-p}\) oracle calls, where \(p,q\geq0\), then \[N_{\mathrm{tot}}(\varepsilon)\leq C\sum_{k=0}^{K(\varepsilon)-1}\rho_k^{q}\varepsilon_k^{-p}.\] If additionally \(\varepsilon_k\geq c\varepsilon\), then \(N_{\mathrm{tot}}(\varepsilon)\leq Cc^{-p}\varepsilon^{-p}\sum_{k<K(\varepsilon)}\rho_k^q\). Thus unbounded penalty growth cannot be suppressed as an accuracy-independent constant when \(q>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When inner cost grows with the penalty, increasing penalties contribute an explicit sum of penalty powers to total oracle complexity.
review_flags: The bound is conditional bookkeeping; a source specifying an ALM and its penalty-dependent inner oracle model is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity_bound kind matches the terminal container, and the summation follows from the assumed per-subproblem cost. It remains an abstract accounting identity without a source tying the penalty-dependent oracle model to a specified ALM and epsilon-KKT guarantee. The positivity domains of C and c should be stated explicitly.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Complexity for Increasing Unbounded Penalty Schedules
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let an augmented-Lagrangian method use a nondecreasing sequence \((\rho_k)_{k\ge0}\) with \(\rho_k>0\), terminal cycle \(K_P(\varepsilon)\), and cumulative work \(Q_P(K)\). Define the penalty-update count \(U_P(\varepsilon)=|\{k<K_P(\varepsilon):\rho_{k+1}>\rho_k\}|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Runs for which no tolerance-independent finite upper bound on the penalty is assumed; complexity must expose penalty growth or its update count.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The unbounded-penalty complexity profile is \(N_{\rm up}^{\mathcal A}(\varepsilon;\Theta)=\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_{\rm up}}Q_P(K_P(\varepsilon))\), accompanied by an explicit growth descriptor such as \(\rho_{\max,P}(\varepsilon)=\max_{k\le K_P(\varepsilon)}\rho_k\) or \(U_P(\varepsilon)\). For a multiplicative rule \(\rho_{k+1}\in\{\rho_k,\tau\rho_k\}\), \(\tau>1\), one has the defining schedule identity \(\rho_{max,P}(\varepsilon)=\rho_0\tau^{U_P(\varepsilon)}\). A complete profile states how outer and inner work depend on this growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unbounded-penalty complexity concerns increasing penalty schedules for which no tolerance-independent finite upper bound is assumed. The work profile must therefore report the largest penalty reached, the number of penalty increases, or another explicit growth descriptor. Under a multiplicative update, the largest penalty is determined by the initial penalty, update factor, and number of increases. The regime does not require divergence on every finite run; it means that the analysis does not impose one uniform cap across tolerances and instances.
assumptions_latex: No finite constant \(\bar\rho\) independent of tolerance and instance is assumed to bound all admitted runs.
The certificate, work measure, update rule, and problem class are fixed.
For the multiplicative special form, \(\rho_{k+1}\) is either \(\rho_k\) or \(\tau\rho_k\) with \(\tau>1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unbounded-penalty complexity is the work-to-certificate profile together with explicit dependence on \(\rho_{\max}(\varepsilon)\), \(U(\varepsilon)\), or an equivalent declared growth statistic.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Under multiplicative updates, reporting \(U_P(\varepsilon)\) is equivalent to reporting \(\log_\tau(\rho_{\max,P}(\varepsilon)/\rho_0)\).
special_cases_latex: A schedule \(\rho_k=\rho_0\tau^k\) increases at every outer cycle.
An adaptive schedule may remain constant for many cycles and increase only after failed feasibility tests.
immediate_consequences_latex: Penalty growth may enlarge Lipschitz or conditioning constants of augmented subproblems.
A rate hiding \(\rho_{\max}(\varepsilon)\) can conceal tolerance dependence.
boundary_notes: The term unbounded does not mean that infinitely large penalties occur before any fixed finite stopping time.
A decreasing or oscillatory schedule requires a different growth descriptor.
The displayed growth identity contains a text-encoding anomaly in the maximum-penalty symbol and requires verifier correction.

notation.meaning: Number of strict penalty increases through certification.

review_flags: No inspected source supports the precise growth-descriptor convention.

children.title: Proximal-Regularization Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity families using proximal stabilization of augmented subproblems.

assumptions_latex: Each regularized subproblem is differentiable, \(\mu_k\)-strongly convex, and has an \(L_k\)-Lipschitz gradient, with \(0<\mu_k\leq L_k<\infty\).
\(0<\eta_k\leq\Delta_k\), where \(\Delta_k\) bounds the initial objective gap.
The counted inner method is accelerated gradient or ordinary gradient with its standard strongly-convex smooth guarantee.

notation.meaning: condition number of the kth regularized subproblem
initial objective-gap bound and requested final objective error

review_flags: The bounds count inner gradient evaluations conditionally; no unspecified outer epsilon-KKT rate is asserted.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inner and aggregate complexity variants for strongly convex smooth proximally stabilized augmented subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At outer iteration \(k\), add \(\frac{1}{2\tau_k}\|x-x^k\|^2\) to the augmented subproblem, with \(0<\underline\tau\leq\tau_k\leq\bar\tau\). Suppose the resulting differentiable objective is \(\mu_k\)-strongly convex and has \(L_k\)-Lipschitz gradient, and put \(\kappa_k=L_k/\mu_k\). Reducing an initial objective-gap bound \(\Delta_k\) to objective error \(\eta_k\in(0,\Delta_k]\) takes \[O\!\left(\sqrt{\kappa_k}\log\frac{\Delta_k}{\eta_k}\right)\] gradient evaluations with accelerated gradient and \[O\!\left(\kappa_k\log\frac{\Delta_k}{\eta_k}\right)\] with ordinary gradient descent. Summing these bounds through outer iteration \(K-1\) gives the corresponding total inner work. If \(\sup_k\kappa_k<\infty\), conditioning contributes only an iteration-independent factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For smooth strongly convex proximally stabilized subproblems, accelerated gradient gives square-root condition-number dependence and ordinary gradient gives linear condition-number dependence; total work is the sum over outer iterations.
knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Inner-Complexity Variants

assumptions_latex: The proximal term is present, but no uniform positive lower bound on the resulting strong-convexity modulus or uniform upper bound on its condition number is assumed.

notation.meaning: strong-convexity modulus and condition number of the kth regularized subproblem

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of a uniform proximal-regularization complexity constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A positive proximal term at every iteration does not by itself give a uniform inner-complexity bound. If its metric degenerates, if \(\tau_k\to\infty\) so that the added curvature vanishes, or if other curvature makes \(\mu_k\downarrow0\) or \(L_k/\mu_k\to\infty\), then the conditioning factors in both accelerated and nonaccelerated bounds can diverge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proximal stabilization yields uniform complexity constants only when the resulting subproblem conditioning remains uniformly controlled.
knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Conditioning Degeneracy
Proximal-Regularization Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional complexity decomposition for proximally stabilized augmented subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At outer iteration \(k\), augment the subproblem by \(\tfrac{1}{2\tau_k}\lVert x-x^k\rVert^2\), with \(0<\underline\tau\leq\tau_k\leq\bar\tau\). Suppose the regularized subproblem is \(\mu_k\)-strongly convex and has gradient Lipschitz constant \(L_k\), and a linearly convergent inner method reduces its residual from \(R_k\) to \(\eta_k\) in at most \(C\sqrt{L_k/\mu_k}\log(R_k/\eta_k)\) oracle calls. Then, through outer iteration \(K-1\), \[N_{\mathrm{tot}}\leq C\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\sqrt{L_k/\mu_k}\log(R_k/\eta_k).\] Uniform bounds on \(L_k/\mu_k\) therefore separate conditioning from the outer ALM iteration count.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proximal stabilization yields a total-work sum governed by each regularized subproblem’s condition number and requested inner residual.
assumptions_latex: Each regularized subproblem is \(\mu_k\)-strongly convex with \(L_k\)-Lipschitz gradient
The chosen inner method has the stated linear-convergence cost

notation.meaning: condition number of the regularized subproblem

review_flags: A specific proximal ALM and matching inner-oracle theorem are needed to certify this conditional family.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity_bound kind fits the leaf, but the square-root condition-number rate is not a consequence of generic linear convergence; it requires a particular accelerated inner method and its hypotheses. A source must identify the proximal ALM, oracle model, residual definition, and conditions such as R_k>=eta_k>0.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Complexity of Proximally Stabilized Augmented Subproblems
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At outer cycle \(k\), let \(x_k\in X\), multiplier \(y_k\), and penalty \(\rho_k>0\) be given. Let \(M_k:X\to X\) be self-adjoint positive semidefinite and \(\gamma_k>0\). Define \(\Phi_k(x)=\mathcal L_{\rho_k}(x,y_k)+(2\gamma_k)^{-1}\|x-x_k\|_{M_k}^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested augmented-Lagrangian methods whose inner objectives contain an explicit proximal stabilization centered at the preceding accepted primal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A proximal-regularization complexity profile is \(N_{\rm prox}^{\mathcal A}(\varepsilon;\Theta,\rho_{0:K},\gamma_{0:K},M_{0:K})=\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P}\sum_{k=0}^{K_P(\varepsilon)}Q_k(\eta_k;\Phi_k)\), where \(Q_k\) counts the declared work required to return \(x_{k+1}\) with subproblem residual \(R_k(x_{k+1})\le\eta_k\). The profile must expose or uniformly bound the regularization strength \(\lambda_{\min}^+(M_k)/\gamma_k\), the smoothness or conditioning of \(\Phi_k\), and the cost of applying \(M_k\) or its proximal metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proximal-regularization complexity totals the work needed to solve augmented subproblems that include an explicit quadratic stabilization about the previous accepted primal point. The profile depends on the penalty, proximal stepsize, metric, inner accuracy, and the conditioning these quantities induce. It must also charge the cost of applying the metric. The proximal term can improve stability or subproblem convexity, but those benefits are not part of the definition and require separate assumptions.
assumptions_latex: \(M_k\) is self-adjoint and positive semidefinite, and \(\gamma_k>0\).
The stabilized subproblem objective \(\Phi_k\), residual \(R_k\), and target \(\eta_k\) are specified.
The terminal cycle is determined by a declared outer certificate.
The resource count \(Q_k\) includes metric applications and all inner-solver work.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Proximal-regularization complexity is the cumulative inner work \(\sum_{k\le K_P(\varepsilon)}Q_k(\eta_k;\Phi_k)\), parameterized by the penalty and proximal-metric trajectories.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(M_k=I\), the stabilization is \((2\gamma_k)^{-1}\|x-x_k\|^2\).
Writing \(H_k=M_k/\gamma_k\) gives the equivalent proximal term \(\tfrac12\langle x-x_k,H_k(x-x_k)\rangle\).
special_cases_latex: A constant metric and stepsize use \(M_k=M\) and \(\gamma_k=\gamma\) for all \(k\).
If \(M_k=0\), the profile reduces to an unregularized augmented-subproblem account and no longer belongs to the strictly stabilized subclass.
immediate_consequences_latex: Different metric choices can change both iteration counts and per-iteration costs.
A uniform complexity bound must control the relevant metric eigenvalues and conditioning.
boundary_notes: The definition does not assert strong convexity when \(M_k\) is singular or the augmented objective has negative curvature.
A proximal point applied only to multipliers is a different stabilization unless explicitly incorporated.
Regularization bias and outer convergence require separate analysis.

notation.meaning: Proximal stepsize or inverse regularization scale.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For the equality-constrained problem \(\min_x f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), define \(L(x,y)=f(x)+\langle y,c(x)\rangle\), \(\mathcal L_\rho(x,y)=L(x,y)+\tfrac\rho2\|c(x)\|^2\), and the primal–dual residual \(F(x,y)=(\nabla_xL(x,y),c(x))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A structural family encompassing proximal stabilization, second-order primal–dual corrections, and quasi-Newton approximations; it is not a convergence or acceleration-rate theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A method belongs to the multiplier stabilization-acceleration family when each accepted transition combines an augmented or stabilized primal step with a multiplier step and has one of the forms: \(x_{k+1}\approx\arg\min_x\{\mathcal L_{\rho_k}(x,y_k)+\tfrac12\|x-x_k\|_{H_k}^2\}\), \(y_{k+1}=y_k+\alpha_k\rho_kc(x_{k+1})\); or \(z_{k+1}=z_k+s_k\), where \(z_k=(x_k,y_k)\) and \(B_ks_k=-F(z_k)+r_k\). Here \(H_k\succeq0\), \(\alpha_k>0\), \(B_k\) is the exact primal–dual Jacobian or a nonsingular secant approximation, and \(r_k\) is a declared inexactness residual. Globalization and acceptance rules are part of the method specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The multiplier stabilization-acceleration family consists of multiplier methods that augment the classical primal minimization and multiplier update with a proximal metric, a second-order primal–dual correction, or a quasi-Newton secant approximation. A proximal member approximately minimizes a stabilized augmented Lagrangian and then performs a possibly damped multiplier update. A second-order or quasi-Newton member solves an exact or approximate linearized primal–dual residual equation. The metric, damping, inexactness, matrix update, and globalization rules distinguish individual methods within the family.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are differentiable wherever the displayed residual is evaluated.
For proximal members, \(H_k\) is self-adjoint positive semidefinite and \(\rho_k,\alpha_k>0\).
For second-order or quasi-Newton members, \(B_k\) is nonsingular on accepted steps and \(r_k\) has a declared control rule.
Each method declares its subproblem accuracy, acceptance, and globalization conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Membership in the family is defined by an accepted transition of the stabilized augmented-minimization form or the exact/quasi-Newton primal–dual residual-correction form, together with a multiplier update.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With exact derivatives, \(B_k=F'(z_k)\) gives a Newton-type primal–dual correction.
A quasi-Newton member replaces \(F'(z_k)\) by \(B_k\) satisfying a declared secant relation such as \(B_{k+1}(z_{k+1}-z_k)=F(z_{k+1})-F(z_k)\).
special_cases_latex: Setting \(H_k=0\) and \(\alpha_k=1\) recovers the classical method-of-multipliers update form.
Choosing \(H_k\succ0\) gives explicit proximal stabilization of the primal subproblem.
Using an approximate KKT matrix for \(B_k\) yields a quasi-Newton multiplier method.
immediate_consequences_latex: The family separates the residual being corrected from the matrix model used for that correction.
Acceleration terminology alone does not specify a convergence rate; the update and regularity assumptions must do so.
boundary_notes: An arbitrary momentum extrapolation is not included unless it is coupled to a declared stabilized or residual-correction multiplier step.
Nonsmooth problems require generalized derivatives or proximal residuals not represented by the smooth map \(F\).
The definition does not claim global convergence, superlinear convergence, or improved worst-case complexity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Proximal augmented-Lagrangian method for linear equality constraints
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex, let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and consider \(\min_x f(x)\) subject to \(Ax=b\). For \(\alpha>0\), define \(\mathcal L_\alpha(x,u)=f(x)+\langle u,Ax-b\rangle+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|Ax-b\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex equality-constrained formulation with a scalar Euclidean proximal regularizer and exact primal subproblem solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A proximal augmented-Lagrangian method, also called a proximal method of multipliers, is the iteration that, from \((x^k,u^k)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\), selects \[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{\mathcal L_\alpha(x,u^k)+\frac{1}{2\alpha}\|x-x^k\|^2\right\}\] and then sets \[u^{k+1}=u^k+\alpha(Ax^{k+1}-b).\] Thus the defining distinction from the ordinary method of multipliers is the proximal term centered at the preceding primal iterate. Equivalently, with the saddle operator \(T(x,u)=(\partial f(x)+A^\top u,\,b-Ax)\), the complete update is the resolvent step \[(x^{k+1},u^{k+1})=(I+\alpha T)^{-1}(x^k,u^k).\] The definition requires the displayed minimizer to exist; under total duality and the standard convex hypotheses, the cited formulation treats the iteration as a primal-dual proximal-point step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper closed convex objective with linear equality constraints, a proximal augmented-Lagrangian method minimizes the augmented Lagrangian plus a squared distance from the preceding primal iterate, and then updates the multiplier by the scaled constraint residual. The whole primal-multiplier update is equivalently a resolvent step for the saddle operator. The added squared-distance term is what distinguishes this method from the ordinary method of multipliers.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex, and \(\alpha>0\).
The constrained problem is \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(Ax=b\), and each displayed proximal subproblem attains its minimum.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \((x^{k+1},u^{k+1})=(I+\alpha T)^{-1}(x^k,u^k)\), where \(T(x,u)=(\partial f(x)+A^\top u,b-Ax)\).
\(0\in\partial f(x^{k+1})+A^\top u^{k+1}+\alpha^{-1}(x^{k+1}-x^k)\) together with \(u^{k+1}-u^k=\alpha(Ax^{k+1}-b)\).
special_cases_latex: Deleting \((2\alpha)^{-1}\|x-x^k\|^2\) gives the ordinary method of multipliers.
If \(A=0\) and \(b=0\), the primal update reduces to the proximal-point iteration for \(f\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The proximal term makes the primal objective \(\alpha^{-1}\)-strongly convex whenever \(\mathcal L_\alpha(\cdot,u^k)\) is convex, so the primal minimizer is then unique.
At a fixed point, \(Ax=b\) and \(0\in\partial f(x)+A^\top u\), which are the convex KKT conditions.
boundary_notes: This definition does not cover alternating block minimization, inexact subproblem solution, variable metrics, or nonlinear constraints.
The convergence assertion in the cited source uses total duality; total duality is not part of the bare iteration formula.

If \(\tau_k^{-1}\leq\beta_k\), the proximal term alone does not guarantee strong convexity or uniqueness.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global convergence of exact primal-only proximal stabilization for a solvable convex affine equality problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex, and suppose \(\min\{f(x):Ax=b\}\) has a primal-dual solution. Fix \(\rho,\tau>0\), and compute
\[
0\in\partial f(x^{k+1})+A^\top y^{k+1}+\tau^{-1}(x^{k+1}-x^k),
\qquad y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}-b).
\]
Then \((x^k,y^k)\) converges to a primal-dual solution. In particular, \(Ax^k-b\to0\), \(\tau^{-1}(x^{k+1}-x^k)\to0\), and the primal objective values converge to the optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a solvable convex affine problem, exact primal-proximal ALM with fixed positive parameters converges to a primal-dual solution.
assumptions_latex: The affine-constrained problem has a primal-dual solution.
\(\rho>0\) and \(\tau>0\) are fixed, and each proximal subproblem is solved exactly.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_x f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), choose \(\rho_k>0\), \(\tau_k>0\), and initialize \((x^0,y^0)\). Define \(L_{\rho}(x,y)=f(x)+\langle y,c(x)\rangle+\tfrac{\rho}{2}\lVert c(x)\rVert^2\). At iteration \(k\), compute \[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\left\{L_{\rho_k}(x,y^k)+\frac{1}{2\tau_k}\lVert x-x^k\rVert^2\right\},\qquad y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho_k c(x^{k+1}).\] Stop when both a primal residual \(\lVert c(x^{k+1})\rVert\) and a Lagrangian-stationarity residual are below prescribed tolerances; output \((x^{k+1},y^{k+1})\).
