knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For the equality-constrained convex problem \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(Ax=b\), fix \(\alpha>0\), a reference point \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\), and a multiplier \(u\in\mathbb R^m\). Let \(\mathcal L_\alpha(x,u)=f(x)+\langle u,Ax-b\rangle+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|Ax-b\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition isolates the stabilized primal subproblem; it does not itself prescribe how the multiplier is subsequently changed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The primal proximal stabilization of the augmented-Lagrangian subproblem at \((\bar x,u)\) is the solution mapping \[S_\alpha(\bar x,u):=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{\mathcal L_\alpha(x,u)+\frac{1}{2\alpha}\|x-\bar x\|^2\right\}.\] A point \(x^+\) is a stabilized primal update precisely when \(x^+\in S_\alpha(\bar x,u)\). In the convex setting this is equivalently characterized by \[0\in\partial f(x^+)+A^\top u+\alpha A^\top(Ax^+-b)+\alpha^{-1}(x^+-\bar x).\] The final term is the proximal restoring force: it vanishes at the reference point and penalizes displacement from it. If the remaining augmented objective is convex, the added quadratic makes the subproblem strongly convex and hence makes \(S_\alpha(\bar x,u)\) single-valued.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal proximal stabilization is the operation of minimizing the augmented Lagrangian after adding a positive quadratic distance from a given reference primal point. It can be described either by its minimization problem or by the corresponding subgradient inclusion. This record defines only that stabilized primal operation, not the full multiplier algorithm.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(u\in\mathbb R^m\), \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\alpha>0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(x^+\in S_\alpha(\bar x,u)\iff 0\in\partial f(x^+)+A^\top u+\alpha A^\top(Ax^+-b)+\alpha^{-1}(x^+-\bar x)\).
If \(u^+=u+\alpha(Ax^+-b)\), the inclusion becomes \(0\in\partial f(x^+)+A^\top u^++\alpha^{-1}(x^+-\bar x)\).
special_cases_latex: For \(A=0\) and \(b=0\), \(S_\alpha(\bar x,u)=\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha f}(\bar x)\).
If the proximal term is omitted, \(S_\alpha\) becomes the ordinary augmented-Lagrangian minimizer mapping.
immediate_consequences_latex: The stabilized subproblem has at most one minimizer because its objective is strongly convex.
The displacement satisfies \(\bar x-x^+\in\alpha(\partial f(x^+)+A^\top u^+)\) when the standard multiplier update is attached.
boundary_notes: Only Euclidean scalar regularization is covered; matrix metrics and Bregman distances are nearby variants.
This operation does not imply convergence unless embedded in an algorithm satisfying appropriate duality and solvability conditions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preconditioned proximal-point stabilization of the full KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_x f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), define the KKT residual operator \(F(x,y)=(\nabla f(x)+\nabla c(x)^{\mathsf T}y,-c(x))\). Initialize \(w^0=(x^0,y^0)\), choose symmetric positive-definite matrices \(M_k\), and compute \(w^{k+1}\) from \[0=F(w^{k+1})+M_k(w^{k+1}-w^k).\] Equivalently, the primal and multiplier displacements are jointly damped in the metric induced by \(M_k\). Stop when \(\lVert F(w^{k+1})\rVert\leq\varepsilon\), and output \(w^{k+1}\). Block-diagonal or coupled blocks of \(M_k\) respectively give separate or coupled primal–dual stabilization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply a metric proximal-point step to the complete KKT residual, stabilizing primal and multiplier displacements simultaneously.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex and let \(Ax=b\) be a linear equality constraint. Define the maximal monotone saddle operator \(T:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\) by \(T(x,u)=(\partial f(x)+A^\top u,\,b-Ax)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex primal-dual stabilization in the product Euclidean metric; both components are defined simultaneously by one resolvent equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Primal–dual proximal stabilization with parameter \(\alpha>0\) is the joint update \[z^{k+1}=J_{\alpha T}(z^k):=(I+\alpha T)^{-1}(z^k),\qquad z^k=(x^k,u^k).\] Equivalently, \((x^{k+1},u^{k+1})\) is the unique pair satisfying \[0\in\partial f(x^{k+1})+A^\top u^{k+1}+\alpha^{-1}(x^{k+1}-x^k),\] \[0=b-Ax^{k+1}+\alpha^{-1}(u^{k+1}-u^k).\] Eliminating \(u^{k+1}\) gives the proximal augmented-Lagrangian primal subproblem, while the second relation gives \(u^{k+1}=u^k+\alpha(Ax^{k+1}-b)\). The term “primal–dual” refers to the product-space proximal step: the new primal and multiplier variables are jointly constrained by the resolvent inclusion, even though an implementation may compute the primal variable first and then recover the multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal-dual proximal stabilization is a proximal-point step applied to the saddle operator of the equality-constrained problem. The new primal point and multiplier jointly satisfy two coupled proximal equations. Eliminating the new multiplier produces the proximal augmented-Lagrangian subproblem, and the remaining equation is the usual multiplier update.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex, and \(A\) and \(b\) define a linear equality constraint.
\(T(x,u)=(\partial f(x)+A^\top u,b-Ax)\) is considered on the product Euclidean space, and \(\alpha>0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(x^{k+1}\in\arg\min_x\{f(x)+\langle u^k,Ax-b\rangle+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|Ax-b\|^2+\frac{1}{2\alpha}\|x-x^k\|^2\}\) and \(u^{k+1}=u^k+\alpha(Ax^{k+1}-b)\).
\(z^k-z^{k+1}\in\alpha T(z^{k+1})\).
special_cases_latex: If \(A=0\) and \(b=0\), the multiplier is unchanged and the primal component is the proximal-point update for \(f\).
At a fixed point \(z^{k+1}=z^k\), the inclusion is \(0\in T(z^k)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Fixed points of \(J_{\alpha T}\) are exactly primal-dual KKT pairs.
The resolvent is single-valued and firmly nonexpansive when \(T\) is maximal monotone.
boundary_notes: This definition is not the same as independently adding arbitrary proximal terms to two sequential subproblems.
Nonconvex saddle operators need not be maximal monotone and are outside the stated scope.

The outer residuals are \(\|c(x^{k+1})\|\) and \(\|\nabla f(x^{k+1})+Jc(x^{k+1})^\top y^{k+1}\|\); the displayed norm is the inner regularized-stationarity residual. knowledge_statements.scope_note: Non-equivalent objective, absolute first-order, summable-error, and relative-error controls for proximal augmented subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Phi_k(x)=L_{\rho_k}(x,y^k)+\tfrac1{2\tau_k}\|x-x^k\|^2\). Common inexactness rules include
\[
\Phi_k(x^{k+1})-\inf\Phi_k\le\varepsilon_k,
\qquad \operatorname{dist}(0,\partial\Phi_k(x^{k+1}))\le\eta_k,
\]
the summable absolute-error condition \(\sum_k\eta_k<\infty\), and the relative rule
\[
\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial\Phi_k(x^{k+1}))\le\sigma\tau_k^{-1}\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|,
\quad 0\le\sigma<1.
\]
These rules are not equivalent without additional error-bound or curvature hypotheses; in particular, pointwise vanishing of \(\eta_k\) is weaker than summability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective-gap, absolute stationarity, summable stationarity, and relative stationarity rules are distinct inexact proximal-ALM regimes unless extra curvature or error bounds connect them.
assumptions_latex: \(\Phi_k\) is proper and bounded below whenever the objective-gap rule is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed acceptance regimes cannot generally be substituted for one another without further hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.title: Distinct Inexactness Regimes

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Persistent Inner Error Can Produce a Nonstationary Limit
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of convergence when an absolute first-order error is merely uniformly bounded away from zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the unconstrained convex problem \(\min_x \tfrac12x^2\), take \(\tau_k=1\), and accept proximal iterates satisfying
\[
e_{k+1}=x^{k+1}+(x^{k+1}-x^k),
\qquad |e_{k+1}|\le1.
\]
Starting from \(x^0=1\), the constant sequence \(x^{k+1}=1\) is admissible with \(e_{k+1}=1\) for every \(k\), but its limit is not stationary because \(\nabla f(1)=1\ne0\). Thus a uniform nonvanishing absolute tolerance alone does not imply approach to the KKT set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed nonzero inner tolerance can admit a constant nonstationary proximal sequence even for a one-dimensional strongly convex problem.
assumptions_latex: The only inner requirement is the absolute residual bound \(|e_{k+1}|\le1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^k\equiv1\) is admissible, but \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x^k))=1\) for every \(k\).
knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Inner Error Can Produce a Nonstationary Limit

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global convergence of an inexact primal-proximal multiplier iteration for a convex affine equality problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex, and suppose \(\min\{f(x):Ax=b\}\) has a primal-dual solution. Fix \(\rho,\tau>0\). If
\[
e^{k+1}\in\partial f(x^{k+1})+A^\top y^{k+1}+\tau^{-1}(x^{k+1}-x^k),
\qquad y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}-b),
\]
with \(\sum_{k=0}^\infty\|e^{k+1}\|<\infty\), then \((x^k,y^k)\) converges to a primal-dual solution. Consequently \(Ax^k-b\to0\), the KKT residual tends to zero, and \(f(x^k)\to p^*\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable, let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(Ax=b\). For \(\alpha_k>0\), define \(\Psi_k(x)=f(x)+\langle u^k,Ax-b\rangle+\frac{\alpha_k}{2}\|Ax-b\|^2+\frac{1}{2\alpha_k}\|x-x^k\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional equality-constrained formulation with approximate solution measured by the gradient residual of the proximal augmented subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An inexact proximal augmented-Lagrangian iteration is specified by a tolerance \(\varepsilon_k\geq0\), a computed point \(x^{k+1}\), and the conditions \[\|
abla\Psi_k(x^{k+1})\|\leq\varepsilon_k,\qquad u^{k+1}=u^k+\alpha_k(Ax^{k+1}-b).\] In expanded form, the inexactness condition is \[\left\|
abla f(x^{k+1})+A^	op u^k+\alpha_kA^	op(Ax^{k+1}-b)+\alpha_k^{-1}(x^{k+1}-x^k)ight\|\leq\varepsilon_k.\] Exact proximal ALM is recovered when \(\varepsilon_k=0\). A relative-error variant additionally imposes \[\|
abla\Psi_k(x^{k+1})\|\leq\min\{\varepsilon_k,\gamma_k\|Ax^{k+1}-b\|\},\] where \(\varepsilon_k	o0\) and \(\gamma_k	o0\). The definition separates the approximate inner solve from the exact algebraic multiplier update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact proximal ALM stops the stabilized augmented-Lagrangian subproblem when its gradient norm is below a prescribed tolerance, rather than computing its exact minimizer. It then performs the usual multiplier update with the computed constraint residual. A stronger relative stopping rule also scales the allowed stationarity error by the current feasibility residual.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuously differentiable, \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(\alpha_k>0\).
The tolerance satisfies \(\varepsilon_k\geq0\); for the stated vanishing-error regime, \(\varepsilon_k\to0\) and \(\gamma_k\to0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(u^{k+1}=u^k+\alpha_k(Ax^{k+1}-b)\), the residual is \(\nabla f(x^{k+1})+A^\top u^{k+1}+\alpha_k^{-1}(x^{k+1}-x^k)\).
special_cases_latex: \(\varepsilon_k=0\) gives exact primal proximal stabilization.
Removing the proximal term gives the classical inexact augmented-Lagrangian stopping criterion.
immediate_consequences_latex: The computed point is an \(\varepsilon_k\)-stationary point of the stabilized inner objective.
If \(\varepsilon_k\to0\), any convergent subsequence with vanishing primal displacement and feasibility residual satisfies the limiting first-order KKT equation.
boundary_notes: The two cited sources separately support the proximal subproblem and the residual-controlled inexact ALM criterion; their combined formulation is a direct specialized synthesis.
Objective-gap and summable-distance error criteria are not included.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Newton methods on the augmented dual function
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\), with \(f\) and \(h\) twice continuously differentiable. Let \(L_c(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^\top h(x)+\frac c2\|h(x)\|^2\), and suppose a local minimizer \(x(\lambda,c)\) of \(L_c(\cdot,\lambda)\) is well defined. Define \(d_c(\lambda)=L_c(x(\lambda,c),\lambda)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local smooth equality-constrained regime in which the augmented dual is twice differentiable and its Hessian is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A second-order multiplier method is a multiplier-space Newton method applied to the augmented dual function. Its defining update is \[\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k-[
abla^2d_{c_k}(\lambda^k)]^{-1}
abla d_{c_k}(\lambda^k).\] Since \(
abla d_c(\lambda)=h(x(\lambda,c))\), the update can be written \[\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+B_k^{-1}h(x(\lambda^k,c_k)),\] where \[B_k=
abla h(x_k)^	op[
abla^2_{xx}L_{c_k}(x_k,\lambda^k)]^{-1}
abla h(x_k),\qquad x_k=x(\lambda^k,c_k).\] Thus curvature is modeled in multiplier space through a Schur complement of the augmented primal Hessian. Nonsingularity of the displayed matrices and existence of the local augmented-Lagrangian minimizer are part of the method’s domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A second-order multiplier method applies Newton’s method to the smooth augmented dual function. The dual gradient is the current constraint residual, and the negative dual Hessian is represented by a Schur-complement matrix built from the augmented-Lagrangian Hessian and the constraint Jacobian. The multiplier correction is the inverse of this matrix applied to the residual.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(h\) are twice continuously differentiable in the neighborhood under consideration.
The local minimizer \(x(\lambda,c)\) exists, \(\nabla^2_{xx}L_c(x(\lambda,c),\lambda)\) is invertible, and \(\nabla h(x(\lambda,c))\) has full column rank.
\(\nabla^2d_c(\lambda)\) is nonsingular at each generated multiplier.
equivalent_formulations_latex:
\(-
abla^2d_c(\lambda)=
abla h(x)^	op[
abla^2_{xx}L_c(x,\lambda)]^{-1}
abla h(x)\) at \(x=x(\lambda,c)\).
special_cases_latex: For a quadratic objective and linear equality constraints, the curvature matrix is determined by the corresponding constant augmented Hessian.
Replacing \(B_k\) by a secant approximation gives a quasi-Newton multiplier method.
immediate_consequences_latex: The multiplier correction is zero exactly when the augmented-dual gradient, equivalently the constraint residual, is zero.
The method requires second derivatives or equivalent Hessian-vector information.
boundary_notes: The definition is local and smooth; it does not assert global convergence from an arbitrary multiplier.
Singular constraint Jacobians or indefinite, singular augmented Hessians require modifications not included here.

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Multiplier Iterations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local Newton iteration on a twice-differentiable equality-constrained dual function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(d(y)=\inf_x\{f(x)+\langle y,c(x)angle\}\). Assume that near a dual solution \(y^*\), the minimizing branch \(x(y)\) is unique and twice continuously differentiable, so \(d\) is twice continuously differentiable and \(
abla^2d(y^k)\) is nonsingular. Initialize \(y^0\) in this neighborhood and iterate \[x^k=x(y^k),\qquad 
abla^2d(y^k)s^k=-
abla d(y^k),\qquad y^{k+1}=y^k+s^k.\] Since \(
abla d(y^k)=c(x^k)\), stop when \(\lVert c(x^k)Vert\leq\varepsilon\); output \((x^k,y^k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply Newton’s method to the smooth dual stationarity equation, using the primal constraint residual as the dual gradient.
assumptions_latex: The local minimizer \(x(y)\) is unique and twice continuously differentiable

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The second-order multiplier iteration first performs the ordinary augmented-Lagrangian multiplier update. It then applies one Newton correction to the unaugmented KKT system at the predicted primal-multiplier pair. Equivalently, the two stages implement the direct Schur-complement Newton step in multiplier space.

abla h(x_k)^	op[
abla^2_{xx}L_{c_k}(x_k,\lambda^k)]^{-1}
abla h(x_k)\).
special_cases_latex: If the Newton correction is omitted, only the ordinary first-order multiplier predictor remains.
For linear constraints and a quadratic objective, the bordered system is linear with constant unaugmented KKT curvature.
immediate_consequences_latex: The iteration separates feasibility prediction from second-order correction.
The primal and multiplier corrections are computed from one bordered linear system.

knowledge_statements.title: Geometric View of Second-Order Multiplier Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local quadratic-model geometry of Newton displacement in multiplier space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(d:\mathbb R^m	o\mathbb R\) be a twice continuously differentiable concave dual function, and suppose \(-
abla^2d(y)\succ0\). The second-order multiplier displacement is equivalently represented by \[s_N=\operatorname*{argmax}_{s\in\mathbb R^m}\left\{\langle
abla d(y),sangle+ rac12\langle s,
abla^2d(y)sangleight\}=-[
abla^2d(y)]^{-1}
abla d(y).\] Thus \(-
abla^2d(y)\) defines a local multiplier-space metric, and the Newton step is the metric-scaled dual gradient. The quadratic model’s level sets are ellipsoids whose principal axes are the eigenvectors of \(-
abla^2d(y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual curvature defines an ellipsoidal local metric; the second-order multiplier step is the gradient scaled by the inverse curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_N=-[\nabla^2d(y)]^{-1}\nabla d(y)\) uniquely maximizes the local concave quadratic model.

abla d(y)\in\operatorname{range}(M)\). In that case \(\operatorname*{argmax}q=M^\dagger

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal-value curvature interpretation of the second-order multiplier update
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\), define the local primal value function \(p(v)=\inf\{f(x):h(x)=v\}\). Assume \(p\) is twice differentiable near the residual \(v_k=h(x_k)\), and let \(\nabla_xL_{c_k}(x_k,\lambda_k)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local differential-geometric interpretation in constraint-perturbation space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The geometric form of the second-order multiplier iteration is defined by \[v_k=h(x_k),\qquad \widetilde\lambda_k=\lambda_k+c_kv_k,\] \[\lambda_{k+1}=\lambda_k+[
abla^2p(v_k)+c_kI]v_k=\widetilde\lambda_k+
abla^2p(v_k)v_k.\] Let \[\widetilde p_k(v)=p(v_k)+
abla p(v_k)^	op(v-v_k)+ rac12(v-v_k)^	op
abla^2p(v_k)(v-v_k)\] be the quadratic Taylor model of the primal value function at \(v_k\). Because the stationary augmented-Lagrangian relation gives \(\widetilde\lambda_k=-
abla p(v_k)\), the same update is characterized by \[\lambda_{k+1}=-
abla\widetilde p_k(0).\] Hence the new multiplier is the negative gradient at feasibility of the local quadratic model of the perturbation-value surface; the first-order multiplier update corresponds instead to using only its affine model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The geometric view uses the primal value function whose argument is the constraint perturbation. The second-order multiplier update predicts the negative value-function gradient at zero residual from a quadratic model constructed at the current residual. The ordinary multiplier predictor supplies the first-order part, while the value-function Hessian supplies the curvature correction.
assumptions_latex: The local value function \(p\) is twice differentiable at \(v_k=h(x_k)\).
The local value-function and augmented-dual sensitivity identities are well defined.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\lambda_{k+1}=\lambda_k+[\nabla^2p(v_k)+c_kI]v_k\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\nabla^2p(v_k)v_k=0\), the second-order and first-order multiplier predictions coincide.
For a locally quadratic value function, \(\widetilde p_k=p\) on the local model domain.
immediate_consequences_latex: Multiplier-space curvature is identified with curvature of the primal perturbation-value surface.
The correction depends on the residual direction \(v_k\), not on the full primal displacement.
boundary_notes: This is a local smooth interpretation and does not apply directly to a nondifferentiable value function.
The Taylor model is an interpretation of the iteration, not a global approximation guarantee.

notation.meaning: quadratic local model of the value function

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(r_c(\lambda)=h(x(\lambda,c))=\nabla d_c(\lambda)\) denote the residual or augmented-dual gradient for a smooth equality-constrained problem. Let \(C_k\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) be a nonsingular approximation of \(-\nabla^2d_{c_k}(\lambda^k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth local family encompassing direct dual secant models and multiplier curvature induced from primal quasi-Newton matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A quasi-Newton multiplier method is any iteration of the form \[\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+C_k^{-1}r_{c_k}(\lambda^k),\] in which \(C_k\) is updated from first-order information to approximate the positive multiplier curvature \(-
abla^2d_{c_k}(\lambda^k)\), rather than recomputed from exact second derivatives. The approximation may be constructed directly from multiplier secant pairs, or induced from a primal inverse-Hessian approximation \(D_k\) through \[C_k=
abla h(x_k)^	op D_k
abla h(x_k),\qquad D_k\approx[
abla^2_{xx}L_{c_k}(x_k,\lambda^k)]^{-1}.\] A valid direct secant update uses \(s_k=\lambda^{k+1}-\lambda^k\) and \(y_k=-(r_{c_{k+1}}(\lambda^{k+1})-r_{c_k}(\lambda^k))\), and imposes \(C_{k+1}s_k=y_k\) when parameter changes are absent or otherwise accounted for.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quasi-Newton multiplier method replaces the exact augmented-dual Hessian in a second-order multiplier step by a matrix learned from first-order changes. The approximation can be maintained directly in multiplier space through a secant equation or inherited from a quasi-Newton approximation to the augmented primal Hessian. The residual is then multiplied by the inverse approximate curvature.
assumptions_latex: The residual mapping \(r_c(\lambda)=h(x(\lambda,c))\) is locally single-valued and differentiable.

For an induced approximation, \(D_k\) and \(
abla h(x_k)\) have dimensions making \(
abla h(x_k)^	op D_k
abla h(x_k)\) nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+C_k^{-1}r_{c_k}(\lambda^k)\) with \(C_k\) obtained by a secant or induced quasi-Newton curvature update.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(C_k=\nabla h(x_k)^\top D_k\nabla h(x_k)\), the update is the approximate second-order iteration stated in equation (49) of the cited source.
A direct Hessian approximation may instead model \(\nabla^2p(h(x_k))+c_kI\).
special_cases_latex: Taking \(D_k=[\nabla^2_{xx}L_{c_k}(x_k,\lambda^k)]^{-1}\) recovers the exact second-order multiplier step.
BFGS and DFP are standard choices for generating the approximating matrix.
immediate_consequences_latex: Exact second derivatives are not required.
Curvature information accumulated during augmented-Lagrangian minimization may be reused in the multiplier update.
boundary_notes: A secant equation alone does not guarantee positive definiteness or convergence; update safeguards may be needed.
Penalty-parameter changes require transporting or modifying the stored curvature approximation.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Quasi-Newton Multiplier Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Secant approximation of the negative dual Hessian for multiplier updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(d:\mathbb R^m	o\mathbb R\) be a differentiable concave dual function. Initialize \(y^0\) and a symmetric positive-definite approximation \(B_0\approx-
abla^2d(y^0)\). At iteration \(k\), solve \(B_ks^k=
abla d(y^k)\), choose \(\alpha_k>0\), and set \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\alpha_ks^k\). Define \(p_k=y^{k+1}-y^k\) and \(q_k=-
abla d(y^{k+1})+
abla d(y^k)\), then update \(B_{k+1}\) by a symmetric secant formula satisfying \(B_{k+1}p_k=q_k\), whenever its curvature safeguard holds. Stop when \(\lVert
abla d(y^k)Vert\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace the negative dual Hessian by a positive-definite secant approximation and update multipliers along the resulting scaled dual gradient.
assumptions_latex: \(d\) is differentiable and concave on the iterates’ domain
The secant update is accepted only under its positive-curvature safeguard
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The multiplier direction satisfies \(s^k=B_k^{-1}\nabla d(y^k)\), while accepted updates satisfy \(B_{k+1}p_k=q_k\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Fix a penalty parameter \(c>0\) and let \(d_c:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) be a twice differentiable augmented dual function with gradient \(g(\lambda)=\nabla d_c(\lambda)=h(x(\lambda,c))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct multiplier-space quasi-Newton model with a fixed penalty parameter over each secant pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A dual quasi-Newton multiplier method maintains a nonsingular matrix \(H_k\) approximating the inverse dual Hessian \([
abla^2d_c(\lambda^k)]^{-1}\) and updates \[\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k-H_kg_k,\qquad g_k=
abla d_c(\lambda^k).\] After evaluating \(g_{k+1}\), define \(s_k=\lambda^{k+1}-\lambda^k\) and \(y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k\). The next approximation is required to satisfy the inverse secant relation \[H_{k+1}y_k=s_k.\] Equivalently, one may maintain \(B_k\approx
abla^2d_c(\lambda^k)\), impose \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\), and solve \(B_kp_k=-g_k\). This definition constructs curvature solely from multiplier displacements and augmented-dual gradient changes, unlike an induced method that imports a primal augmented-Hessian approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual quasi-Newton multiplier method applies a quasi-Newton iteration directly to the augmented dual function. Its curvature matrix is updated from changes in multipliers and changes in the constraint residual, which is the dual gradient. The defining secant equation approximates the dual Hessian or its inverse without using a primal Hessian approximation.
assumptions_latex: \(d_c\) is differentiable at all generated multipliers, and the penalty parameter is fixed while a secant pair is formed.
The maintained Hessian or inverse-Hessian approximation is nonsingular.
The secant vectors satisfy the nondegeneracy conditions required by the chosen update formula.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(B_kp_k=-g_k\), \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+p_k\), and \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\).
Because \(g_k=h(x(\lambda^k,c))\), the secant data are obtainable from successive constraint residuals.
special_cases_latex: Choosing \(H_k=[\nabla^2d_c(\lambda^k)]^{-1}\) gives the exact dual Newton iteration.
For \(m=1\), the secant condition reduces to the scalar secant approximation of the dual derivative.
immediate_consequences_latex: No second derivatives of \(f\), \(h\), or \(d_c\) are explicitly required by the dual update.
The stored matrix has dimension \(m\times m\), so direct dual quasi-Newton modeling is especially attractive when the number of constraints is small.
boundary_notes: Changing \(c\) changes the augmented dual function and invalidates an unadjusted secant pair.
The source discusses generating primal-value curvature approximations from computed values and gradients; the abstract secant equations here state that construction in standard quasi-Newton notation.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing a tangent-space basis transforms the reduced Hessian by congruence.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a smooth equality-constrained problem, let \(J_k=\nabla h(x_k)^\top\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank. Let \(Z_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) have orthonormal columns spanning \(\ker J_k\), so \(Z_k^\top Z_k=I\) and \(J_kZ_k=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local smooth method in which quasi-Newton curvature is stored only on the tangent space of the current constraint manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A reduced-Hessian quasi-Newton ALM represents primal curvature by a matrix \(R_k\in\mathbb R^{(n-m)	imes(n-m)}\) approximating \[Z_k^	op
abla^2_{xx}L(x_k,\lambda_k)Z_k.\] The tangential component of a primal correction is \(p_k^T=Z_kw_k\), where \[R_kw_k=-Z_k^	op
abla_xL(x_k,\lambda_k).\] A normal correction \(p_k^N\) is selected to satisfy the linearized feasibility equation \[J_k(p_k^N+p_k^T)=-h(x_k).\] The reduced matrix is then updated from projected displacement and projected Lagrangian-gradient differences, for example through a symmetric secant condition \[R_{k+1}s_k^R=y_k^R,\quad s_k^R=Z_k^	op(x_{k+1}-x_k),\quad y_k^R=Z_k^	op(
abla_xL(x_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1})-
abla_xL(x_k,\lambda_{k+1})).\] The method is “reduced” because only tangent-space curvature is approximated; normal behavior is governed by the constraints and multiplier equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduced-Hessian quasi-Newton ALM stores and updates curvature only in directions tangent to the constraint manifold. The tangential step solves a reduced quasi-Newton system, while a normal component enforces linearized feasibility. Projected steps and projected Lagrangian-gradient changes provide the reduced secant data.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(h\) are continuously differentiable, and the Lagrangian has the derivatives required to define its local Hessian model.
\(J_k\) has full row rank, and \(Z_k\) is an orthonormal null-space basis.
Each reduced approximation \(R_k\) is nonsingular; positive definiteness on the tangent space may be imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_kw_k=-Z_k^\top\nabla_xL(x_k,\lambda_k)\), \(p_k^T=Z_kw_k\), and \(J_k(p_k^N+p_k^T)=-h(x_k)\), with \(R_k\) updated by a reduced secant equation.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A full-space matrix \(H_k\) represents the same model when \(Z_k^\top H_kZ_k=R_k\) and \(z^\top H_kz>0\) for all nonzero \(z\in\ker J_k\).
special_cases_latex: If \(m=0\), then \(Z_k=I\) and the method reduces to an unconstrained quasi-Newton method.
Using the exact matrix \(R_k=Z_k^\top\nabla^2_{xx}L(x_k,\lambda_k)Z_k\) gives an exact reduced-Newton tangential step.
immediate_consequences_latex: The principal quasi-Newton matrix has dimension \((n-m)\times(n-m)\).
Positive definiteness of \(R_k\) is precisely positive definiteness of the modeled curvature on the tangent space.
boundary_notes: The cited source explicitly develops tangent-plane curvature modification and quasi-Newton Lagrangian variants; the displayed reduced secant notation is a canonical null-space specialization.
Changing the tangent basis requires transporting or reprojecting stored curvature information.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let an optimization model be represented by an objective \(F\), a feasible domain \(X\), and coupling constraints \(G(x)=0\) or \(G(x)\leq0\). An augmented-Lagrangian regime is determined jointly by the analytic class of \(F,G\) and the product structure of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A formal taxonomy covering nonsmooth composite, continuous separable, and discrete separable structures; “large-scale” is structural rather than a fixed dimension threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the specialized augmented-Lagrangian regime class by \[\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{spec}}:=\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{ns}}\cup\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{sep}}\cup\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{disc}},\] where \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{ns}}\) contains models with a proper lower-semicontinuous nonsmooth term \(\gamma(g(x))\); \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{sep}}\) contains continuous block models \[\min_{x_i\in X_i}\sum_{i=1}^N f_i(x_i)\quad\text{subject to}\quad\sum_{i=1}^N(A_ix_i-b_i)=0;\] and \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{disc}}\) contains separable models with at least one block domain having an integrality restriction. An ALM is specialized to such a regime when its augmented subproblem or multiplier update preserves or explicitly exploits the defining structure—for example, infimal-convolution smoothing for \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{ns}}\), block or incremental minimization for \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{sep}}\), or Lagrangian relaxation and structured discrete subproblem solution for \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{disc}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Specialized augmented-Lagrangian regimes are formally grouped by the structure that changes how augmented subproblems are represented or solved. The class includes nonsmooth composite models, continuous block-separable models with coupling constraints, and separable models containing discrete variables. A method belongs to the specialized family only when it preserves or uses that structure in its augmented subproblem or multiplier update.
assumptions_latex: Every model has a well-defined objective, block domain, and equality or inequality coupling map.
Membership in a subclass is determined by the displayed nonsmooth, separable, or discrete structure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{spec}}=\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{ns}}\cup\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{sep}}\cup\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{disc}}\), with membership and structural use defined as above.
special_cases_latex: A smooth dense nonlinear program with no separability or discrete variables is not specialized under this taxonomy.
A nonsmooth separable mixed-integer model may belong to all three subclasses simultaneously.
immediate_consequences_latex: The subclasses are not disjoint.
A specialized formulation must state which structural feature its augmented construction preserves.
boundary_notes: No universal numerical dimension defines “large-scale”; the term indicates that block or distributed structure is algorithmically material.
This union taxonomy synthesizes three source-supported regimes rather than quoting a single named definition.

children.top_down_role: Approximation and composite interfaces for nondifferentiable augmented models.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(f\) and \(g_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{r_i}\) be smooth on their domains, and let \(\gamma_i:\mathbb R^{r_i}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions. Consider \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)+\sum_i\gamma_i(g_i(x))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex outer nonsmooth terms composed with smooth inner mappings, treated through auxiliary variables and quadratic multiplier regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonsmooth augmented-Lagrangian regime of infimal-convolution type introduces variables \(v_i\in\mathbb R^{r_i}\) and the equivalent constraints \(v_i=0\) in \[\min_{x\in X,v_i}\ f(x)+\sum_i\gamma_i(g_i(x)-v_i).\] For \(c_k>0\) and multipliers \(y_i^k\), define \[p_{c_k}^i(t,y_i^k):=\min_{v_i}\left\{\gamma_i(t-v_i)+\langle y_i^k,v_i\rangle+\frac{c_k}{2}\|v_i\|^2\right\}.\] The augmented primal step minimizes \[f(x)+\sum_i p_{c_k}^i(g_i(x),y_i^k)\quad\text{over }x\in X,\] and, if \(v_i^k\) attains the inner minimum at the selected \(x^k\), the multiplier update is \[y_i^{k+1}=y_i^k+c_kv_i^k.\] The envelope \(p_c^i(\cdot,y)\) is finite-valued, convex, and continuously differentiable, despite possible nondifferentiability of \(\gamma_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This nonsmooth ALM regime handles a convex nonsmooth outer function by introducing an auxiliary displacement variable. Quadratic augmentation in that displacement produces an infimal-convolution envelope that is smooth in the composite argument. The outer augmented problem minimizes these envelopes, and the auxiliary minimizers determine the multiplier updates.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\gamma_i\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
Each \(c_k>0\), and the inner minimization defining \(p_{c_k}^i\) is over \(\mathbb R^{r_i}\).
The mappings needed to solve the outer subproblem are defined on \(X\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(p_c(t,y)=\sup_z\{\langle t,z\rangle-\gamma^*(z)-(2c)^{-1}\|z-y\|^2\}\).
The updated multiplier is the unique maximizer in the dual envelope representation and equals \(\nabla_tp_c(t,y)\).
special_cases_latex: \(\gamma(t)=|t|\) yields a smooth piecewise-quadratic envelope.
Indicator functions of equality, one-sided, or two-sided constraints recover corresponding multiplier constructions.
immediate_consequences_latex: The nonsmooth outer term is replaced in each augmented subproblem by a continuously differentiable envelope.
Only one multiplier vector is required for each composite term in the displayed formulation.
boundary_notes: Nonconvex or non-Lipschitz outer terms outside proper closed convex analysis are not covered.
Smoothness of the envelope in \(t\) does not imply twice differentiability.

children.top_down_role: Approximation procedures for nondifferentiable constraint systems.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative transfer from smoothed feasibility to the original nondifferentiable constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\sup_{x\in X}\|c_\mu(x)-c(x)\|\le\omega(\mu)\) with \(\omega(\mu)\to0\). Then \(\|c(x)\|\le\|c_\mu(x)\|+\omega(\mu)\). Thus \(\mu_k\downarrow0\) and \(\|c_{\mu_k}(x_k)\|+\omega(\mu_k)\to0\) imply \(\|c(x_k)\|\to0\). For an inequality component, \([c_i(x)]_+\le[c_{i,\mu}(x)]_++|c_{i,\mu}(x)-c_i(x)|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smoothed feasibility residual certifies original feasibility only after adding a quantitative approximation-error allowance.
assumptions_latex: The uniform error bound holds on the iterate-containing set.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Approximation Feasibility Transfer

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized-derivative consistency for smooth approximations of locally Lipschitz constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c_i\) be locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\), and let \(c_{i,\mu}\) be continuously differentiable for \(\mu>0\). The family is Clarke-gradient consistent at \(\bar x\) when \(c_{i,\mu}(x)\to c_i(\bar x)\) as \((x,\mu)\to(\bar x,0)\), and every finite cluster point of \(\nabla c_{i,\mu_j}(x^j)\), for \((x^j,\mu_j)\to(\bar x,0)\), belongs to \(\partial_Cc_i(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Values must converge to the original constraint, and every finite limiting smoothing gradient must be a Clarke subgradient.
knowledge_statements.title: Gradient-Consistent Constraint Smoothing

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer template coupling smoothing, inner accuracy, and corrected feasibility tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), choose \(\mu_k>0\), form an augmented model using \(c_{\mu_k}\), compute a point with stated inner stationarity residual at most \(\varepsilon_k\), and update multipliers using the smoothed constraint residual. When \(\|c_\mu(x)-c(x)\|\le\omega(\mu)\) on the iterate-containing set, a consistency schedule uses \(\mu_k\downarrow0\), \(\varepsilon_k\downarrow0\), and a feasibility test such as \(\|c_{\mu_k}(x_k)\|+\omega(\mu_k)\le\eta_k\) with \(\eta_k\downarrow0\). This is a template, not a stationarity-convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Smoothing, inner-solve, and corrected feasibility tolerances must be driven to zero together.
assumptions_latex: A known iterate-set value-error bound \(\|c_\mu-c\|\le\omega(\mu)\) is available.
knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance-Coupled Smoothing ALM Template

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Smoothing Does Not Transfer Feasibility on Escaping Iterates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of feasibility transfer without uniform control on the iterate-containing set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c(x)\equiv1\) and \(c_\mu(x)=1-\exp(-(\mu x-1)^2/\mu^2)\). For every fixed \(x\), \(c_\mu(x)\to1=c(x)\) as \(\mu\downarrow0\). However, for \(x_\mu=1/\mu\), \(c_\mu(x_\mu)=0\) while \(c(x_\mu)=1\). Hence pointwise approximation alone does not let a vanishing smoothed residual certify original feasibility along an escaping sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pointwise-consistent smoothing can have zero residual along unbounded points where the original residual remains one.
knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Smoothing Does Not Transfer Feasibility on Escaping Iterates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Original-problem stationarity bound from quantified smoothing-gradient errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(v_i\in\partial_Cc_i(x)\) and \(\|
abla c_{i,\mu}(x)-v_i\|\le\delta_i(\mu,x)\). If \[\left\|
abla f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i
abla c_{i,\mu}(x)ight\|\le\varepsilon,\] then \[\operatorname{dist}\left(0,
abla f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i\partial_Cc_i(x)ight)\le\varepsilon+\sum_{i=1}^m|\lambda_i|\delta_i(\mu,x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Original nonsmooth stationarity is bounded by the smoothed residual plus multiplier-weighted gradient-approximation errors.
assumptions_latex: For each \(i\), a vector \(v_i\in\partial_Cc_i(x)\) satisfies the stated approximation bound.
The smoothed stationarity residual is at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier-Weighted Stationarity Transfer

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Why vanishing smoothing-gradient error alone does not guarantee original stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Multiplier-weighted stationarity errors enter as \(\sum_i|\lambda_i^k|\delta_i^k\). Conditions \(\delta_i^k\to0\) alone are insufficient: \(\lambda^k=k\) and \(\delta^k=1/k\) give \(\delta^k\to0\) but \(|\lambda^k|\delta^k=1\). Thus transfer requires bounded multipliers or the coupled condition \(\sum_i|\lambda_i^k|\delta_i^k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing gradient-approximation errors may retain a nonzero multiplier-weighted contribution.
knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded-Multiplier Obstruction to Stationarity Transfer

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Log-Sum-Exp Approximation of a Finite Maximum Constraint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete gradient-consistent smoothing with a uniform constraint-value error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(c(x)=\max_{1\le\ell\le q}\phi_\ell(x)\), where each \(\phi_\ell\) is continuously differentiable, and define \[c_\mu(x)=\mu\log\!\left(\sum_{\ell=1}^q\exp(\phi_\ell(x)/\mu)ight),\qquad \mu>0.\] Then \[c(x)\le c_\mu(x)\le c(x)+\mu\log q,\qquad 
abla c_\mu(x)=\sum_{\ell=1}^qw_\ell(x,\mu)
abla\phi_\ell(x),\] where \(w_\ell\ge0\) and \(\sum_\ell w_\ell=1\). If \((x_k,\mu_k)	o( ar x,0)\), every finite cluster point of \(
abla c_{\mu_k}(x_k)\) lies in \(\operatorname{conv}\{
abla\phi_\ell( ar x):\phi_\ell( ar x)=c( ar x)\}=\partial_Cc( ar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Log-sum-exp approximates a finite maximum within μ log q, and limiting smoothing gradients are convex combinations of active gradients.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\phi_\ell\) is continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.title: Log-Sum-Exp Approximation of a Finite Maximum Constraint

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential transfer from smoothed equality-constrained stationarity to Clarke stationarity of the original constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_k	o ar x\), \(\mu_k\downarrow0\), and \(\lambda^k	o ar\lambda\). Let \(f\) be continuously differentiable near \( ar x\), and let each equality constraint \(c_i\) be locally Lipschitz there. Suppose \(\|c_{\mu_k}(x_k)-c(x_k)\|	o0\), \(\|c_{\mu_k}(x_k)\|	o0\), and \[\left\|

assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuously differentiable and each \(c_i\) is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\).
Constraint-value approximation, smoothed feasibility, smoothed stationarity, and the displayed Clarke-gradient approximation errors vanish.

notation.meaning: selected Clarke subgradient of the original constraint

knowledge_statements.title: Limit Stationarity Transfer under Quantified Smoothing Errors
Nondifferentiable Constraint Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency conditions for smooth approximations of locally Lipschitz constraint components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be locally Lipschitz and let \(c_{i,\mu}\) be continuously differentiable approximations for \(\mu>0\). A gradient-consistent approximation at \(\bar x\) satisfies \[c_{i,\mu}(x)\to c_i(\bar x)\quad\text{whenever}\quad(x,\mu)\to(\bar x,0),\] and \[\left\{\lim_j\nabla c_{i,\mu_j}(x^j):(x^j,\mu_j)\to(\bar x,0)\right\}\subseteq\partial_Cc_i(\bar x),\] for every convergent gradient subsequence. Using \(c_{i,\mu_k}\) in an augmented subproblem is consistent only if \(\mu_k\downarrow0\) and the approximation error is controlled relative to the outer feasibility and stationarity tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth constraint approximation must converge in value, and every limiting approximate gradient must be a Clarke subgradient of the original constraint.
assumptions_latex: The displayed gradient sequences have finite limits
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All limiting approximation gradients belong to \(\partial_Cc_i(\bar x)\), and approximation values converge to \(c_i(\bar x)\).

notation.meaning: smooth approximation of the ith constraint

children.title: Nonsmooth Composite ALM
children.top_down_role: Augmented methods preserving nonsmooth composite objective structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact augmented-Lagrangian method preserving a convex nonsmooth composite term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_x f(x)+h(Ax)\), introduce \(z=Ax\). Given \(y^k\) and \(\rho_k>0\), compute a global minimizer \[(x^{k+1},z^{k+1})\in\arg\min_{x,z}\left\{f(x)+h(z)+\langle y^k,Ax-z\rangle+\frac{\rho_k}{2}\|Ax-z\|^2\right\},\] then update \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho_k(Ax^{k+1}-z^{k+1})\). The term \(h\) remains unsmoothed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split the composite argument, solve the joint augmented subproblem exactly, and update the multiplier from the split residual.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex and is differentiable on its domain.
\(A\) is linear and each displayed joint minimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax-z\) is the ALM feasibility residual while \(h(z)\) retains its nonsmooth structure.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Split Composite ALM

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order certificate for the split composite formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the split problem \(\min f(x)+h(z)\) subject to \(Ax-z=0\), a primal-dual point \((x,z,y)\) satisfies the convex KKT system exactly when \[Ax-z=0,\qquad \nabla f(x)+A^\top y=0,\qquad y\in\partial h(z).\] Accordingly, the feasibility residual, smooth stationarity residual, and distance \(\operatorname{dist}(y,\partial h(z))\) form a complete first-order residual certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composite stationarity requires split feasibility, smooth x-stationarity, and the nonsmooth subgradient condition together.
assumptions_latex: A standard convex qualification ensures KKT necessity for optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax=z,\ \nabla f(x)+A^\top y=0,\ y\in\partial h(z)\) certifies primal-dual optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Composite Split KKT Residual

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Proximal Elimination of the Composite Block
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact elimination of the nonsmooth split variable for fixed x and multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \((x,y,\rho)\), \[\inf_z\left\{h(z)+\langle y,Ax-z\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax-z\|^2\right\}=e_{1/\rho}h(Ax+y/\rho)-\frac{\|y\|^2}{2\rho},\] where \(e_{1/\rho}h(v):=\inf_z\{h(z)+(\rho/2)\|z-v\|^2\}\). The unique minimizing block is \(z^+=\operatorname{prox}_{h/\rho}(Ax+y/\rho)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For fixed x, the nonsmooth split block is solved by a proximal map and can be represented by a Moreau envelope.

notation.meaning: Moreau envelope with quadratic coefficient rho

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Elimination of the Composite Block

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order error rule for an inexact joint split-ALM subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho_k(Ax^{k+1}-z^{k+1})\). An inexact joint subproblem may be certified by \[a_x^{k+1}=\nabla f(x^{k+1})+A^\top y^{k+1},\qquad a_z^{k+1}\in\partial h(z^{k+1})-y^{k+1},\] with \(\|(a_x^{k+1},a_z^{k+1})\|\le\varepsilon_k\). The exact subproblem inclusion is recovered when \(\varepsilon_k=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate joint composite subproblems require explicit smooth and nonsmooth stationarity errors.
assumptions_latex: h is proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Composite Subproblem Residual

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fenchel Dual of the Split Composite Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual formulation of the split equality z=Ax.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\inf_x\{f(x)+h(Ax)\}\), the split formulation \(\inf_{x,z}\{f(x)+h(z):Ax-z=0\}\) has dual \[\sup_y\{-f^*(-A^\top y)-h^*(y)\}.\] If \(f\) and \(h\) are proper closed convex and \(A\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\cap\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}h)\ne\varnothing\), strong duality holds and the KKT conditions are \(Ax=z\), \(-A^\top y\in\partial f(x)\), and \(y\in\partial h(z)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The split composite problem has a Fenchel dual formed from the conjugates of its two objective terms.
assumptions_latex: f and h are proper, closed, and convex.
The stated relative-interior qualification is used for strong duality.
knowledge_statements.title: Fenchel Dual of the Split Composite Problem

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact inner stationarity does not force split feasibility when positive penalty parameters have finite total mass.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x \tfrac12x^2+\tfrac12x^2\), split as \(\min_{x,z}\{\tfrac12x^2+\tfrac12z^2:x-z=0\}\). Apply exact split ALM with penalties \(\rho_k>0\). With \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho_k(x^{k+1}-z^{k+1})\), exact subproblem stationarity gives \(x^{k+1}=-y^{k+1}\), \(z^{k+1}=y^{k+1}\), and \(y^{k+1}=y^k/(1+2\rho_k)\). If \(y^0\ne0\) and \(\sum_k\rho_k<\infty\), then \(y^k\) converges to a nonzero limit and \(x^{k+1}-z^{k+1}=-2y^{k+1}\not\to0\), although every inner first-order residual is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even exact composite-subproblem stationarity can leave a persistent split residual when the positive penalty sequence is summable.
assumptions_latex: Every joint augmented subproblem is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.title: Summable-Penalty Failure of Split-Residual Convergence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact residual identity and finite-iterate feasibility bound for split composite ALM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho_k(Ax^{k+1}-z^{k+1})\) with \(\rho_k>0\), \[Ax^{k+1}-z^{k+1}=\frac{y^{k+1}-y^k}{\rho_k}.\] Hence \(\|y^{k+1}-y^k\|\le\rho_k\eta_k\) certifies \(\|Ax^{k+1}-z^{k+1}\|\le\eta_k\). If \(\inf_k\rho_k>0\) and \(y^{k+1}-y^k\to0\), the split residual tends to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The split residual equals the multiplier increment divided by the penalty.
assumptions_latex: The multiplier update is applied exactly.
knowledge_statements.title: Split Feasibility from Multiplier Increments
Nonsmooth Composite ALM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structure-preserving ALM for a smooth-plus-nonsmooth composite objective via variable splitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x f(x)+h(Ax)\), where \(f\) is differentiable and \(h\) is proper, closed, and convex. Introduce \(z=Ax\) and initialize \((x^0,z^0,y^0)\). For \(\rho_k>0\), compute an exact or prescribed-accuracy minimizer \[(x^{k+1},z^{k+1})\approx\operatorname*{argmin}_{x,z}\left\{f(x)+h(z)+\langle y^k,Ax-z\rangle+\frac{\rho_k}{2}\lVert Ax-z\rVert^2\right\},\] then set \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho_k(Ax^{k+1}-z^{k+1})\). Stop when primal feasibility and the composite KKT residuals are below tolerance. The \(z\)-optimality condition retains \(\partial h(z^{k+1})\) without smoothing \(h\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split the composite argument, minimize an augmented objective that keeps the nonsmooth term intact, then update the multiplier from the coupling residual.
assumptions_latex: \(h:\mathbb R^p\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The nonsmooth structure is preserved through the condition \(0\in\partial h(z^{k+1})-y^k-\rho_k(Ax^{k+1}-z^{k+1})\).
review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports composite nonsmooth ALM with variable splitting.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and variable-splitting construction fit the nonsmooth composite ALM leaf. However, the statement allows an exact or prescribed-accuracy minimizer while asserting an exact z-optimality inclusion; an approximate solve requires a defined residual or error inclusion. A source is needed to select and state the intended exact or inexact composite ALM variant.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The proposed theorem claims that saddle-point existence, bounded positive penalties, bounded iterates, and \(\sum_k\varepsilon_k<\infty\) imply KKT cluster points for the displayed first-order residual rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proposed convergence theorem is not accepted without a direct inexact-ALM result and conditions ensuring primal residual or multiplier-increment convergence.
assumptions_latex: The proposed assumptions do not explicitly ensure \(Ax^{k+1}-z^{k+1}\to0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Convergence is not established by the stated record.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Structure-preserving ALM for a two-block nonsmooth composite model
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(h_1:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(h_2:\mathbb R^p\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper closed convex functions. Consider \(\min_{x,z}h_1(x)+h_2(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\), where \(A\) and \(B\) are linear maps.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex two-block composite model with exact joint minimization; nonsmooth terms remain unlinearized.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The nonsmooth composite augmented Lagrangian is \[L_\rho(x,z;y)=h_1(x)+h_2(z)+\langle y,Ax+Bz-c\rangle+\frac\rho2\|Ax+Bz-c\|^2,\qquad\rho>0.\] A nonsmooth composite ALM is the iteration \[(x^{k+1},z^{k+1})\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x,z}L_\rho(x,z;y^k),\] \[y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c).\] The defining structural property is that \(h_1\) and \(h_2\) are retained exactly in the primal subproblem, so their extended-valued domains and nondifferentiability are preserved. Only the linear coupling constraint is quadratically augmented. The joint minimization distinguishes this ALM from ADMM, which replaces the joint primal minimization by successive block minimizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a two-block convex composite problem, the nonsmooth composite ALM adds a quadratic penalty only to the linear coupling constraint. It jointly minimizes the resulting augmented Lagrangian while keeping both nonsmooth functions unchanged, and then updates the multiplier by the coupling residual. Sequential block minimization would instead define ADMM.
assumptions_latex: \(h_1\) and \(h_2\) are proper, closed, and convex.
\(A\) and \(B\) are linear, \(c\) is in the coupling space, and \(\rho>0\).
The joint augmented-Lagrangian subproblem attains a minimum.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The primal step also minimizes \(h_1(x)+h_2(z)+\frac\rho2\|Ax+Bz-c+\rho^{-1}y^k\|^2\), up to a constant independent of \((x,z)\).
special_cases_latex: Setting \(B=-I\) and \(c=0\) gives a lifted composite model with constraint \(Ax=z\).
Indicator functions among \(h_1,h_2\) encode convex set constraints without changing the formula.
immediate_consequences_latex: The first-order conditions use \(\partial h_1\) and \(\partial h_2\), so differentiability is unnecessary.
The multiplier update is the scaled residual of the sole coupling constraint.
boundary_notes: Alternating, linearized, and proximal block variants are not part of this exact joint-minimization definition.
Nonconvex composite functions require separate assumptions and are excluded.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vacuity of Limiting Stationarity at an Ell-p Singularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity pathology for a canonical non-Lipschitz sparsity term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\phi(t)=|t|^p\) with \(0<p<1\), \(\widehat\partial\phi(0)=\partial\phi(0)=\mathbb R\), where \(\widehat\partial\) and \(\partial\) denote the Fréchet and limiting subdifferentials. Hence \(0\in\partial\phi(0)+q\) for every finite \(q\in\mathbb R\). In a constrained objective containing \(|x_j|^p\), the limiting-stationarity inclusion in a zero coordinate therefore imposes no balance on a finite smooth Lagrangian contribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a zero ell-p coordinate with p below one, the limiting subdifferential is the whole line, making ordinary limiting stationarity noninformative in that coordinate.
assumptions_latex: All other Lagrangian contributions in the coordinate have finite derivatives.
knowledge_statements.title: Vacuity of Limiting Stationarity at an Ell-p Singularity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Majorized Reweighting Inside an ALM Subproblem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safeguarded surrogate step for an ell-p term within a fixed augmented subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0<p<1\) and \(\epsilon>0\), concavity of \(u\mapsto(u+\epsilon)^p\) gives \[(|x_j|+\epsilon)^p\le (|x_j^t|+\epsilon)^p+p(|x_j^t|+\epsilon)^{p-1}(|x_j|-|x_j^t|).\] Thus a fixed augmented subproblem containing \(\sum_j(|x_j|+\epsilon)^p\) admits the weighted-\(\ell_1\) majorizer \(\sum_jw_j^t|x_j|\), where \(w_j^t=p(|x_j^t|+\epsilon)^{p-1}\), plus the unchanged augmented terms and the constants making the bound tight at \(x^t\). A surrogate step that does not increase this tight majorizer does not increase that fixed smoothed augmented objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Safeguarded reweighting supplies a finite weighted-ell-one majorizer for a fixed smoothed ell-p augmented subproblem.
assumptions_latex: The multiplier, penalty, and smoothing parameter remain fixed during the majorization step.
The new point does not increase the tight surrogate.
knowledge_statements.title: Majorized Reweighting Inside an ALM Subproblem
Non-Lipschitz ALM Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies why classical smooth ALM stationarity tests fail for non-Lipschitz objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(0<p<1\) and consider \(\min_x |x|^p\) subject to \(h(x)=0\), with augmented Lagrangian \(\mathcal L_\rho(x,y)=|x|^p+y^\top h(x)+(\rho/2)\lVert h(x)\rVert^2\). The objective is not locally Lipschitz at \(x=0\), and its classical derivative is unbounded as \(x\to0\) through nonzero points. Consequently, an ALM analysis based on a locally Lipschitz objective, the Clarke subdifferential, or a uniform bound on objective subgradients cannot be applied at a feasible solution having a zero component. A valid non-Lipschitz regime must instead specify an appropriate limiting stationarity notion and a subproblem rule that remains meaningful at singular coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For objectives such as |x|^p with 0<p<1, classical Lipschitz-based ALM stationarity and bounded-subgradient arguments fail at zero components; a singularity-compatible stationarity notion is required.
assumptions_latex: \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is continuously differentiable near the point considered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Classical locally Lipschitz ALM theory is inapplicable at feasible points where a term \(|x_j|^p\) is singular.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, but the scalar example uses x while the assumptions declare h on R^n and the conclusion generalizes to components x_j. More importantly, the required non-Lipschitz stationarity framework and the asserted inapplicability of Clarke-based ALM analysis have no cited source.

e0\), to \(

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous but not locally Lipschitz at at least one point of its effective domain, and let \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be continuously differentiable. Consider \(\min F(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Candidate finite-dimensional equality-constrained definition using limiting subdifferentials; no inspected source in the supplied corpus established this exact regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A non-Lipschitz ALM regime is an augmented-Lagrangian construction for which the objective \(F\) is nonconvex and fails to be locally Lipschitz on a relevant part of its domain. For \(c_k>0\), define \[\mathcal L_{c_k}(x,\lambda^k)=F(x)+\langle\lambda^k,h(x)\rangle+\frac{c_k}{2}\|h(x)\|^2.\] An exact iteration selects \[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\mathcal L_{c_k}(x,\lambda^k),\qquad \lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+c_kh(x^{k+1}).\] A limiting-stationary inexact variant requires \[\operatorname{dist}\!\left(0,\partial F(x^{k+1})+\nabla h(x^{k+1})\lambda^k+c_k\nabla h(x^{k+1})h(x^{k+1})\right)\leq\varepsilon_k,\] where \(\partial F\) denotes the limiting subdifferential. The non-Lipschitz designation concerns the analytic class of \(F\), not a different multiplier formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A non-Lipschitz ALM applies quadratic augmentation to equality constraints when the proper lower-semicontinuous objective is nonconvex and not locally Lipschitz. Exact inner minimization or a limiting-subdifferential stationarity residual replaces gradient-based smooth subproblem conditions, while the multiplier update remains the scaled constraint residual.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is proper and lower semicontinuous and is not locally Lipschitz at some relevant point.
For the inexact form, the limiting subdifferential expression is nonempty at the computed point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}\) satisfies the exact minimization or displayed limiting-stationarity condition, and \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+c_kh(x^{k+1})\).
special_cases_latex: Objectives containing \(\sum_i|x_i|^q\) with \(0<q<1\) are non-Lipschitz at coordinates equal to zero.
If \(F\) is locally Lipschitz, the regime leaves this subclass and Clarke-type stationarity may become available.
immediate_consequences_latex: Ordinary gradient residuals need not exist at a computed primal point.
Smooth-ALM convergence statements cannot be transferred without additional variational assumptions.
boundary_notes: No inspected authoritative source supported the exact formulation and scope of this slot.
This definition does not assert convergence, constraint qualification, or exact-penalty properties.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Joint ALM regime for block-separable objectives with linear coupling
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(N\geq2\), let \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\) be nonempty closed convex sets, let \(f_i:\mathbb R^{n_i}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper closed convex functions, and consider \(\min\sum_{i=1}^Nf_i(x_i)\) subject to \(x_i\in X_i\) and \(\sum_{i=1}^N(A_ix_i-b_i)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous finite-block separable model with a shared linear equality; “large-scale” refers to the importance of block structure, not a numerical cutoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the residual \[r(x_1,\ldots,x_N)=\sum_{i=1}^N(A_ix_i-b_i),\] the standard joint augmented Lagrangian is \[\mathcal L_c(x_1,\ldots,x_N;\lambda)=\sum_{i=1}^N f_i(x_i)+\langle\lambda,r(x)\rangle+\frac c2\|r(x)\|^2.\] A large-scale separable ALM regime is the iteration \[(x_1^{k+1},\ldots,x_N^{k+1})\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_i\in X_i}\mathcal L_{c_k}(x_1,ldots,x_N;\lambda^k),\] \[\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+c_kr(x_1^{k+1},\ldots,x_N^{k+1}).\] The objective and domain are block separable, but the quadratic residual term generally couples all blocks. Consequently, this definition describes joint augmented minimization; incremental, distributed, and alternating architectures are distinct mechanisms designed to recover computational separability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A large-scale separable regime has a sum of block objectives and Cartesian-product block constraints, together with a shared linear coupling equation. Its standard ALM jointly minimizes the augmented Lagrangian and then updates the common multiplier. Although the unaugmented Lagrangian separates by blocks, the squared sum of coupling residuals generally destroys exact separability.
assumptions_latex: Each \(X_i\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and each \(f_i\) is proper, closed, and convex.
The coupling maps \(A_i\) are linear and \(c_k>0\).
The joint augmented subproblem attains its minimum.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The quadratic term is \(\frac{c_k}{2}\|\sum_i(A_ix_i-b_i)\|^2\), which explicitly displays cross-block coupling.
special_cases_latex: For \(N=2\), the model is the standard two-block linearly coupled composite problem.
If every \(A_i=0\) and \(\sum_i b_i=0\), the primal minimization decomposes completely.
immediate_consequences_latex: The ordinary Lagrangian dual function decomposes into independent block infima.
The standard quadratic augmented subproblem is generally nonseparable despite the separable objective.
boundary_notes: Alternating direction and incremental augmented-Lagrangian methods are not identified with the exact joint iteration.
Discrete block domains are excluded and belong to a discrete multiplier regime.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Method-classification boundary for continuously separable multiplier iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(L(x,y)=\sum_i f_i(x_i)+y^\top(\sum_iA_ix_i-b)\), minimization over \(\prod_iX_i\) always decomposes by blocks. For \(\mathcal L_\rho=L+(\rho/2)\|\sum_iA_ix_i-b\|^2\), the same decomposition generally fails because of cross terms \(\rho x_i^\top A_i^\top A_jx_j\). Consequently, independent minimization of the ordinary local Lagrangians followed by a residual subgradient update is dual decomposition, not an exact quadratic-ALM primal step, unless the cross terms vanish on the block domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ordinary Lagrangian dual decomposition is always separable, whereas quadratic ALM is separable only under the cross-term criterion.
assumptions_latex: The objective and domains are block separable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{independent ordinary-Lagrangian minimization}\not\equiv\text{exact quadratic-ALM minimization}\) in general.
knowledge_statements.title: Ordinary-Dual Versus Augmented Separability

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain-sensitive criterion for block separability of an affine-coupling quadratic augmented Lagrangian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_i=X_i-X_i\) and \(r(x)=\sum_{i=1}^N A_ix_i-b\). The quadratic augmented Lagrangian is additively separable on \(\prod_iX_i\) if and only if \(u_i^\top A_i^\top A_j u_j=0\) for every \(i\ne j\), \(u_i\in D_i\), and \(u_j\in D_j\). In particular, \(A_i^\top A_j=0\) for all \(i\ne j\) is sufficient, and is necessary when each difference set spans its block space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic augmentation preserves block separability exactly when every cross-block bilinear term vanishes on the feasible block-difference spaces.
assumptions_latex: The objective and domain are block separable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal L_\rho\text{ is block separable on }\prod_iX_i\iff u_i^\top A_i^\top A_j u_j=0\) for all admissible cross-block differences.

notation.meaning: difference set of block domain Xi

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Quadratic-Augmentation Separability Criterion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact continuous separable ALM under the domain-sensitive cross-term criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{\sum_i f_i(x_i):x_i\in X_i,\ \sum_iA_ix_i=b\}\), suppose \(u_i^{\mathsf T}A_i^{\mathsf T}A_ju_j=0\) for all \(i\ne j\), \(u_i\in X_i-X_i\), and \(u_j\in X_j-X_j\). At iteration \(k\), independently minimize the resulting separated augmented block objectives, concatenate their global minimizers into \(x^{k+1}\), form \(r^{k+1}=\sum_iA_ix_i^{k+1}-b\), and set \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho_kr^{k+1}\). The concatenated point globally minimizes the joint augmented subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When all augmented cross terms vanish on the continuous block domains, independent global block solves exactly implement the joint ALM primal step.
assumptions_latex: Each \(X_i\) is nonempty and every displayed block minimum is attained.
For every \(i\ne j\), the cross bilinear form vanishes on \((X_i-X_i)\times(X_j-X_j)\).

notation.meaning: affine coupling matrix for block i

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Separable Continuous ALM Step
Continuous Separable Multiplier Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual multiplier iteration for continuously valued block-separable problems with linear coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{\sum_{i=1}^N f_i(x_i):x_i\in X_i,\ \sum_{i=1}^N A_i x_i=b\}\), where every \(X_i\) is a nonempty continuous-variable set. Given \(y^0\) and stepsizes \(\alpha_k>0\), iteration \(k\) solves, independently for each block, \(x_i^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x_i\in X_i}\{f_i(x_i)+(y^k)^\top A_i x_i\}\). A coordinator forms \(r^{k+1}=\sum_i A_i x_i^{k+1}-b\) and updates \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\alpha_k r^{k+1}\). Stop when a prescribed primal-residual and dual-progress test is met; output the final blocks and multiplier. The independent minimizations implement a separable dual multiplier step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each continuous block minimizes its local Lagrangian independently; a coordinator aggregates the coupling residual and updates the common multiplier.
assumptions_latex: \(f_i:X_i\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) are proper and each displayed block minimum is attained.
\(A_i\) and \(b\) define the sole cross-block coupling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal oracle decomposes into \(N\) independent continuous subproblems, followed by one multiplier update.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Incremental augmented-Lagrangian multiplier method for continuous separable blocks
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min\sum_{i=1}^Nf_i(x_i)\) subject to \(x_i\in X_i\) and \(\sum_i(A_ix_i-b_i)=0\), where the \(X_i\) are nonempty closed convex subsets of Euclidean spaces and the \(f_i\) are convex.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous separable blocks processed sequentially through decomposable incremental augmented-Lagrangian subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a stepsize \(\alpha_k>0\), define the block incremental augmented Lagrangian \[\mathcal L_{\alpha_k,i}(x_i,\psi)=f_i(x_i)+\langle\psi,A_ix_i-b_i\rangle+\frac{\alpha_k}{2}\|A_ix_i-b_i\|^2.\] A continuous separable incremental multiplier cycle starts with \(\psi_k^0=\lambda^k\) and, for \(i=1,\ldots,N\), computes \[x_i^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_i\in X_i}\mathcal L_{\alpha_k,i}(x_i,\psi_k^{i-1}),\] \[\psi_k^i=\psi_k^{i-1}+\alpha_k(A_ix_i^k-b_i).\] The outer multiplier is then \[\lambda^{k+1}=\psi_k^N.\] Each primal minimization involves only one continuous block, so the method exploits separability that the standard joint quadratic augmented Lagrangian would destroy. The multiplier passed between blocks aggregates their residual contributions over one cycle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous separable multiplier method can preserve block decomposition by processing one block at a time. Each block solves its own augmented-Lagrangian subproblem using the current intermediate multiplier, after which that multiplier is updated by the block residual. The multiplier remaining after a complete block cycle becomes the next outer multiplier.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is convex and each \(X_i\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
Each \(A_i\) is linear, \(b_i\) lies in the common coupling space, and \(\alpha_k>0\).
Every block subproblem attains a minimizer.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Each intermediate update is the dual proximal step \(\psi_k^i\in\arg\max_\lambda\{q_i(\lambda)-(2\alpha_k)^{-1}\|\lambda-\psi_k^{i-1}\|^2\}\).
special_cases_latex: For \(N=1\), the cycle is the ordinary augmented-Lagrangian multiplier update for one block.
If block minimizations are carried out simultaneously from a common multiplier, the resulting architecture is parallel rather than incremental.
immediate_consequences_latex: The block primal subproblems are independent in dimension and data except for the multiplier communicated between them.
The full-cycle multiplier change equals \(\alpha_k\sum_i(A_ix_i^k-b_i)\).
boundary_notes: The method is sequential within each cycle; asynchronous and parallel variants require separate coordination rules.
The source’s convergence framework places additional effective-domain conditions on the component dual functions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact block separability of the quadratic augmented Lagrangian for affine coupling constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(r(x)=\sum_{i=1}^N A_i x_i-b\), the quadratic term expands as \[\frac{\rho}{2}\|r(x)\|^2=\frac{\rho}{2}\sum_i\|A_ix_i\|^2+\rho\sum_{i<j}x_i^\top A_i^\top A_jx_j-\rho\sum_i b^\top A_ix_i+\frac{\rho}{2}\|b\|^2.\] Hence the augmented Lagrangian \(\sum_i f_i(x_i)+y^\top r(x)+(\rho/2)\|r(x)\|^2\) is additively block-separable for every \(x\) if and only if \(A_i^\top A_j=0\) for all \(i\ne j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic augmentation normally introduces cross-block terms. Exact independent block minimization survives precisely when the coupling images of distinct blocks are mutually orthogonal.
assumptions_latex: The objective and block domains are additively separable.

children.title: Parallel Block ALM Architectures
children.top_down_role: Parallel and blockwise augmented architectures short of operator splitting.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\), \(f_i:X_i\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), \(A_i\in\mathbb R^{m\times n_i}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\). Consider \(\min\{\sum_{i=1}^q f_i(x_i):x_i\in X_i,\ \sum_{i=1}^qA_ix_i=b\}\), with augmented Lagrangian \(\mathcal L_\rho(x,\lambda)=\sum_i f_i(x_i)+\langle\lambda,\sum_iA_ix_i-b\rangle+\frac\rho2\|\sum_iA_ix_i-b\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, deterministic, equality-coupled block optimization; the definition describes a Jacobi-style block ALM architecture and does not assert convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A parallel block ALM architecture is a sequence \(\{(x^k,\lambda^k,\rho_k)\}\) with \(\rho_k>0\) for which every block update at outer iteration \(k\) is computed concurrently from the same frozen state: \[x_i^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u_i\in X_i}\mathcal L_{\rho_k}(x_1^k,\ldots,x_{i-1}^k,u_i,x_{i+1}^k,\ldots,x_q^k;\lambda^k),\quad i=1,\ldots,q.\] After all block results are synchronized, the multiplier is updated by \[\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\rho_k\left(\sum_{i=1}^qA_ix_i^{k+1}-b\right).\] An inexact architecture replaces each block minimization by \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial_{x_i}\mathcal L_{\rho_k}(x_i^{k+1};x_{-i}^k,\lambda^k)+N_{X_i}(x_i^{k+1}))\leq\varepsilon_{i,k}\). Parallelism means that no update \(x_j^{k+1}\) is used in computing another block during the same sweep.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a separable objective with a shared linear equality, a parallel block ALM is the Jacobi architecture in which all blocks independently minimize the same augmented Lagrangian using the old values of every other block. The results are synchronized before one residual-based multiplier update is performed. Inexact block solves are allowed when their first-order residuals satisfy declared tolerances. This definition excludes Gauss–Seidel sweeps, because those use newly computed blocks within the current sweep.
assumptions_latex: \(q\geq2\), \(X_i\neq\varnothing\), and every displayed exact block argmin is nonempty whenever the exact form is used.
All workers use the common triple \((x^k,\lambda^k,\rho_k)\) during iteration \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining synchronization invariant is \(x_i^{k+1}=T_{i,k}(x^k,\lambda^k)\) for every \(i\), followed by the single dual update based on \(x^{k+1}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The block computation may be written \(x^{k+1}\in T_{1,k}(x^k,\lambda^k)\times\cdots\times T_{q,k}(x^k,\lambda^k)\), emphasizing the product of concurrently evaluated maps.
immediate_consequences_latex: The coupling residual available after synchronization is \(r^{k+1}=\sum_iA_ix_i^{k+1}-b\), and \(\lambda^{k+1}-\lambda^k=\rho_kr^{k+1}\).
boundary_notes: This definition does not include correction, proximal, damping, or operator-splitting steps that may be required for convergence.
No inspected source precisely supported this complete canonical architecture; the formulation requires source verification.
