knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concurrent block updates from a common synchronized augmented-Lagrangian iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{\sum_i f_i(x_i):x_i\in X_i,\ \sum_iA_ix_i=b\}\), all workers read the same \((x^k,y^k)\) and concurrently choose \[x_i^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x_i\in X_i}\left\{f_i(x_i)+(y^k)^\top A_ix_i+\frac{\rho_k}{2}\left\|A_ix_i+\sum_{j\ne i}A_jx_j^k-b\right\|^2+\frac{\tau_i^k}{2}\|x_i-x_i^k\|^2\right\}.\] After synchronization, the architecture forms \(r^{k+1}=\sum_iA_ix_i^{k+1}-b\) and updates \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho_kr^{k+1}\). This defines a proximal-Jacobi augmented architecture; convergence requires additional conditions on the model and proximal weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All blocks update concurrently from one common snapshot, followed by synchronization and a shared multiplier update.
assumptions_latex: Each displayed block subproblem has a selected minimizer.
All workers use the same iteration snapshot.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal phase is parallel, but it is generally a Jacobi approximation rather than an exact joint augmented minimization.
knowledge_statements.title: Synchronous Proximal-Jacobi ALM Architecture

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Divergence of an unstabilized synchronous Jacobi augmented-Lagrangian architecture.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x_1,x_2}0\) subject to \(x_1+x_2=0\), with \(\rho=1\) and zero proximal weights. Exact synchronous Jacobi block minimization gives \[x_1^{k+1}=-x_2^k-y^k,\qquad x_2^{k+1}=-x_1^k-y^k,\] followed by \[y^{k+1}=y^k+x_1^{k+1}+x_2^{k+1}=-x_1^k-x_2^k-y^k.\] From \((x_1^0,x_2^0,y^0)=(1,1,0)\), the iterates include \((-1,-1,-2)\), \((3,3,4)\), and \((-7,-7,-10)\), and their norm diverges.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unstabilized synchronous Jacobi ALM can diverge on a feasible convex two-block problem despite exact solution of every block subproblem.
assumptions_latex: The synchronous Jacobi architecture uses \(\rho=1\), zero proximal weights, and exact scalar block minimization.
knowledge_statements.title: Unstabilized Synchronous Jacobi Divergence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of synchronized block optimality residuals into a joint augmented-subproblem residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_k(x)=\sum_i f_i(x_i)+(y^k)^\top(\sum_iA_ix_i-b)+(\rho_k/2)\|\sum_iA_ix_i-b\|^2\). Suppose the proximal-Jacobi block update satisfies \[0\in\partial f_i(x_i^{k+1})+A_i^\top y^k+\rho_kA_i^\top\left(A_ix_i^{k+1}+\sum_{j\ne i}A_jx_j^k-b\right)+\tau_i^k(x_i^{k+1}-x_i^k).\] Then \[e_i^{k+1}=\rho_kA_i^\top\sum_{j\ne i}A_j(x_j^{k+1}-x_j^k)-\tau_i^k(x_i^{k+1}-x_i^k)\in\partial_iF_k(x^{k+1}).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cross-block changes and proximal corrections convert separate Jacobi optimality conditions into a joint augmented-subproblem stationarity residual.
assumptions_latex: Each block satisfies the displayed exact proximal-Jacobi inclusion.
The smooth-perturbation subdifferential rule applies to each \(f_i\); convexity is sufficient.
knowledge_statements.title: Jacobi-to-Joint Stationarity Correction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous Jacobi architecture for linearly coupled block-separable augmented-Lagrangian subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{\sum_i f_i(x_i):x_i\in X_i,\ \sum_i A_i x_i=b\}\), initialize \(x^0\), \(y^0\), penalty \(\rho>0\), and proximal weights \(\tau_i>0\). At iteration \(k\), all workers simultaneously compute \(x_i^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x_i\in X_i}\{f_i(x_i)+(y^k)^\top A_i x_i+(\rho/2)\lVert A_i x_i+\sum_{j\ne i}A_jx_j^k-b\rVert^2+(\tau_i/2)\lVert x_i-x_i^k\rVert^2\}\). After synchronization, a reducer forms \(r^{k+1}=\sum_iA_ix_i^{k+1}-b\) and sets \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho r^{k+1}\). Terminate under prescribed primal- and iterate-residual tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers update all primal blocks concurrently from the same synchronized iterate; a reducer then aggregates residuals and performs the multiplier update.
assumptions_latex: Every parallel block subproblem has a selected minimizer.
All workers read the same \((x^k,y^k)\) before computing updates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal phase is executable in parallel, with synchronization required before computing \(y^{k+1}\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit failure of coordinatewise minimality to imply joint local minimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(u,v)=(1-uv)^2\), every \(u\) minimizes \(F(u,0)=1\) and every \(v\) minimizes \(F(0,v)=1\). Hence \((0,0)\) is a fixed point of exact cyclic block minimization. Nevertheless, \(F(t,t)=(1-t^2)^2<1=F(0,0)\) for every sufficiently small nonzero \(t\), so \((0,0)\) is not a local minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth two-block objective can be minimal along each coordinate slice at a point while decreasing along a joint direction.
assumptions_latex: The two blocks range over \(\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((0,0)\text{ is coordinatewise minimal but not locally minimal for }F\).
knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Coordinatewise-Minimum Counterexample

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality limitation of an exact cyclic block sweep.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \((y,\rho)\), let \(F(x)=\mathcal L_\rho(x,y)\). A fixed point \(\bar x\) of exact cyclic block minimization is coordinatewise minimal: \(F(\bar x)\le F(\bar x_1,\ldots,x_i,\ldots,\bar x_N)\) for every \(x_i\in X_i\). Without joint convexity or another sufficient regularity condition, this need not imply local or global joint minimality. On differentiable open domains it implies \(\nabla F(\bar x)=0\), which likewise need not imply minimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A blockwise fixed point may satisfy every one-block minimization test without solving the joint augmented subproblem required by exact ALM.
assumptions_latex: Every block update is solved exactly.
The displayed fixed point is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{coordinatewise minimum}\not\Rightarrow\bar x\in\arg\min_x\mathcal L_\rho(x,y)\) without additional assumptions.
knowledge_statements.title: Coordinatewise Versus Joint Augmented Minimization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint-optimality certificate for a convex differentiable augmented subproblem at a blockwise fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\prod_{i=1}^NX_i\), with each \(X_i\) nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(F\) be convex and continuously differentiable. Then \[-\nabla_iF(\bar x)\in N_{X_i}(\bar x_i)\quad(i=1,\ldots,N)\] is equivalent to \(-\nabla F(\bar x)\in N_X(\bar x)\), and hence to \(\bar x\in\arg\min_{x\in X}F(x)\). Without convexity, the block conditions give stationarity but do not certify minimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex differentiable augmented subproblem on a Cartesian convex domain, all block optimality conditions together certify global joint optimality.
assumptions_latex: Each \(X_i\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(F\) is convex and continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl[-\nabla_iF(\bar x)\in N_{X_i}(\bar x_i)\ \forall i\bigr]\iff \bar x\in\arg\min_{x\in X}F(x).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential newest-value block sweeps inside an augmented-Lagrangian outer iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{\sum_{i=1}^N f_i(x_i):x_i\in X_i,\ \sum_iA_ix_i=b\}\), define \(\mathcal L_{\rho_k}(x,y^k)=\sum_i f_i(x_i)+(y^k)^\top(\sum_iA_ix_i-b)+(\rho_k/2)\|\sum_iA_ix_i-b\|^2\). Starting from \(x^k\), one cyclic sweep selects \[x_i^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_i\in X_i}\mathcal L_{\rho_k}(x_1^{k+1},\ldots,x_{i-1}^{k+1},x_i,x_{i+1}^k,\ldots,x_N^k,y^k),\quad i=1,\ldots,N,\] and then sets \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho_k(\sum_iA_ix_i^{k+1}-b)\). Multiple sweeps may instead be performed until a declared joint inner residual tolerance is met. This algorithmic definition alone makes no outer-convergence claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Process the augmented subproblem sequentially with newest available block values, then update the shared multiplier from the complete coupling residual.
assumptions_latex: Each displayed block minimum has a selected solution.
The block order and number or stopping rule of inner sweeps are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho_k(\sum_iA_ix_i^{k+1}-b)\) after the prescribed sequential block sweep or sweeps.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Essentially Cyclic and Randomized Inner Block Selections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noncyclic block-selection variants for solving a fixed augmented-Lagrangian subproblem before the outer multiplier update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At outer iteration \(k\), hold \((y^k,\rho_k)\) fixed and generate inner iterates \(z^{t+1}\) by updating only block \(i_t\) to an exact or explicitly residual-controlled approximate minimizer of \(\mathcal L_{\rho_k}(\cdot,y^k)\). An essentially cyclic rule requires a finite \(B\ge N\) such that every block occurs in every \(B\)-update window. A randomized rule requires \(\Pr(i_t=i\mid\mathcal H_t)\ge p_i>0\) for every block. Update the multiplier only after a declared joint augmented-subproblem residual test accepts an inner iterate: \(x^{k+1}=z^{t_k}\), \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho_k(\sum_iA_ix_i^{k+1}-b)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Essentially cyclic or randomized choices may replace a fixed cyclic order, but the multiplier update follows a joint inner stopping test.
assumptions_latex: Selected block updates and the joint inner residual are well defined.
A finite coverage window exists, or every block has a uniformly positive conditional selection probability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Every block is selected in each bounded window, or has uniformly positive conditional selection probability, before an accepted outer update.}

notation.meaning: block selected at inner iteration t

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{\sum_i f_i(x_i):x_i\in X_i,\ \sum_i A_ix_i=b\}\), define \(\mathcal L_\rho(x,y)=\sum_i f_i(x_i)+y^\top(\sum_iA_ix_i-b)+(\rho/2)\lVert\sum_iA_ix_i-b\rVert^2\). Given \((x^k,y^k)\), visit blocks in order and choose \(x_i^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x_i\in X_i}\mathcal L_\rho(x_1^{k+1},\ldots,x_{i-1}^{k+1},x_i,x_{i+1}^k,\ldots,x_N^k,y^k)\). After one sweep, set \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho(\sum_iA_ix_i^{k+1}-b)\). Stop when prescribed feasibility and block-change tolerances hold, and output \((x^{k+1},y^{k+1})\).

assumptions_latex: Each displayed block minimization is well defined and attains a selected solution.

children.title: Parallel Block Coordination
children.top_down_role: Coordination regimes for parallel work across coupled augmented blocks.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinator invariant for reproducing the centralized ALM multiplier update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If worker \(i\) returns \(s_i^{k+1}=A_ix_i^{k+1}\), a synchronous coordinator reproduces the centralized update by reducing exactly one current contribution from every block, setting \(r^{k+1}=\sum_i s_i^{k+1}-b\), and broadcasting \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho_kr^{k+1}\). Missing, duplicated, or stale contributions violate this algebraic equivalence unless explicitly corrected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One current contribution from every block must be reduced exactly once to reproduce the centralized residual and multiplier update.
assumptions_latex: All contributions carry the same iteration label.
Each block contribution is included exactly once.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Synchronous Reduction Invariant

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Propagation of residual-aggregation error into multiplier updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widehat r^{k+1}=r^{k+1}+e^{k+1}\). If the coordinated and exact-reference updates start from the same multiplier, then \(\widehat y^{k+1}-y_{\rm ex}^{k+1}=\rho_ke^{k+1}\). Across \(K\) updates using the same primal blocks and penalties, \[\widehat y^K-y_{\rm ex}^K=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\rho_ke^{k+1}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregation error is scaled by the penalty at each update and accumulates additively.
assumptions_latex: The compared updates use identical primal blocks, initial multiplier, and penalty sequence.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Perturbation from Inexact Reduction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asynchronous coordinator maintaining a coherent aggregate despite delayed or repeated messages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain one accepted contribution \(\bar s_i\) and version \(v_i\) for each block. Accept a message \((i,v,s)\) only if \(v>v_i\), then atomically set \(S\leftarrow S+s-\bar s_i\), \(\bar s_i\leftarrow s\), and \(v_i\leftarrow v\); otherwise discard it. The invariant \(S=\sum_i\bar s_i\) then holds after every accepted message. Thus duplicates and out-of-order older messages do not corrupt the maintained residual \(S-b\). This invariant alone does not make mixed-version multiplier updates equivalent to synchronous centralized ALM.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Versioned delta replacement preserves a coherent latest-accepted aggregate, although mixed-version updates are not synchronous ALM updates.
assumptions_latex: Each message identifies its block and carries a strictly ordered block-local version.
The coordinator updates the aggregate, stored contribution, and version atomically.

notation.meaning: latest accepted contribution of block i
latest accepted version for block i

knowledge_statements.title: Timestamped Asynchronous Delta Coordination

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Error condition ensuring convergence of the cumulative multiplier perturbation for a fixed reference sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\widehat r^{k+1}=r^{k+1}+e^{k+1}\), the perturbed and reference updates use the same initial multiplier and penalties, and \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\rho_k\|e^{k+1}\|<\infty\), then \(\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\rho_ke^{k+1}\) converges absolutely. This controls the cumulative multiplier perturbation but does not by itself establish primal or dual convergence of an asynchronous ALM.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Summable penalty-weighted aggregation errors yield a convergent cumulative multiplier perturbation, not a standalone ALM convergence theorem.
assumptions_latex: The perturbed and reference updates use identical initial multipliers, primal-reference residuals, and penalty sequences.
knowledge_statements.title: Summable Coordination-Error Condition
Parallel Block Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinator invariant linking local block contributions to the global ALM residual and multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose worker \(i\) returns a block \(x_i^{k+1}\) and contribution \(s_i^{k+1}=A_ix_i^{k+1}\) for the coupling equation \(\sum_iA_ix_i=b\). A correct synchronous coordination step computes \(s^{k+1}=\sum_i s_i^{k+1}\), broadcasts the same residual \(r^{k+1}=s^{k+1}-b\), and updates the unique shared multiplier by \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho r^{k+1}\). Thus the distributed update is algebraically identical to the centralized ALM multiplier update whenever the reduction includes exactly one contribution from every block computed at the designated iteration. Missing, duplicated, or stale contributions destroy this equivalence unless the algorithm explicitly compensates for them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact reduction of one current contribution per block makes distributed residual and multiplier updates identical to their centralized ALM counterparts.
assumptions_latex: All block contributions belong to the same synchronous iteration.
The reduction sums each contribution exactly once.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(I\geq1\), let each discrete block domain \(Z_i\) be nonempty, and consider \(p^*=\inf\{\sum_{i=1}^I f_i(z_i):z_i\in Z_i,\ \sum_{i=1}^Ih_i(z_i)\leq b\}\), where \(h_i:Z_i\to\mathbb R^m\). Its Lagrangian dual function is \(d(\mu)=\inf_{z_i\in Z_i}\{\sum_i[f_i(z_i)+\langle\mu,h_i(z_i)\rangle]-\langle\mu,b\rangle\}\) for \(\mu\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional separable discrete or mixed-integer minimization with complicating coupling inequalities and nonquadratic multiplier constructions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The discrete-integer multiplier regime family consists of methods that preserve the block domains \(Z_i\), dualize only the coupling inequality, and generate dual or smoothing parameters from a separable nonquadratic construction. Formally, a member is specified by functions \(\Phi_{i,k}(\mu;z_i)\) and performs \[z_i^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z_i\in Z_i}\Phi_{i,k}(\mu^k;z_i),\qquad i=1,\ldots,I,\] together with a multiplier or probability-weight update that maintains \(\mu^k\in\mathbb R_+^m\) or block weights in their probability simplices. The canonical Lagrangian member has \(\Phi_{i,k}=f_i+\langle\mu^k,h_i\rangle\). Exponential members replace the nonsmooth block minimum by a log-sum-exp approximation over finitely many block alternatives. Membership in the family requires that the coupling enter through \(\sum_i h_i(z_i)-b\), so evaluation or smoothing remains block separable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This regime is the family of multiplier constructions for separable discrete or mixed-integer problems in which local integrality is retained and only the shared coupling constraint is dualized. Each local block is evaluated independently for a common multiplier. Classical Lagrangian relaxation uses the exact minimum of affine multiplier terms; nonquadratic variants, especially exponential log-sum-exp smoothing, approximate those block minima and update either nonnegative coupling multipliers or probability weights over discrete alternatives.
assumptions_latex: Each block minimization or finite-alternative sum used by the selected member is well defined.
The coupling multiplier satisfies \(\mu\geq0\) for the convention \(\sum_i h_i(z_i)\leq b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every member exposes the separable representation \(d(\mu)=\sum_i d_i(\mu)-\langle\mu,b\rangle\), where \(d_i(\mu)=\inf_{z_i\in Z_i}[f_i(z_i)+\langle\mu,h_i(z_i)\rangle]\), or a declared smooth approximation of these block values.
equivalent_formulations_latex: When every \(Z_i\) is finite, \(d_i(\mu)\) is the minimum of finitely many affine functions of \(\mu\).
special_cases_latex: The production-region integer program with bounded integer choices \(n_i\in N_i\) and continuous variables \(x_i\in X_i(n_i)\) is obtained by taking \(z_i=(x_i,n_i)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The dual value \(d(\mu)\) is a lower bound on \(p^*\) for every \(\mu\geq0\).
Block evaluation can be distributed because the only shared argument is \(\mu\).
boundary_notes: The definition does not relax the local integer restrictions themselves.
A vanishing discrete duality gap is not part of the definition.

knowledge_statements.title: Exponential Method of Multipliers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential augmented-multiplier scheme for separable problems with inequality coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x_i\in X_i}\sum_i f_i(x_i)\) subject to \(g(x)=\sum_iA_ix_i-b\le0\). Choose \(y^0\in\mathbb R_{++}^m\) and \(c_k>0\). At iteration \(k\), compute \(x^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x_i\in X_i}\{\sum_i f_i(x_i)+(1/c_k)\sum_{j=1}^m y_j^k[\exp(c_k g_j(x))-1]\}\), exactly or to a prescribed tolerance. Update each multiplier by \(y_j^{k+1}=y_j^k\exp(c_k g_j(x^{k+1}))\). Stop when the chosen primal-feasibility and multiplier-change tests hold; output \((x^{k+1},y^{k+1})\). Positivity of every multiplier is preserved by the exponential update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exponential penalty augments the separable objective, and each positive inequality multiplier is updated multiplicatively using its constraint residual.
assumptions_latex: Each \(X_i\) is nonempty and may encode discrete or integer restrictions.
\(y_j^0>0\) and \(c_k>0\) for every constraint and iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update satisfies \(y_j^{k+1}>0\) and defines an exponential method-of-multipliers iteration.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent additive-coordinate form of the positive multiplicative multiplier update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(y_j^{k+1}=y_j^k\exp(c_k g_j(x^{k+1}))\) with \(y_j^k>0\), define \(s_j^k=\log y_j^k\). Then \[s_j^{k+1}=s_j^k+c_k g_j(x^{k+1}).\] Thus the exponential update is additive in log-multiplier coordinates, and positivity of every multiplier is invariant at finite iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Taking logarithms converts the positive multiplicative multiplier update into an additive residual step.
knowledge_statements.title: Log-Multiplier Additive Representation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure when discrete exponential subproblems are not solved to convergence-supporting accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(X=\{-1,1\}\), \(f(x)=0\), and \(g(x)=x\le0\), whose unique feasible point is \(-1\). Let \(c_k=1\), \(y^0=1\), and suppose an uncontrolled inexact oracle always returns \(x^{k+1}=1\). Then \(y^{k+1}=y^ke\), so \(y^k=e^k\), while \(g(x^{k+1})=1\) for every \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a two-point discrete problem, repeatedly accepting the wrong exponential-subproblem point keeps every iterate infeasible and makes the multiplier diverge.
assumptions_latex: \(c_k=1\), \(y^0=1\), and the oracle may return a nonglobal point.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Exponential-Subproblem Failure

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Iterate Persistence of Strict Multiplier Positivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero-attainment boundary for the multiplicative exponential update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(y_j^0>0\) and every \(c_k g_j(x^{k+1})\) is finite, then \(y_j^{k+1}=y_j^k\exp(c_k g_j(x^{k+1}))\) gives \(y_j^k>0\) at every finite iteration. Therefore a limiting complementary multiplier \(y_j^*=0\) cannot be attained finitely without an additional truncation rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strictly positive exponential multiplier never becomes exactly zero at a finite iteration.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Iterate Persistence of Strict Multiplier Positivity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact recovery of an exponential-method constraint residual from consecutive positive multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(y_j^k>0\), \(y_j^{k+1}>0\), and \(c_k>0\), then \[g_j(x^{k+1})=\frac1{c_k}\log\!\left(\frac{y_j^{k+1}}{y_j^k}\right).\] Hence, when the update is exact, \[\|g(x^{k+1})\|_\infty=\frac1{c_k}\max_j\left|\log\frac{y_j^{k+1}}{y_j^k}\right|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaled logarithmic multiplier changes equal the constraint residuals exactly.
assumptions_latex: The exponential multiplier update is applied exactly.
knowledge_statements.title: Log-Multiplier Residual Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero Multiplier as an Absorbing State
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Initialization boundary for a multiplicative exponential multiplier component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(y_j^0=0\) and every exponent \(c_kg_j(x^{k+1})\) is finite, then the update \(y_j^{k+1}=y_j^k\exp(c_kg_j(x^{k+1}))\) gives \(y_j^k=0\) for every \(k\), irrespective of the residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiplier initialized at zero remains zero and cannot respond multiplicatively to violation.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero Multiplier as an Absorbing State

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combined original-feasibility and global exponential-subproblem accuracy certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\Phi_k(x)=\sum_i f_i(x_i)+c_k^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^m y_j^k[\exp(c_kg_j(x))-1]\). Suppose \(L_k\le\inf_{x_i\in X_i}\Phi_k(x)\) is a certified lower bound. If \(\hat x\) satisfies \(\|[g(\hat x)]_+\|_\infty\le\eta_k\) and \(\Phi_k(\hat x)-L_k\le\delta_k\), then it is \(\eta_k\)-feasible and its exponential-subproblem objective gap is at most \(\delta_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified lower bound and the original inequality residual jointly certify inner global accuracy and primal feasibility.

notation.meaning: certified global lower bound for the discrete subproblem

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible Discrete-Subproblem Gap Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Entropic Mirror-Ascent Form of the Multiplier Update
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact dual-coordinate interpretation of the positive multiplicative multiplier update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(y^k\in\mathbb R_{++}^m\), \(c_k>0\), and \(g^k=g(x^{k+1})\), define \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(z,y)=\sum_j[z_j\log(z_j/y_j)-z_j+y_j]\). Then \[y^{k+1}=\operatorname*{argmax}_{z\in\mathbb R_+^m}\left\{\langle g^k,z\rangle-\frac1{c_k}D_{\mathrm{KL}}(z,y^k)\right\}\] is unique and satisfies \(y_j^{k+1}=y_j^k\exp(c_kg_j^k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The multiplicative multiplier update is exactly a KL-proximal mirror-ascent step on the nonnegative orthant.
assumptions_latex: \(c_k>0\) and every component of \(g^k\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.title: Entropic Mirror-Ascent Form of the Multiplier Update

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exponential Multiplier Approximation for a Separable Integer Dual
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For each block \(i\), let \(S_i\) be a finite set of alternatives \(s\), with cost \(f_i(s)\) and coupling vector \(h_i(s)\). Put \(a_i(\mu,s)=f_i(s)+\langle\mu,h_i(s)\rangle\), where \(\mu\in\mathbb R_+^m\), and let \(p_i^k\) be a strictly positive probability vector on \(S_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-alternative separable discrete optimization; this is the exponential approximation method for the discrete dual, not the continuous inequality-constrained exponential ALM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(c_k>0\), define the smooth approximate dual function \[d_{c_k}(\mu;p^k)=-\frac1{c_k}\sum_{i=1}^I\log\!\left(\sum_{s\in S_i}p_i^k(s)e^{-c_ka_i(\mu,s)}\right)-\langle\mu,b\rangle.\] The exponential method of multipliers selects \[\mu^k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{\mu\geq0}d_{c_k}(\mu;p^k)\] and then updates every block probability by \[p_i^{k+1}(s)=\frac{p_i^k(s)e^{-c_ka_i(\mu^k,s)}}{\sum_{t\in S_i}p_i^k(t)e^{-c_ka_i(\mu^k,t)}},\qquad s\in S_i.\] Initial weights satisfy \(p_i^0(s)>0\) and \(\sum_{s\in S_i}p_i^0(s)=1\); the standard parameter rule has \(0<c_k\leq c_{k+1}\). These equations define the method and preserve each probability simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each discrete block, the method replaces the minimum of its affine Lagrangian alternatives by a negative log-sum-exp expression. It maximizes the resulting smooth approximate dual over nonnegative coupling multipliers, then exponentially reweights each block alternative according to its Lagrangian cost and renormalizes. Positive initial weights remain positive and sum to one. The construction is block separable and twice differentiable in the dual variable when the alternative data are finite.
assumptions_latex: The approximate dual maximization is solved in the exact definition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For all \(i,k\), \(p_i^{k+1}(s)>0\) and \(\sum_{s\in S_i}p_i^{k+1}(s)=1\), while \(d_{c_k}(\cdot;p^k)\) is the declared exponential smoothing of the separable dual.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The update is the softmax relation \(p_i^{k+1}(s)\propto p_i^k(s)\exp[-c_ka_i(\mu^k,s)]\).
special_cases_latex: For production-region models, \(s=(j,n_i)\) indexes an extreme point \(x_i(j,n_i)\) of region \(X_i(n_i)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The approximate dual separates into \(I\) log-sum-exp block terms plus \(-\langle\mu,b\rangle\).
The normalization denominator is strictly positive.
boundary_notes: This definition does not state convergence of \(\mu^k\) or \(p^k\).
It is distinct from the continuous exponential ALM with update \(\mu_j^{k+1}=\mu_j^k e^{c_j^kg_j(x^k)}\).

notation.meaning: Finite alternative set of block i.

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete Duality-Gap Estimation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computable primal–dual gap certificate for a discrete Lagrangian relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\min\{f(x):x\in X_D,\ h(x)=0\}\), where \(X_D\) is discrete, and define \(d(y)=\inf_{x\in X_D}\{f(x)+y^\top h(x)\}\). For any feasible \(\bar x\in X_D\) and any multiplier \(y\), weak duality gives \(d(y)\le P\le f(\bar x)\). Hence \(G(\bar x,y)=f(\bar x)-d(y)\ge0\) is a verifiable upper bound on the unknown primal suboptimality \(f(\bar x)-P\). If the dual subproblem is solved only to a certified lower bound \(\underline d(y)\le d(y)\), then \(f(\bar x)-\underline d(y)\) remains a valid, possibly looser, gap estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible discrete objective value minus a certified Lagrangian-dual lower bound bounds the candidate solution's unknown suboptimality.
assumptions_latex: The value \(d(y)\), or a certified lower bound on it, is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le f(\bar x)-P\le f(\bar x)-d(y)\), with the analogous bound using \(\underline d(y)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite discrete equality problem in which the best Lagrangian lower bound is strictly below the discrete optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_D=\{0,1,2\}\), impose \(h(x)=x-1=0\), and set \(f(0)=f(2)=0\) and \(f(1)=1\). The primal value is \(P=1\), whereas \(d(y)=\min\{-y,1,y\}\), so \(\sup_{y\in\mathbb R}d(y)=0\). Therefore \(P-\sup_y d(y)=1\), although the primal optimum exists and every dual subproblem can be solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite feasible discrete problem can retain a positive Lagrangian duality gap even after exact multiplier optimization.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive Discrete Lagrangian Duality Gap

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal–Dual Gap Estimator for Separable Discrete Optimization
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(p^*=\inf(P)\) be the value of a feasible separable discrete minimization problem and \(d^*=\sup(D)\) the value of its Lagrangian dual. For a primal-feasible point \(z\) and a dual-feasible multiplier \(\mu\geq0\), write \(U(z)=\sum_i f_i(z_i)\) and \(L(\mu)=d(\mu)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional minimization with weak duality; the estimator applies to any feasible primal point and dual-feasible multiplier, with a sharper structural bound for the separable regime of Proposition 5.26.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The discrete duality-gap estimate associated with \((z,\mu)\) is \[G(z,\mu)=U(z)-L(\mu).\] Its absolute certified optimality gap is \(G(z,\mu)\), and, when \(L(\mu)>0\), a relative estimator is \(G_{\mathrm{rel}}(z,\mu)=G(z,\mu)/L(\mu)\). The intrinsic duality gap is \(G^*=p^*-d^*\geq0\). For the separable problem \(\min\{\sum_i f_i(x_i):x_i\in X_i,\sum_i h_i(x_i)\leq b\}\) satisfying assumptions (A1)–(A3) of the cited result, define block nonconvexity quantities \(\rho_i\) there and \(E=\max_i\rho_i\); the structural estimate is \[0\leq G^*\leq(m+1)E.\] For average cost \(I^{-1}\sum_i f_i\), the bound becomes \((m+1)E/I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A discrete duality-gap estimate is the difference between the objective value of any feasible discrete solution and the Lagrangian dual value at any dual-feasible multiplier. Weak duality makes this a computable upper bound on the unknown suboptimality of the feasible solution. The intrinsic gap is the difference between the optimal primal and optimal dual values. Under the cited compactness, feasibility, and block-recovery assumptions, the intrinsic gap is at most the number of coupling dimensions plus one, multiplied by the largest block nonconvexity measure. For average cost, this bound is divided by the number of blocks.
assumptions_latex: \(z\) is feasible for \((P)\), and \(\mu\geq0\) is feasible for \((D)\).
The structural estimate additionally uses assumptions (A1)–(A3) and \(m\)-dimensional coupling as specified in Proposition 5.26.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\leq U(z)-p^*\leq G(z,\mu)\), and under the structural assumptions \(0\leq p^*-d^*\leq(m+1)E\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(U\) is called \(UB\) and \(L\) is called \(LB\), then \(G=UB-LB\).
special_cases_latex: For the normalized objective \(I^{-1}\sum_i f_i\), \(G^*\leq(m+1)E/I\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(G(z,\mu)\leq\varepsilon\), then \(z\) is \(\varepsilon\)-optimal.
The normalized structural bound tends to zero as \(I\to\infty\) when \(m\) and \(E\) remain bounded.
boundary_notes: The ratio \(G/L\) is not used when \(L\leq0\); another positive scaling must then be declared.
A small duality gap does not itself construct a feasible discrete point.

notation.meaning: Largest block nonconvexity quantity in the structural estimate.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Interface Between a Discrete Lagrangian Dual and Its Convexified Relaxation
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let each finite block alternative be indexed by \(s\in S_i\), with vectors \((h_i(s),f_i(s))\). The primal chooses one alternative per block and enforces \(\sum_i h_i(s_i)\leq b\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-alternative separable discrete minimization; the relaxation randomizes independently over each block's alternatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The dual-relaxation interface is the pair formed by the Lagrangian dual \[\max_{\mu\geq0}\left\{\sum_{i=1}^I\min_{s\in S_i}[f_i(s)+\langle\mu,h_i(s)\rangle]-\langle\mu,b\rangle\right\}\] and the relaxed primal \[\min_{p}\sum_{i=1}^I\sum_{s\in S_i}p_i(s)f_i(s)\] subject to \[\sum_{i=1}^I\sum_{s\in S_i}p_i(s)h_i(s)\leq b,\qquad \sum_{s\in S_i}p_i(s)=1,\quad p_i(s)\geq0.\] The interface map sends relaxation weights \(p\) to expected block costs and resources and sends a dual multiplier \(\mu\) to the reduced costs \(f_i(s)+\langle\mu,h_i(s)\rangle\). These two displayed programs are a primal-dual linear-program pair and therefore have equal optimal values whenever either has a finite optimum and the usual finite-dimensional LP feasibility conditions hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface consists of a convexified primal relaxation and the Lagrangian dual of the original separable discrete problem. The relaxation replaces the choice of one alternative in each block by a probability distribution over that block's alternatives and constrains expected resource use. A coupling multiplier assigns a reduced cost to each alternative. The relaxed program and the dual are linear-program duals, so their optimal values agree under ordinary LP feasibility and finiteness conditions, while their common value remains a lower bound on the discrete optimum.
assumptions_latex: The relaxed linear program is feasible and has finite optimal value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup(D)=\inf(R)\leq\inf(P)\), where \((R)\) is the probability relaxation and \((P)\) is the original discrete problem.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The relaxed feasible set replaces each block image by its convex hull \(\operatorname{conv}\{(h_i(s),f_i(s)):s\in S_i\}\).
special_cases_latex: If every optimal \(p_i\) is a unit vector, the relaxed solution is a feasible discrete solution and the discrete duality gap is zero.
immediate_consequences_latex: Optimal relaxation weights provide fractional information for constructing a discrete feasible point.
The dual optimum supplies the relaxation's exact lower bound.
boundary_notes: Independent block randomization need not be implementable as one deterministic discrete decision.
Equality with the relaxed value does not imply equality with the discrete primal value.

notation.meaning: Relaxation probability assigned to alternative s of block i.

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete Dual Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrangian-dual interface exposing separable discrete oracle calls and a global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P=\min\{\sum_i f_i(x_i):x_i\in X_i^D,\ \sum_iA_ix_i=b\}\), the Lagrangian dual function is \(d(y)=\inf_x\{\sum_i f_i(x_i)+y^\top(\sum_iA_ix_i-b)\}\). Because the domain is Cartesian, it has the separable representation \(d(y)=-y^\top b+\sum_i\inf_{x_i\in X_i^D}\{f_i(x_i)+y^\top A_ix_i\}\). Thus a dual interface need only pass \(y\) to independent discrete block oracles and aggregate their values. For every \(y\), the returned exact value satisfies \(d(y)\le P\); certified lower oracle values also aggregate to a valid lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The discrete Lagrangian dual separates into independent block-oracle values plus a coupling constant, furnishing a global primal lower bound.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order interface between exact discrete Lagrangian minimization and multiplier-space optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(d(y)=\inf_{x\in X_D}\{f(x)+y^\top h(x)\}\), suppose the infimum is attained at \(x_y\). Then for every \(z\), \[d(z)\le d(y)+h(x_y)^\top(z-y).\] Thus \(h(x_y)\) is a supergradient of the concave function \(d\) at \(y\). If distinct minimizing oracle solutions have different residuals, \(d\) need not be differentiable at \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact discrete dual oracle returns a lower bound and a constraint residual that is a dual supergradient; oracle ties can make the dual nonsmooth.

notation.meaning: superdifferential of the concave dual function

children.title: Relaxed-Problem Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Connections between multiplier constructions and continuous or surrogate relaxations.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxed-Problem Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interface between an integer model and a continuous or partially relaxed lower-bounding problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_D\) be the feasible set of a minimization problem and let \(F_R\supseteq F_D\) be obtained by dropping constraints or replacing integrality restrictions by a continuous relaxation. Define \(P_D=\inf_{x\in F_D}f(x)\) and \(P_R=\inf_{x\in F_R}f(x)\). The relaxed-problem interface maps the original objective and retained constraints to \(F_R\), returns a certified value \(L_R\le P_R\), and optionally returns a relaxed optimizer. Set inclusion yields \(L_R\le P_R\le P_D\). If a relaxed optimizer belongs to \(F_D\), then it is also optimal for the discrete problem whenever its objective equals the reported relaxed optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enlarging a discrete feasible set gives a relaxed lower bound; a relaxation optimizer that is discrete-feasible closes the relaxation gap.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
The interface's reported \(L_R\) is certified not to exceed \(P_R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_R\le P_R\le P_D\); if \(x_R\in F_D\) and \(f(x_R)=P_R\), then \(P_D=P_R\).

children.title: Dual–Relaxation Gap Transfer
children.top_down_role: Relationships between dual information and bounds obtained from relaxed problems.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual–Relaxation Gap Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfers lower bounds from dual or relaxed models into a discrete primal gap bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_D\) be the optimal value of a discrete minimization problem, let \(U=f(\bar x)\) for a discrete-feasible point \(\bar x\), and suppose a relaxation has value \(P_R\le P_D\). If \(L_D\le P_R\) is obtained from a dual bound or a certified inexact relaxation solve, then \(L_D\le P_D\le U\). Consequently, the discrete incumbent gap satisfies \(0\le U-P_D\le U-L_D\). If both \(P_R\) and a dual lower bound \(L_D\) are known, the identity \(U-L_D=(U-P_R)+(P_R-L_D)\) separates the primal relaxation gap from the dual-to-relaxation gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any certified lower bound on a relaxation transfers to the discrete problem, and the incumbent gap decomposes into relaxation and dual-relaxation components.
assumptions_latex: The original and relaxed problems are minimization problems.
\(\bar x\) is feasible for the discrete problem.

notation.meaning: certified dual or relaxation lower bound

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete-Variable Multiplier Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier iteration whose augmented subproblems retain an explicitly discrete primal domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{f(x):x\in X_D,\ h(x)=0\}\), where \(X_D\) is discrete. Given \(y^0\), penalties \(\rho_k>0\), and subproblem tolerances \(\varepsilon_k\ge0\), choose \(x^{k+1}\in X_D\) satisfying \(\mathcal L_{\rho_k}(x^{k+1},y^k)\le\inf_{x\in X_D}\mathcal L_{\rho_k}(x,y^k)+\varepsilon_k\), where \(\mathcal L_\rho(x,y)=f(x)+y^\top h(x)+(\rho/2)\lVert h(x)\rVert^2\). Update \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho_k h(x^{k+1})\). Terminate under a prescribed feasibility and certified-subproblem-gap test; output the best feasible discrete incumbent together with the final multiplier and available lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each augmented-Lagrangian subproblem is solved over the original discrete domain, followed by the standard residual-based multiplier update.
assumptions_latex: Each augmented subproblem is solved with a certified error \(\varepsilon_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration preserves discrete primal iterates and updates multipliers by \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho_kh(x^{k+1})\).

children.title: Integer-Constraint Multiplier Regimes
children.top_down_role: Multiplier constructions organized around integrality restrictions and integer-feasible structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer-Constraint Multiplier Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Augmented formulation separating algebraic constraints from retained integrality restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_I=\{x\in X:x_j\in\mathbb Z\text{ for }j\in I\}\) and consider \(\min\{f(x):x\in X_I,\ h(x)=0\}\). An integer-constraint multiplier regime retains \(x\in X_I\) as a hard domain restriction while augmenting only \(h(x)=0\): \(\mathcal L_\rho(x,y)=f(x)+y^\top h(x)+(\rho/2)\lVert h(x)\rVert^2\), minimized over \(X_I\). Thus integrality is not represented by a differentiable residual and receives no ordinary real-valued multiplier. Given an augmented-subproblem solution \(x^{k+1}\in X_I\), the algebraic multiplier update is \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho_kh(x^{k+1})\), so every primal iterate satisfies the designated integrality restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integrality remains a hard subproblem-domain restriction, while only algebraic coupling constraints are augmented and assigned real-valued multipliers.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) indexes the components required to be integer.
\(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) defines the algebraic equalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(x^{k+1}\) minimizes the augmented subproblem over \(X_I\), then \(x_j^{k+1}\in\mathbb Z\) for all \(j\in I\), independently of multiplier feasibility.

children.title: Progress and Breakdown Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Progress interpretation, degeneracy, infeasibility, inner-solution failures, and numerical breakdown modes.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Numerical Optimization
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Numerical Optimization

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\leq0\), with estimates \((x^k,\lambda^k,\mu^k)\), \(\mu^k\geq0\), penalty \(\rho_k>0\), and inner optimality residual \(e_k\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear programming; this is a diagnostic state definition, not a convergence or infeasibility theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A progress-breakdown diagnostic system is a sequence of states \[\mathscr D_k=(r_{\mathrm{feas}}^k,r_{\mathrm{stat}}^k,r_{\mathrm{comp}}^k,r_{\mathrm{dual}}^k,e_k,\rho_k,\kappa_k),\] where \[r_{\mathrm{feas}}^k=\left\|\big(h(x^k),[g(x^k)]_+\big)\right\|,\quad r_{\mathrm{stat}}^k=\|\nabla_xL(x^k,\lambda^k,\mu^k)\|,\] \[r_{\mathrm{comp}}^k=\|\mu^k\odot g(x^k)\|,\quad r_{\mathrm{dual}}^k=\|[-\mu^k]_+\|,\] and \(\kappa_k\) is a declared conditioning estimate for the current augmented-Lagrangian subproblem. Given tolerances \(\tau\) and a progress window \(w\), the state is successful when all four KKT residuals and \(e_k\) meet their tolerances. A breakdown flag is any declared predicate based on nondecrease over \(w\) iterations, unbounded control quantities, failed inner accuracy, or nonfinite arithmetic. The diagnostic system is the residual map together with these explicit predicates; it does not identify a cause unless the corresponding predicate is satisfied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ALM progress-breakdown system records feasibility, stationarity, complementarity, dual-sign, inner-solve, penalty, and conditioning quantities at every outer iteration. Success means that the declared KKT and inner-solve tolerances all hold. Breakdown is not simply failure to terminate: it is a separately declared predicate such as residual stagnation over a fixed window, uncontrolled penalty or multiplier growth, inner-solve failure, severe conditioning, or nonfinite arithmetic. The state definition separates observable symptoms from conclusions such as infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(f,h,g\) are continuously differentiable at every recorded iterate.
The norm, tolerances, window length, conditioning estimator, and breakdown thresholds are fixed before interpreting the state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scalar aggregate \(R_k=\max\{r_{\mathrm{feas}}^k,r_{\mathrm{stat}}^k,r_{\mathrm{comp}}^k,r_{\mathrm{dual}}^k,e_k\}\) is zero exactly at a KKT-consistent state with an exact inner solve.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Componentwise stopping tolerances may replace \(R_k\leq\tau\).
special_cases_latex: For equality constraints only, \(r_{\mathrm{comp}}^k=r_{\mathrm{dual}}^k=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Residual stagnation and penalty escalation can be reported independently.
A large feasibility residual with a small stationarity residual may indicate stationarity of an infeasibility measure rather than constrained optimality.
boundary_notes: A diagnostic flag alone is not a mathematical certificate of infeasibility.
The precise conditioning estimator is implementation-dependent.

children.title: Primal–Dual Progress Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Outer progress families used in termination and parameter control.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\), \(g(x)\leq0\), define \(L(x,\lambda,\mu)=f(x)+\langle\lambda,h(x)\rangle+\langle\mu,g(x)\rangle\), with \(\mu\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional nonlinear programming; diagnostics measure approximate first-order KKT satisfaction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The primal-dual progress diagnostic at \(z=(x,\lambda,\mu)\) is the nonnegative vector \[\mathcal R(z)=\left(\|h(x)\|,\ \|[g(x)]_+\|,\ \|\nabla_xL(x,\lambda,\mu)\|,\ \|\mu\odot g(x)\|,\ \|[-\mu]_+\|\right).\] For an iterate sequence \(z^k\), progress from \(k\) to \(k+1\) is recorded componentwise by \(\Delta\mathcal R_k=\mathcal R(z^{k+1})-\mathcal R(z^k)\), or by the contraction ratio \(q_k=\|\mathcal R(z^{k+1})\|_\infty/\max\{\|\mathcal R(z^k)\|_\infty,\delta\}\), where \(\delta>0\) prevents division by zero. A point is \(\varepsilon\)-KKT under this diagnostic when \(\|\mathcal R(z)\|_\infty\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal-dual progress diagnostic is the vector of equality violation, positive inequality violation, Lagrangian stationarity error, complementarity error, and negative-multiplier error. Progress is assessed componentwise or through the contraction of the maximum residual. A point is epsilon-KKT precisely when every recorded residual is at most epsilon. This diagnostic keeps different failure modes visible instead of allowing a small residual to conceal a large one.
assumptions_latex: A fixed norm and sign convention \(g(x)\leq0\), \(\mu\geq0\) are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal R(x,\lambda,\mu)=0\) if and only if primal feasibility, stationarity, dual feasibility, and complementary slackness all hold.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A weighted aggregate is \(R_W(z)=\|W\mathcal R(z)\|_\infty\) for a fixed positive diagonal scaling \(W\).
special_cases_latex: With equality constraints only, \(\mathcal R=(\|h(x)\|,\|\nabla_xL(x,\lambda)\|)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(q_k<1\), the aggregate maximum residual decreases at iteration \(k\).
Separate components identify whether progress is primarily primal or dual.
boundary_notes: Residual scaling affects numerical comparisons but not the zero set.
Small KKT residuals need not imply global optimality.

children.title: Feasibility-Progress Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Constraint-satisfaction progress used in outer control.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Progress Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual and contraction tests for equality and inequality feasibility in an outer augmented-Lagrangian iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For equality constraints \(c(x)=0\) and inequality constraints \(g(x)\le 0\), define the feasibility residual at outer iterate \(x_k\) by \[r_{\mathrm{feas},k}=\max\{\lVert c(x_k)\rVert,\lVert[g(x_k)]_+\rVert\}.\] Given a required contraction factor \(\eta_k\in(0,1)\), feasibility progress occurs when \(r_{\mathrm{feas},k+1}\le \eta_k r_{\mathrm{feas},k}\). If the test fails, an outer controller may retain or increase the penalty parameter; termination for feasibility requires \(r_{\mathrm{feas},k}\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasibility progress is measured by contraction of the combined equality-violation and positive inequality-violation residual; termination requires that residual to meet its tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p\) are defined at every tested iterate.
The norm and feasibility tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}>0\) are fixed consistently across outer iterations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasibility-progress predicate is \(r_{\mathrm{feas},k+1}\le\eta_k r_{\mathrm{feas},k}\), and the feasibility termination predicate is \(r_{\mathrm{feas},k}\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\).

notation.meaning: componentwise positive part of a vector
combined primal-feasibility residual at outer iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distance residual and contraction test for equality constraints combined with membership in a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(c(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\in-K\), where \(K\) is a nonempty closed convex cone, define \[r_{\mathrm{feas}}^K(x)=\max\{\|c(x)\|,\operatorname{dist}(g(x),-K)\}.\] Then \[r_{\mathrm{feas}}^K(x)=0\iff c(x)=0\ \text{and}\ g(x)\in-K.\] With Euclidean distance, Moreau decomposition gives \(\operatorname{dist}(g(x),-K)=\|\Pi_{K^*}(g(x))\|\); for \(K=\mathbb R_+^p\), this is \(\|[g(x)]_+\|\). Conic feasibility progress may be tested by \(r_{\mathrm{feas}}^K(x_{k+1})\le\eta_k r_{\mathrm{feas}}^K(x_k)\), with \(\eta_k\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distance to the negative constraint cone extends the positive-part feasibility residual, vanishes exactly at conically feasible points, and supports the same outer contraction test.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a nonempty closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
The distance and projection use the same Euclidean norm.

notation.meaning: Euclidean distance from z to the negative cone
Euclidean projection onto the dual cone

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Feasibility Residual

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let the constraint set be \(\Omega=\{x:h(x)=0,\ g(x)\leq0\}\), where \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^r\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional equality-and-inequality constrained optimization; no stationarity or optimality information is included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed vector norm, the feasibility diagnostic is \[\theta(x)=\left\|\big(h(x),[g(x)]_+\big)\right\|.\] Given iterates \(x^k\), the absolute improvement is \(I_k=\theta(x^k)-\theta(x^{k+1})\), and the safeguarded relative contraction is \[q_k^{\mathrm{feas}}=\frac{\theta(x^{k+1})}{\max\{\theta(x^k),\delta\}},\qquad\delta>0.\] For a prescribed forcing factor \(\eta_k\in(0,1)\), iteration \(k\) has sufficient feasibility progress when \(\theta(x^{k+1})\leq\eta_k\theta(x^k)\). It is \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\)-feasible when \(\theta(x^k)\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The feasibility-progress diagnostic is the norm of the equality residual together with the positive parts of inequality violations. It vanishes exactly at feasible points. Progress can be measured as an absolute decrease, a safeguarded contraction ratio, or satisfaction of a prescribed forcing inequality. This is solely a constraint-satisfaction measure and says nothing about objective stationarity or complementarity.
assumptions_latex: The same norm and constraint scaling are used at all compared iterations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta(x)=0\iff x\in\Omega\), and sufficient progress is exactly the declared inequality \(\theta(x^{k+1})\leq\eta_k\theta(x^k)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: With the \(\ell_\infty\) norm, \(\theta(x)=\max\{\max_i|h_i(x)|,\max_j[g_j(x)]_+\}\).
special_cases_latex: For equality constraints only, \(\theta(x)=\|h(x)\|\).
For inequalities only, \(\theta(x)=\|[g(x)]_+\|\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(\theta(x^{k+1})\leq\eta\theta(x^k)\) for a fixed \(\eta<1\) eventually, then \(\theta(x^k)\to0\).
boundary_notes: Constraint scaling can materially change the numerical value of \(\theta\).
Feasibility progress does not imply decrease of the objective.

notation.meaning: Componentwise maximum of g and zero.

children.title: Stationarity-Progress Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Primal–dual stationarity progress used in termination.

knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity-Progress Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order primal–dual residual tests for outer progress and termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L(x,\lambda,\mu)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}c(x)+\mu^{\mathsf T}g(x)\). For an outer primal–dual iterate \((x_k,\lambda_k,\mu_k)\), define \[r_{\mathrm{stat},k}=\lVert\nabla_xL(x_k,\lambda_k,\mu_k)\rVert.\] Given \(\theta_k\in(0,1)\), stationarity progress occurs when \(r_{\mathrm{stat},k+1}\le\theta_k r_{\mathrm{stat},k}\). First-order termination requires \(r_{\mathrm{stat},k}\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{stat}}\), together with separately tested primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stationarity progress is contraction of the Lagrangian-gradient norm. First-order termination additionally requires feasibility, nonnegative inequality multipliers, and complementarity.
assumptions_latex: \(f\), \(c\), and \(g\) are continuously differentiable near the tested iterates.
The sign convention is \(g(x)\le0\) with inequality multiplier \(\mu\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stationarity-progress predicate is \(r_{\mathrm{stat},k+1}\le\theta_k r_{\mathrm{stat},k}\), while stationarity termination requires \(r_{\mathrm{stat},k}\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{stat}}\).

notation.meaning: ordinary Lagrangian under the inequality convention g(x)≤0

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity residual and progress test when a closed convex set remains explicit in an augmented-Lagrangian subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(L(x,\lambda,\mu)\) be the ordinary Lagrangian for the augmented constraints. Define \[r_{\mathrm{pstat}}(x,\lambda,\mu)=\|x-\Pi_X(x-
abla_xL(x,\lambda,\mu))\|.\] Then \[r_{\mathrm{pstat}}(x,\lambda,\mu)=0\iff 0\in
abla_xL(x,\lambda,\mu)+N_X(x).\] When \(X=\mathbb R^n\), this reduces to \(\|
abla_xL(x,\lambda,\mu)\|\). Projected-stationarity progress may be tested by \(r_{\mathrm{pstat},k+1}\le	heta_k r_{\mathrm{pstat},k}\), with \(	heta_k\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projected-gradient residual exactly tests stationarity when bounds or another closed convex set remain explicit, reduces to the ordinary Lagrangian-gradient residual in free space, and supports the same contraction test.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) is differentiable with respect to x at each tested point.

notation.meaning: convex-analytic normal cone to X at x

knowledge_statements.title: Projected Stationarity Diagnostic

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(L(x,\lambda,\mu)=f(x)+\langle\lambda,h(x)\rangle+\langle\mu,g(x)\rangle\) for a smooth nonlinear program, and optionally let \(x\in X\) for a nonempty closed convex simple set \(X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order smooth stationarity; the projected form covers explicitly enforced convex simple constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The unconstrained-in-\(x\) stationarity diagnostic is \[s(x,\lambda,\mu)=\|\nabla_xL(x,\lambda,\mu)\|.\] If \(x\in X\) is enforced explicitly, the projected stationarity diagnostic is \[s_X(x,\lambda,\mu)=\left\|x-P_X\big(x-\nabla_xL(x,\lambda,\mu)\big)\right\|.\] For a sequence \(z^k=(x^k,\lambda^k,\mu^k)\), sufficient stationarity progress with factor \(\gamma_k\in(0,1)\) means \(s(z^{k+1})\leq\gamma_ks(z^k)\), or the analogous inequality for \(s_X\). A point is \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{stat}}\)-stationary when the selected residual is at most \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{stat}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stationarity progress is measured by the norm of the Lagrangian gradient. When simple convex constraints are enforced directly, it is measured instead by the projected-gradient mapping. The selected residual is zero exactly when the corresponding first-order stationarity inclusion holds. Progress is a declared contraction of that residual, while approximate stationarity means it lies below a fixed tolerance.
assumptions_latex: For the projected form, \(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex so that \(P_X\) is single valued.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The projected residual may be scaled as \(\alpha^{-1}\|x-P_X(x-\alpha\nabla_xL)\|\) for fixed \(\alpha>0\).
special_cases_latex: For box constraints \(X=[l,u]\), \(P_X\) is componentwise clipping, as in the bound-constrained ALM stopping test.
immediate_consequences_latex: The diagnostic can distinguish an accurate inner augmented-Lagrangian solve from primal feasibility.
boundary_notes: A small stationarity residual without feasibility and complementarity does not define an approximate KKT point.
Nonsmooth objectives require a subdifferential residual instead.

notation.meaning: Normal cone to X at x.

children.title: Complementarity-Progress Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Progress diagnostics specialized to inequality and cone constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Complementarity-Progress Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Natural-residual test combining inequality feasibility, multiplier nonnegativity, and complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For inequalities \(g(x)\le0\) and multipliers \(\mu\ge0\), define the componentwise natural complementarity residual by \[r_{\mathrm{comp}}(x,\mu)=\lVert\min\{\mu,-g(x)\}\rVert.\] It vanishes exactly when \(g(x)\le0\), \(\mu\ge0\), and \(\mu_i g_i(x)=0\) for every \(i\). Given \(\gamma_k\in(0,1)\), complementarity progress occurs when \(r_{\mathrm{comp}}(x_{k+1},\mu_{k+1})\le\gamma_k r_{\mathrm{comp}}(x_k,\mu_k)\); termination requires the residual not to exceed \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{comp}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The natural residual measures inequality feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementarity simultaneously; its contraction indicates progress, and it is zero exactly at complementary pairs.
assumptions_latex: \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p\) is defined at the tested primal iterates.
Minimum and vector products are interpreted componentwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{\mathrm{comp}}(x,\mu)=0\) if and only if \(g(x)\le0\), \(\mu\ge0\), and \(\mu_i g_i(x)=0\) for all \(i\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection residual and progress test for complementarity over a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be a nonempty closed convex cone, impose \(g(x)\in-K\), and let \(\mu\in K^*\). Define \[F_K(g(x),\mu)=\mu-\Pi_{K^*}(\mu+g(x)),\qquad r_{\mathrm{comp}}^K(x,\mu)=\|F_K(g(x),\mu)\|.\] Then \[r_{\mathrm{comp}}^K(x,\mu)=0\iff g(x)\in-K,\ \mu\in K^*,\ \langle\mu,g(x)\rangle=0.\] For \(K=\mathbb R_+^p\), \(F_K(g(x),\mu)=\min\{\mu,-g(x)\}\) componentwise. Conic complementarity progress may be tested by \(r_{\mathrm{comp},k+1}^K\le\gamma_k r_{\mathrm{comp},k}^K\), with \(\gamma_k\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projection fixed-point residual exactly characterizes conic primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementarity; contraction of its norm supplies the conic progress test and the orthant case is the usual natural residual.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a nonempty closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
\(K^*=\{y:\langle y,z\rangle\ge0\ \forall z\in K\}\), and \(\Pi_{K^*}\) is Euclidean projection.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let inequalities use the convention \(g(x)\leq0\) with multipliers \(\mu\geq0\). For conic constraints, let \(G(x)\in-K\) and \(y\in K^*\), where \(K\) is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional inequality or conic constraints; feasibility and stationarity are monitored separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The componentwise complementarity diagnostic for scalar inequalities is \[c(x,\mu)=\|\mu\odot g(x)\|,\] accompanied by the dual-feasibility residual \(d(\mu)=\|[-\mu]_+\|\). A sign-robust combined complementarity diagnostic is \[c_{\min}(x,\mu)=\|\min\{\mu,-g(x)\}\|,\] with the minimum taken componentwise. For a cone pair \((G(x),y)\), the complementarity diagnostic is \(c_K(x,y)=|\langle y,G(x)\rangle|\), used together with distances to \(-K\) and \(K^*\). Sufficient progress is a declared contraction of the selected diagnostic; \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{comp}}\)-complementarity means that it and its associated primal- and dual-feasibility residuals are at most their tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For scalar inequalities, complementarity progress is measured by the products of multipliers and constraint values, with a separate check that multipliers are nonnegative. An equivalent zero-set residual takes the componentwise minimum of the nonnegative multiplier and the nonnegative slack. For cone constraints, complementarity is the absolute primal-dual pairing, accompanied by membership residuals for the primal and dual cones. Approximate complementarity requires these residuals to satisfy declared tolerances.
assumptions_latex: For the conic form, \(K\) is a closed convex cone and \(K^*\) is its dual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under primal and dual feasibility, \(c(x,\mu)=0\iff\mu_jg_j(x)=0\) for every \(j\); likewise \(c_K(x,y)=0\) is the conic complementarity relation.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Under \(\mu\geq0\) and \(g(x)\leq0\), \(c_{\min}=0\) and \(c=0\) have the same zero set.
special_cases_latex: For a single inequality, complementarity is \(\mu g(x)=0\) with \(\mu\geq0\) and \(g(x)\leq0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: An inactive strict inequality requires a zero multiplier at exact complementarity.
A positive multiplier can persist only on an active constraint at a KKT point.
boundary_notes: A small product alone can conceal simultaneous sign violations; primal and dual feasibility must also be checked.
The scalar product residual may require scaling when constraints have disparate units.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
At a feasible point \(x\) of \(h(x)=0\), \(g(x)\leq0\), let \(A(x)=\{j:g_j(x)=0\}\) and define the KKT multiplier set \[\Lambda(x)=\{(\lambda,\mu):
abla f(x)+

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional nonlinear programming at a specified feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a feasible point, regularity-multiplier failure is classified as failure of a declared constraint qualification, absence of KKT multipliers, an unbounded multiplier set, or a non-singleton multiplier set. LICQ fails when active constraint gradients are linearly dependent. MFCQ fails when equality gradients are dependent or no direction remains tangent to the equalities while moving strictly into every active inequality. These cases are related but are not interchangeable.
assumptions_latex: The point \(x\) is feasible and the active set is defined by exact equality \(g_j(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The failure-mode set is \(\mathfrak F(x)=\{\ell\in\{1,2,3,4\}:F_\ell\text{ holds at }x\}\), allowing multiple simultaneous labels.
equivalent_formulations_latex: MFCQ holds exactly when the KKT multiplier set at a local solution is nonempty and bounded, under the cited smooth finite-dimensional setting.
special_cases_latex: Under LICQ, any KKT multiplier is unique, so \(F_4\) cannot occur.
immediate_consequences_latex: An unbounded sequence selected from \(\Lambda(x)\) witnesses \(F_3\).
Multiplier nonuniqueness does not by itself imply nonexistence.
boundary_notes: Constraint qualifications are sufficient regularity conditions; their failure alone does not prove that KKT conditions fail.
Numerical near-dependence is distinct from exact LICQ failure.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Regularity Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of MFCQ at a feasible nonlinear-programming point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At a feasible point \(x_*\), let \(I(x_*)=\{i:g_i(x_*)=0\}\). The Mangasarian–Fromovitz constraint qualification fails when either the equality gradients \(\{
abla c_j(x_*)\}_{j=1}^m\) are linearly dependent, or no direction \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfies \[
abla c(x_*)^{\mathsf T}d=0,\qquad 
abla g_i(x_*)^{\mathsf T}d<0\quad(i\in I(x_*)).\] At this boundary, standard conclusions asserting existence and local boundedness of KKT multipliers are no longer guaranteed; augmented-Lagrangian dual estimates may therefore be nonunique or unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MFCQ fails through dependent equality gradients or absence of a direction strictly reducing every active inequality while remaining tangent to equalities; multiplier guarantees may then fail.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) and \(g\) are continuously differentiable near the feasible point \(x_*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure of the displayed MFCQ predicate removes the general guarantee of locally bounded KKT multiplier sets near \(x_*\).

notation.meaning: index set of inequalities active at the feasible point

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regularity Failure Can Destroy KKT Multipliers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth equality-constrained local minimizer at which no Lagrange multiplier satisfies stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R} x\qquad\text{subject to}\qquad c(x)=x^2=0.\] The feasible set is \(\{0\}\), so \(x_*=0\) is a local minimizer. Equality regularity fails because \(c'(0)=0\), and every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\) satisfies \[\nabla_xL(0,\lambda)=1+\lambda c'(0)=1\ne0.\] Thus no KKT multiplier exists at this local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular equality can make a feasible point a local minimizer while preventing every multiplier from satisfying Lagrangian stationarity.
assumptions_latex: The objective and equality constraint are smooth real-valued functions on \(\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_*=0\ \text{is a local minimizer, MFCQ fails at }x_*,\ \text{and }\Lambda(x_*)=\varnothing.

notation.meaning: KKT multiplier set at the feasible point

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure of MFCQ at a Feasible Point
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x\) satisfy \(h(x)=0\), \(g(x)\leq0\), with active set \(A(x)=\{j:g_j(x)=0\}\), where \(h\) and \(g\) are continuously differentiable.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional nonlinear programming; MFCQ is used as the canonical regularity condition because it directly controls multiplier boundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Constraint-regularity failure at \(x\) means failure of the Mangasarian–Fromovitz constraint qualification: either the equality gradients \(\{
abla h_i(x)\}_{i=1}^m\) are linearly dependent, or \[
exists d\in\mathbb R^n\quad	ext{such that}\quad 
abla h(x)d=0\quad	ext{and}\quad
abla g_j(x)^Td<0\ 	ext{for all }j\in A(x).\] Equivalently, when the equality gradients are independent, failure occurs if every direction tangent to all equalities has nonnegative directional derivative for at least one active inequality. LICQ failure is the separate, stronger-gradient-dependence event in which the combined equality and active-inequality gradients are linearly dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint-regularity failure is defined here as failure of MFCQ. It occurs if the equality gradients are dependent or if there is no direction tangent to every equality that moves strictly inside all active inequalities. LICQ failure is a stronger and separate test based on linear independence of all equality and active-inequality gradients. The definition concerns local constraint geometry, not failure of an algorithm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Regularity fails exactly when \(\operatorname{rank}\nabla h(x)<m\) or the displayed strict-feasible-direction system is infeasible.
equivalent_formulations_latex: By a theorem of alternatives, failure of the direction system can be represented by a nonzero abnormal combination of equality and active-inequality gradients with nonnegative inequality coefficients.
special_cases_latex: With equality constraints only, regularity failure reduces to \(\operatorname{rank}\nabla h(x)<m\).
LICQ implies MFCQ, so MFCQ failure implies LICQ cannot hold.
immediate_consequences_latex: At a local solution, MFCQ failure removes the standard guarantee that the KKT multiplier set is nonempty and bounded.
boundary_notes: Failure of MFCQ does not prove that no KKT multiplier exists.
Near rank deficiency is a numerical diagnostic, not exact regularity failure.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Multiplier Sequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Redundant equalities permit divergent multiplier estimates with exact primal feasibility and stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a differentiable objective \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) with redundant equalities \(c_1(x)=x\) and \(c_2(x)=2x\). At \(x_*=0\), choose any multiplier \(\bar\lambda\) satisfying \(f'(0)+\bar\lambda_1+2\bar\lambda_2=0\), and set \[\lambda_k=\bar\lambda+k(2,-1).\] Then \(\lVert\lambda_k\rVert\to\infty\), whereas \(c(x_*)=0\) and \(\nabla_xL(x_*,\lambda_k)=0\) for every \(k\). Thus vanishing primal and stationarity residuals alone do not certify bounded or reliable multiplier estimates when constraint gradients are dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With redundant equality gradients, multipliers can diverge along a null direction while primal feasibility and Lagrangian stationarity remain exact.
assumptions_latex: The equality constraints are represented separately despite their linear dependence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sequence satisfies \(\lVert\lambda_k\rVert\to\infty\), \(c(x_*)=0\), and \(\nabla_xL(x_*,\lambda_k)=0\) for all \(k\).

notation.meaning: one multiplier satisfying stationarity at the feasible point

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(y^k=(\lambda^k,\mu^k)\in\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R_+^r\) be the equality and inequality multiplier estimates generated by a multiplier method or selected from KKT multiplier sets.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional multiplier sequences; unboundedness is a sequence property and is distinct from nonuniqueness at a fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The multiplier sequence \(\{y^k\}_{k\geq0}\) is unbounded when \[\sup_{k\geq0}\|y^k\|=+\infty.\] It diverges in norm when the stronger condition \(\|y^k\|\to+\infty\) holds. It has an unbounded subsequence when there are indices \(k_\ell\uparrow\infty\) such that \(\|y^{k_\ell}\|\to+\infty\); in finite dimensions this is equivalent to unboundedness of the full sequence. For equality ALM with update \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\rho_kr^{k+1}\), multiplier unboundedness is assessed on the accumulated dual estimates, not merely on a single large increment \(\rho_kr^{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiplier sequence is unbounded if its norms have no finite uniform bound. Norm divergence is stronger: every sufficiently late multiplier must be large. In finite dimensions, unboundedness is equivalent to the existence of a subsequence whose norms tend to infinity. For ALM, the diagnostic is applied to the accumulated multiplier estimates; one unusually large update does not by itself make the entire sequence unbounded.
assumptions_latex: A fixed norm is used; all norms are equivalent for boundedness in finite dimensions.
Inequality estimates use the declared sign convention \(\mu^k\geq0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Unboundedness is equivalent to: for every \(M>0\), there exists \(k\) with \(\|y^k\|>M\).
special_cases_latex: If \(y^k\in\Lambda(x^k)\), \(x^k\to x^*\), and the local multiplier sets admit selections of arbitrarily large norm, an unbounded selected sequence can result.
immediate_consequences_latex: An unbounded sequence has no convergent subsequence containing all sufficiently late iterates.
MFCQ at a local solution rules out unboundedness of the exact KKT multiplier set there.
boundary_notes: Unboundedness does not imply monotone norm growth.
A large but finite multiplier is not an unbounded sequence.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Nonuniqueness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonuniqueness of KKT multipliers at a fixed feasible stationary point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a feasible point \(x_*\), define its KKT multiplier set by \[\Lambda(x_*)=\{(\lambda,\mu):\nabla_xL(x_*,\lambda,\mu)=0,\ \mu\ge0,\ \mu_i g_i(x_*)=0\ \text{for all }i\}.\] Multipliers are nonunique at \(x_*\) precisely when \(\Lambda(x_*)\) contains two distinct elements. Dependent equality gradients or dependent active-inequality gradients can create nonzero multiplier directions that preserve stationarity and complementarity, so an augmented-Lagrangian multiplier sequence may approach different dual limits while its primal iterates approach the same \(x_*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: KKT multipliers are nonunique when a single feasible stationary point admits at least two distinct multiplier vectors; dependent active constraint gradients are a standard mechanism.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Multiplier nonuniqueness at \(x_*\) is the condition \(|\Lambda(x_*)|>1\).

notation.meaning: set of KKT multiplier pairs associated with the fixed primal point

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Redundant Equalities Produce an Affine Multiplier Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit fixed-primal-point example of multiplier nonuniqueness caused by redundant equality gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R}0\qquad\text{subject to}\qquad c_1(x)=x=0,\quad c_2(x)=2x=0.\] At the unique feasible point \(x_*=0\), KKT stationarity is \[\lambda_1+2\lambda_2=0.\] Hence \[\Lambda(0)=\{(-2t,t):t\in\mathbb R\},\] so the same primal stationary point has infinitely many multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two redundant equality constraints leave a one-dimensional affine family of KKT multipliers at the same feasible point.
assumptions_latex: Equality multipliers are unrestricted in sign.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniqueness boundary for KKT multipliers at a fixed feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_*\) be feasible and suppose that two KKT multiplier pairs \((\lambda,\mu)\) and \((\widehat\lambda,\widehat\mu)\) exist. If the equality gradients together with all active inequality gradients are linearly independent at \(x_*\), then \[(\lambda,\mu)=(\widehat\lambda,\widehat\mu).\] Thus KKT multipliers at a LICQ point are unique whenever they exist. Failure of LICQ is necessary for multiplier nonuniqueness but is not sufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear independence of equality and active-inequality gradients makes any KKT multiplier unique; dependence is necessary but does not itself force nonuniqueness.
assumptions_latex: Both multiplier pairs satisfy stationarity, dual sign feasibility, and complementarity under \(g(x)\le0\).
