children.title: Penalty-Conditioning Failure Modes
children.top_down_role: Breakdown modes caused by ineffective penalty management or distorted subproblem geometry.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\rho_k>0\) be the ALM penalty parameter and let \(H_k\) be the Hessian or symmetric model used for the \(k\)-th augmented-Lagrangian subproblem, restricted to the algorithm's free-variable subspace.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional ALM; conditioning is measured only when the restricted model is nonsingular and its condition number is meaningful.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A penalty-conditioning failure mode is any declared occurrence of \[(P_1)\quad \rho_{k+1}>\rho_k\text{ although the accepted feasibility-progress test is satisfied},\] \[(P_2)\quad \sup_k\rho_k=\infty\text{ or penalty increases occur infinitely often},\] \[(P_3)\quad \kappa(H_k)\geq\kappa_{\max}\text{ or }H_k\text{ is singular},\] \[(P_4)\quad\text{the prescribed inner residual tolerance cannot be attained at the current }\rho_k.\] For equality ALM, the characteristic curvature model is \(H_k\approx\nabla_{xx}^2L(x^k,\lambda^k)+\rho_kJ_h(x^k)^TJ_h(x^k)\). Thus penalty control and conditioning are recorded separately even though growth of \(\rho_k\) can magnify curvature disparities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Penalty-conditioning failures comprise an unnecessary penalty increase despite acceptable feasibility, unbounded or indefinitely repeated penalty escalation, a singular or excessively ill-conditioned subproblem model, and failure of the inner solver to attain its requested residual. The characteristic ALM Hessian adds a penalty-weighted constraint-Jacobian Gram matrix to the Lagrangian Hessian. This explains why penalty behavior and conditioning are related, but the definition records them as distinct events.
assumptions_latex: The feasibility acceptance test, inner tolerance, and threshold \(\kappa_{\max}\) are fixed by the algorithm.
\(\kappa(H_k)\) denotes a condition estimate on the relevant free subspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The active penalty-conditioning labels at iteration \(k\) are \(\mathfrak P_k=\{j:P_j\text{ holds at }k\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For positive-definite \(H_k\), \(\kappa_2(H_k)=\lambda_{\max}(H_k)/\lambda_{\min}(H_k)\).
special_cases_latex: For the quadratic penalty method, forcing \(\rho_k\to\infty\) commonly produces the large-curvature term \(\rho_kJ_h^TJ_h\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A bounded-penalty regime excludes \(P_2\).
A singular model activates \(P_3\) regardless of the numerical condition threshold.
boundary_notes: A large condition estimate is basis- and scaling-dependent.
Penalty growth alone is not a convergence failure unless it violates the declared control regime.

notation.meaning: Subproblem Hessian or symmetric curvature model.

children.title: Premature Penalty Growth
children.top_down_role: Over-aggressive augmentation before useful primal–dual progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Premature Penalty Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational test for increasing the penalty before the current subproblem or feasibility test justifies it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the equality augmented Lagrangian \(L_{\rho}(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}c(x)+(\rho/2)\lVert c(x)\rVert^2\), let \(s_{k+1}=\lVert\nabla_xL_{\rho_k}(x_{k+1},\lambda_k)\rVert\). Given inner tolerance \(\epsilon_k\) and feasibility factor \(\eta_k\in(0,1)\), a penalty increase is premature when \[\rho_{k+1}>\rho_k\quad\text{and}\quad\bigl(s_{k+1}>\epsilon_k\ \text{or}\ \lVert c(x_{k+1})\rVert\le\eta_k\lVert c(x_k)\rVert\bigr).\] The first alternative confounds inner-solve error with inadequate penalization; the second increases curvature despite satisfactory feasibility progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Penalty growth is premature if imposed before adequate inner solution or despite already satisfactory feasibility contraction, thereby adding curvature without a justified outer-progress failure.
assumptions_latex: The outer method uses the displayed quadratic equality augmented Lagrangian.
The controller has declared inner and feasibility-progress tolerances \(\epsilon_k\ge0\) and \(\eta_k\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed conjunction is a verifiable diagnostic for an unjustified penalty increase at iteration \(k\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Penalty Increase Contrary to the Feasibility-Acceptance Branch
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let an ALM use penalty \(\rho_k>0\), feasibility measure \(\theta_k=\theta(x^k)\), inner residual \(e_k\), feasibility threshold \(\eta_k\), and inner tolerance \(\omega_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rule-relative definition for practical ALM controllers that retain the penalty when current feasibility is acceptable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A premature penalty-growth event occurs at iteration \(k\) when \[\rho_{k+1}>\rho_k\quad\text{and}\quad\theta_k\leq\eta_k\quad\text{and}\quad e_k\leq\omega_k.\] Thus the penalty is increased even though the current subproblem has been solved to its requested accuracy and the algorithm's own feasibility-acceptance test has succeeded. More generally, if acceptance is expressed by a predicate \(A_k\), premature growth is the event \(A_k\land(\rho_{k+1}>\rho_k)\) whenever the declared controller specifies \(A_k\Rightarrow\rho_{k+1}=\rho_k\). The definition is relative to that controller and does not label an increase premature when the feasibility test fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Premature penalty growth occurs when an ALM increases its penalty even though the current inner solve meets its requested accuracy and the controller's feasibility-acceptance test has already passed. In a generic controller, it is the simultaneous occurrence of the acceptance predicate and a penalty increase when acceptance is supposed to retain the current penalty. The event is rule-relative; an increase after inadequate feasibility is not premature under this definition.
assumptions_latex: The controller explicitly specifies that successful feasibility acceptance retains the penalty.
The quantities \(\theta_k,e_k,\eta_k,\omega_k\) are evaluated before selecting \(\rho_{k+1}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: With a Boolean acceptance predicate \(A_k\), the event is \(A_k\wedge(\rho_{k+1}>\rho_k)\).
special_cases_latex: In Algorithm 17.4, \(\theta_k=\|c(x_k)\|\); passing \(\theta_k\leq\eta_k\) prescribes \(\rho_{k+1}=\rho_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A premature increase violates the controller's intended separation between multiplier-update iterations and feasibility-restoration iterations.
boundary_notes: This definition does not claim that every early large penalty is harmful.
Controllers that intentionally increase penalties after accepted steps require a different definition.

children.title: Persistent Penalty Escalation
children.top_down_role: Failure to enter a bounded-penalty convergence regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Penalty Escalation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infinite multiplicative penalty updates exclude entry into a bounded-penalty regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an augmented-Lagrangian controller satisfies \(\rho_{k+1}\ge\rho_k>0\), and whenever its progress test fails it sets \(\rho_{k+1}\ge\tau\rho_k\) for a fixed \(\tau>1\). Let \(k_j\) denote the iteration at which the \(j\)-th progress failure occurs, for \(j=1,2,\ldots\). If the test fails infinitely often, then \[\rho_{k_j+1}\ge\tau^j\rho_0\longrightarrow\infty.\] Hence the method never enters a bounded-penalty tail. Any convergence theorem whose hypotheses require eventual constancy or boundedness of \(\{\rho_k\}\) is therefore inapplicable unless a separate result handles the unbounded-penalty regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If multiplicative penalty increases occur infinitely often, the penalty after the j-th such update is at least the initial penalty multiplied by the j-th power of the update factor. The penalty is therefore unbounded, so bounded-penalty convergence guarantees cannot be invoked.
assumptions_latex: The penalty sequence is positive and nondecreasing.
Every declared progress failure multiplies the current penalty by at least a fixed \(\tau>1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Infinitely many escalation events imply \(\rho_{k_j+1}\ge\tau^j\rho_0\to\infty\), hence \(\sup_k\rho_k=\infty\) and no eventually bounded-penalty regime exists.

notation.meaning: penalty parameter at outer iteration k
iteration at which the j-th penalty-escalation event is triggered

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure to Enter an Eventually Constant Penalty Regime
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\{\rho_k\}_{k\geq0}\subset(0,\infty)\) be a nondecreasing ALM penalty sequence, and let \(U=\{k:\rho_{k+1}>\rho_k\}\) be its update-index set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer penalty-control behavior in deterministic ALM; no conclusion about feasibility or infeasibility is built into the definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Persistent penalty escalation means that the penalty is increased infinitely often: \[|U|=\infty,\qquad U=\{k\geq0:\rho_{k+1}>\rho_k\}.\] The method enters a bounded-penalty convergence regime when there exist \(K\) and \(\bar\rho<\infty\) such that \(\rho_k=\bar\rho\) for every \(k\geq K\). Therefore persistent escalation is exactly the failure of eventual constancy for a nondecreasing sequence whose controller changes \(\rho_k\) only by strict increases. If every increase obeys \(\rho_{k+1}\geq\gamma\rho_k\) for a fixed \(\gamma>1\), persistent escalation additionally implies \(\rho_k\to+\infty\). Without a uniform multiplicative factor, infinite escalation need not imply divergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Persistent penalty escalation means that a nondecreasing ALM penalty is strictly increased at infinitely many outer iterations. A bounded-penalty regime is eventually constant: after some iteration, one finite penalty is retained forever. For controllers that only retain or increase the penalty, persistent escalation is the failure to enter that regime. If every increase multiplies the penalty by at least a fixed factor greater than one, persistent escalation forces the penalty to diverge; otherwise infinitely many small increases can remain bounded.
assumptions_latex: The controller changes the penalty only through retention or strict increase.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Persistent escalation holds iff \(\forall K\ \exists k\geq K:\rho_{k+1}>\rho_k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The bounded-penalty regime is \(\exists K,\bar\rho<\infty\ \forall k\geq K:\rho_k=\bar\rho\).
special_cases_latex: For the update \(\rho_{k+1}=100\rho_k\) on every failed feasibility test, infinitely many failures imply \(\rho_k\to\infty\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Persistent escalation prevents eventual use of one fixed augmented-Lagrangian subproblem family.
Under uniform multiplicative growth, the curvature contribution \(\rho_kJ_h^TJ_h\) becomes unbounded along directions seen by \(J_h\).
boundary_notes: Infinite increases do not alone certify infeasibility or constraint degeneracy.
A penalty sequence can be bounded but not eventually constant if its increases have vanishing size.

children.title: Subproblem Ill-Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Numerical difficulty caused by highly anisotropic augmented curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Subproblem Ill-Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition-number growth in a quadratic augmented-Lagrangian subproblem with anisotropic constraint curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(f(x)=(\alpha/2)\lVert x\rVert^2\), \(c(x)=Ax-b\), and \(\alpha>0\). The Hessian of the equality augmented-Lagrangian subproblem is \[H_{\rho}=\alpha I+\rho A^{\mathsf T}A.\] Its Euclidean spectral condition number is \[\kappa_2(H_{\rho})=\frac{\alpha+\rho\sigma_{\max}(A)^2}{\alpha+\rho\sigma_{\min}(A)^2},\] where \(\sigma_{\min}(A)\) includes zero singular values on the domain. Thus large \(\rho\) produces severe anisotropy when the extreme singular values differ substantially; if \(A\) has a nullspace, the condition number grows linearly in \(\rho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic augmentation adds curvature proportional to squared constraint singular values. A large penalty can therefore make inner subproblems highly ill-conditioned, especially when the constraint Jacobian has a nullspace.
assumptions_latex: Conditioning is measured in the Euclidean norm on \(\mathbb R^n\).

notation.meaning: extreme singular values of the constraint matrix on the full domain

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), where \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) are twice continuously differentiable. For \(\rho_k>0\) and \(\lambda_k\in\mathbb R^m\), let \(\mathcal L_{\rho_k}(x,\lambda_k)=f(x)+\lambda_k^{\mathsf T}c(x)+(\rho_k/2)\|c(x)\|_2^2\), and let \(H_k=\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L_{\rho_k}(x_k,\lambda_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, smooth, equality-constrained augmented-Lagrangian subproblems. The definition measures local spectral conditioning and does not assert convergence or numerical failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_k\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the subspace on which the inner method solves its local quadratic model, and assume \(H_k|_{S_k}\) is positive definite. Define \(\kappa_k=\lambda_{\max}(H_k|_{S_k})/\lambda_{\min}(H_k|_{S_k})\). The subproblem at iteration \(k\) is \(\bar\kappa\)-ill-conditioned when \(\kappa_k\geq\bar\kappa\), for a specified threshold \(\bar\kappa>1\). A sequence of subproblems is asymptotically ill-conditioned when \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}\kappa_k=+\infty\). If \(H_k|_{S_k}\) is singular or indefinite, its conditioning is declared infinite for this positive-definite local-model convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the smooth equality-constrained augmented Lagrangian, restrict the subproblem Hessian to the subspace used by the inner solver. Its condition number is the largest restricted eigenvalue divided by the smallest. A subproblem is ill-conditioned when this ratio exceeds a prescribed threshold, and a sequence is asymptotically ill-conditioned when the ratios are unbounded. Singularity or indefiniteness counts as infinite conditioning under this convention.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(x_k\).
\(S_k\) is a nonzero linear subspace, and the finite-ratio case requires \(d^{\mathsf T}H_kd>0\) for every \(0\neq d\in S_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_k:=\lambda_{\max}(H_k|_{S_k})/\lambda_{\min}(H_k|_{S_k})\), with ill-conditioning defined by \(\kappa_k\geq\bar\kappa\) or, asymptotically, \(\limsup_k\kappa_k=+\infty\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For positive-definite \(H_k|_{S_k}\), \(\kappa_k=\|H_k|_{S_k}\|_2\,\|(H_k|_{S_k})^{-1}\|_2\).
The asymptotic condition is equivalent to the existence of a subsequence \(k_j\) such that \(\kappa_{k_j}\to+\infty\).
special_cases_latex: If \(c(x)=Ax-b\), then \(H_k=\nabla^2 f(x_k)+\rho_k A^{\mathsf T}A\); large \(\rho_k\) can create strong anisotropy between \(\operatorname{range}(A^{\mathsf T})\) and \(\ker A\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A small gradient residual alone does not certify an accurately computed minimizer when \(\lambda_{\min}(H_k|_{S_k})\) is very small.
boundary_notes: This definition is scaling-dependent: rescaling variables or constraints can change \(\kappa_k\).
Nonsmooth subproblems require a generalized-Hessian or error-bound definition not covered here.

notation.meaning: Spectral condition number of the restricted augmented-Lagrangian Hessian.
Subspace used by the inner local model.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: spectral conditioning is the standard local numerical-conditioning measure for a positive-definite smooth subproblem Hessian.
No inspected authoritative locator was available to support this exact diagnostic definition.
knowledge_statements.title: Ill-conditioning of an augmented-Lagrangian subproblem

children.title: Inner-Solution Failures
children.top_down_role: Breakdown modes arising from unsuitable or insufficient subproblem solutions.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure of an augmented-Lagrangian inner solution
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At outer iteration \(k\), let \(\phi_k:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be the augmented-Lagrangian subproblem objective on a closed set \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). Let \(x_k^{\mathrm{in}}\) be the point returned by the inner solver, \(r_k\) a stationarity residual, \(\varepsilon_k\geq0\) a value tolerance, and \(\eta_k\geq0\) a stationarity tolerance.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic inner solves. This is an admissibility definition encompassing inaccurate, unsuitable, or unsuccessful returned points; it does not identify the particular numerical cause.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the admissible inner-solution set by \(\mathcal A_k=\{x\in X:\phi_k(x)\leq\inf_{z\in X}\phi_k(z)+\varepsilon_k,\ r_k(x)\leq\eta_k\}\). An inner-solution failure occurs at iteration \(k\) when the solver returns no point, returns \(x_k^{\mathrm{in}}\notin X\), produces a nonfinite objective value, or returns \(x_k^{\mathrm{in}}\notin\mathcal A_k\). A persistent inner-solution failure is an infinite index set \(K\subseteq\mathbb N\) for which failure occurs at every \(k\in K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inner solve succeeds only if it returns an admissible point whose augmented objective is within the prescribed value tolerance of the subproblem infimum and whose stationarity residual is within the prescribed residual tolerance. Failure means that no point is returned, the point is outside the domain, its objective is nonfinite, or either accuracy test fails. Failure is persistent when it occurs at infinitely many outer iterations.
assumptions_latex: \(r_k:X\to[0,+\infty]\) is a specified residual satisfying \(r_k(x)=0\) at the intended stationary points.
The tolerances \(\varepsilon_k\) and \(\eta_k\) are fixed before classifying the returned point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k^{\mathrm{in}}\) is a failed inner solution exactly when it is absent, inadmissible, nonfinite, or lies outside \(\mathcal A_k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: When a point is returned in \(X\) with finite value, failure is the disjunction \(\phi_k(x_k^{\mathrm{in}})-\inf_X\phi_k>\varepsilon_k\) or \(r_k(x_k^{\mathrm{in}})>\eta_k\).
special_cases_latex: For unconstrained smooth inner minimization, one may take \(r_k(x)=\|\nabla\phi_k(x)\|_2\).
For composite \(\phi_k=g_k+h\), one may take \(r_k(x)=\operatorname{dist}(0,\nabla g_k(x)+\partial h(x))\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A returned local stationary point can still be an inner-solution failure if it violates the value-accuracy requirement.
Solver termination is not itself success unless the returned point satisfies the declared admissibility tests.
boundary_notes: The definition separates classification from cause; ill-conditioning, iteration limits, and attraction to a spurious local minimum are possible causes but are not equivalent to failure.
If the global infimum is unavailable, an implementable surrogate certificate must be specified separately.

notation.meaning: Set of inner points satisfying both value and stationarity requirements.
Chosen stationarity residual for the inner subproblem.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: approximate value and stationarity conditions are standard mathematical acceptance criteria for inexact subproblem solutions.
No inspected source supports this exact umbrella classification and its persistence clause.
knowledge_statements.title: Failure of an augmented-Lagrangian inner solution

knowledge_statements.title: Insufficient Inner Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inner first-order errors that do not vanish cannot force outer stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For equality constraints, let \(x_{k+1}\) be an approximate stationary point of \(L_{ho_k}(\cdot,\lambda_k)\), and update \(\lambda_{k+1}=\lambda_k+ho_k c(x_{k+1})\). Then \[
abla_xL(x_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1})=
abla_xL_{ho_k}(x_{k+1},\lambda_k).\] Consequently, if the inner residuals satisfy only \(\lVert
abla_xL_{ho_k}(x_{k+1},\lambda_k)Vert\le\epsilon_k\) with \(\limsup_k\epsilon_k>0\), the update supplies no implication that the outer stationarity residual converges to zero. Vanishing inner tolerances are therefore necessary for this identity-based stationarity guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After the standard multiplier update, the outer Lagrangian-gradient residual equals the inner augmented-gradient residual. Nonvanishing inner tolerances therefore cannot guarantee asymptotic stationarity.
assumptions_latex: The method uses the quadratic equality augmented Lagrangian and its standard multiplier update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The condition \(\epsilon_k\to0\) is required to deduce \(\lVert\nabla_xL(x_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1})\rVert\to0\) solely from the inner stopping inequalities.

assumptions_latex: The equality constraint is identically zero, so the standard multiplier update leaves the multiplier unchanged.
The inner stopping rule permits any point satisfying \(\lvert\nabla_xL_\rho(x,\lambda)\rvert\le\varepsilon\) for a fixed \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The admissible choice \(x_{k+1}=\varepsilon\) for all \(k\) gives \(\lvert\nabla_xL(x_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1})\rvert=\varepsilon\not\to0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp example showing that a fixed positive inner gradient tolerance permits permanent nonstationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^2\) with the identically zero equality constraint \(c(x)=0\). Then \(L_\rho(x,\lambda)=\tfrac12x^2\), and the multiplier update changes nothing. For any fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), choosing \(x_{k+1}=\varepsilon\) at every inner solve satisfies \(\lvert\nabla_xL_\rho(x_{k+1},\lambda_k)\rvert=\varepsilon\), yet the outer stationarity residual is identically \(\varepsilon\) and does not converge to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed positive inner tolerance can be met forever by the same nonstationary point, so the outer stationarity residual need not decrease.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inner accuracy insufficient for the prescribed outer forcing rule
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\phi_k\) be the augmented-Lagrangian subproblem objective, let \(x_{k+1}\) be its computed inner solution, and let \(r_k(x_{k+1})\geq0\) be a stationarity residual. Let \(v_k\geq0\) measure the current outer violation, for example \(v_k=\|c(x_k)\|_2\), and let \(\eta_k^{\mathrm{req}}\) be the forcing tolerance required by the outer convergence regime.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic inexact ALM with an explicitly declared forcing sequence. This definition concerns incompatibility with the required outer accuracy schedule, not mere nonzero inner error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The inner solution at iteration \(k\) has sufficient accuracy when \(r_k(x_{k+1})\leq\eta_k^{\mathrm{req}}\). It has insufficient inner accuracy when \(r_k(x_{k+1})>\eta_k^{\mathrm{req}}\). For a relative forcing rule \(\eta_k^{\mathrm{req}}=\gamma_k v_k\), insufficiency is \(r_k(x_{k+1})>\gamma_k v_k\). A trajectory has asymptotically insufficient accuracy when there exist \(\delta>0\) and infinitely many \(k\) such that \(r_k(x_{k+1})\geq\eta_k^{\mathrm{req}}+\delta\), or when a required summability condition \(\sum_k r_k(x_{k+1})<\infty\) is violated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inner accuracy is sufficient when the returned point's stationarity residual meets the forcing tolerance prescribed by the outer method. It is insufficient when the residual exceeds that tolerance. Under relative forcing, the threshold is a factor times the current constraint violation. Persistent excess by a positive margin, or violation of a required summability condition, defines asymptotically insufficient accuracy.
assumptions_latex: A nonnegative residual \(r_k\) and a nonnegative required tolerance \(\eta_k^{\mathrm{req}}\) are specified for every outer iteration.
For relative forcing, \(v_k\) and \(\gamma_k\) are specified before the inner point is assessed.
A summability failure is invoked only when summability is an explicit hypothesis of the selected outer convergence result.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Insufficient accuracy is the quantified failure \(r_k(x_{k+1})>\eta_k^{\mathrm{req}}\), with persistent or nonsummable failure defined relative to the declared outer forcing regime.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(\eta_k^{\mathrm{req}}>0\), the point is insufficiently accurate exactly when \(r_k(x_{k+1})/\eta_k^{\mathrm{req}}>1\).
special_cases_latex: For smooth unconstrained inner solves, \(r_k(x)=\|\nabla_x\mathcal L_{\rho_k}(x,\lambda_k)\|_2\).
An absolute schedule uses \(\eta_k^{\mathrm{req}}=\eta_k\downarrow0\); a relative schedule uses \(\eta_k^{\mathrm{req}}=\gamma_k\|c(x_k)\|_2\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A fixed inner tolerance is eventually insufficient whenever the required tolerance tends to zero below that fixed level.
Nonzero inner error can remain sufficient if it respects the prescribed forcing sequence.
boundary_notes: No universal forcing sequence is canonical across all ALM variants; the applicable convergence statement determines the required schedule.
This definition does not classify a highly accurate stationary point that is nevertheless a poor global augmented minimizer.

notation.meaning: Inner tolerance demanded by the outer convergence regime.
Outer feasibility or progress measure used by a relative forcing rule.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: forcing inequalities and summable-error requirements are standard ways to couple inner and outer accuracy.
The exact forcing alternatives require an inspected convergence source before promotion.

children.title: Nonunique Augmented Minimizers
children.top_down_role: Ambiguous subproblem selection and unstable primal tracking.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonunique Augmented Minimizers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-valued minimization of a fixed augmented-Lagrangian subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed multiplier \(\lambda\) and penalty \(\rho>0\), define the augmented minimizer set \[M(\lambda,\rho)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}L_{\rho}(x,\lambda).\] The subproblem has nonunique augmented minimizers when \(|M(\lambda,\rho)|>1\). For example, with \(X=\mathbb R\), \(f(x)=0\), \(c(x)=x^2-1\), and \(\lambda=0\), one has \(L_{\rho}(x,0)=(\rho/2)(x^2-1)^2\) and \(M(0,\rho)=\{-1,1\}\). An unspecified inner solver may therefore select different, separated primal branches under identical outer parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An augmented subproblem is nonunique when its argmin set has multiple points. Without a selection rule, identical outer parameters can produce different primal branches.
assumptions_latex: The augmented-Lagrangian subproblem attains its minimum on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nonuniqueness is exactly the predicate \(|M(\lambda,\rho)|>1\); in the displayed example, \(M(0,\rho)=\{-1,1\}\).

notation.meaning: global minimizer set of the augmented subproblem

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be convex and suppose that, for fixed \((\lambda,\rho)\), the mapping \(x\mapsto L_\rho(x,\lambda)\) is strictly convex on \(X\) and attains its minimum. Then \(M(\lambda,ho)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}L_\rho(x,\lambda)\) contains exactly one point. Thus strict convexity on the relevant convex domain excludes augmented-minimizer branch ambiguity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An attained strictly convex augmented subproblem on a convex domain has a unique global minimizer, so branch ambiguity is excluded.

children.title: Spurious Local Augmented Minima
children.top_down_role: Nonconvex augmented minima disconnected from the desired constrained solution branch.

knowledge_statements.title: Spurious Local Augmented Minima
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A nonconvex equality augmented Lagrangian can possess a strict infeasible local minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(f(x)=0\) subject to \(c(x)=x^2-1=0\), whose feasible points are \(x=\pm1\). For \(\rho>0\) and \(\lambda>\rho\), the augmented Lagrangian is \[L_{\rho}(x,\lambda)=\lambda(x^2-1)+\frac{\rho}{2}(x^2-1)^2.\] At \(x=0\), its derivative vanishes and \(L_{\rho}''(0,\lambda)=2(\lambda-\rho)>0\), so \(x=0\) is a strict local augmented minimum. Nevertheless, \(c(0)=-1\), so this local minimum is infeasible and is not a solution of the constrained problem. A local inner solver may therefore return an augmented minimum irrelevant to the constrained solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonconvex augmented Lagrangian may have a strict infeasible local minimum. A local inner solver can converge to that point rather than return a constrained solution.
assumptions_latex: The inner solver is permitted to return a local rather than global augmented minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The point \(x=0\) satisfies \(L_{\rho}'(0,\lambda)=0\), \(L_{\rho}''(0,\lambda)>0\), and \(c(0)\ne0\), so it is a strict infeasible local augmented minimum.

e0\), or because \(\hat x\) is feasible but \(f(\hat x)>\min\{f(x):c(x)=0\}\). Thus local augmented minimality alone is not a certificate of constrained feasibility or global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local augmented minimum is spurious when it is not a global solution of the constrained problem, whether because it is infeasible or feasible but suboptimal.

children.title: Infeasibility-Divergence Regime Family
children.top_down_role: Behavior when the constraint system is inconsistent or outer sequences fail to stabilize.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Infeasibility–divergence regime family for ALM trajectories
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), let an augmented-Lagrangian method generate \(z_k=(x_k,\lambda_k,\rho_k)\). Write \(v_k=\|c(x_k)\|_2\) and let \(s_k\geq0\) be a declared stationarity residual.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A trajectory-classification definition in finite dimensions. It groups several nonconvergent regimes without claiming that they are exhaustive or mutually exclusive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The infeasibility–divergence regime family \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{ID}}\) consists of trajectories \(\{z_k\}\) satisfying at least one of: (i) structural infeasibility, \(\inf_{x\in X}\|c(x)\|_2>0\); (ii) primal or dual escape, \(\sup_k\|x_k\|_2=+\infty\) or \(\sup_k\|\lambda_k\|_2=+\infty\); (iii) penalty escape, \(\sup_k\rho_k=+\infty\), together with \(\liminf_k v_k>0\); or (iv) bounded nonsettling behavior, where \(\{(x_k,\lambda_k)\}\) is bounded but has no single limit and \(\limsup_k(v_k+s_k)>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The regime family contains an ALM trajectory if the constraint system is inconsistent, the primal or dual sequence is unbounded, the penalty grows without bound while violation remains bounded away from zero, or the bounded primal-dual sequence fails to settle and retains positive feasibility or stationarity residual. These alternatives classify behavior; they need not be exclusive.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, and \(c:X\to\mathbb R^m\) is defined.
The sequences \(x_k\), \(\lambda_k\), and \(\rho_k>0\), and the residual \(s_k\), are generated or recorded by the method.
A norm and a stationarity residual are fixed throughout the classification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{z_k\}\in\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{ID}}\) exactly when at least one of conditions (i)–(iv) holds.
equivalent_formulations_latex: In finite dimensions, primal or dual escape is equivalent to failure of relative compactness of the corresponding sequence.
Structural infeasibility is equivalent to emptiness of \(\{x\in X:c(x)=0\}\) when the minimum violation is attained and positive.
special_cases_latex: If \(X\) is compact, primal escape is impossible, but dual escape, penalty escape, and bounded nonsettling behavior remain possible.
immediate_consequences_latex: Membership in one branch does not determine membership in another; an infeasible problem may produce bounded or unbounded primal iterates.
Ordinary convergence to a feasible stationary primal-dual point lies outside this family.
boundary_notes: The condition \(\inf_X\|c\|_2=0\) does not guarantee feasibility when the infimum is unattained.
Slow convergence with residuals tending to zero is not classified as stagnation by condition (iv).

notation.meaning: Family of infeasible, escaping, or nonsettling ALM trajectories.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: infeasibility, unboundedness, penalty escalation, and bounded nonsettling trajectories are standard distinct failure diagnostics.
No inspected source establishes this exact four-branch regime taxonomy.
knowledge_statements.title: Infeasibility–divergence regime family for ALM trajectories

children.title: Infeasible-Problem Behavior
children.top_down_role: Augmented-Lagrangian behavior when no feasible point exists.

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible-Problem Behavior
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostic behavior of equality-constrained augmented-Lagrangian iterations when the constraint system is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), and define \(\mathcal L_{\rho}(x,y)=f(x)+y^{\mathsf T}c(x)+(\rho/2)\lVert c(x)\rVert^2\). Suppose \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) are continuous and \(\{x\in\mathbb R^n:c(x)=0\}=\varnothing\). For every convergent subsequence \(x_{k_j}\to\bar x\), continuity gives \(\lVert c(x_{k_j})\rVert\to\lVert c(\bar x)\rVert>0\); hence the outer sequence has no feasible accumulation point. If at least one convergent subsequence exists, then \(\lVert c(x_k)\rVert\not\to0\). More strongly, if all \(x_k\) lie in a compact set \(K\), then \(\inf_{x\in K}\lVert c(x)\rVert>0\). Without such compactness, infeasibility alone does not exclude an unbounded sequence with \(\lVert c(x_k)\rVert\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an infeasible continuous constraint system, every primal accumulation point has positive constraint residual. A convergent subsequence therefore prevents the full residual sequence from tending to zero, while compact containment gives a uniform positive residual bound; without compactness, infeasibility alone does not rule out residuals approaching zero along an unbounded sequence.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) are continuous.
For the uniform residual bound, \(x_k\in K\) for a compact set \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(x_{k_j}\to\bar x\), then \(\lVert c(\bar x)\rVert>0\); if \(x_k\in K\) for compact \(K\), then \(\inf_{x\in K}\lVert c(x)\rVert>0\).

notation.meaning: compact set containing the primal iterates when a uniform residual bound is asserted

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: ALM behavior on a strongly infeasible equality system
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and closed, and consider \(c(x)=0\) with \(c:X\to\mathbb R^m\) continuous. Define the least violation \(\delta_*:=\inf_{x\in X}\|c(x)\|_2\). Let an augmented-Lagrangian method generate \((x_k,\lambda_k,\rho_k)\), with violation \(v_k=\|c(x_k)\|_2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality constraints with positive minimum residual. The definition describes observable least-violation behavior and does not assert that every ALM must exhibit it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The problem is strongly infeasible when \(\delta_*>0\). An ALM trajectory exhibits least-violation infeasible-problem behavior when the problem is strongly infeasible and \(v_k\to\delta_*\). It exhibits penalty-driven infeasible behavior when, additionally, \(\rho_k\to+\infty\). It exhibits multiplier-divergent infeasible behavior when \(\|\lambda_k\|_2\to+\infty\). These modifiers may hold jointly or separately and are properties of the trajectory, not consequences included in the definition of strong infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint system is strongly infeasible when the smallest attainable or approachable residual norm is strictly positive. An ALM trajectory has least-violation infeasible behavior if its residual norms converge to that positive infimum. Penalty-driven behavior adds divergence of the penalty parameters, while multiplier-divergent behavior adds divergence of the multiplier norms. The modifiers describe observations and are not asserted to follow automatically from infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty and closed, and \(c\) is continuous on \(X\).
The equality-constrained feasible set is \(F=\{x\in X:c(x)=0\}\).
The least-violation behavioral classification requires \(\delta_*>0\) and a recorded ALM trajectory.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strong infeasibility is \(\delta_*>0\); least-violation behavior is \(v_k\to\delta_*\), optionally accompanied by \(\rho_k\to+\infty\) or \(\|\lambda_k\|_2\to+\infty\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\delta_*>0\) is equivalent to the existence of \(\epsilon>0\) such that \(\|c(x)\|_2\geq\epsilon\) for every \(x\in X\).
Strong infeasibility implies \(F=\varnothing\), but the converse can fail if \(\delta_*=0\) is unattained.
special_cases_latex: If \(X\) is compact and \(F=\varnothing\), continuity of \(c\) implies \(\delta_*>0\) and the infimum is attained.
immediate_consequences_latex: A trajectory with \(v_k\to\delta_*>0\) cannot have a feasible accumulation point.
Residual stagnation at a value strictly larger than \(\delta_*\) is not least-violation behavior.
boundary_notes: Weak infeasibility, defined by \(F=\varnothing\) and \(\delta_*=0\), is excluded.
Inequality constraints require a violation mapping such as the positive part of the constraint vector.

notation.meaning: Infimum of the constraint-residual norm over the primal domain.
Constraint violation at the kth primal iterate.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: positive minimum residual is a precise finite-dimensional notion of strong infeasibility, while sequence modifiers distinguish observed ALM behavior.
No inspected source supports the exact trajectory terminology used here.

children.title: Primal or Dual Sequence Divergence
children.top_down_role: Loss of boundedness or compactness in outer sequences.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal or Dual Sequence Divergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundedness failure of primal iterates or multiplier estimates in an augmented-Lagrangian outer iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an outer sequence \(z_k=(x_k,y_k)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\), primal divergence occurs when \(\{x_k\}\) is unbounded, and dual divergence occurs when \(\{y_k\}\) is unbounded. Equivalently, these conditions are \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}\lVert x_k\rVert=\infty\) and \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}\lVert y_k\rVert=\infty\), respectively. Either condition destroys compactness of the corresponding sequence and prevents any convergence argument requiring a bounded full outer sequence. Divergence alone does not certify infeasibility: it may also result from noncoercive subproblems, inaccurate inner solves, unstable multiplier updates, or unsuitable penalty control.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unbounded primal or multiplier iterates mark loss of compactness, invalidate bounded-sequence convergence arguments, and do not alone certify infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: The outer iterates \((x_k,y_k)\) lie in finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\limsup_k\lVert x_k\rVert=\infty\) or \(\limsup_k\lVert y_k\rVert=\infty\) implies loss of primal or dual sequential compactness, respectively.

assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accumulation point \(v\) of \(y_k/\lVert y_k\rVert\) satisfies \(\lVert v\rVert=1\) and \(Jc(\bar x)^{\mathsf T}v=0\); hence full row rank of \(Jc(\bar x)\) excludes this dual-divergence regime.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary Jacobian degeneracy for multiplier divergence along a convergent primal sequence with vanishing Lagrangian-stationarity residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_k=\nabla f(x_k)+Jc(x_k)^{\mathsf T}y_k\). If \(x_k\to\bar x\), \(r_k\to0\), and \(\lVert y_k\rVert\to\infty\), then every accumulation point \(v\) of \(v_k=y_k/\lVert y_k\rVert\) satisfies \(\lVert v\rVert=1\) and \(Jc(\bar x)^{\mathsf T}v=0\). Consequently, if \(Jc(\bar x)\) has full row rank, convergent primal iterates and vanishing stationarity residual are incompatible with multiplier divergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If primal iterates converge and stationarity residuals vanish while multipliers diverge, normalized multipliers expose a nonzero left-null direction of the limiting constraint Jacobian. Full row rank rules out this regime.
knowledge_statements.title: Normalized-Multiplier Degeneracy

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal and dual escape of an ALM trajectory
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let an augmented-Lagrangian method generate primal iterates \(x_k\in\mathbb R^n\) and multiplier iterates \(\lambda_k\in\mathbb R^m\). Equip both spaces with fixed norms. A trajectory means the ordered sequence \(\{(x_k,\lambda_k)\}_{k\geq0}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional sequence classification. Divergence means loss of boundedness or compactness, not merely failure to converge to a unique point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The trajectory has primal sequence divergence when \(\sup_{k\geq0}\|x_k\|=+\infty\), equivalently when there exists a subsequence \(x_{k_j}\) with \(\|x_{k_j}\|\to+\infty\). It has dual sequence divergence when \(\sup_{k\geq0}\|\lambda_k\|=+\infty\), equivalently when a subsequence satisfies \(\|\lambda_{k_j}\|\to+\infty\). Primal-or-dual divergence is the union of these events. Joint divergence means both events occur, without requiring the same subsequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal sequence diverges in the escape sense when its norms are unbounded; the dual sequence diverges when the multiplier norms are unbounded. In finite dimensions, either condition is equivalent to the existence of a subsequence whose norm tends to infinity. Primal-or-dual divergence means at least one sequence escapes. Joint divergence means both escape, possibly along different subsequences.
assumptions_latex: \(x_k\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\lambda_k\in\mathbb R^m\) are defined for all relevant outer iterations.
The dimensions are finite and the norms are fixed; the classification is norm-independent because all norms are equivalent in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Primal-or-dual divergence holds exactly when \(\sup_k\|x_k\|=+\infty\) or \(\sup_k\|\lambda_k\|=+\infty\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The primal sequence diverges exactly when \(\{x_k:k\geq0\}\) is not relatively compact; the analogous statement holds for \(\{\lambda_k\}\).
Primal-or-dual divergence is equivalent to \(\sup_k\|(x_k,\lambda_k)\|=+\infty\) for any product norm.
special_cases_latex: If the primal domain \(X\) is compact and every \(x_k\in X\), primal divergence is impossible.
A bounded primal sequence may coexist with an unbounded multiplier sequence under degeneracy or infeasibility.
immediate_consequences_latex: An escaping sequence has no convergent full sequence and no bounded subsequence containing all sufficiently large iterates.
Failure to converge by cycling is not divergence under this definition when the sequence remains bounded.
boundary_notes: Oscillation between bounded accumulation points is classified separately as cycling or nonsettling behavior.
In infinite-dimensional spaces, boundedness need not imply relative compactness, so the equivalence requires modification.

notation.meaning: A subsequence of primal iterates witnessing escape.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: unboundedness and loss of relative compactness are canonical finite-dimensional notions of sequence escape.
A source specific to ALM failure diagnostics was not inspected.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal and dual escape of an ALM trajectory

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cycling and stagnation of bounded ALM iterates
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(z_k=(x_k,\lambda_k)\in\mathbb R^{n+m}\) be a bounded ALM primal-dual sequence. Let \(v_k\geq0\) and \(s_k\geq0\) denote declared feasibility and stationarity residuals, and set \(R_k=v_k+s_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional bounded trajectories. Cycling and stagnation are defined separately and may overlap; unbounded escape is excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The sequence exhibits an asymptotic cycle of period \(p\geq2\) when there exist distinct points \(\bar z_0,\ldots,\bar z_{p-1}\) such that \(z_{jp+r}\to\bar z_r\) for every \(r\in\{0,\ldots,p-1\}\). It exhibits residual stagnation when \(R_k\to\bar R>0\) and \(\|z_{k+1}-z_k\|\to0\). More generally, it exhibits window stagnation of width \(q\geq1\) when \(\lim_{k\to\infty}(\max_{0\leq j\leq q}R_{k+j}-\min_{0\leq j\leq q}R_{k+j})=0\) while \(\liminf_k R_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded primal-dual sequence cycles with period at least two when each residue class of iteration indices converges to a different point in a finite periodic orbit. It stagnates when feasibility plus stationarity residual converges to a positive value while consecutive iterates become indistinguishable. Window stagnation instead requires vanishing residual variation over fixed windows while the residual remains bounded away from zero.
assumptions_latex: The residuals \(v_k\) and \(s_k\) are nonnegative and use fixed definitions across iterations.
For a cycle, the limiting points \(\bar z_r\) are pairwise distinct and \(p\geq2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Cycling is convergence of residue-class subsequences to a nontrivial finite orbit; stagnation is vanishing progress with \(\liminf_k(v_k+s_k)>0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For an exact period-\(p\) cycle, \(\operatorname{dist}(z_k,\{\bar z_0,\ldots,\bar z_{p-1}\})\to0\) with phase determined by \(k\bmod p\).
special_cases_latex: A two-cycle has \(z_{2j}\to\bar z_0\), \(z_{2j+1}\to\bar z_1\), and \(\bar z_0\neq\bar z_1\).
If \(R_k\equiv\bar R>0\) eventually and \(\|z_{k+1}-z_k\|\to0\), residual stagnation holds.
immediate_consequences_latex: A nontrivial asymptotic cycle prevents convergence of the full primal-dual sequence.
Residual stagnation excludes convergence to a point certified by \(v_k+s_k\to0\).
boundary_notes: Slow but genuine convergence with \(R_k\to0\) is not stagnation.
Chaotic bounded nonconvergence need not satisfy the finite-cycle definition.
A fixed point with positive residual is stagnation, not a period-one cycle under the stated convention.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: periodic subsequence limits and positive residual plateaus give precise sequence-theoretic meanings to cycling and stagnation.
No inspected ALM source supports these exact diagnostic thresholds.
knowledge_statements.title: Cycling and stagnation of bounded ALM iterates

children.title: Outer-Iteration Cycling
children.top_down_role: Repeated outer-iteration patterns that prevent sustained progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Outer-Iteration Cycling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact or asymptotic recurrence of augmented-Lagrangian outer states without convergence to one state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z_k=(x_k,y_k,\rho_k)\) be the outer state. Exact outer-iteration cycling of period \(p\ge2\) from index \(K\) means \(z_{k+p}=z_k\) for every \(k\ge K\), while the states \(z_K,\ldots,z_{K+p-1}\) are not all equal. Asymptotic cycling of period \(p\) means \(\lVert z_{k+p}-z_k\rVert\to0\) but \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}\lVert z_{k+1}-z_k\rVert>0\). The latter condition excludes ordinary convergence and distinguishes recurrence among separated states from stagnation with vanishing successive changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cycling is repeated or asymptotically repeated outer states of period at least two, with persistent separation between successive states.
assumptions_latex: The state variables are represented in a finite-dimensional normed space.
For asymptotic cycling, the penalty coordinate is scaled so state norms are meaningful.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Cycling has period \(p\ge2\) and does not reduce to convergence toward a single stationary state.

notation.meaning: combined primal, multiplier, and penalty state
first index of an exact cycle

children.title: Outer-Iteration Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Outer regimes with negligible improvement in feasibility or stationarity.

knowledge_statements.title: Outer-Iteration Stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vanishing outer-step changes without satisfaction of the prescribed optimality and feasibility tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z_k=(x_k,y_k,\rho_k)\), let \(r_k\ge0\) be a KKT-residual measure, and fix tolerances \(\tau_z>0\) and \(\tau_r>0\). Outer-iteration stagnation is present when \(\lVert z_{k+1}-z_k\rVert\to0\) while \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}r_k>\tau_r\). A finite-window stagnation flag over \(W\ge1\) iterations is the checkable condition \(\max_{k-W<j\le k}\lVert z_j-z_{j-1}\rVert\le\tau_z\) together with \(\min_{k-W<j\le k}r_j>\tau_r\). This definition separates lack of motion from successful convergence, for which both state changes and residuals may be small.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stagnation means outer steps become negligible while the KKT residual remains above tolerance; a finite-window test provides an operational flag.
assumptions_latex: The residual \(r_k\) vanishes only when the chosen KKT conditions are satisfied.
State components are scaled consistently in the norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Small state changes combined with \(r_k>\tau_r\) diagnose unsuccessful stagnation rather than convergence.
review_flags: no supplied locator specifically defines outer-iteration stagnation
tolerances and residual scaling are implementation-dependent

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits stagnation, but the residual threshold, scaling assumptions, and finite-window rule are implementation-dependent and uncited. The finite-window rule also overlaps the dedicated Cycle–Stagnation Diagnostics leaf. A source must establish the intended stagnation convention and clarify which operational material belongs in each terminal container.

children.title: Cycle–Stagnation Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Diagnostic distinctions between recurrent motion and near-static nonprogress.

knowledge_statements.title: Cycle–Stagnation Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-history certificates distinguishing approximate recurrence from negligible motion at an unacceptable residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given states \(z_{k-W},\ldots,z_k\), residuals \(r_j\), tolerances \(\tau_c,\tau_s,\tau_r>0\), and a candidate period \(2\le p\le W\), an approximate-cycle certificate is \(\max_{k-W+p\le j\le k}\lVert z_j-z_{j-p}\rVert\le\tau_c\) and \(\max_{k-W<j\le k}\lVert z_j-z_{j-1}\rVert>\tau_s\). A stagnation certificate is \(\max_{k-W<j\le k}\lVert z_j-z_{j-1}\rVert\le\tau_s\) and \(\min_{k-W<j\le k}r_j>\tau_r\). Each certificate is directly verifiable from the stored window; neither establishes infeasibility or global nonconvergence beyond that window.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stored iterates certify approximate cycling through lagged recurrence, or stagnation through tiny steps and persistently unacceptable residuals; neither proves infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: All state components and residual components use fixed, compatible scaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequalities provide mutually interpretable finite-window cycle and stagnation flags without certifying infeasibility.
review_flags: diagnostic thresholds are proposed operational conventions
no supplied locator supports this precise finite-window certificate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind correctly matches the diagnostics leaf, and the formulas are finite-history checks rather than claims of global nonconvergence. The precise lag, window, scaling, and threshold conventions have no supporting source, so the proposed certificates require sourcing before acceptance.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Structural linkage of the augmented Lagrangian to neighboring method families
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(\min_x f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), define \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}c(x)\) and \(\mathcal L_\rho(x,\lambda)=L(x,\lambda)+(\rho/2)\|c(x)\|_2^2\), with \(\rho\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth equality constraints and algebraic or algorithmic interfaces. A linkage records a precise specialization, reformulation, or update decomposition rather than a historical or thematic association.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An augmented-Lagrangian linkage is a map between \(\mathcal L_\rho\) and a neighboring optimization construction that preserves an explicitly stated mathematical object. The canonical linkage set consists of: \(\mathcal L_0=L\) (ordinary Lagrangian specialization); \(\mathcal L_\rho(\cdot,0)=f+(\rho/2)\|c\|_2^2\) (quadratic-penalty specialization); \(\mathcal L_\rho=f+(\rho/2)\|c+\lambda/\rho\|_2^2-\|\lambda\|_2^2/(2\rho)\) for \(\rho>0\) (shifted-penalty representation); multiplier updating \(\lambda^+=\lambda+\rho c(x^+)\); and, for block-separable variables, blockwise minimization of the same coupled augmented objective. Each linkage is identified by the preserved objective, stationarity system, or multiplier update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linkage is a precise specialization, reformulation, or decomposition of the augmented Lagrangian that preserves a named mathematical object. Setting the penalty to zero gives the ordinary Lagrangian; setting the multiplier to zero gives the quadratic penalty; completing the square gives a shifted penalty; the residual produces the multiplier update; and separable variables permit blockwise minimization of the coupled objective.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) are defined on a common domain.
A decomposition linkage additionally requires an explicit partition of the primal variables and objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The linkage family is determined by exact identities or declared update decompositions involving \(L\), \(\mathcal L_\rho\), the quadratic penalty, and the multiplier residual step.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(\rho>0\), minimizing \(\mathcal L_\rho(x,\lambda)\) over \(x\) is equivalent to minimizing \(f(x)+(\rho/2)\|c(x)+\lambda/\rho\|_2^2\), because the omitted term is constant in \(x\).
special_cases_latex: With \(c(x)=Ax-b\), the augmentation contributes the quadratic curvature \(\rho A^{\mathsf T}A\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Pure penalty and ordinary Lagrangian models occur at different parameter boundaries and should not be conflated.
Block splitting changes the update architecture while retaining the same coupled augmented objective.
boundary_notes: An informal resemblance without a preserved identity, stationarity system, or update is not a linkage under this definition.
Inequality-constrained augmented Lagrangians require projection or slack-variable variants.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the listed algebraic specializations and square-completion identity are standard structural relations.
No single inspected source was available to support the complete linkage taxonomy.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Interface between quadratic penalties and multiplier augmentation
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\). Define the quadratic-penalty objective \(Q_\rho(x)=f(x)+(\rho/2)\|c(x)\|_2^2\) and the augmented Lagrangian \(\mathcal L_\rho(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}c(x)+(\rho/2)\|c(x)\|_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality constraints with quadratic augmentation. The interface is structural: it distinguishes a primal penalty family from a primal-dual multiplier family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The penalty-method interface is the embedding \(Q_\rho(x)=\mathcal L_\rho(x,0)\), together with the distinction between the pure-penalty update \(x_{k+1}\approx\arg\min_{x\in X}Q_{\rho_k}(x)\), which has no multiplier state, and the multiplier update \(x_{k+1}\approx\arg\min_{x\in X}\mathcal L_{\rho_k}(x,\lambda_k)\), \(\lambda_{k+1}=\lambda_k+\rho_k c(x_{k+1})\). Thus the pure quadratic-penalty method is the zero-multiplier objective slice, whereas ALM evolves the linear constraint-price term across outer iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The quadratic-penalty objective is exactly the zero-multiplier slice of the augmented Lagrangian. A pure penalty method minimizes that primal objective and changes only its penalty parameter. A multiplier method minimizes a shifted objective containing the current multiplier and then updates that multiplier by the scaled constraint residual. This state update is the defining boundary between the two architectures.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), and \(c:X\to\mathbb R^m\).
The symbol \(\approx\arg\min\) permits an explicitly controlled inexact inner solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_\rho=\mathcal L_\rho(\cdot,0)\), while ALM differs algorithmically by retaining and updating \(\lambda_k\) through \(\lambda_{k+1}=\lambda_k+\rho_kc(x_{k+1})\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(\rho>0\), \(\mathcal L_\rho(x,\lambda)=f(x)+(\rho/2)\|c(x)+\lambda/\rho\|_2^2-\|\lambda\|_2^2/(2\rho)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\lambda_k=0\) is forcibly reset at every iteration, the primal subproblem reduces to a quadratic-penalty subproblem.
For linear constraints \(c(x)=Ax-b\), both models add curvature \(\rho A^{\mathsf T}A\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A nonzero multiplier shifts the target residual in the completed-square representation.
The algebraic embedding does not make a pure penalty iteration identical to ALM, because their state updates differ.
boundary_notes: Exact \(\ell_1\) penalties are outside this quadratic interface.
Inequality constraints require projected multiplier updates or an equivalent slack formulation.

notation.meaning: Multiplier state absent from a pure penalty method and updated by ALM.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the zero-multiplier identity and residual multiplier update canonically separate quadratic penalty and ALM architectures.

children.title: Quadratic-Penalty Comparison
children.top_down_role: Structural comparison of primal penalty and augmented multiplier models.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-Penalty Comparison
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic comparison for smooth equality constraints under a fixed multiplier estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the constraint \(c(x)=0\), the quadratic-penalty objective is \(Q_{\rho}(x)=f(x)+(\rho/2)\lVert c(x)\rVert^2\), whereas the augmented Lagrangian is \(\mathcal L_{\rho}(x,y)=f(x)+y^{\mathsf T}c(x)+(\rho/2)\lVert c(x)\rVert^2\). Completing the square gives \[\mathcal L_{\rho}(x,y)=f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\left\lVert c(x)+\frac{y}{\rho}\right\rVert^2-\frac{1}{2\rho}\lVert y\rVert^2.\] Thus, for fixed \(y\), augmented-Lagrangian minimization is a shifted quadratic-penalty subproblem; unlike the pure penalty method, multiplier updates can represent first-order constraint forces without requiring feasibility to be driven solely by \(\rho\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The augmented Lagrangian is a shifted quadratic penalty plus an irrelevant constant, with multiplier estimates carrying first-order constraint information.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For fixed \(y\), minimizing \(\mathcal L_{\rho}(\cdot,y)\) is equivalent to minimizing the displayed shifted quadratic-penalty expression.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order comparison identifying the implicit multiplier carried by a quadratic-penalty stationary point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Q_\rho(x)=f(x)+(\rho/2)\lVert c(x)\rVert^2\), define the effective multiplier \(y_\rho=\rho c(x_\rho)\). Then \(\nabla Q_\rho(x_\rho)=\nabla f(x_\rho)+J_c(x_\rho)^{\mathsf T}y_\rho\). Thus stationarity of a quadratic-penalty subproblem is exactly Lagrangian stationarity with multiplier estimate \(y_\rho\), but it does not itself impose \(c(x_\rho)=0\). If \(y_\rho\) remains bounded along a sequence with \(\rho\to\infty\), then \(\lVert c(x_\rho)\rVert=O(1/\rho)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stationary quadratic-penalty point carries the implicit multiplier estimate equal to the penalty parameter times its residual; bounded effective multipliers yield inverse-penalty feasibility decay.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Algebraic comparison of quadratic-penalty and augmented models
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For an equality-constrained problem, let \(Q_\rho(x)=f(x)+(\rho/2)\|c(x)\|_2^2\) and \(\mathcal L_\rho(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}c(x)+(\rho/2)\|c(x)\|_2^2\), with \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An exact objective-level comparison for quadratic augmentation. It does not claim identical minimizers for arbitrary nonzero multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The quadratic-penalty comparison is the pair of identities \(\mathcal L_\rho(x,\lambda)=Q_\rho(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}c(x)\) and \(\mathcal L_\rho(x,\lambda)=f(x)+(\rho/2)\|c(x)+\lambda/\rho\|_2^2-\|\lambda\|_2^2/(2\rho)\). Hence, for fixed \((\lambda,\rho)\), an augmented-Lagrangian subproblem is a quadratic-penalty subproblem centered at residual \(-\lambda/\rho\), up to an additive constant independent of \(x\). The pure quadratic penalty is recovered exactly at \(\lambda=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The augmented objective equals the pure quadratic penalty plus a linear multiplier term. Completing the square shows that it is also a quadratic penalty whose residual target is shifted from zero to minus the multiplier divided by the penalty, plus a constant that does not affect primal minimization. Setting the multiplier to zero recovers the pure penalty exactly.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) share a common primal domain.
The Euclidean norm and its associated inner product are used.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For fixed \((\lambda,\rho)\), \(\arg\min_x\mathcal L_\rho(x,\lambda)=\arg\min_x\{f(x)+(\rho/2)\|c(x)+\lambda/\rho\|_2^2\}\).
special_cases_latex: If \(c(x)=Ax-b\), the two objectives have the same quadratic augmentation Hessian contribution \(\rho A^{\mathsf T}A\); only the linear constraint term changes.
At \(\lambda=0\), both the residual center and additive constant vanish.
immediate_consequences_latex: The multiplier changes first-order terms without changing the coefficient of the quadratic residual penalty.
A finite \(\rho\) can be retained while the residual target changes through multiplier updates.
boundary_notes: The comparison is algebraic and does not guarantee convexity or uniqueness of a subproblem minimizer.
Weighted quadratic penalties replace \(\rho I\) by a positive-definite weight and require the corresponding weighted square completion.

notation.meaning: Shifted residual target of the augmented model.

children.top_down_role: Globalization interfaces combining exact penalties with multiplier models.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Penalty Hybridization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Globalization combining an exact merit function with augmented-Lagrangian or multiplier-model trial steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \((x_k,y_k)\), form a trial step \(d_k\) from an augmented-Lagrangian, Newton, or quasi-Newton model. Choose \(\sigma_k>0\) and define the exact merit function \(\Phi_{\sigma_k}(x)=f(x)+\sigma_k\lVert c(x)\rVert_1\). Accept a step length \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\) only if it provides the prescribed sufficient decrease in \(\Phi_{\sigma_k}\); otherwise reduce \(\alpha_k\) or revise the model. Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), update \(y_{k+1}\) from the accepted multiplier model, and stop when the chosen feasibility and stationarity residuals meet tolerance. Exactness requires \(\sigma_k\) eventually to dominate relevant optimal multipliers locally.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hybrid computes multiplier-model steps but accepts them using an exact penalty merit function whose weight eventually dominates local multipliers.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are continuously differentiable near the iterates.
Trial directions and multiplier estimates are available from a local constrained model.
The merit weight can be increased when sufficient decrease is unavailable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accepted iterates decrease the selected exact merit function, while sufficiently large \(\sigma_k\) makes local merit minimizers compatible with constrained solutions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact-penalty globalization of augmented or primal-dual steps
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_x f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\). Let \(d_k\) be a trial step generated from an augmented-Lagrangian or primal-dual local model. Define the nonsmooth exact-penalty merit function \(\Phi_\sigma(x)=f(x)+\sigma\|c(x)\|_1\), where \(\sigma>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth equality constraints with an \(\ell_1\) exact-penalty merit function used for globalization. Exactness itself requires additional local regularity and a sufficiently large penalty weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exact-penalty hybrid is an iteration in which the trial direction \(d_k\) is computed from an augmented-Lagrangian, Lagrangian-Newton, or primal-dual model, while the accepted step \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\) is selected by a sufficient-decrease condition for \(\Phi_{\sigma_k}\). With directional derivative \(\Phi_{\sigma_k}'(x_k;d_k)\), a canonical line-search test is \(\Phi_{\sigma_k}(x_k+\alpha_kd_k)\leq\Phi_{\sigma_k}(x_k)+\theta\alpha_k\Phi_{\sigma_k}'(x_k;d_k)\), where \(0<\theta<1\) and the direction must satisfy \(\Phi_{\sigma_k}'(x_k;d_k)<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact-penalty hybrid computes a trial direction using an augmented or primal-dual local model but globalizes that direction using an exact-penalty merit function. A step is accepted only if it provides the prescribed directional sufficient decrease in the merit function. The local model and globalization function are therefore mathematically distinct components of the iteration.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are continuously differentiable near the iterates.
\(0<\theta<1\), \(\alpha_k>0\), and the accepted direction is a descent direction for \(\Phi_{\sigma_k}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Hybridization is the conjunction of augmented or primal-dual direction generation and acceptance by sufficient decrease in \(\Phi_{\sigma_k}=f+\sigma_k\|c\|_1\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: A trust-region variant is hybrid under the same definition when the acceptance ratio uses actual and predicted reduction of \(\Phi_{\sigma_k}\) while the trial step comes from the augmented local model.
special_cases_latex: For a single equality, \(\Phi_\sigma(x)=f(x)+\sigma|c(x)|\).
An augmented-Lagrangian Newton direction may be accepted by backtracking on \(\Phi_\sigma\) without using \(\Phi_\sigma\) to form the direction.
immediate_consequences_latex: A step can solve the local augmented model accurately yet be rejected by the exact-penalty globalization test.
The merit weight \(\sigma_k\) and augmentation parameter \(\rho_k\) are distinct algorithmic quantities.
boundary_notes: The definition does not assert that a particular \(\sigma\) is exact; that requires multiplier bounds and constraint qualification assumptions.
Squared \(\ell_2\) penalties are generally not exact at finite penalty values and are excluded from the exact-penalty component.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: combining a primal-dual direction with an exact-penalty line search is a standard globalization architecture.
The exact hybrid definition and acceptance formula need an inspected source locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Augmented globalization of a constrained Newton step
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(\min_x f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), let \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}c(x)\), \(J(x)=\nabla c(x)\), and \(F(x,\lambda)=(\nabla_xL(x,\lambda),c(x))\). A constrained Newton step \((d_k,\delta\lambda_k)\) solves a linearization of \(F=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth equality-constrained problems. The interface separates a local Newton model of the KKT equations from a global acceptance mechanism based on an augmented merit function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The constrained Newton globalization interface consists of the KKT Newton system \(\begin{pmatrix}B_k&J_k^{\mathsf T}\\J_k&0\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}d_k\\\delta\lambda_k\end{pmatrix}=-\begin{pmatrix}\nabla_xL(x_k,\lambda_k)\\c(x_k)\end{pmatrix}\), with symmetric \(B_k\) approximating \(\nabla_{xx}^2L(x_k,\lambda_k)\), coupled to an acceptance rule for a scalar augmented merit function \(M_k(x,\lambda)\). The accepted update \((x_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1})=(x_k,\lambda_k)+\alpha_k(d_k,\delta\lambda_k)\) must satisfy a declared sufficient-decrease or trust-region ratio test for \(M_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constrained Newton step is obtained by linearizing the primal-dual KKT equations. The globalization interface couples that local saddle-point system to a scalar augmented merit function used to accept, shorten, or reject the step. The Newton equations define the direction, while the merit or trust-region test controls global progress.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(x_k\).
\(B_k\) is symmetric and the displayed KKT linear system is solvable, exactly or to a declared residual tolerance.
The merit function \(M_k\) and its acceptance parameters are specified before step acceptance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface is the pairing of a KKT-Newton direction with globalization by an augmented scalar merit or trust-region acceptance test.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The Newton system is the linear equation \(DF(x_k,\lambda_k)(d_k,\delta\lambda_k)=-F(x_k,\lambda_k)\) when \(B_k=\nabla_{xx}^2L(x_k,\lambda_k)\).
special_cases_latex: A line-search interface chooses \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\) by sufficient decrease in \(M_k\).
A trust-region interface constrains \(d_k\) and accepts it by an actual-to-predicted reduction ratio.
immediate_consequences_latex: The full Newton step may be rejected far from a solution even when the KKT system is solved exactly.
Changing the merit function alters globalization without changing the formal KKT Newton equations.
boundary_notes: The displayed system treats equality constraints only; active-set or complementarity equations are needed for inequalities.
Penalty-free primal-dual methods that globalize the residual equations without augmentation form a neighboring interface.

notation.meaning: Exact or approximate Lagrangian Hessian in the Newton system.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the saddle-point Newton system and merit-function acceptance are standard components of constrained Newton globalization.
No inspected source was available for the exact augmented-interface formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian–Newton Hybrids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Augmented-Lagrangian globalization followed by local Newton correction of the equality-constrained KKT equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(c(x)=0\), define \(F(x,y)=(\nabla f(x)+J_c(x)^{\mathsf T}y,c(x))\). From \((x_k,y_k)\), use an augmented-Lagrangian merit model to globalize a trial pair \((d_k,\delta y_k)\). Once the iterate enters a neighborhood where the KKT matrix is nonsingular and a full step passes the acceptance test, compute the Newton correction from \[\begin{pmatrix}\nabla^2_{xx}L(x_k,y_k)&J_c(x_k)^{\mathsf T}\\J_c(x_k)&0\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}d_k\\\delta y_k\end{pmatrix}=-F(x_k,y_k),\] and set \((x_{k+1},y_{k+1})=(x_k,y_k)+(d_k,\delta y_k)\). Stop when \(\lVert F(x_k,y_k)\rVert\) meets tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method globalizes with an augmented merit model, then switches locally to Newton steps for the primal–dual KKT system.
assumptions_latex: The local KKT matrix is nonsingular near the target solution.
The globalization test accepts sufficiently accurate local full Newton steps.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The outer method transitions from safeguarded augmented-Lagrangian steps to full primal–dual Newton corrections of \(F(x,y)=0\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a smooth equality-constrained problem, define \(F(x,\lambda)=(\nabla_xL(x,\lambda),c(x))\) and the augmented merit function \(M_\rho(x,\lambda)=\mathcal L_\rho(x,\lambda)+(\tau/2)\|\nabla_xL(x,\lambda)\|_2^2\), where \(\rho,\tau\geq0\) are globalization parameters.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A structural definition for methods combining a local primal-dual Newton model with augmented-Lagrangian globalization. The particular merit function may vary by method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Lagrangian–Newton hybrid is an iteration whose local direction \(p_k=(d_k,\delta\lambda_k)\) satisfies \(DF(x_k,\lambda_k)p_k=-F(x_k,\lambda_k)+e_k\) for a controlled linear-solve residual \(e_k\), while its step length or trust-region acceptance is determined by an augmented scalar model such as \(M_{\rho_k}\). The update is \((x_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1})=(x_k,\lambda_k)+\alpha_kp_k\), where \(\alpha_k\) is accepted only under the declared decrease test. The method is hybrid because its local equation is the unaugmented KKT Newton equation while its global control contains augmentation or constraint-violation penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Lagrangian–Newton hybrid computes its local direction from a Newton linearization of the primal-dual KKT residual, possibly inexactly, but controls acceptance using an augmented scalar merit model. Thus the local fast model and the global safeguarding model are different mathematical objects joined in one iteration.
assumptions_latex: The KKT residual map \(F\) is differentiable at the current primal-dual point.
The Newton residual \(e_k\) obeys a declared forcing bound, and the globalization test is specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Hybrid status requires both \(DF(z_k)p_k=-F(z_k)+e_k\) and acceptance of \(z_k+\alpha_kp_k\) by an augmented merit or trust-region rule.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(e_k=0\), the direction is the exact primal-dual Newton step for \(F=0\).
A quasi-Newton hybrid replaces the Lagrangian Hessian block in \(DF\) by a symmetric approximation while retaining the same constraint Jacobian blocks.
special_cases_latex: If the full Newton step satisfies the augmented decrease test, then \(\alpha_k=1\) may be accepted.
A line-search hybrid and a trust-region hybrid differ in global control but share the KKT-based local model.
immediate_consequences_latex: Augmentation need not appear in the Newton equations to influence global convergence behavior.
Local Newton behavior may emerge once the globalization mechanism consistently accepts full steps.
boundary_notes: A method that computes directions by minimizing the augmented Lagrangian itself, without a KKT Newton system, is not a Lagrangian–Newton hybrid under this definition.
No local convergence rate is included in this definitional slot.

knowledge_statements.title: Linearly Constrained Lagrangian Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local augmented-objective model restricted by the affine linearization of nonlinear equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(x_k\), replace \(c(x_k+d)=0\) by the affine constraint \(c(x_k)+J_c(x_k)d=0\). A linearly constrained augmented-Lagrangian interface computes \(d_k\) from \[\min_d\; \nabla f(x_k)^{\mathsf T}d+\frac12d^{\mathsf T}B_kd+y_k^{\mathsf T}\bigl(c(x_k)+J_c(x_k)d\bigr)+\frac{\rho_k}{2}\left\lVert c(x_k)+J_c(x_k)d\right\rVert^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad c(x_k)+J_c(x_k)d=0.\] On the affine constraint, the last two terms are zero; hence this formulation exposes the same equality-constrained quadratic step as a Lagrangian model while retaining augmentation for relaxed or inexact variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting an augmented quadratic model to linearized feasibility removes its penalty terms and reveals the equality-constrained Lagrangian subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On the linearized constraint set, the augmented model equals \(\nabla f(x_k)^{\mathsf T}d+(1/2)d^{\mathsf T}B_kd\).
